processes.title: From applying for divorce by agreement to the divorce report
processes.summary: If the spouses have agreed on the divorce and on matters concerning the children, they obtain the court's confirmation and report the divorce. The court does not confirm property matters, so you need a separate written agreement for those.

steps.title: Settling the terms and writing an agreement
steps.desc: Along with the divorce itself, you decide property division, compensation for emotional distress, the person with parental authority and the custodial parent, child support and visitation. Since the court does not confirm property matters, keep a separate agreement that states amounts and payment dates, and even the address of any real estate and when ownership will be transferred. If money is to be paid later, one option is to have it made into a notarized deed (공정증서) that includes a clause consenting to compulsory execution.
steps.tip: If the agreement does not say that all other assets and debts stay with whoever's name they are in, you may end up fighting again over the remaining assets after the divorce.

steps.title: Applying for confirmation of intent to divorce
steps.desc: The spouses go together to the family court with jurisdiction over their place of family registration (등록기준지) or address and submit the application. Each spouse attaches a family relationship certificate and a marriage relationship certificate, and if there are minor children, you submit one agreement on custody and the designation of the person with parental authority plus two copies. If one spouse is a Korean national living abroad or is in prison, the other spouse may apply alone.
steps.period: If you do not receive the divorce guidance within 3 months from the day after applying, the application is treated as withdrawn (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 77(3))
steps.tip: Two confirmation hearing dates are usually set and notified together, so write them in your calendar on the spot.

steps.title: Divorce guidance and the cooling-off period
steps.desc: On the day you apply, you receive the divorce guidance provided by the court. If you have minor children, you must also attend the child-rearing guidance and submit a certificate of attendance. The format differs by court, and some courts accept the application only after the education is completed, so ask the court with jurisdiction before applying. Confirmation can be given only after the cooling-off period (숙려기간) has passed from the day of the guidance. Use this time to reread the wording of the agreement, and ask the bank in advance whether the home loan can be taken over.
steps.period: 3 months if there are minor children (including a child in pregnancy), or 1 month if not (Civil Act Article 836-2(2))
steps.tip: If there are circumstances that make waiting difficult, such as violence, you can submit a written statement of reasons with material like a medical certificate and ask for the cooling-off period to be shortened or waived (Article 836-2(3)).

steps.title: Attending the confirmation hearing
steps.desc: The spouses appear together with their ID. The judge confirms whether you intend to divorce and what you have agreed about the children, and if there are minor children, the court draws up a child support protocol (양육비부담조서). The confirmation itself often takes only a few minutes.
steps.period: If you fail to appear twice after receiving notice, the application is treated as withdrawn (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 77(2))
steps.tip: If one of you missed the first hearing, the process is not over. Check the date of the second hearing first.

steps.title: Reporting the divorce
steps.desc: After receiving a certified copy of the confirmation, the divorce takes effect only once it is reported to the city hall, district office, or town or township office. Either spouse may file the report. Before the report, a spouse who has changed their mind can submit a withdrawal of intent to divorce, but if the other spouse files the report first, that report is accepted.
steps.period: Within 3 months of receiving the certified copy of the confirmation. After that, the court's confirmation loses its effect (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 75)

steps.title: Checking that the agreement is carried out
steps.desc: After the divorce is reported, check that property registration transfers, payments and child support deposits are made as agreed. The child support protocol can be used for compulsory execution without a separate lawsuit. If you divorced without settling property division, you must claim it within the deadline.
steps.period: A property division claim must be made within 2 years of the divorce (Civil Act Article 839-2(3))
steps.tip: Once child support starts being late once or twice, keep a monthly table of payments received. That table will be used in every procedure that follows.

processes.title: Divorce mediation and lawsuits
processes.summary: If your spouse will not agree to a divorce, or you cannot agree on the terms, the matter is decided through mediation and a lawsuit in the family court. Divorce is a case that must go through mediation first, so most cases begin with a mediation session.

steps.title: Organizing the facts and materials
steps.desc: Write down in date order what happened that led to the divorce, and collect KakaoTalk messages, recordings, medical certificates and photos in their original form. For assets in your spouse's name, knowing just the names of banks or securities firms, the address of real estate and the workplace is enough to have them checked through the court later.
steps.tip: At Jisan Law, the managing partner handles consultations personally, and in the first consultation we begin by organizing the grounds for divorce and the list of assets with you.

steps.title: Considering provisional attachment and an injunction against disposal
steps.desc: If your spouse has put the home up for sale or there are signs of money being moved, we apply for a preservation measure before filing the complaint. You need material showing the risk of disposal, and the court often orders you to provide security through a cash deposit or a surety bond.
steps.period: Filing for mediation is treated as filing the main lawsuit (Family Litigation Act Article 63(3))
steps.tip: A provisional attachment is usually decided without notice to the other side, so do not tell your spouse before applying.

steps.title: Filing for mediation or a complaint
steps.desc: You can start by filing for mediation, and even if you file a complaint, the court usually refers the case to mediation. Along with the divorce, you claim compensation for emotional distress, property division, designation of the person with parental authority and the custodial parent, child support and visitation all at once.
steps.period: Judicial divorce is a case in which mediation must be requested first (Family Litigation Act Article 50)

steps.title: Answer and counterclaim
steps.desc: The person who receives the complaint files an answer that separates what they admit from what they dispute in the plaintiff's claims. If you should receive compensation or property division, or want to be the custodial parent, you file a counterclaim at the same time.
steps.period: Within 30 days of being served with the copy of the complaint (Civil Procedure Act Article 256; Family Litigation Act Article 12)

steps.title: Applying for a pre-trial measure
steps.desc: You ask the court to decide temporarily who will care for the child until the judgment, how much child support and living expenses will be paid, and how visitation will work. A pre-trial measure is not enforceable, but violating it without a valid reason can lead to an administrative fine.
steps.period: Applied for after filing for mediation or a lawsuit (Family Litigation Act Articles 62 and 67)
steps.tip: If your living expenses have been cut off, it is better to apply at the same time as you file the complaint or the mediation request.

steps.title: Family investigation and checking assets
steps.desc: A family investigator interviews both sides and, if needed, visits the home or interviews the child. If assets are disputed, the court checks the other spouse's assets and severance pay through an asset disclosure order, an asset inquiry, an order to submit financial transaction information and fact inquiries.
steps.period: A family investigation usually takes from a few weeks to a few months
steps.tip: Before the family investigation, reread your notes by date so that what you say does not contradict what is in the complaint or answer.

steps.title: Mediation session
steps.desc: The judge and mediators hear both sides and narrow down the terms. If an agreement is reached, a mediation record is drawn up, which has the same effect as a judicial settlement, and the divorce takes effect as is. Even without agreement, the court may issue a decision in lieu of mediation.
steps.period: A decision in lieu of mediation becomes final if no objection is made within 2 weeks of being served with the original copy (Family Litigation Act Article 49; Civil Conciliation Act Article 34)
steps.tip: Decide in advance the minimum terms you can accept, so that you are not pressured into signing on the spot in the mediation room.

steps.title: Hearings and judgment
steps.desc: If mediation fails, the lawsuit is treated as filed when mediation was requested, and the case moves to litigation. If you receive a correction order to pay the shortfall in stamp fees, you must pay it before the deadline. At the hearings, the case is argued with written submissions and evidence, and a judgment is issued.
steps.period: The first instance usually takes about 6 months to a year, longer if property or custody is heavily disputed
steps.tip: If you move, tell the court your new address for service right away so you do not miss correction orders or hearing notices.

steps.title: Appeal, finality and reporting the divorce
steps.desc: If you disagree with the judgment, you appeal. Once the deadline passes, the judgment becomes final, and you report the divorce within 1 month of that date, attaching a certified copy of the judgment and a certificate of finality. The matter is only over once the property registration and child support payments actually take place.
steps.period: An appeal must be filed within 14 days of being served with the original copy of the judgment (Family Litigation Act Article 19), and the divorce must be reported within 1 month of the judgment becoming final (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Articles 78 and 58)

processes.title: Claiming compensation from the affair partner (plaintiff)
processes.summary: This is the sequence from the day you learn of the affair to the day you receive payment after judgment. If the other side does not contest, it can end within a few months; if the facts are hotly disputed, the first instance alone can take over a year.

steps.title: Consultation and checking the time limit
steps.desc: We start by sorting out when and how you found out about the affair, where your marriage stands now, and what you know about the affair partner (상간자). From this we decide whether the time limit for a claim is still open, and whether to claim together with a divorce lawsuit or against the affair partner only.
steps.period: 3 years from the day you learned of the infidelity and the affair partner; 10 years from the day of the infidelity (Civil Act (민법) Article 766)
steps.tip: Keep any written pledge or message that shows when you found out. Its date can become the starting point for calculating the time limit, so bring it with you.

steps.title: Organizing evidence and identifying the other party
steps.desc: Put KakaoTalk screenshots, photos, card statements, lodging receipts and call logs into one file in date order. If you don't know the affair partner's name or address, also write down any clue that can identify them, such as a phone number, bank account number or car plate number.
steps.period: Usually about 1–3 weeks
steps.tip: Take screenshots so the date and the other person's name appear on the same screen, and do not delete the original chats or files.

steps.title: Considering evidence preservation and provisional attachment
steps.desc: For material that will soon be erased, such as motel or parking-lot CCTV, we apply to the court for evidence preservation (증거보전) even before filing the lawsuit. If there is a risk the other party will dispose of their assets, we also consider placing a provisional attachment (가압류) on their bank deposits or salary.
steps.period: It varies by business, but many places overwrite CCTV within a few weeks to about a month.
steps.tip: If you get the footage directly from the business, you could face a criminal complaint over personal data, so go through the court procedure.

steps.title: Certified letter or filing the complaint
steps.desc: If there is room for a settlement, we first send your position and the amount by certified letter (내용증명); if not, we file the complaint (소장) right away. If you stay married and claim only against the affair partner, the case goes to the district court; if you claim together with a divorce, it goes to the family court.
steps.tip: Do not send the certified letter to the other person's workplace or family. Once a defamation dispute starts, negotiations only get more tangled.

steps.title: Service of the complaint and the answer
steps.desc: The court sends a copy of the complaint to the defendant, and a defendant who intends to contest files an answer (답변서). If the address is wrong or nobody is ever home, we check the address again and correct it; if service still fails, we apply for service by publication (공시송달).
steps.period: The defendant must file an answer within 30 days of receiving the copy of the complaint (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 256). If service is delayed, this stage alone can take several months.
steps.tip: If the defendant does not file an answer, the court can rule for the plaintiff without a hearing (Article 257 of the same Act).

steps.title: Mediation and hearing dates
steps.desc: The court may first send the case to mediation (조정) or go straight to hearings. In mediation, besides compensation, you can include terms such as a ban on further contact, a penalty for breach (위약벌), and a promise not to exercise the right to reimbursement (구상권). If the defendant argues they didn't know, or that the marriage had already broken down, we submit evidence in rebuttal.
steps.period: The first hearing date is usually set a few months after the complaint is filed.
steps.tip: A recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정) or a decision in lieu of mediation (조정을 갈음하는 결정) becomes final as it stands unless an objection is filed within 2 weeks of receiving the original (Civil Procedure Act Article 226; Civil Mediation Act (민사조정법) Article 34).

steps.title: Judgment and appeal
steps.desc: If mediation fails, the court delivers a judgment. If you disagree with the result, you can appeal within 2 weeks of receiving the written judgment; if the other side appeals, the case is argued again on appeal.
steps.period: 2 weeks from service of the written judgment (Civil Procedure Act Article 396)
steps.tip: If the judgment includes a provisional execution (가집행) clause, enforcement can begin before the judgment becomes final, even if the other side appeals.

steps.title: Collecting after the judgment is final
steps.desc: If the other party does not pay, we apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) so they must submit a list of their assets, and we seize their salary or bank deposits. Even if they have no assets right now, a claim confirmed by judgment stays alive for a long time.
steps.period: The limitation period for a claim confirmed by judgment is 10 years (Civil Act Article 165)
steps.tip: Avoid shaming the other person by sending a certified letter to their company. Use procedures set by law, such as salary garnishment.

processes.title: When you receive an affair complaint (defendant)
processes.summary: The deadline for your answer starts running from the day you receive the copy of the complaint. This is the order for deciding what to check and how to contest within that deadline.

steps.title: Confirming the service date and calculating the deadline
steps.desc: Check whether you received the complaint (소장) yourself or a family member living with you received it on your behalf, and write down that date. The envelope and notice show the case number and the court division, so keep them rather than throwing them away.
steps.period: Answer (답변서) within 30 days of receiving the copy of the complaint (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 256)
steps.tip: As a rule, the day a family member received it counts as the day of service, so the deadline is not extended just because you saw it later.

steps.title: Reading the complaint and attached evidence
steps.desc: Go through the amount claimed, the period and places of the relationship the plaintiff alleges, the grounds for saying you knew they were married, and each attached Plaintiff's Exhibit (갑 제○호증). Marking separately what is true, what is wrong and what is exaggerated helps you decide on a direction quickly.
steps.tip: You need to see the level of the plaintiff's evidence first to judge whether to contest liability or only the amount.

steps.title: Preserving records and stopping contact
steps.desc: Do not delete your chats, photos or call records with the other person's spouse. They may also contain material in your favor, such as a message saying they were single. Also stop contacting the plaintiff or the other person's spouse directly to explain yourself.
steps.tip: Contacting the other person's spouse to get your stories straight can come back later as a reason to doubt your entire account.

steps.title: Deciding how to contest
steps.desc: Decide whether to deny the infidelity itself, argue you didn't know they were married, argue the marriage had already broken down at the time, or admit liability and contest the amount. Choose only the arguments your evidence can support.
steps.tip: If you say you didn't know and then evidence shows you did, even your argument for a reduced amount loses force. Look at the evidence first, then decide.

steps.title: Filing the answer
steps.desc: Separate the parts of the plaintiff's claims you admit from the parts you contest, and attach your reasons and evidence for contesting. If you don't have enough time to prepare, first file an answer within the deadline stating that you contest the claim, and add detailed arguments later in a brief (준비서면).
steps.period: Within 30 days of service
steps.tip: If you file an answer contesting the claim before judgment is delivered, the court will not issue a judgment without a hearing (Civil Procedure Act Article 257(1), proviso). Still, filing within the deadline is the safe course.

steps.title: Mediation and recommendation for settlement
steps.desc: At the mediation (조정) session, the parties negotiate the amount and payment method, confidentiality, a bar on further claims, and how the right to reimbursement (구상권) will be handled. If the court sends a recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정) or a decision in lieu of mediation (조정을 갈음하는 결정), you must decide whether to accept it or object.
steps.period: Objection within 2 weeks of receiving the original of the decision (Civil Procedure Act Article 226; Civil Mediation Act (민사조정법) Article 34)
steps.tip: If you want to end the case without a written judgment on record, it is better to settle the terms carefully at the mediation stage.

steps.title: Judgment and appeal
steps.desc: If mediation fails, the case goes through hearings to a judgment. If you think the amount awarded is excessive, you can appeal within 2 weeks of receiving the written judgment.
steps.period: 2 weeks from service of the written judgment (Civil Procedure Act Article 396)
steps.tip: Rather than repeating the same arguments as in the first instance, you need to point out which part of the first-instance ruling was wrong.

steps.title: Considering reimbursement after payment
steps.desc: If you paid all of the compensation yourself, we look at whether you can claim back the other person's share from the spouse who took part in the infidelity with you. If you waived the right to reimbursement in mediation or a settlement, you cannot claim it.
steps.tip: Keep your transfer records and receipts. The amount you actually paid is the starting point for reimbursement.

processes.title: Three Months After a Death: Up to Acceptance of Renunciation or Limited Acceptance
processes.summary: To avoid inheriting debts, you must file with the family court within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began. Here are the steps in order, from searching for assets to filing and the court's decision to accept.

steps.title: Report the death and apply for an asset search
steps.desc: Take the death certificate to the community service center (주민센터, your local district office) to report the death, and apply for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service (안심상속 원스톱서비스, a government service that searches a deceased person's assets and debts in one application) at the same time. You can check financial accounts, land, vehicles, taxes and pension memberships at once, and each agency sends its results by text message.
steps.period: Report the death within 1 month from the day you learned of it (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률) Article 84). Apply for the Safe Inheritance service within 1 year from the last day of the month of death
steps.tip: Automatic transfers may stop, so change how utility bills and insurance premiums are paid in advance.

steps.title: Do not touch the deceased's property
steps.desc: Until the search results come in, do not dispose of the deceased's bank deposits, car or lease deposit. Disposing of estate property can be treated as simple acceptance (단순승인), which may later block renunciation or limited acceptance. For funeral costs and unpaid hospital bills, use the financial institution's exceptional withdrawal so the money goes directly to the hospital or funeral home.
steps.tip: From September 11, 2026, financial transactions in the deceased's name are blocked from the day after the death is reported. Avoid withdrawing money with the deceased's PIN before then.

steps.title: Compare assets and debts
steps.desc: Put the search results, any collection notices sent to the home and any guarantor documents into one table. There may be private loans or surety debts that the search does not show, so also look at the deceased's notebook, text messages and the money that left their bank account each month.
steps.period: Most search results usually arrive within one or two months after the death

steps.title: Decide as a whole family
steps.desc: If the debts are clearly larger, consider renunciation. If it is unclear, or there are many relatives further down the order of heirs, consider limited acceptance. When there is a surviving spouse, a common combination is limited acceptance by the spouse and renunciation by the children. Tell the family that if the spouse also renounces, the grandchildren, siblings and cousins up to the fourth degree become heirs in that order.
steps.tip: If it is hard to decide, you can ask the family court to extend the period before the 3 months run out (Civil Act (민법) Article 1019(1), proviso).

steps.title: Prepare documents
steps.desc: Prepare the deceased's basic certificate (기본증명서), detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) and resident registration abstract of a deregistered person (말소자 주민등록초본), and the filer's family relationship certificate, resident registration certificate (주민등록등본) and certificate of seal impression (인감증명서). For limited acceptance, attach a list of the estate showing both assets and debts, with supporting proof such as balance certificates.
steps.tip: Even a one-character difference between the address you write and the address on the resident registration abstract often leads to an order to correct. Copy the address on the filing exactly as it appears on the abstract.

steps.title: File with the family court
steps.desc: File in person, or through the electronic litigation system (전자소송), with the family court that has jurisdiction over the deceased's last address (where there is no family court, the district court or its branch). Family members can file together on one form or file separately.
steps.period: File within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began (Civil Act Article 1019(1))

steps.title: Corrections and the decision to accept
steps.desc: If documents are missing or details do not match, you will receive an order to correct (보정명령). Once the corrections are done, the court issues a decision accepting the filing and sends you the written decision.
steps.period: Usually 1 to 2 months after filing, sometimes longer when the court is busy
steps.tip: Keep several copies and photos of the written decision. You will use it as it is if collection demands or lawsuits come later.

steps.title: Next-in-line heirs and dealing with creditors
steps.desc: Tell the family members who became heirs next in line because of your renunciation, and have them renounce too if needed. Do not ignore a complaint or payment order that arrives after the acceptance. File an answer or an objection within the deadline, attaching the written decision.
steps.period: An objection to a payment order within 2 weeks from the day it was served (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 470); an answer to a complaint within 30 days (Article 256)

processes.title: Mediation and Adjudication for Division of the Estate
processes.summary: If the heirs cannot agree, you ask the family court for an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할). Because mediation must come first in these cases, most begin with a mediation date.

steps.title: Confirm the heirs and the estate
steps.desc: Identify every heir using the certificate of removed family register (제적등본) and family relationship documents, and list the assets and debts as of the date of death, together with lifetime gifts. If an heir is a minor, first apply for a special representative (특별대리인); if an heir is missing, first apply for an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인).

steps.title: File the petition
steps.desc: One or more heirs file against all the remaining heirs as respondents. The petition lists the interested parties, any heirs who received lifetime gifts or bequests and what they received, and a list of the estate.
steps.period: There is no statutory deadline for requesting division (Civil Act Article 1013). Jurisdiction lies with the family court for the respondent's address (or one of them, if there are several) (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 46)
steps.tip: If you want to claim a contribution share, file a petition to determine the contribution share together with the request for division.

steps.title: Responses and checking the estate
steps.desc: The respondents submit written opinions, and if needed, orders to submit financial transaction information and fact-finding inquiries are used to check lifetime withdrawals and gifts. The value of real estate is set by appraisal.
steps.tip: The party who requests an appraisal usually pays its cost up front, so budget for it in advance.

steps.title: Deadline for contribution share claims
steps.desc: Once division has been requested, the court may set and announce a period for claiming a contribution share. A contribution share claim filed after that period may be dismissed.
steps.period: Set at 1 month or more (Family Litigation Rules (가사소송규칙) Article 113)

steps.title: Mediation sessions
steps.desc: You narrow down the method and amounts of division with the mediation committee. If you reach agreement, a mediation record is drawn up, which has the same effect as an in-court settlement (Family Litigation Act Article 59(2)).
steps.period: A case that must go through mediation first (Family Litigation Act Article 50)

steps.title: Hearing and adjudication
steps.desc: If mediation fails, the court holds a hearing, calculates each heir's specific share and issues an adjudication. For property that is hard to divide, such as a home, the court may give it to one person and order the difference to be settled in cash, or order an auction.
steps.period: Usually around one year, including mediation

steps.title: Immediate appeal
steps.desc: If you disagree with the adjudication, file an immediate appeal (즉시항고). An appeal by one heir takes effect for all the heirs.
steps.period: Within 14 days from the day you were notified of the adjudication (Family Litigation Act Article 43(5), Family Litigation Rules Article 116)

steps.title: Registration and settlement after it becomes final
steps.desc: Once the adjudication becomes final, obtain a certificate of finality, register the inheritance and receive the settlement money. If it is not paid, you can enforce the adjudication through compulsory execution.

areaPages.title: Divorce by Agreement
areaPages.lead: If the spouses agree to divorce, the court does not ask for the reasons. But the court only confirms the intent to divorce and matters concerning the children, so property division and compensation for emotional distress must be settled separately in a written agreement.

seo.title: Divorce by Agreement in Korea: Procedure, Cooling-Off Period and Settlement Agreement | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: A step-by-step guide to divorce by agreement in Korea, from applying for confirmation of intent to divorce to the cooling-off period, the confirmation hearing and reporting the divorce within 3 months. Also covers how to record property division and compensation, which the court does not confirm, in a settlement agreement, the child support protocol, and how to withdraw.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: We both agree to divorce, but we haven't decided how to divide our assets
My spouse says we should divorce first and sort out the assets later
I don't know how to write the person with parental authority and child support in the agreement
Verbal abuse and violence make it hard to wait out the cooling-off period
We wrote an agreement, but I'm not sure it's safe to sign as is
We received the court's confirmation of intent to divorce, but I've changed my mind

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 834 and 836 (Divorce by agreement and reporting)
items.text: Spouses may divorce by agreement. A divorce by agreement takes effect only when it is confirmed by the family court and reported under the Act on the Registration of Family Relationships.

items.name: Civil Act Article 836-2 (Divorce procedure)
items.text: Confirmation of intent to divorce can be given only after 3 months have passed from the day of the divorce guidance if there is a child to be raised (including a child in pregnancy), or 1 month if not. This period may be shortened or waived in urgent circumstances such as violence, and the court records the agreed child support in a child support protocol.

items.name: Act on the Registration of Family Relationships (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률) Article 75
items.text: The divorce must be reported within 3 months of the day the certified copy of the confirmation is issued or served, and once this period passes, the family court's confirmation loses its effect.

items.name: Civil Act Article 839-2 (Right to claim property division)
items.text: A person divorced by agreement may also claim property division from the other spouse. This right expires 2 years after the date of divorce.

table.title: What the court does and does not confirm in a divorce by agreement
rows: Intent to divorce
Confirmed

Confirmed (if there are minor children)
Submit an agreement on custody and the designation of the person with parental authority. If it goes against the child's welfare, the court orders a correction
Child support
Confirmed
The court draws up a child support protocol, which can be used for compulsory execution

Write the frequency and method of visits in the agreement

table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 836-2 and 837 and Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 75 (checked on the Korea Law Information Center, the government's official legislation database, October 2026).

sections.title: Agreeing is not the end of the divorce
body: A divorce by agreement (협의이혼) begins when the spouses together submit an application for confirmation of intent to divorce (협의이혼의사확인 신청서) to the family court with jurisdiction over their place of family registration (등록기준지) or address. After applying, you receive the court's divorce guidance, and once the cooling-off period (숙려기간) has passed, both of you appear together at the scheduled confirmation hearing (확인기일) to have your intent to divorce confirmed.

Receiving the confirmation does not immediately end the marriage. The divorce takes effect only when it is reported (이혼신고) to the city, district, town or township office within 3 months of receiving the certified copy of the confirmation, and until then you are legally married. If either spouse fails to appear twice at the confirmation hearing, the application is treated as withdrawn, so coordinate your schedules in advance.

sections.title: The cooling-off period can be shortened or waived
body: The cooling-off period is counted from the day you receive the divorce guidance. It is 3 months if there is a child to be raised, or 1 month if not, and a child in pregnancy counts as a child to be raised. It is different if your child will soon become an adult. If the guidance day is within 1 month before the child becomes an adult, 1 month applies, and if it is between 1 and 3 months before, the confirmation hearing is set for a date after the child becomes an adult.

If there are urgent circumstances, such as expected unbearable suffering from a spouse's violence, you can apply to have the period shortened or waived. Simply wanting a quick divorce is not accepted, so submit material showing the urgency, such as records of 112 (police) reports, medical certificates and counseling records.

sections.title: Record property division and compensation in a separate agreement
body: The court does not confirm property division (재산분할) or compensation for emotional distress (위자료). If you go along with the idea of reporting the divorce first and sorting out the assets later, and your spouse then disposes of assets or cuts off contact, you will have to fight it out again in a lawsuit. Even in a divorce by agreement, it is safer to settle property matters in writing before the report.

The shorter the agreement, the more likely disputes will arise later over how to interpret it. If you combine compensation and property division into a single amount, the other spouse may later file a separate property division claim. We recommend writing down every item below.
bullets: Separate amounts for compensation and property division (and if there is none, say so)
Payment amounts and deadlines, and late payment damages if payment is delayed
For real estate, identify it down to the lot number, and state when ownership will be transferred on the ground of property division
Who will repay debts such as the mortgage loan
Whether each spouse keeps their own severance pay and pension, and that no separate claim will be made to divide them
A clause stating that neither spouse will make any further claims beyond what is agreed

sections.title: If you have minor children, write a detailed agreement
body: If there is a child to be raised, you can receive the confirmation only after submitting an agreement that sets the person with parental authority (친권자), the custodial parent (양육자), child support (양육비) and visitation (면접교섭). The child support protocol (양육비부담조서) the court draws up can be enforced like a judgment, so state not only the amount but the monthly payment date, the account to receive it, and until when it will be paid. This makes it easier to calculate any overdue amounts later.

For visitation as well, rather than only writing a number of times per month, setting the days and times, where the child will be dropped off, and how school vacations and holidays will be shared reduces disputes after the divorce.

sections.title: If you change your mind after the confirmation
body: Even after the confirmation of intent to divorce, the divorce does not take effect unless it is reported, and after 3 months the confirmation loses its effect. If you are worried the other spouse will report it first, you can submit a withdrawal of intent to divorce (이혼의사철회서) to the city, district, town or township office.
However, if the other spouse's divorce report is received before your withdrawal, the divorce takes effect, so once you decide to withdraw, act right away.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center helps with a divorce by agreement

items.title: Separating what is agreed from what is left
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and lists the terms already agreed and the terms still in dispute. At this stage we also judge whether the matter can end by agreement or whether mediation would be better.

items.title: Listing the assets
items.desc: We list real estate, deposits, insurance, expected severance pay and loans by whose name they are in, so you can see at a glance what will be divided.

items.title: Drafting the agreement
items.desc: We write compensation and property division separately and set payment deadlines and the timing of registration. If money is to be received in the future, we also consider whether to record it in a notarized deed.

items.title: Reviewing the agreement on the children
items.desc: We check whether the child support payment date and account and the visitation schedule fit your actual life, and refine the agreement to be submitted to the court.

items.title: Checking performance after the report
items.desc: After the divorce is reported, we check that the registration transfer and the first child support payment were made as promised. If any property issues remain unsettled, we also keep track of the 2-year claim period with you.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Each spouse's family relationship certificate, marriage relationship certificate and resident registration certificate
Certified copies of real estate registers and loan balance records
Deposit, share and insurance details (as far as you know)
Documents showing the expected amount of severance pay or retirement pension
Messages exchanged with your spouse about the divorce terms
Monthly child-rearing costs such as tutoring and medical expenses

faqs.q: Can a lawyer apply for divorce by agreement on my behalf?
faqs.a: Confirmation of intent to divorce is a procedure in which the court directly confirms the spouses' own intentions, so you must apply and attend the confirmation hearing in person. Jisan Law handles drafting and reviewing the settlement agreement and the agreement on the children, and negotiating the terms with the other spouse. There are separate procedures if one spouse is abroad or in a correctional facility.

faqs.q: Do we need two witnesses on the divorce report?
faqs.a: The Civil Act requires the signatures of two adult witnesses on a report of divorce by agreement, but if a certified copy of the family court's confirmation of intent to divorce is attached, the witnesses' signatures are deemed to be included (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 76). If your divorce by agreement went through court confirmation, you do not need to find witnesses.

faqs.q: Do we need to have the agreement notarized?
faqs.a: An agreement signed by both spouses is valid as a contract even without notarization. However, if money is to be received in the future, it must be made into a notarized deed (공정증서) consenting to compulsory execution for it to be enforced directly without a judgment. A promise that is not about money, such as transferring ownership of real estate, is hard to enforce with a notarized deed alone, so also set the date on which the registration documents will be handed over.

faqs.q: My spouse started seeing someone else during the cooling-off period. Can I receive compensation?
faqs.a: The mere fact that you applied for divorce by agreement does not mean the marriage has completely ended. Liability for compensation may be recognized depending on whether you were still living together at the time and whether there was room to repair the relationship. Keep records of when the relationship started and what your life together looked like at that time.

faqs.q: What happens if the terms fall apart during the divorce-by-agreement process?
faqs.a: Until the confirmation is given, you can withdraw the application and move to mediation or a lawsuit. A property division agreement written on the premise of a divorce by agreement may have its validity questioned if the divorce by agreement does not happen, so in a lawsuit, property division may have to be argued again from the beginning.

areaPages.areaName: Judicial Divorce and Emotional Distress Compensation
areaPages.title: Judicial Divorce and Emotional Distress Compensation
areaPages.lead: If your spouse will not agree to a divorce or you cannot agree on the terms, the court decides. The grounds for divorce and the claim for compensation require proof of different things, so prepare the evidence separately for each claim from the start.

seo.title: Divorce Lawsuits, Divorce by Mediation and Compensation Claims in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Key issues in a Korean divorce lawsuit: how to prove each ground for divorce under Civil Act Article 840, mandatory mediation and decisions in lieu of mediation, how compensation for emotional distress is assessed and the deadlines to claim it, how to gather evidence lawfully, and pre-trial measures for temporary custody and child support during the lawsuit.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My spouse insists they will never agree to a divorce
I found out about an affair, but I don't know what evidence I need
Verbal abuse and violence continued, so I left home with my child
We've been separated for years, and now I want to settle things legally
I can no longer bear the insults and interference from my in-laws
I received a notice of a divorce mediation session from the court

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 840 (Grounds for judicial divorce)
items.text: A divorce may be claimed if the spouse committed an unchaste act, maliciously deserted the other, the spouse or the spouse's lineal ascendants treated one extremely unfairly, the spouse treated one's own lineal ascendant extremely unfairly, the spouse has been missing for 3 years or more, or there is any other serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 841 and 842 (Extinction of the right to claim divorce)
items.text: A divorce cannot be claimed on the ground of infidelity if there was prior consent or later forgiveness, or once 6 months have passed since learning of it or 2 years since it occurred; on the ground in Item 6, it cannot be claimed once 6 months have passed since learning of it or 2 years since it occurred.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 843 and 806 (Damages)
items.text: Damages arising from a judicial divorce follow the rules on damages for breaking off an engagement, so a claim can be made against the spouse at fault for property damage as well as for emotional distress.

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 50 (Mandatory mediation)
items.text: For a judicial divorce, mediation must be requested first, and if a lawsuit is filed without mediation, the family court refers it to mediation. Exceptions apply when the other party can only be summoned by public notice or when mediation is deemed impossible.

table.title: The divorce claim and the compensation claim are assessed separately
rows: Legal basis
Civil Act Article 840
Civil Act Articles 843 and 806
What must be proved
A legal ground for divorce and the breakdown of the marriage
The other party's wrongful conduct and the emotional distress it caused
Against whom
Your spouse
Your spouse, and third parties responsible for the breakdown (an affair partner, in-laws, etc.)
Deadline
For Items 1 and 6, 6 months from learning of the ground and 2 years from when it occurred (except where the ground continues)
3 years from learning of the damage and the person responsible (Civil Act Article 766)
When both are similarly at fault
A divorce may be granted if the marriage has broken down
The compensation claim may not be accepted
table.note: Based on current provisions on the Korea Law Information Center, the government's official legislation database (checked October 2026). There is no legal standard for the amount of compensation; the court decides it case by case.

sections.title: A divorce lawsuit starts with mediation
body: Divorce is a case that must go through mediation (조정) before a lawsuit. At the mediation session, the mediators and the judge hear both sides and work out, all at once, whether to divorce along with property division (재산분할), compensation for emotional distress (위자료), parental authority and custody, and child support. If mediation succeeds, it has the same effect as a judicial settlement and the divorce becomes final.

If no agreement is reached, the court may on its own issue a decision in lieu of mediation (조정을 갈음하는 결정). If you disagree with this decision, you must file an objection within 2 weeks of being served with the original copy, and if there is no objection, it becomes final as is. If mediation ultimately fails, the matter is decided by judgment after hearings.

sections.title: Each ground for divorce is proved differently
body: A judicial divorce (재판상 이혼) is possible even without the other spouse's consent if a ground set by law is recognized. However, the plaintiff must prove that ground, so the material to collect depends on which ground you claim. Infidelity can qualify even without sexual intercourse if the act breaks the spouses' duty of fidelity.
bullets: Infidelity: messages and photos, lodging and card payment records, conversations in which the other person admitted the facts
Malicious desertion: account records showing living expenses were cut off, and when and how the spouse left home
Extremely unfair treatment: medical certificates and medical records, records of 112 (police) reports, recordings of verbal abuse
Other serious reasons making it difficult to continue the marriage: the length and circumstances of the separation, records showing communication stopped, records of couples counseling

sections.title: Evidence must be gathered lawfully
body: Recording a conversation you take part in is not a problem, but secretly recording a conversation between other people that you are not part of can violate the Protection of Communications Secrets Act. Unlocking your spouse's phone to read messages, secretly logging into their accounts, or putting a GPS tracker on their car can also turn into criminal matters.

Material obtained this way can instead give the other side grounds to strike back. For financial transaction records or call records that are hard to obtain on your own, we first consider getting them after the lawsuit begins through the court's fact inquiries and document production orders.

sections.title: Compensation is set by the degree of responsibility
body: Compensation for emotional distress is money claimed from the person responsible for the breakdown of the marriage to make up for the emotional suffering caused. The court sets the amount by considering how the breakdown came about, the degree of responsibility, the length of the marriage, both spouses' ages and occupations, and their financial situation. There is no table of standard amounts set by law.

Compensation is a different kind of claim from property division, so both can be claimed together. Claims can also be brought against third parties, such as your spouse's affair partner or in-laws directly responsible for the breakdown, and these are sometimes handled together with the divorce case.

sections.title: You can also ask the court to set arrangements during the lawsuit
body: A divorce lawsuit can take more than a year, but questions like who will care for the child and how to cover living expenses cannot wait. When you file the lawsuit or request mediation, you can also apply for pre-trial measures (사전처분) such as designating a temporary custodial parent, payment of child support, visitation, and a ban on disposing of assets.

If there is a risk that the other spouse will dispose of assets, we first consider provisional attachment (가압류) or a provisional injunction (가처분) before or when filing. In cases involving children, a family investigator (가사조사관) often interviews both sides and visits the home to look at the child-rearing environment, so we prepare for that as well.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles a divorce lawsuit

items.title: Building a timeline of the marriage
items.desc: The managing partner hears your story personally and arranges, in date order, when conflicts arose and what happened after the marriage. From this timeline, we pick out the grounds for divorce and the grounds for compensation.

items.title: Sorting the evidence
items.desc: We sort the material you have by whether it will be used for the grounds for divorce, compensation, property division or custody, and check whether anything missing can be obtained through the court.

items.title: Preservation measures and pre-trial measures
items.desc: If you are worried about assets being disposed of, we apply first for provisional attachment or a provisional injunction, and if matters concerning the child or living expenses are urgent, we apply first for a pre-trial measure.

items.title: Mediation and hearings
items.desc: Before the mediation session, we decide which terms you can accept and which you cannot give up. If mediation fails, we proceed with the hearings using briefs and evidence.

items.title: Wrapping up after the decision is final
items.desc: Once the judgment or mediation becomes final, we check that the divorce is reported within 1 month and that compensation payments and registration transfers actually take place, and apply for compulsory execution if needed.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: A note listing the major events since the marriage in date order
Original messages exchanged with your spouse (the entire chat)
Material on verbal abuse or violence, such as medical certificates, records of 112 reports and counseling records
Material showing when and why the separation began
Any notice of a mediation session or complaint you received from the court
Details of the couple's assets and loans (as far as you know)

faqs.q: Will it hurt my case if I leave home with my child before the lawsuit?
faqs.a: A separation with a reason, such as escaping violence or living apart by agreement, is not a disadvantage in itself. However, if you leave home without any explanation and also cut off living expenses, the other spouse may claim it was malicious desertion. Keep a record, such as messages, of the date you left and the reason.

faqs.q: My spouse has cut off contact and I don't know where they live. Can I still sue?
faqs.a: If the address is unknown, the court can proceed by service by public notice (공시송달), and in that case the trial may go ahead directly without mediation. Being out of contact is a different ground from it being unknown for 3 years or more whether the spouse is alive, so we organize how contact was lost and the circumstances before and after, and decide which ground to claim.

faqs.q: Can I also claim compensation from my spouse's affair partner?
faqs.a: You can also claim compensation from a person who engaged in infidelity knowing your spouse was married. It can be handled together with the divorce case or brought as a separate lawsuit. The claim cannot be made once 3 years have passed since you learned of the damage and the person responsible, so check the deadline first.

faqs.q: Do I have to attend the mediation session in person?
faqs.a: In family litigation, the parties are in principle required to attend in person. If there are special circumstances, only your lawyer may attend with the permission of the presiding judge or the head of the mediation committee (Family Litigation Act Article 7). However, in mediation the parties often need to decide the terms themselves, so whether to attend is decided to suit the case.

faqs.q: Can I claim compensation and property division at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes. Compensation is damages for responsibility for the breakdown, while property division settles the assets built together, so the legal basis and the standards for judging them are different. That is why even a spouse responsible for the breakdown can claim property division, and conversely, even for the spouse not at fault, the division ratio is set by contribution.

areaPages.areaName: Property Division (Real Estate, Severance Pay, Pensions)
areaPages.title: Property Division
areaPages.lead: Property division looks less at whose name an asset is in and more at how it was accumulated during the marriage and who kept it. Before the other spouse disposes of anything, make a list first and decide which assets to freeze.

seo.title: Property Division in a Korean Divorce: What Is Divided, Contribution and Provisional Attachment | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Which of real estate, deposits, severance pay, pensions, businesses and debts are divided in a Korean divorce; separate property and the reference date; proving contribution; asset disclosure orders, asset inquiries, provisional attachment and revocation of fraudulent transfers; and how assets are divided and the tax issues involved.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: Our home and deposits are all in my spouse's name
My parents helped pay for part of our home when we married
My spouse runs a business, so I can't tell how much the assets are worth
After divorce came up, my spouse put our home up for sale
We have more loans than assets, and I want to know how they are divided
I can't tell whether the division amount my spouse offered is fair

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2 (Right to claim property division)
items.text: If no agreement is reached, the family court decides the amount and method of division, taking into account the amount of assets built through both parties' cooperation and other circumstances. The right to claim expires 2 years after the date of divorce. This also applies to judicial divorce (Article 843).

items.name: Civil Act Article 830 (Separate property and property of unclear ownership)
items.text: Property owned before the marriage and property acquired in one's own name during the marriage is that person's separate property, and property whose ownership is unclear is presumed to be jointly owned by the spouses.

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Articles 48-2, 48-3 and 67-3
items.text: In a property division case, the family court can order the other party to submit a list of assets, and if that is not enough, it can make inquiries about assets with financial institutions and others. Failing to submit the list without a valid reason, or submitting a false list, is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million.

items.name: Civil Act Article 839-3 (Right to revoke fraudulent acts)
items.text: If a spouse disposes of assets knowing it will harm the right to claim property division, the other spouse can ask the family court to revoke the disposal and restore the assets. The lawsuit must be filed within 1 year of learning the grounds for revocation and within 5 years of the disposal (Article 406(2)).
