table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 830 and 839-2, National Pension Act Article 64 and Supreme Court case law. Whether individual assets are included, and the ratio, differ from case to case.

sections.title: First, settle the reference date for division
body: In a judicial divorce, the assets to be divided and their values are in principle set as of the end of the final hearing on the facts, and if you claim after a divorce by agreement, the date the divorce took effect is the reference point. So if apartment prices rise or fall during the lawsuit, the division amount changes too.

If you have been separated for a long time, a dispute may arise over whether assets one spouse built up alone after the separation should be included in property division (재산분할). You need to organize the date the separation began and who paid the living costs after that to make your argument about the reference date.

sections.title: Contribution doesn't belong only to the spouse who earned the money
body: There is no fixed formula for the division ratio. The court looks not only at income-earning activity but also at housework and childcare, efforts to manage the assets and repay loans, the length of the marriage, and both spouses' ages and occupations. In the end, the ratio is set when you show with material what you did to build and keep the assets.

If both of you worked, it is effective to show through account flows how each income was used for living costs and loan repayments. Even pre-marital assets or assets received from parents can be argued to be included in the division if you jointly repaid loans or managed them so their value was maintained.

sections.title: Hidden or diverted assets are found through court procedures
body: Even if you do not know what assets are in your spouse's name, once a lawsuit begins you can apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) to have your spouse submit a list of assets, and if that is not enough, the court can make an asset inquiry (재산조회) with financial institutions and public agencies. Transaction records for specific accounts are checked through fact inquiries (사실조회) and an order to submit financial transaction information.

If you are already worried about assets being disposed of, apply for an injunction against disposal of real estate (처분금지가처분) or provisional attachment (가압류) of deposits and wages before or when filing. Once a disposal is complete, you have to file a lawsuit to revoke a fraudulent act (사해행위취소), and it is hard to undo if the buyer says they did not know the circumstances, so freezing the assets comes first.
bullets: Asset disclosure order: the other spouse submits a list of their own assets
Asset inquiry: the court searches financial institutions and public agencies for assets in the other spouse's name
Provisional attachment: blocks the disposal of monetary claims such as deposits, wages and rental deposits, and of real estate
Injunction against disposal: freezes a specific property so it cannot be transferred
Revocation of a fraudulent act: cancels the disposal of assets already diverted and brings them back

sections.title: You also need to decide how to divide
body: The method used most in practice is for one spouse to keep a specific asset, such as the home, and pay the other spouse a settlement amount. Assets can also be divided in kind as they are, or sold and the proceeds shared. The spouse who keeps a home with a loan on it must also settle who will repay the loan.

When real estate is transferred, the tax may differ depending on whether the ground for registration is property division or compensation for emotional distress (위자료). The tax office looks not only at the label but at the actual substance and at whether the transfer was made before or after the divorce report. Before finalizing the wording of the agreement and the timing of registration, we check together whether a tax review is needed.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center prepares for property division

items.title: Mapping the assets
items.desc: We gather the real estate, deposits, insurance, shares, severance pay, pensions and loans in both spouses' names in one table. Unknown assets are left blank and filled in through court procedures.

items.title: Tracing the flow of money
items.desc: We organize through account flows when and with what money each asset was bought, building the basis for arguments about separate property and contribution.

items.title: Preservation measures
items.desc: We pick out the assets at risk of disposal and apply first for provisional attachment or an injunction.

items.title: Applying for asset disclosure and inquiries
items.desc: Assets the other spouse has not disclosed are checked through an asset disclosure order, asset inquiries and fact inquiries.

items.title: Presenting a division plan and mediation
items.desc: We prepare a division plan reflecting market prices and loans as of the reference date, present it in mediation, and decide in advance the range you can accept.

items.title: Checking registration and payment
items.desc: After the decision is final, we check that the ownership transfer registration and settlement payment have been made, and proceed with compulsory execution if payment is not made.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Certified copies of real estate registers, sale contracts and pre-sale contracts
Lease contracts (jeonse or monthly rent deposits)
Loan agreements and repayment records
Transaction records for accounts in your name and pay statements
What you know about your spouse, such as their workplace, banks and vehicles
Records of money transferred from either family at the time of the marriage

faqs.q: My parents helped pay for our home when we married. Will that money be divided too?
faqs.a: It depends on to whom your parents gave the money, how long the marriage has lasted, and whether the two of you managed the home and repaid the loan together afterward. Support from one side's parents can be argued as that spouse's contribution, but if the marriage was long and the asset was maintained together, it is often included in the division. Find the transfer records and conversations from that time.

faqs.q: Is there property division even if our debts exceed our assets?
faqs.a: If the debts arose for the couple's life together, they are also considered in the division. Case law holds that even when debts exceed assets, the court may, depending on the circumstances, divide the burden of the debts. However, debts one spouse incurred for gambling or personal purposes are in principle borne by that spouse.

faqs.q: My spouse has already sold our home. Is there nothing I can do?
faqs.a: We start by tracing where the sale proceeds went. If the money is still there, we argue that it should be divided and provisionally attach the deposits. If the home was transferred to a family member or acquaintance to avoid property division, we consider a lawsuit to revoke a fraudulent act, which must be filed within 1 year of learning the grounds for revocation.

faqs.q: Can a spouse who had an affair also claim property division?
faqs.a: Yes. Property division is a procedure for settling assets built together, so it is judged separately from responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage. Responsibility for the breakdown is dealt with through compensation for emotional distress, so a claim for compensation against the spouse who had the affair is made separately from property division.

areaPages.title: Parental Authority, Custody and Visitation
areaPages.lead: The court decides the person with parental authority and the custodial parent based not on which parent was more at fault but on which environment is better for the child. The starting point is to show with material who has cared for the child until now and what the parenting plan will be.

seo.title: Parental Authority and Custody in a Korean Divorce, and Visitation | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The difference between parental authority and custody in Korea, what the court looks at when choosing the custodial parent, preparing for the family investigation, pre-trial measures for temporary custody during separation, how to set visitation and performance orders when it is not followed, and changing the person with parental authority or custodial parent after divorce.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I want to raise my child, but I earn less than my spouse
My spouse left home with our child and is hard to reach
I've been told it's hard to get custody because I'm the father
I have a family investigation coming up and don't know how to prepare
After the divorce, my ex won't let me see our child
My ex, the custodial parent, doesn't seem to be taking proper care of our child

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 909(4) to (6) (Person with parental authority)
items.text: When parents divorce, they decide the person with parental authority by agreement, and if they cannot agree, the family court decides. In a judicial divorce, the court decides on its own authority, and if needed for the child's welfare, the person with parental authority can be changed at the request of a relative within the fourth degree.

items.name: Civil Act Article 837 (Divorce and responsibility for raising children)
items.text: The custodial parent, the sharing of child-rearing costs, and whether and how visitation takes place are decided by agreement. If the agreement goes against the child's welfare or cannot be reached, the family court decides, taking into account the child's wishes and age and the parents' financial situations. These can be changed later if needed.

items.name: Civil Act Article 837-2 (Right of visitation)
items.text: A parent who does not directly raise the child and the child have the right to visit each other. If that parent cannot exercise visitation because of death or other reasons, the grandparents may also request it, and the court may restrict, exclude or change visitation for the child's welfare.

items.name: Rules on Family Litigation (가사소송규칙) Article 100 (Hearing the child's opinion)
items.text: In proceedings such as designating the person with parental authority or the custodial parent, if the child is 13 or older, the family court must in principle hear the child's opinion.

table.title: How parental authority and custody differ
rows: What it covers
Acting as the child's legal representative, managing the child's property, decisions about the child's legal status
Living with the child, protecting and educating the child
At divorce
Decided by agreement, but in a judicial divorce the court decides on its own authority
Decided by agreement, or by the court if no agreement is reached
Can they be split?
A person other than the custodial parent can be designated
If they are split, parental authority covers only matters other than child-rearing
Can they be joint?
Joint parental authority is possible
Joint custody is possible, but assumes the parents can cooperate
Change
Changed by the court at the request of a relative within the fourth degree
Changed by the court at the request of the father, mother, child or a prosecutor, or on its own authority
table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 837 and 909. In practice, the same parent is often designated as both the person with parental authority and the custodial parent.

sections.title: What the court looks at when choosing the custodial parent
body: The greatest weight is given to who has actually cared for the child until now and where and how the child is living now. Courts tend to prefer the side where the child's life will not be greatly disrupted, so it is important to show with records of daily life that you have been the primary caregiver.

Financial ability is a factor but not a decisive one, because if the parent with lower income becomes the custodial parent (양육자), this can be made up for with child support (양육비) from the other parent. Gender is not a standard either, and it is not unusual for fathers to be designated as the custodial parent.
bullets: Who has mainly cared for the child (school drop-offs and pick-ups, doctor visits, meals, school meetings)
The child's age and sex, and whether siblings can be raised together
The desire to raise the child, and housing and work arrangements after the divorce
Whether there are people, such as grandparents, who can help with child care
The child's wishes (the court must hear the child's opinion if 13 or older)
Whether there are problems of violence, neglect or drinking
An attitude that respects the child's relationship with the other parent

sections.title: The family investigation checks the child-rearing environment directly
body: If custody is disputed, a family investigator interviews each parent, meets the child, and if necessary visits the home during the family investigation (가사조사). The report the investigator writes is an important piece of material when the judge decides the custodial parent.

In the interview, rather than listing the other parent's faults at length, you should be able to answer about concrete daily life, such as the child's daily routine, the school and academies the child attends, and who takes the child to the doctor when sick. Preparing a parenting plan in advance, stating where you will live after the divorce and who will look after the child after work, makes the interview easier to prepare for.

sections.title: What happens with the child at the start of separation matters
body: Once a separation begins, the child-rearing situation from then on affects later decisions. If one parent leaves with the child and raises the child for a long time, that situation can become fixed, so if you have been separated from your child, respond without delay.

When you file for divorce mediation or a lawsuit, you can also apply for pre-trial measures (사전처분) to designate a temporary custodial parent and set temporary child support and temporary visitation. If the other parent takes the child and does not return the child, we consider a ruling ordering the child to be handed over (유아인도) together with a pre-trial measure. On the other hand, taking a child out of the home unilaterally can look bad to the court, so be careful.

sections.title: The more specific the visitation arrangement, the fewer the disputes
body: Visitation (면접교섭) is both a parent's right and the child's right. If you only set a frequency, such as every other weekend, you will clash every time over the time and place. It is better to set the start and end times, the handover location, whether the child stays overnight, school vacations and holidays, and even video calls.

If the custodial parent blocks visitation without a valid reason, you can apply to the family court for a performance order (이행명령), and if the performance order is also ignored, an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million may be imposed. Conversely, if there are circumstances that could harm the child, you can ask the court to restrict visitation or to have it take place at a third location such as a visitation center.

sections.title: Arrangements can be changed even after divorce
body: Even the person with parental authority (친권자) or custodial parent set at the divorce can be changed by applying to the family court if it is needed for the child's welfare. Typical cases are when the custodial parent neglects the child, the child strongly wants to live with the other parent, or the custodial parent's circumstances have changed greatly.

A change often does not happen just because the parents agree; it usually has to go through a ruling by the court. You need to explain with material such as school records and health records how the child is doing now and what would improve with a change.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center prepares a custody case

items.title: Organizing the history of care
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and organizes, period by period, who has cared for the child and how since the child's birth.

items.title: Gathering everyday records
items.desc: We collect material showing actual care, such as records of communication with the daycare or school, medical records, photos with the child and daily schedules.

items.title: Considering pre-trial measures
items.desc: If you have been separated from your child during the separation or child support has been cut off, we first apply for designation of a temporary custodial parent and temporary child support.

items.title: Parenting plan and preparing for the family investigation
items.desc: We prepare a parenting plan covering housing, working hours and care arrangements after the divorce, and go over in advance the questions the investigator is likely to ask in the interview.

items.title: Drafting a visitation plan
items.desc: We draft a visitation plan suited to the child's age and school schedule so that it is reflected as is in the mediation or judgment.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: A note on the child's daily routine and who has handled school drop-offs, pick-ups and doctor visits
Notices and counseling records from the daycare or school
Photos and videos with the child
Material showing where you will live and how you will work after the divorce
Records showing the other parent's violence or neglect (if any)
Messages exchanged about visitation

faqs.q: Is it hard to get custody because I'm the father?
faqs.a: The court decides the custodial parent based on the child's welfare, not gender. If the father has actually been the main caregiver and shows that he can raise the child stably after the divorce, he can be designated as the custodial parent. Plans for working hours and for people who can help with care are especially important.

faqs.q: My child is still young. Will the court ask for my child's opinion?
faqs.a: If the child is 13 or older, the court must in principle hear the child's opinion. Even if the child is younger, the investigator may explore the child's feelings during the family investigation in a way suited to the child's age. Signs that a parent pressured the child to choose a side may actually be judged unfavorably.

faqs.q: Can we set up joint custody?
faqs.a: Joint parental authority and joint custody are legally possible. However, the parents need to live close to each other and be able to consult often about the child's schedule, so in cases with intense conflict, the court is unlikely to accept it. If you want joint custody, you need to present specific arrangements for where each parent will live and how the schedule will be shared.

faqs.q: Every visitation day, my child says they don't want to go. Can I just not send them?
faqs.a: First, find out why your child does not want to go. If the custodial parent stops the set visitation on their own, they may face a performance order and an administrative fine. If there are circumstances that could harm the child, the proper step is to ask the court to change or restrict how visitation takes place.

faqs.q: If my ex keeps obstructing visitation, can the custodial parent be changed?
faqs.a: Obstructing visitation alone does not change the custodial parent, but if repeated obstruction is harming the child's relationship with the other parent, it becomes a factor considered in proceedings to change the custodial parent. The first step is to keep records of applications for performance orders and how visitation was obstructed.

areaPages.title: Child Support Claims and Enforcement
areaPages.lead: Child support is a duty both parents share and a right of the child. Setting the amount and actually collecting it are separate procedures, so from the moment you set it, think about how you will collect it.

seo.title: Child Support in Korea: Claims, Past Child Support and Non-Payment | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How child support is set in Korea using the Child Support Guidelines, past child support and the limitation period, requests to increase or decrease it, direct payment orders, security orders, performance orders and detention when support is not paid, driver's license suspension, travel bans, public disclosure of names, and advance payment of child support.
keywords: child support direct payment order Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: We didn't set child support at the divorce, and I've been raising our child alone
Child support hasn't come in for months
My ex said they lost their job and cut child support on their own
Education costs went up sharply when my child started middle school
My ex is self-employed, so I can't have it deducted from wages
I'm the one paying, and my income has dropped so child support is a burden

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 63-2 (Direct payment order for child support)
items.text: If a person obligated to pay child support regularly fails to pay twice or more without a valid reason, the court can order the company paying that person's wages to deduct child support from the wages and pay it directly to the person entitled to it.

items.name: Family Litigation Act Article 63-3 (Security order, etc.)
items.text: To secure payment of child support, the family court can order the payer to provide security, and if the security is not provided within the deadline, it can order all or part of the child support to be paid as a lump sum.

items.name: Family Litigation Act Articles 64, 67 and 68 (Performance orders and sanctions)
items.text: If child support set by a judgment, mediation record or child support protocol is not paid, you can apply for a performance order. If it is violated, an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million can be imposed, and if three or more periodic payments are missed, detention for up to 30 days can be ordered.

items.name: Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments (양육비 이행확보 및 지원에 관한 법률) Article 27(2)
items.text: A person who, after receiving a detention order, fails to pay child support within 1 year without a valid reason is punished by imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Prosecution cannot be brought if the victim explicitly does not want it.

table.title: Procedures available when child support is not paid
rows: Direct payment order
Two or more missed periodic child support payments, and the payer is a wage earner
The employer deducts child support from wages and sends it directly
Security order and lump-sum payment order
Failure to pay without a valid reason
Order to provide security, and if not provided, an order to pay a lump sum
Performance order
Failure to perform a duty set by a judgment, mediation record, child support protocol, etc.
Administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million for violation
Detention
Three or more missed payments despite a performance order
Detention for up to 30 days until payment
Compulsory execution
An enforceable title such as a judgment or record
Seizure and collection of deposits, wages and real estate
Administrative sanctions
Non-payment despite a performance order or lump-sum payment order
After review by a committee, requests for driver's license suspension and a travel ban, and public disclosure of the name
Criminal punishment
Non-payment within 1 year after a detention order
Imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
table.note: Based on the Family Litigation Act and the Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments (checked on the Korea Law Information Center, the government's official legislation database, October 2026). Detailed requirements for administrative sanctions are set by Presidential Decree.

sections.title: The amount starts from the guidelines, then circumstances are added or subtracted
body: The court uses the Child Support Guidelines (양육비 산정기준표) published by the Seoul Family Court to find the standard child support (양육비) for the parents' combined income and the children's ages and number, then divides it by the parents' income ratio to set the non-custodial parent's share. The guidelines are only a starting point, and the amount can be increased or reduced depending on the circumstances.

If the child needs long-term treatment, has already been receiving costly education such as in arts or sports, or the parents have substantial assets compared to their income, you need to show those circumstances with material. Conversely, the paying parent argues for a reduction by proving their actual income and other dependents.

sections.title: You can also claim child support for the period you raised the child alone
body: Child support you paid alone during a separation before divorce, or during a period when child support was not set at the divorce, can be claimed as past child support (과거양육비). The court sets the amount by considering the costs actually spent during that period, the other parent's finances, and the burden of paying it all at once.

A 2024 Supreme Court en banc decision established that the limitation period for past child support that was not set in advance starts running when the child becomes an adult and the duty to raise the child ends. For child support already set by a judgment or record, the limitation period runs separately from each payment date, so if child support has been overdue for a long time, start by calculating the periods.

sections.title: Increases and decreases go through the court
body: If circumstances change after child support is set, it can be changed. If education costs rose because the child moved up to a higher school, prices have risen a lot, or the child became ill and has medical costs, you can ask for an increase. If the paying parent lost their job or became seriously ill, they can ask for a decrease.

The important point is that you must not reduce or stop payments on your own judgment. Until the court decides on a reduction, the original amount keeps building up as a debt, and a performance order and compulsory execution may follow for the overdue amount.

sections.title: When support is not paid, act in a set order
body: If the other parent works for a company, the fastest route is to apply for a direct payment order (직접지급명령) once two or more payments are overdue. If they are self-employed or a freelancer, we consider a security order (담보제공명령), a lump-sum payment order, and compulsory execution against deposits or real estate after an asset inquiry.

If three or more payments are missed despite a performance order (이행명령), you can apply for detention (감치), and if payment is still not made within 1 year after the detention order, the payer becomes subject to criminal punishment. Through the Child Support Enforcement Agency (양육비이행관리원), you can consider driver's license suspension, a request for a travel ban and public disclosure of the name. If you meet the legal requirements, you can also apply for advance payment of child support (양육비 선지급), in which the Child Support Enforcement Agency pays the child support first in place of the other parent.

sections.title: The wording you choose at the start determines what happens later
body: A record or agreement setting child support should clearly state the amount, the monthly payment date, the account to receive it, and until when it will be paid. If these points are vague, disputes arise as soon as you try to calculate the overdue amount.

It is also a good idea to decide in advance how to share large, hard-to-predict costs such as school admission fees or surgery costs. In a divorce by agreement, check that these terms are accurately included in the child support protocol (양육비부담조서) the court draws up.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles child support cases

items.title: Calculating the amount to claim
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and calculates separately the guideline amount, grounds for an increase, the overdue amount and past child support.

items.title: Checking the enforceable title
items.desc: We check whether you have a judgment, a mediation record or a child support protocol, and if you have none, we start by asking the court for a ruling on child support.

items.title: Checking the other parent's income and assets
items.desc: We check their workplace, whether they run a business, and their assets to decide whether a direct payment order is possible or an asset inquiry is needed.

items.title: Applying for enforcement procedures
items.desc: We choose and apply for the procedure most likely to work against the other parent among a direct payment order, a security order, a performance order and compulsory execution.

items.title: Considering further sanctions
items.desc: If payment still does not come after a performance order, we guide you through applying for detention, sanctions through the Child Support Enforcement Agency, and advance payment.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Documents that set child support, such as a judgment, mediation record or child support protocol
Records of child support deposits (bank transaction history)
The other parent's workplace or business information
Receipts for the child's education and medical costs
Your own income documents (such as a withholding tax receipt)
Messages exchanged with the other parent about child support

faqs.q: My ex says they lost their job and is sending only half the child support. Do I have to accept that?
faqs.a: If the other parent reduced it on their own without a court decision on a reduction, the difference from the original amount is also overdue child support. You can apply for a performance order or compulsory execution for the difference. If their circumstances really have changed, the other parent must ask the court for a reduction.

faqs.q: My ex has remarried. Do they no longer have to pay child support?
faqs.a: Remarriage alone does not end the duty to pay child support. Having a new family and a greater support burden can be a reason to ask for a reduction, but even then it must go through the court. The same applies if the custodial parent remarries: unless the legal relationship changes, for example through the new spouse adopting the child by full adoption, the duty remains.

faqs.q: My ex is self-employed, so I can't have it deducted from wages.
faqs.a: A direct payment order can only be used if there is a company paying wages. If the other parent is self-employed, you can apply to the court for a security order, and if security is not provided, obtain a lump-sum payment order. Finding deposits or real estate through an asset inquiry and enforcing against them is also used alongside these.

faqs.q: Can anyone receive advance payment of child support?
faqs.a: You must meet the requirements set by law. The child support the other parent paid must fall short of the advance payment amount, and you must have applied to the Child Support Enforcement Agency for legal or collection support or have gone through an enforcement procedure such as a performance order. For cases decided by October 28, 2026, household income must be no more than 1.5 times the standard median income, but from cases decided on or after October 29, this income requirement no longer applies. Once you apply to the Child Support Enforcement Agency, it decides in principle within 30 days whether to pay.

faqs.q: Can I also claim university tuition after my child becomes an adult?
faqs.a: Child support set by the court in principle covers costs until the child becomes an adult. Tuition after adulthood can be claimed according to a separate promise if the parents made one. That is why many people write the sharing of university tuition into the agreement at the time of divorce.

areaPages.title: Ending a De Facto Marriage
areaPages.lead: Even without a marriage report, if it is recognized that you actually lived as a married couple, you can claim property division and compensation for emotional distress. But unlike a legal marriage, you must first prove for yourself that it was a de facto marriage.

seo.title: Ending a De Facto Marriage in Korea: Property Division, Compensation and Proof | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When a de facto marriage in Korea, where a couple lived together without a marriage report, comes to an end: the standards and evidence for recognition as a de facto marriage, what assets are divided and the deadline to claim, compensation for wrongful termination, acknowledging a child and child support, and issues when the partner has died.
keywords: de facto marriage property division Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: We had a wedding and lived together for years, but never filed a marriage report
My partner claims we were just living together
The home we bought with money we saved together is in my partner's name
My partner suddenly packed up, left, and said it's over
I want child support for our child born without a marriage report
It turned out my partner already had a legal spouse

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 2(1) (Category Na and Category Da cases)
items.text: Confirmation of whether a de facto marital relationship exists is a Category Na family litigation case, and a damages claim for wrongful termination of a de facto marriage (including claims against third parties) is a Category Da family litigation case, and both are handled by the family court. Both go through mediation first (Article 50).

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2 (Right to claim property division), applied mutatis mutandis
items.text: The law has no separate provision on property division in a de facto marriage, but case law applies the property division provision to the end of a de facto marriage, directly or by analogy, on the ground that the substance of the couple's shared life is the same.

items.name: Civil Act Article 806 (Breaking off an engagement and the right to claim damages)
items.text: Under this provision, case law holds a person who ends a de facto marriage without a valid reason liable for property damage and emotional distress.

table.title: How legal marriage and de facto marriage differ
rows: How the relationship ends
Divorce by agreement or judicial divorce
Ends by agreement or by one partner's notice, without any report
Property division
Civil Act Article 839-2

Compensation for emotional distress

No right to inherit, and under case law a property division claim is also difficult
table.note: Based on the Civil Act, the Family Litigation Act and Supreme Court case law. Individual laws on matters such as pensions and housing sometimes separately recognize de facto spouses.

sections.title: A de facto marriage is different from simply living together
body: A de facto marriage (사실혼) is a relationship in which both partners intended to marry and lived a shared life that society would recognize as a married couple, but never filed a marriage report. Having lived together for a long time is not enough on its own; the key is whether you treated each other as spouses and were known to others as a married couple.

There is no rule on how many years you must live together for it to be a de facto marriage. Conversely, even if you lived together for a long time, it is hard to be protected as a de facto marriage if it was cohabitation with no intention to marry. That is why most de facto marriage cases begin with a dispute over the nature of the relationship.

sections.title: Show with material that you lived as a married couple
body: If the other partner claims you were only living together, you have to prove the intention to marry and the reality of your shared life, one point at a time. It is easier to be recognized when several pieces of material point in the same direction rather than just one.
bullets: Photos of the meeting between the families, the wedding and the honeymoon, and wedding invitations
Resident registration at the same address, and a lease signed together
Accounts and card records used together for living costs
Records of attending holidays and family events on both sides as a married couple
Registration as a dependent under health insurance, and applications for family allowances at work
Messages in which you called each other husband or wife, and written statements from acquaintances

sections.title: Property division covers assets built during the de facto marriage
body: Assets the two of you built through cooperation while the de facto marriage lasted are subject to property division (재산분할), whoever's name they are in. Assets owned before the relationship began are in principle excluded, but as in a legal marriage, they may be included if the other partner helped maintain or increase them.

Case law sets the assets to be divided and their values as of the date the de facto marriage ended. The 2-year rule for legal marriage is considered to apply to the claim period, so prepare on the basis that you must claim within 2 years of the date the relationship ended. The end date itself can be disputed, so keep a record of the last day you lived together and the day the belongings were moved out.

sections.title: Claim compensation from the person who wrongfully ended the relationship
body: A de facto marriage can end with just one partner's notice, but if the partner ended it unilaterally without a valid reason, or broke the relationship through wrongful conduct such as an affair or violence, you can claim compensation for emotional distress (위자료). If a third party, such as the partner's parents, is responsible for the breakdown, you can also claim against that person.

A de facto marriage in which one partner has a legal spouse is in principle not protected. However, an exception may be recognized if that legal marriage was already effectively over, and if the partner lied about being married, a separate damages claim can be considered.

sections.title: If there is a child, check acknowledgment first
body: For a child born without a marriage report, a legal father–child relationship arises only when the father acknowledges the child (인지). If the father does not report the acknowledgment himself, a lawsuit claiming acknowledgment (인지청구) is needed, and only after acknowledgment can the person with parental authority, the custodial parent and child support be set.

Once the child is acknowledged, you can also consider claiming child support from the child's birth as past child support. Matters concerning the child proceed separately from property division, so it is a good idea to handle them together at the stage of negotiating the end of the relationship.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles de facto marriage cases

items.title: Checking the nature of the relationship
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and first judges whether a de facto marriage can be argued, based on when you met, how long you lived together, the wedding and contact between the families.

items.title: Organizing the evidence
items.desc: We group resident registration records, photos, accounts and messages by period and build a file showing the intention to marry and the shared life.

items.title: Listing and preserving assets
items.desc: We list the assets and loans built during the de facto marriage, and if there is a risk of disposal, we first apply for provisional attachment or an injunction.

items.title: Mediation and lawsuit
items.desc: We file for mediation covering property division, compensation and matters concerning the child together, and proceed to a lawsuit if no agreement is reached.

items.title: Procedures concerning the child
items.desc: If the child has not been acknowledged, we also consider a claim for acknowledgment, and then set parental authority, the custodial parent and child support.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Photos of the wedding and the meeting between the families, and wedding invitations
A resident registration certificate (or abstract) or lease showing the same address
Bank and card records used together for living costs
Records of the funds used to buy a home or car in the partner's name
Messages in which you were told the relationship was over
The child's birth certificate and family relationship certificate (if you have a child)

faqs.q: How many years do we have to live together to be recognized as a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: There is no period set by law. Even after a short time together, it can be a de facto marriage if you held a wedding and lived as a couple recognized by both families. Even after a long time, it is hard to be recognized if it was cohabitation with no intention to marry. The standard is the intention to marry and how you lived, not the length of time.

faqs.q: My partner died suddenly. What happens to the assets we built together?
faqs.a: A de facto spouse is not an heir, and case law does not allow a property division claim when the relationship ended because the partner died. You need to check whether you have rights to get assets back on other grounds, such as your share in jointly owned property or money you lent to your partner. We also look separately at cases where individual laws recognize de facto spouses, such as survivors' pensions.

faqs.q: We held a wedding but broke up before filing the marriage report. Is that a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: If you actually lived together and began married life after the wedding, it may be seen as a de facto marriage. If you broke up before living together, it is treated more as the breaking off of an engagement than a de facto marriage, and the dispute is about returning wedding gifts and damages. What you can claim differs depending on which it is.

faqs.q: Do I need a court procedure to end a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: A de facto marriage is not a registered relationship, so a court procedure is not required to end it. However, if you cannot agree on property division, compensation or matters concerning the child, you must apply to the family court for mediation and a lawsuit. If you settle by agreement, keep a written agreement.

areaPages.areaName: Divorce Claims by the Spouse at Fault
areaPages.title: Divorce Claims by the Spouse at Fault
areaPages.summary: A divorce claim by the spouse mainly responsible for the breakdown, for example through an affair, is in principle dismissed, but case law recognizes exceptions.
areaPages.lead: If the spouse mainly responsible for breaking up the marriage files for divorce first, the court in principle does not accept the claim. However, exceptions may be recognized where the other spouse also has no intention of continuing the marriage, or so much time has passed that weighing responsibility has become meaningless. Whichever side you are on, start by examining whether the case falls under one of these exceptions.

seo.title: Divorce Claims by the Spouse at Fault in Korea and How to Respond | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Based on Supreme Court case law: the standards the court applies when a spouse responsible for the breakdown of the marriage through an affair or leaving home files for divorce, the three exceptions, how the spouse who does not want a divorce can respond, and preparing a counterclaim for compensation and property division.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My spouse had an affair and left home, and now they've sued me for divorce
I'm seeing someone else and we're separated, and I want to finalize the divorce
We've been separated for over 10 years, but my spouse refuses only the divorce
I don't want a divorce, but I don't know what to do in the lawsuit
My spouse has filed a counterclaim for compensation and property division

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 840 (Grounds for judicial divorce)
items.text: Along with infidelity, malicious desertion, extremely unfair treatment and the spouse's whereabouts or survival being unknown for 3 years or more, Item 6 sets 'any other serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage' as a ground for divorce. Divorce claims by a spouse at fault are mostly fought over this Item 6.

items.name: Civil Act Article 842 (Extinction of the right to claim divorce on other grounds)
items.text: A divorce cannot be claimed on the ground in Article 840, Item 6 once 6 months have passed since the other spouse learned of it, or 2 years since it occurred.

sections.title: The rule is that such claims are not accepted
body: In its en banc decision of September 15, 2015 (2013므568), the Supreme Court kept its existing position that, in principle, a divorce claim by the spouse at fault (유책배우자) is not allowed. Its reasons were that Korea offers divorce by agreement, so even the responsible spouse can persuade the other to divorce, and that allowing divorce based on breakdown alone, without a system to secure the other spouse's livelihood after divorce, could result in that spouse being forced out unilaterally.

So a spouse who had an affair and left home will have difficulty getting a divorce judgment just by arguing that 'the marriage is over anyway'. The issues in the lawsuit come down to who broke up the marriage, and whether the case falls under one of the exceptions below.

sections.title: When exceptions are recognized
body: The same decision said that divorce may be allowed as an exception if there are special circumstances in which the responsibility no longer remains to an extent that should block the divorce claim. The court looks broadly at the nature and degree of the responsibility, the other spouse's intention to continue the marriage, the ages of both spouses and the length of the marriage, the length of the separation and life after it, how the other spouse's livelihood will be secured after divorce, and the situation of any minor children.

In a decision of June 16, 2022 (2021므14258), the Supreme Court said that the other spouse's intention to continue the marriage should not be judged only by what is said in the lawsuit, but objectively, by looking at what efforts were actually made to repair the relationship.
bullets: When the other spouse also has no intention of continuing the marriage but refuses only the divorce out of emotion
When the spouse at fault has steadily sent living expenses and child support and shown consideration to the other spouse and children, enough to offset the responsibility
When so much time has passed that weighing the degree of responsibility has become meaningless

sections.title: If you are the spouse who does not want a divorce
body: If you want to keep the marriage, you need to show that intention in both words and actions. Agreeing to couples counseling recommended by the court, keeping in contact about the children, and keeping records of requests for living expenses all support your intention to continue the marriage. Conversely, if you have only blamed the other spouse and cut off communication, that can be used against you when the court judges the exceptions.

However, no one can be sure how the lawsuit will end, so we also consider whether to make alternative claims for compensation for emotional distress (위자료), property division and child-rearing arrangements in case the divorce is granted.

sections.title: If you are the spouse seeking divorce
body: If you bear the responsibility, agreement is often a more realistic path than a lawsuit. The 'protection and consideration' the case law speaks of shows in whether you faithfully sent living expenses and child support during the separation, and whether you proposed a property settlement that would allow the other spouse to live after the divorce.

Many cases are also hard to see as one spouse's fault alone. If the other spouse also engaged in conduct such as verbal abuse or a long period of coldness, we can organize those circumstances in time order and argue that both spouses share responsibility.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Sorting out responsibility
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally, organizes in date order how the separation came about and each spouse's wrongdoing, and first judges whether there is room to fall under an exception.

items.title: Setting the goal
items.desc: We decide whether to keep the marriage or to divorce if the terms are right, and set the order of arguments accordingly.

items.title: Preparing evidence and records of daily life
items.desc: We gather material on the affair or leaving home, records of living expenses and child support sent after the separation, and records of contact made to repair the relationship.

items.title: Responding in mediation and the lawsuit
items.desc: In mediation, we weigh realistic terms, and if no agreement is reached, we argue the case through an answer, a counterclaim and briefs.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: The complaint or mediation application you received
A note on when and how the separation began
Messages and photos showing the affair or leaving home
Records of living expenses and child support sent after the separation
Records of couples counseling or attempts to reconcile

faqs.q: After how many years of separation can a spouse at fault get a divorce?
faqs.a: There is no period set by law. The length of separation is considered as one of many circumstances, together with how living expenses and child support were paid during that time and whether the other spouse actually tried to continue the marriage.

faqs.q: If I had an affair, can I not receive property division either?
faqs.a: Property division is a system for dividing assets built together during the marriage, so it is judged separately from responsibility for the breakdown. Compensation for that responsibility is argued through compensation for emotional distress, while property division looks at how much each spouse contributed to building the assets.

faqs.q: If my divorce claim is dismissed, can I never sue again?
faqs.a: A new claim based only on the same circumstances is unlikely to be accepted. However, if new circumstances arise after the judgment, such as a long continued separation or a change in the other spouse's attitude, there may be room for a new decision.

areaPages.areaName: Domestic Violence Divorce and Protection Orders
areaPages.title: Domestic Violence, Divorce and Victim Protection Orders
areaPages.summary: Even without filing a criminal complaint, you can apply directly to the family court for a victim protection order to obtain a restraining order and restrictions on visitation.
areaPages.cardLaw: Domestic Violence Punishment Act Article 55-2; Civil Act Article 840, Item 3
areaPages.lead: In a divorce involving violence, secure your safety first and then take the legal steps. Separately from a criminal complaint, the victim can apply directly to the family court for a protection order, and this can run alongside the divorce lawsuit.

seo.title: Domestic Violence Divorce in Korea: Victim Protection Orders and Restraining Orders | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When preparing for divorce in Korea because of a spouse's violence: the differences and durations of emergency measures, temporary measures and victim protection orders, restrictions on issuing certificates to keep your address from being exposed, and how violence is dealt with in compensation, custody and visitation.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: Whenever my spouse drinks, they throw things and hit me
I left home, but my spouse shows up outside my workplace
My spouse was violent in front of our child, so I'm worried about visitation
I'm afraid my spouse will find out my new address
I don't necessarily want them punished, but I want all contact to stop

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence Crimes (가정폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 55-2 (Victim protection orders)
items.text: At the request of the victim, the victim's legal representative or a prosecutor, a judge can order the offender to leave and stay away from the home, not to come within 100 meters of the victim's home or workplace, not to contact the victim by phone, text or other telecommunications, and can restrict the exercise of parental authority or visitation rights. These can also be ordered together.

items.name: Article 55-3 of the same Act (Duration of victim protection orders)
items.text: A protection order cannot last more than 1 year, and if needed it can be extended in 2-month units. Even with extensions or changes in type, the total including the earlier periods cannot exceed 3 years.

items.name: Article 63 of the same Act (Crime of failing to comply with protective dispositions, etc.)
items.text: Anyone who fails to comply with a victim protection order or temporary protection order is punished by imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine of up to KRW 20 million, or short-term detention.

table.title: Protection procedures available to victims of violence
rows: Emergency measures
Police officers dispatched after a report
Stopping the violence, separating the offender, arrest in the act, taking the victim to a counseling center, shelter or hospital
Emergency temporary measures
Judicial police officer
When a court decision cannot be waited for: removal from the home, a 100-meter restraining order, a ban on telecommunications contact
Temporary measures
Judge (at a prosecutor's request)
Removal from the home, restraining orders, etc. during criminal proceedings. Removal and restraining orders last up to 2 months and can be extended twice
Victim protection order
Family court (requested directly by the victim)
Up to 1 year, extendable to a total of 3 years. Includes restrictions on parental authority and visitation
Pre-trial measures
Family court during a divorce lawsuit
Restraining orders, designation of a temporary custodial parent, payment of living expenses, etc.
Restriction on issuing and viewing certificates
City, town or township office; community service center
Prevents a designated offender from obtaining or viewing your family relationship certificate or resident registration record
table.note: Based on the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence Crimes, the Family Litigation Act, the Act on the Registration of Family Relationships and the Resident Registration Act (checked on the Korea Law Information Center, the government's official legislation database, October 2026).

sections.title: Apply directly to the court, separately from criminal proceedings
body: Temporary measures (임시조치) are requested by a prosecutor from the court on the premise that criminal proceedings against the offender are under way. If you do not want punishment or hesitate to report, a victim protection order (피해자보호명령) is often the right fit. The victim applies directly to the family court, and it is decided regardless of whether a criminal complaint has been filed.

Once the application is filed, the judge can, if needed, first issue a temporary protection order (임시보호명령) even before deciding (Article 55-4 of the same Act). You can apply separately either before filing a divorce lawsuit or during the lawsuit.

sections.title: Keep your new address from becoming known
body: After leaving home, the biggest worry is often your address being exposed. A victim of domestic violence can apply to the city, town or township office to designate a spouse or lineal blood relative and restrict the issuing of their family relationship certificate and similar documents to that person (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 14(8)), and can also apply to restrict the viewing of their resident registration record and the issuing of copies and abstracts (Resident Registration Act Article 29).

The address you write on the complaint or mediation application is also served on the other spouse as is. Before filing, decide first with your lawyer which address to use for receiving court documents.

sections.title: Violence is a ground for divorce and for compensation
body: If you were hit or seriously verbally abused by your spouse, you can claim divorce on the ground of 'extremely unfair treatment' (Civil Act Article 840, Item 3) or another serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage. The number of incidents, severity and duration of the violence are also reflected when the amount of compensation for emotional distress (위자료) is set.

The main evidence is medical certificates, photos of injuries, records of 112 (police) reports and dispatches, and records from counseling centers. Even for incidents long ago, writing down the dates and places can show that your account is consistent.

sections.title: How violence is handled in matters concerning the children
body: The court decides the person with parental authority and the custodial parent based on the child's welfare, so violence in front of the child or against the child is an important factor. Visitation can also be restricted or excluded if needed for the child's welfare (Civil Act Article 837-2(3)).

You can already ask for restrictions on visitation rights at the protection order stage, and if it is hard to cut off contact completely, some arrangements start with short meetings at a place where a third party is present.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Checking your safety
items.desc: We first check whether the place you are staying now is safe and where your child is, and if it is urgent, we first guide you to report to the police and connect with a shelter.

items.title: Applying for a protection order
items.desc: We choose the types of protection order needed and file the application, and request a temporary protection order at the same time if needed.

items.title: Protecting your address
items.desc: We sort out the restriction on issuing certificates and the address for service before the complaint is filed.

items.title: Divorce and custody claims
items.desc: We bring the divorce, compensation, property division, designation of the custodial parent and restrictions on visitation together as one case, and ask that mediation be conducted separately so you do not have to face the other spouse.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Medical certificates and photos of injuries showing the date
The date and time of 112 reports and the case reception number
Messages and recordings of verbal abuse or threats
Counseling records from counseling centers or hospitals
If your child witnessed the violence, a note on when and in what situation

faqs.q: If I apply for a protection order, will my spouse get a criminal record?
faqs.a: A victim protection order is not a criminal punishment but a decision to protect the victim. However, approaching or contacting the victim after the order is issued is itself a crime punishable by imprisonment of up to 2 years or other penalties.

faqs.q: Will a protection order be issued if I was hit only once or twice?
faqs.a: It is not decided by the number of incidents alone; the judge must find it necessary to protect the victim. The decision is based on the severity of the violence, recent incidents, and messages or report records showing the risk of it happening again.

faqs.q: My protection order is about to expire, and I'm anxious.
faqs.a: You can apply for an extension. It is extended in 2-month units, up to 3 years including the first period. You need to submit recent circumstances showing why an extension is needed.

areaPages.title: Property Division Claims After Divorce
areaPages.summary: Even if you divorced without settling property, you can still claim within 2 years of the divorce. That period cannot be extended.
areaPages.lead: Many people put off talking about property while rushing through a divorce by agreement, or only learn about the other spouse's assets after the divorce. The right to claim property division disappears 2 years after the date of divorce, so start by calculating the dates.

seo.title: Claiming Property Division After Divorce in Korea: The 2-Year Deadline | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to claim property division separately after a divorce by agreement or a judgment in Korea, calculating the 2-year exclusion period from the date of divorce, Supreme Court decisions on claiming only part of the assets and on hidden assets found later, and provisional attachment and asset inquiries.
keywords: property division after divorce by agreement Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I wanted it over quickly, so we divorced by agreement without discussing assets
After the divorce, I found out there was an apartment in my ex's name
We got a divorce judgment, but severance pay and shares were left out
We wrote 'property matters are settled' in the agreement, but hidden assets have come to light
My ex put the home up for sale after the divorce

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2 (Right to claim property division)
items.text: A person divorced by agreement may claim property division from the other spouse, and if they cannot agree, the family court decides, taking into account the amount of assets built through both parties' cooperation and other circumstances. The right to claim property division expires 2 years after the date of divorce.

items.name: Civil Act Article 843 (Provisions applied mutatis mutandis)
items.text: The provisions on the right to claim property division and the right to revoke fraudulent acts to preserve it also apply to judicial divorce.

items.name: Civil Act Article 839-3 (Right to revoke fraudulent acts to preserve the right to claim property division)
items.text: If a spouse disposed of assets knowing it would harm the exercise of the right to claim property division, you can ask the family court to revoke the disposal and restore the assets.

sections.title: The 2 years cannot be extended
body: The 2 years is not a statute of limitations but an exclusion period (제척기간), so it is not paused or extended just because you made a demand to the other spouse. It is met only if a mediation application or petition for a ruling is filed with the family court within the period.

The reference 'date of divorce' is the day the divorce was reported for a divorce by agreement, or the day the judgment became final for a judicial divorce. Check the date on your detailed marriage relationship certificate (혼인관계증명서 상세), and if the deadline is near, it is safer to file first even if you have not gathered all the material.

sections.title: Assets left out of the claim are hard to claim again
body: In a decision of June 22, 2018 (2018스18), the Supreme Court held that if only some assets were claimed within the 2 years, the right to claim the remaining assets disappears once the period passes. If assets that were not dealt with at all in the proceedings are newly discovered after the decision becomes final, an additional claim is possible, but that additional claim must also be made within 2 years of the date of divorce.

So when you first file the property division (재산분할) claim, list every asset you know of, and it is a good idea to state that you will expand the claim for assets still being checked depending on the results of the asset inquiry.

sections.title: If the agreement contains a waiver clause
body: A clause such as 'neither party will make any claim regarding property in the future' does not block a claim in every case. Its effect may be judged differently depending on whether it was a pledge written before the divorce took effect that simply waived the right in advance, or an agreement that settled accounts after reviewing all the assets.
Organizing the date it was written, the list of assets you knew of at the time, and how you came to sign it can be used to challenge its validity.

sections.title: Keep the assets from disappearing while you wait
body: If the other spouse is trying to sell the home or is moving deposits, apply for provisional attachment (가압류) or an injunction against disposal (처분금지가처분) together with the claim (Family Litigation Act Article 63). If you do not know exactly what the other spouse owns, you can apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회) to obtain records from financial institutions and public agencies (Articles 48-2 and 48-3 of the same Act).

If the assets have already been transferred to someone else's name, we also consider a lawsuit to revoke that disposal. This lawsuit must be filed within 1 year of learning the grounds for revocation and within 5 years of the disposal (Civil Act Articles 839-3(2) and 406(2)).

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Calculating the deadline
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally, checks the date of divorce and the deadline, and sets the filing schedule according to the time remaining.

items.title: Listing the assets
items.desc: We write down every asset you know of, including real estate, deposits, shares, insurance, severance pay and pensions, and separately mark the assets that need to be checked.

items.title: Preservation measures
items.desc: For assets at risk of disposal, we first apply for provisional attachment or an injunction.

items.title: Mediation and ruling
items.desc: We refine the claim to reflect the results of the asset inquiry, and if mediation fails, argue the division ratio and method in the court's ruling proceedings.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Marriage relationship certificate (detailed)
The divorce-by-agreement settlement, divorce judgment or mediation record
A list of assets you know are in your ex-spouse's name, and any leads
Records of your contributions to building assets during the marriage (deposits, loan repayment records)
Signs that your ex-spouse disposed of assets before or after the divorce

faqs.q: It's been 1 year and 11 months since my divorce. Is it too late?
faqs.a: It only needs to be filed before the 2 years pass. If little time remains, we file the mediation application or petition first, even if not all the material has been gathered, and then supplement it with asset inquiries.

faqs.q: I found out about hidden assets after 2 years.
faqs.a: The right to claim property division expires after 2 years, so in principle you cannot claim again. If the other spouse actively deceived you, we can examine whether another civil claim is possible, but that is not an easy path, so it is important to act within the period.

faqs.q: Do I also have to claim compensation for emotional distress within 2 years?
faqs.a: Compensation for emotional distress (위자료) is a damages claim, so a different period from the 2 years for property division applies. However, the starting point can differ depending on the circumstances, so it is a good idea to review it together with property division.

areaPages.title: Claiming Living Expenses and Spousal Support During Separation
areaPages.summary: Until the divorce, the duty of support continues even if you live apart, so you can claim living expenses. Past living expenses are calculated from when you asked for them.
areaPages.lead: Until a divorce is final, you are legally married. If living expenses were cut off when you separated, you can claim spousal support from the family court. Past living expenses are calculated from when you asked for them, so first make a record of your request.

seo.title: Living Expenses and Spousal Support During Separation in Korea, and Pre-Trial Measures | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to petition for a spousal support ruling in Korea when your spouse cuts off living expenses during separation, the Supreme Court decision on how much past support can be received, pre-trial measures during a divorce lawsuit, and performance orders and detention when support is still not paid after the decision.
keywords: living costs during divorce lawsuit Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: Since we separated, my spouse hasn't given me a single won for living costs
I'm staying at my parents' home with our child, and money is very tight
I'm in a divorce lawsuit and don't have enough money to last until the judgment
My spouse says, 'You left, so I don't owe you anything'
I want to know whether I can receive several years of living expenses at once

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 826 (Duties between spouses)
items.text: Spouses must live together, support each other and cooperate. If they temporarily do not live together for a justifiable reason, each must accept this.

items.name: Civil Act Article 833 (Living expenses)
items.text: Unless there is a special agreement, the costs necessary for the spouses' life together are borne jointly by the spouses.

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 2(1)2(b) (Category Ma non-contentious family cases)
items.text: Dispositions concerning the spouses' cohabitation, support, cooperation or sharing of living expenses are Category Ma cases ruled on by the family court, and mediation must come first before petitioning for a ruling.

sections.title: The duty of support remains even if you live apart
body: Support between spouses means maintaining the other spouse's life at the same level as one's own (Supreme Court decision of August 25, 2017, 2014스26). Living expenses cannot be cut off merely because you are separated.

However, the court does look at who left home and why. If you left to escape violence or verbal abuse, a justifiable reason is easily recognized, but if you left for no reason and cut off contact, your claim may be limited. Keep a record of how you came to leave.

sections.title: Past living expenses run from when you asked
body: The same decision said that, unless there are special circumstances, past spousal support (부양료) can be claimed only for the period after support was requested but not provided. Even if you put up with it for years, it will be hard to receive living expenses for that period if there is no record of a request.
So when living expenses are cut off, the first step is to make a request by text message or certified letter (내용증명), stating the date and the amount needed.

sections.title: The amount is set by both spouses' circumstances
body: The court looks at both spouses' incomes and assets, the standard of living during the marriage, and who has the children. If you do not know the other spouse's income, you can apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회) (Family Litigation Act Articles 48-2 and 48-3).

If you have the children with you, the children's share is often claimed as child support and the spouse's share as spousal support. Organizing receipts for the children's tutoring and medical costs, and records of rent and maintenance fees, makes it easier to explain the amount.

sections.title: During a divorce lawsuit, use a pre-trial measure
body: If a divorce lawsuit or mediation is under way, you can apply for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) ordering living expenses to be paid first, without waiting for the judgment (Family Litigation Act Article 62). A pre-trial measure is not enforceable, so it cannot be used to seize assets right away, but failing to follow it can lead to an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (Article 67 of the same Act).

If the spousal support ruling is final and payment still is not made, you can apply for a performance order (이행명령), and if three or more monthly payments are missed, you can even apply for detention (감치) (Articles 64 and 68 of the same Act). The decision can also be used to seize wages or deposits.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Creating a record of the request
items.desc: If there is no record of a request yet, we start by sending a written demand stating the amount and date, which sets the starting point for the claim.

items.title: Working out the amount needed
items.desc: We gather monthly living costs, the children's expenses and both spouses' income records, and calculate the amount to claim.

items.title: Mediation and ruling, or a pre-trial measure
items.desc: Before divorce, we apply for spousal support mediation and a ruling; during a divorce lawsuit, we also apply for a pre-trial measure.

items.title: Securing payment
items.desc: If payment is still not made after the decision, we proceed in order with a performance order, detention and compulsory execution.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Text or KakaoTalk messages, or certified letters, requesting living expenses
The date living expenses were cut off and the amount you received before
Your own income records and information on your spouse's workplace
Receipts for rent, maintenance fees, utilities and the children's education costs
Material showing how you came to leave home

faqs.q: What happens to spousal support after the divorce?
faqs.a: The duty of support between spouses lasts only while the marriage continues, so once the divorce is final, it cannot be claimed for the period after that. Life after divorce is settled through property division, compensation for emotional distress and child support.

faqs.q: My spouse is hiding their income.
faqs.a: If you apply for an asset disclosure order, your spouse must submit a list of assets, and if that is not enough, the court can make asset inquiries with financial institutions and others. Material showing your spouse's card spending or standard of living can also be used to estimate income.

faqs.q: We live together, but my spouse won't give me living expenses. Can I claim in that case too?
faqs.a: Yes. The duty of support exists as long as you are married, whether or not you are separated. First make a record of asking for living expenses.

areaPages.title: Changing Parental Authority and Custody
areaPages.summary: The person with parental authority and the custodial parent set at divorce can be changed, but the parents' agreement alone is not enough; a family court decision is required.
areaPages.lead: Once the person with parental authority and the custodial parent have been set, they do not change just because both parents agree. Changing the person with parental authority recorded in the family relationship register requires a family court decision, and if there is a dispute, you must show with material that the current arrangement is not right for the child.

seo.title: Changing the Person with Parental Authority or Custodial Parent in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The procedure for changing the person with parental authority and the custodial parent after divorce in Korea and what the court looks at, changing parental authority and custody separately, the deadline when the sole person with parental authority dies, hearing the views of children 13 and older, and pre-trial measures for temporary custody.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My child keeps saying they want to live with me
My ex, the custodial parent, leaves our child with the grandparents and barely takes care of them
Since my ex remarried, our child clashes badly with the new family
My child already lives with me, but on paper my ex has parental authority
My ex-spouse, who had sole parental authority, has passed away

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 837(5) (Change of matters concerning child-rearing)
items.text: If the family court finds it necessary for the child's welfare, it may change matters concerning child-rearing or make other appropriate dispositions, at the request of the father, mother, child or a prosecutor, or on its own authority.

items.name: Civil Act Article 909(6) (Change of the person with parental authority)
items.text: If needed for the child's welfare, the family court may change the designated person with parental authority to the other parent at the request of a relative of the child within the fourth degree.

items.name: Civil Act Article 909-2(1) (Death of the sole person with parental authority)
items.text: If the sole person with parental authority dies, the surviving parent, the minor or the minor's relatives may request that the surviving parent be designated as the person with parental authority within 1 month of learning of the death and within 6 months of the date of death.

sections.title: An agreement alone does not change the register
body: Even if the parents agree to change the custodial parent (양육자), changing the person with parental authority (친권자) on record requires a ruling by the family court. Changes of the person with parental authority and of dispositions on child-rearing are Category Ma non-contentious family cases, so they go through mediation first, and if both parents agree, they can end fairly quickly in mediation.

Once the decision is final, you must report the change of the person with parental authority to the city, district, town or township office within 1 month (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 79(2)).

sections.title: Courts do not easily disturb current stability
body: If the child is living stably in the current environment, the fact that the other parent is better off financially is not enough to make a change. You need to show with objective material, such as school attendance, medical records and counseling records, that the current arrangement is harmful to the child or that the change would clearly be better.

If the child is 13 or older, the court in principle hears the child's opinion before deciding (Rules on Family Litigation Article 100). The child's wishes are given significant weight, but they do not automatically decide the outcome.
bullets: Neglect or abuse by the custodial parent, or repeated verbal abuse
The custodial parent leaves the child with others and effectively does not care for the child
Frequent moves and school transfers, or serious conflict within a stepfamily
Continued blocking of the set visitation without a valid reason

sections.title: Parental authority and custody can be changed separately
body: Parental authority is the power to act for the child in legal matters and manage the child's property, while custody means living with and caring for the child. If the child already lives with you but the other parent holds parental authority, you need the other parent's cooperation every time for school transfers, passport applications, opening a bank account or consenting to surgery.

In such cases, we apply to change either both the person with parental authority and the custodial parent or just one of them, depending on the circumstances. If the custodial parent changes, who pays child support to whom must also be set again.

sections.title: If the sole person with parental authority has died
body: Even if the parent designated as the sole person with parental authority at the divorce dies, parental authority does not automatically pass to the other parent. You must request designation of the person with parental authority within 1 month of learning of the death and within 6 months of the date of death, and once that period passes, the family court can appoint a guardian for the minor (Civil Act Article 909-2).

The court decides on designation by looking at the surviving parent's willingness and ability to raise the child and their relationship with the child so far, so records of keeping in touch with the child and sending child support help.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Identifying what has changed
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and compares the reasons the custodial parent was chosen at the divorce with the circumstances that have changed since.

items.title: Gathering material
