items.desc: We collect material the court will find credible, such as school, medical and counseling records, conversations with the child and records of visitation.

items.title: Deciding what to request
items.desc: We decide which of the person with parental authority, the custodial parent, child support and visitation to change, and if it is urgent, we also apply for a pre-trial measure designating a temporary custodial parent.

items.title: Mediation and the family investigation
items.desc: We prepare with you so that you can describe the child's life concretely in mediation and the family investigation (가사조사).

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: The divorce judgment, mediation record or agreement
The child's basic certificate (to check who holds parental authority)
School attendance and student records, and medical records
Records of visitation and child support payments
Messages or photos showing the child's current situation

faqs.q: If my child says they want to live with their father, will it change right away?
faqs.a: Not right away. If the child is 13 or older, the court hears the child's opinion and gives it significant weight, but it judges whether those wishes serve the child's welfare together with the living environment.

faqs.q: I urgently need to bring my child to live with me.
faqs.a: Along with the request for a change, you can apply for a pre-trial measure asking the court to set a temporary custodial parent until the decision (Family Litigation Act Article 62). Forcibly taking the child can actually be judged against you, so go through the procedure first.

faqs.q: My ex also agrees. Do I really need a lawyer?
faqs.a: If both parents agree, the parents sometimes file themselves and finish in mediation. However, child support and visitation often have to be set again at the same time, so it is a good idea to check the wording of the mediation record carefully.

areaPages.areaName: Changing a Child's Surname and Family Origin
areaPages.title: Changing a Child's Surname and Family Origin
areaPages.summary: To change a child's surname because of remarriage or sole custody, you need court permission based on the child's welfare.
areaPages.lead: A child's surname does not change just by reporting a remarriage or designating a custodial parent. The family court must find the change necessary for the child's welfare and grant permission. Permission may be granted even if the biological father objects, and may be refused even if he consents.

seo.title: Permission to Change a Child's Surname in Korea and Stepfamilies | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The procedure in Korea for permission to change a child's surname and family origin after divorce or in a stepfamily, the standards set by the Supreme Court, how to respond when the biological father objects, the difference from full adoption, and the report to be filed within 1 month of permission.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: In our stepfamily, only my child has a different surname, which causes trouble at school
I'm raising my child alone after divorce and want to change their surname to mine
My ex-spouse objects to changing the surname
My child says they want to use their mother's surname
I'm not sure whether to change only the surname or go for full adoption

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 781(6) (Child's surname and family origin)
items.text: If it is necessary to change a child's surname and family origin for the child's welfare, they may be changed with the court's permission at the request of the father, mother or child. If the child is a minor and the legal representative cannot make the request, a relative or a prosecutor may do so.

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 2(1)2(a) (Category Ra non-contentious family cases)
items.text: Permission to change a child's surname and family origin is a Category Ra non-contentious family case, in which permission is requested from the family court without an opposing party.

items.name: Act on the Registration of Family Relationships (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률) Article 100 (Report of change of surname and family origin)
items.text: A person changing a surname and family origin must report it within 1 month of the date the decision becomes final, attaching a certified copy of the decision and a certificate of finality.

sections.title: The court weighs two kinds of disadvantage
body: In a decision of December 11, 2009 (2009스23), the Supreme Court set out how this is judged. First, the court looks at the disadvantages of not changing the surname, such as obstacles to emotional unity within the family and prejudice at school or in social life. Next, it looks at the disadvantages of changing it, such as confusion about identity and a break in ties with the biological father or siblings. It then compares the two from the child's point of view and decides in the direction that helps the child.

The same decision said that if the change is necessary for the child's welfare beyond mere personal preference, and there is no improper purpose such as hiding a crime or avoiding legal restrictions, permission should in principle be granted.

sections.title: The biological father's consent is not strictly required
body: The law contains no provision making the biological father's consent a requirement. The court may hear the biological father's opinion, but it looks more at the actual relationship he has had with the child than at the objection itself. If there has been no visitation and no child support for a long time, that can support the need for the change.

On the other hand, if the request looks like a way to pressure the other parent in a child support dispute, it may be judged unfavorably. The petition should focus on the difficulties the child is facing now and the stability the child will gain after the change, rather than on the other parent's faults.

sections.title: Changing only the surname is different from full adoption
body: A change of surname and family origin (성·본 변경) only changes the name; the legal father–child relationship with the biological father remains. Inheritance, support, visitation and the duty to pay child support all remain.

Full adoption (친양자 입양) is a much weightier procedure that ends the family relationship with the biological parents and makes the child the new parent's own child. To fully adopt a spouse's child, the couple must have been married for at least 1 year, and in principle the biological parents' consent is required (Civil Act Article 908-2). In a stepfamily, first decide which is the right fit.

sections.title: File the report within 1 month of permission
body: Even when the decision granting permission becomes final, the family relationship register does not change by itself. You must file a report with the city, district, town or township office of the place of family registration or address within 1 month of the date the decision became final, and a late report can lead to an administrative fine of up to KRW 50,000 (Article 122 of the same Act).
If there are several siblings, a separate request must be made for each child, so decide in advance whether to file together so the siblings do not end up with different surnames.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Confirming the purpose
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally, and together we first decide whether changing only the surname is enough or whether full adoption is needed.

items.title: Organizing material showing the need
items.desc: We put together material on what the child has experienced at school, the child's wishes, the relationship with the new family, and the extent of contact with the biological father.

items.title: Drafting and filing the petition
items.desc: We file the petition for permission with the family court for the child's address and respond to any correction orders or inquiries from the court.

items.title: Report after the decision is final
items.desc: Once the decision is final, we guide you through the report of the change of surname and family origin, which must be filed within 1 month.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: The child's basic certificate and family relationship certificate
Resident registration certificates for the petitioner and the child
A marriage relationship certificate showing the remarriage
A note on difficulties the child has faced at school
Records of visitation with and child support from the biological father

faqs.q: If I change the surname, will I stop receiving child support from the biological father?
faqs.a: No. Only the surname and family origin change, and the legal father–child relationship remains, so the duty to pay child support also remains. Visitation also continues unless it is separately restricted.

faqs.q: Will the court ask for my child's opinion?
faqs.a: Case law requires the child's wishes to be considered in light of the child's age and maturity. If the child is old enough, the court often checks the child's wishes directly, so talk it through fully with your child in advance.

faqs.q: Can the surname be changed back later?
faqs.a: Changing it back requires the court's permission through the same procedure. Frequent changes of surname can themselves confuse the child, so it is a good idea to decide carefully when you first file.

areaPages.title: International Divorce (Divorcing a Foreign Spouse)
areaPages.summary: In a divorce with a foreign spouse, first check whether a Korean court can hear the case and which country's law applies.
areaPages.cardLaw: Private International Law Act Articles 56 and 66
areaPages.lead: If your spouse is a foreign national or lives abroad, serving the complaint, jurisdiction and the applicable law all become issues. A Korean living in Korea can usually divorce in a Korean court under Korean law, but there are additional points to check for the divorce to take effect in the other country.

seo.title: International Divorce and Divorce Lawsuits with a Foreign Spouse in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Based on the Private International Law Act and case law: international jurisdiction of Korean courts and the governing law when divorcing a foreign spouse, service by public notice on a spouse who cannot be reached, recognition of foreign judgments in Korea and reporting the divorce, and what to watch for when there are children.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My spouse, who came to Korea on a marriage migrant visa, left home and cut off contact
My spouse went back to their home country and won't return
We married abroad, and I want to know if we can divorce in Korea
We divorced in a foreign court, but Korean records still show us as married
I'm worried my foreign spouse will leave the country with our child

items.name: Private International Law Act (국제사법) Article 56 (Special jurisdiction over marital cases)
items.text: Korean courts have jurisdiction in cases such as when one spouse's habitual residence is in Korea and the spouses' last shared habitual residence was also in Korea; when the habitual residence of the plaintiff and a minor child is in Korea; when both spouses are Korean nationals; or when a Korean national habitually resident in Korea files a lawsuit solely to dissolve the marriage.

items.name: Private International Law Act Article 66 (Divorce)
items.text: Divorce is governed, in order, by the law of the spouses' common nationality, the law of their common habitual residence, or the law of the place most closely connected. However, if one spouse is a Korean national habitually resident in Korea, Korean law applies.

items.name: Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 217 (Recognition of foreign judgments)
items.text: A final judgment of a foreign court is recognized in Korea only if it meets all of the requirements: the foreign court's international jurisdiction, lawful service on the defendant (excluding service by public notice) or the defendant's appearance, consistency with good morals and social order, and reciprocity.

sections.title: Whether it can be done in a Korean court under Korean law
body: For a Korean spouse living in Korea, Korean courts usually have jurisdiction, and the law applied to the divorce is the Korean Civil Act (Private International Law Act Articles 56 and 66). So the grounds for divorce are also judged under Civil Act (민법) Article 840.
If both spouses live abroad or both are foreign nationals, jurisdiction and the governing law may differ, so each case must be reviewed separately.

sections.title: When you do not know your spouse's address
body: If your foreign spouse left home and cut off contact, check their name in Roman letters, date of birth and passport number from the documents submitted when you reported the marriage. In a lawsuit, the court can be asked to check immigration records to confirm whether your spouse is in Korea or has left the country.

If it is shown that documents cannot be served by ordinary means, the case proceeds by service by public notice (공시송달) (Civil Procedure Act Article 194). The first service by public notice takes effect 2 weeks after it is posted, and service by public notice for service that would be made abroad takes effect after 2 months (Article 196 of the same Act). If you know a foreign address, service must go through overseas channels, which can take several months.

sections.title: Between grounds for divorce and nullity of marriage
body: If your spouse left home after entering Korea without a valid reason and cut off contact, you claim divorce on the ground of malicious desertion (Civil Act Article 840, Item 2) or another serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage (Item 6 of the same Article). Records of a missing-person report, messages trying to make contact, and immigration records serve as evidence.

If the only purpose from the start was to enter Korea or work, nullity of the marriage (혼인무효) can be considered. In a decision of June 10, 2010 (2010므574), the Supreme Court held that a marriage is void when the marriage was reported as a means of entry without any intention of forming a genuine marital relationship.

sections.title: What remains after the judgment
body: Once a Korean court's divorce judgment becomes final, you report the divorce within 1 month. If you obtained a divorce judgment from a foreign court, that judgment must meet the recognition requirements of Civil Procedure Act Article 217 to be reflected in the Korean family relationship register.

To have the Korean divorce reflected in the other country's civil status records, you must go through that country's procedure separately. If there are children, setting the person with parental authority, the custodial parent and matters about leaving the country together with the divorce will reduce disputes later.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Checking jurisdiction and governing law
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally, checks the spouses' nationalities and places of residence, and first judges whether the lawsuit can be brought in Korea.

items.title: Securing your spouse's personal details
items.desc: Using the marriage report documents and any remaining records, we organize your spouse's name in Roman letters, passport number and last contact details.

items.title: Filing the complaint and service
items.desc: After correcting the address and checking immigration records, we apply for service by public notice if needed.

items.title: Judgment and follow-up
items.desc: After the judgment becomes final, we guide you through the remaining procedures, such as reporting the divorce and reporting the person with parental authority for the child.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Marriage relationship certificate and family relationship certificate
A copy of your spouse's passport or residence card
The police record of a missing-person report
Messages trying to make contact after your spouse left
If there is a foreign court judgment, the original and a translation

faqs.q: Can I get a divorce by agreement with a foreign spouse?
faqs.a: A divorce by agreement (협의이혼) is possible if both spouses can appear together at the court to have their intent to divorce confirmed. However, you need to check separately how the other country recognizes a Korean divorce by agreement.

faqs.q: If I divorce through service by public notice, can matters concerning the child also be decided?
faqs.a: Yes. In a judicial divorce, the court decides the person with parental authority on its own authority and also sets matters concerning child-rearing. However, because it is hard to know the other spouse's assets, there are limits to actually receiving property division or child support.

faqs.q: How long after my spouse left home can I divorce?
faqs.a: There is no set period. It is judged by how your spouse left, how long contact has been cut off, and signs that there is no intention to continue married life. Cases where it has been unknown for more than 3 years whether the spouse is alive are set out as a separate ground for divorce.

areaPages.title: Gray Divorce and Pension Division
areaPages.summary: When a long-married couple divorces, how the home, severance pay and the National Pension or civil service pension are divided shapes life in retirement.
areaPages.cardLaw: Civil Act Article 839-2; National Pension Act Article 64
areaPages.lead: In a divorce after the children are grown, the issue is retirement income rather than child-rearing. A split National Pension is claimed from the National Pension Service separately from property division, and the amount you receive can differ depending on what you set at the time of the divorce.

seo.title: Gray Divorce in Korea: Property Division and Splitting the National Pension | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: An overview of gray divorce after a long marriage in Korea: contribution in property division, dividing severance pay and civil service pensions already being paid, the requirements for a split National Pension and the starting age by year of birth, advance claims, and how to set a different division ratio.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: We've been married over 30 years, and all our assets are in my spouse's name
My spouse is already receiving a retirement pension
I want to know whether I can receive part of the National Pension if we divorce
We've lived apart for several years, and I don't know if that counts as part of the marriage period
Our one home is all we have, and I have no idea where I'll live after the divorce

items.name: National Pension Act (국민연금법) Article 64 (Persons entitled to a split pension)
items.text: A person who was married for 5 years or more during the former spouse's coverage period (excluding periods with no real marital relationship due to separation, leaving home, etc.), who is divorced, whose former spouse is entitled to an old-age pension, and who has reached the pension age, receives a split pension equal to an equal share of the pension amount for the marriage period. It must be claimed within 5 years of meeting all the requirements.

items.name: National Pension Act Articles 64-2 and 64-3
items.text: If the division of the pension was separately set through a property division agreement or a court decision, that is followed. If you divorced before reaching the pension age, you can file an advance claim for the split pension within 3 years of the divorce.

items.name: Public Officials Pension Act (공무원연금법) Article 45 (Persons entitled to a split pension)
items.text: A person who was married for 5 years or more during the former spouse's period of service, who is divorced, whose former spouse is entitled to a retirement pension, and who has reached age 65, receives a split pension. It must be claimed within 3 years of meeting the requirements.

table.title: Age at which a split National Pension begins
rows: Born 1969 or later
table.note: Based on the supplementary provisions of the National Pension Act and the National Pension Service's guidance on split pensions (checked October 2026). It is paid only if the former spouse also qualifies for an old-age pension.

sections.title: The ratio is not set by the length of the marriage alone
body: Assets are not automatically split in half just because you were married a long time. Along with the length of the marriage, the court looks at how the assets were built and what each spouse did through housework, child-rearing, working and managing assets. If you ran the household for decades so that your spouse could work, that contribution is clearly recognized in property division (재산분할).

In a gray divorce (황혼이혼), the ability to support yourself after the divorce is also considered. Show with material your age and health, whether you can work again, and whether you have income other than a pension.

sections.title: Severance pay and pensions already being paid
body: Even if your spouse is still employed, the amount of retirement benefits they would expect to receive if they retired at the close of the final hearing on the facts in the divorce lawsuit is subject to division (Supreme Court en banc decision of July 16, 2014, 2013므2250).

If your spouse is already receiving a civil service retirement pension, that pension entitlement can also be subject to property division, and it can be divided by having a set percentage of the monthly pension paid periodically (Supreme Court en banc decision of July 16, 2014, 2012므2888).

sections.title: The National Pension is claimed separately from the National Pension Service
body: Once you meet the requirements after the divorce, you claim the split National Pension (분할연금) yourself from the National Pension Service. Periods with no real marital relationship due to separation or leaving home are excluded from the marriage period, so if you lived apart for a long time, there may be a dispute over that period.

To set a division ratio different from the equal split set by law, the settlement agreement or mediation record must use clear terms such as National Pension, old-age pension and split pension for the National Pension Service to process it at that ratio. If there is only general wording, it may not be treated as having set a separate ratio.

sections.title: If one home is everything you have
body: If the only asset is one home, you need to decide whether to sell it and split the proceeds, or have one spouse keep it and pay the other in cash. Your retirement plans take shape only once you weigh the remaining loan and where you will live after the divorce.
If assets have been moved into the name of an adult child, you need to check who the real owner is. If only the child's name was borrowed, the assets can be included in the division.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Listing retirement assets
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and puts the home, deposits, insurance, severance pay and all pensions on one page.

items.title: Checking pensions
items.desc: We check the National Pension coverage period and the marriage period, and whether a civil service or private school pension is involved, and decide how to divide them.

items.title: Designing the division method
items.desc: We choose, among cash settlement, division in kind and periodic pension payments, the method that suits your retirement.

items.title: Refining the wording of the record
items.desc: We check the wording so that the pension division in the mediation or judgment can be used as is in the National Pension Service's procedure.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Marriage relationship certificate (detailed)
Certified copy of the real estate register and the loan balance
National Pension coverage records (yours, and your spouse's if available)
Your spouse's workplace, expected retirement date, and whether they receive a pension
Material showing when the separation began

faqs.q: My spouse isn't receiving a pension yet. If we divorce now, can I still receive a share later?
faqs.a: Yes. Payment starts once your spouse becomes entitled to an old-age pension and you also reach the pension age. If you divorced before reaching the pension age, you can also file an advance claim within 3 years of the divorce.

faqs.q: If I remarry someone else while receiving a split pension, will it stop?
faqs.a: A split pension is set to be paid for as long as the recipient is alive, so it does not stop because you remarry someone else. If you remarry the same person, you can apply to give up the split pension and have the original pension restored.

faqs.q: My husband was a public official. Can I receive a share like with the National Pension?
faqs.a: The civil service pension also has a split pension system. You can receive it if the marriage lasted 5 years or more during his period of service and you have reached age 65, and you must claim it from the Government Employees Pension Service within 3 years of meeting the requirements.

areaPages.title: Nullity and Annulment of Marriage
areaPages.summary: If there was never an intention to become spouses, the marriage is void; if there was fraud, duress or a serious hidden reason, you must claim annulment within the deadline.
areaPages.lead: Even if a marriage has been reported, you can seek nullity of the marriage if there was never an intention to become spouses, or annulment if you were deceived or forced into the marriage. The results differ from divorce, and the deadline for annulment is short, so first decide which path to take.

seo.title: Nullity and Annulment of Marriage Lawsuits in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: A table-based comparison of nullity of marriage for marriage reports made without an intention to marry and sham marriages for entry into Korea, the requirements for annulment due to fraud, duress or a serious hidden reason and the 3-month and 6-month deadlines, how the effects differ from divorce, and compensation and matters concerning children.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My partner reported our marriage without my consent
My foreign spouse disappeared as soon as they entered Korea
Only after the wedding did I learn my spouse hid a previous marriage and children
I signed the marriage report because of threats
I don't know whether nullity or divorce is the better option

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 815, Item 1 (Nullity of marriage)
items.text: A marriage is void if there was no agreement to marry between the parties.

items.name: Civil Act Article 816 (Grounds for annulment of marriage)
items.text: Along with violations of the marriageable age or consent requirements and bigamy, you can ask the court to annul a marriage if, at the time of marriage, you did not know of a vicious disease or other serious reason making it impossible to continue married life, or if you married because of fraud or duress.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 822, 823 and 824
items.text: Annulment on the ground of a serious reason cannot be claimed once 6 months have passed since you learned of the reason, and annulment on the ground of fraud or duress cannot be claimed once 3 months have passed since you learned of the fraud or escaped the duress. The effect of annulment does not reach back to the past.

table.title: Nullity versus annulment of marriage
rows: Main grounds
No agreement to marry (Civil Act Article 815)
Fraud or duress, a serious hidden reason, bigamy, etc. (Civil Act Article 816)
Effect
The marriage is treated as never having existed
Dissolved going forward from when the judgment becomes final
Deadline to claim
At any time (Family Litigation Act Article 23)
3 months from learning of the fraud or escaping the duress / 6 months from learning of a serious reason
Children born in the meantime
Treated as born out of wedlock (Civil Act Article 855(1))
Keep their status as children born in wedlock
Mediation
Lawsuit without mediation
Mediation must be requested first (Family Litigation Act Article 50)
table.note: Based on the Civil Act and the Family Litigation Act (checked on the Korea Law Information Center, the government's official legislation database, October 2026).

sections.title: What 'no intention to marry' means
body: In a decision of June 10, 2010 (2010므574), the Supreme Court described an agreement to marry as a meeting of minds to form the emotional and physical union that society recognizes as a married couple. If only one side had that intention and the other reported the marriage as a means of entering Korea or getting work, the marriage is void (혼인무효) even if they agreed to the report itself.

If the other person secretly forged documents to report the marriage, there was also no agreement to marry, so you can claim nullity. On the other hand, a relationship that went bad after the wedding is not a matter of nullity but of divorce.

sections.title: If you were deceived into marriage, the deadline is short
body: Annulment of marriage (혼인취소) due to fraud becomes an issue when important facts that would have affected the decision to marry were hidden through deception. There is no duty to disclose everything in one's past, so you need to examine what was hidden and how important it was to the decision.

Annulment cannot be claimed once 3 months have passed since you learned of the fraud, or 6 months since you learned of a reason such as a serious illness. 'When you found out' becomes a point of dispute, so keep messages or records from the day you found out. If the deadline has passed, we change direction and consider divorce.

sections.title: The outcome depends on which path you choose
body: With nullity, the marriage is treated as never having existed, and the family relationship register is corrected by the judgment. With annulment, the marriage ends when the judgment becomes final, the status of children born in the meantime stays the same, and custody and visitation follow the same rules as in divorce (Civil Act Article 824-2).

You can claim damages for emotional distress from the other person responsible for the nullity or annulment (Civil Act Articles 825 and 806). If you built assets together, how to settle them also has to be examined separately to suit the case.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center proceeds

items.title: Choosing the path
items.desc: The managing partner consults with you personally and chooses among nullity, annulment and divorce the path that fits the facts and the deadlines.

items.title: Checking the deadline
items.desc: For annulment, we pin down the day you learned of the fraud or escaped the duress and calculate the time remaining.

items.title: Organizing the evidence
items.desc: We show the intention to marry or the deception through how the marriage report came about, whether you lived together, messages exchanged and statements from people around you.

items.title: Correction after the judgment
items.desc: Once the judgment is final, we guide you through the register correction or report that must be made within 1 month.

checklist.title: Documents to prepare before the consultation
items: Marriage relationship certificate (detailed)
A note on how the marriage report came to be filed
Messages exchanged before and after the wedding
When and how you learned of the hidden facts
Material showing how long you actually lived together

faqs.q: My spouse hid debts before the marriage. Can the marriage be annulled?
faqs.a: Hidden debts alone do not lead straight to annulment. The court looks at how important the debts were to the decision to marry and whether there was active deception. If annulment is difficult, we also consider pursuing grounds for divorce and compensation for emotional distress (위자료).

faqs.q: If the marriage is declared void, is the marriage record erased from the family relationship register?
faqs.a: Within 1 month of receiving the final judgment, you apply for a correction of the register to set the marriage record right (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 107). How the corrected record is shown may differ depending on the type of certificate.

faqs.q: Can I sue even if I don't know how to contact the other person?
faqs.a: Yes. If it is shown that the address cannot be found, the case proceeds by service by public notice (공시송달). For a foreign spouse, a check of immigration records is also used.

areaPages.title: Claims Against the Affair Partner
areaPages.lead: To receive compensation from your spouse's affair partner, you must show not only that the affair happened, but also that the affair partner knew your spouse had a family. Before filing the complaint, we first work out what material will prove these two points.

seo.title: Suing Your Spouse's Affair Partner in Korea: Requirements, Process, Time Limits | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What you must prove to claim compensation from your spouse's affair partner in Korea, what courts consider when setting the amount, the process from filing to judgment and enforcement, and the time limit for claims. A managing partner consults with you personally.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You have confirmed your spouse's affair and know who the other person is
You don't want a divorce but want to hold the affair partner responsible
You expect the other person to claim they didn't know your spouse was married
The two are still seeing each other even after the affair came out
The affair partner is actually sending you mocking messages
You worry whether you will actually get paid even if you win a judgment

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 750 (Tort)
items.text: A person who causes damage to another through an unlawful act, intentionally or negligently, is liable to compensate for that damage. This is the basic legal ground for a compensation claim against an affair partner.

items.name: Civil Act Article 751(1) (Compensation for non-property damage)
items.text: A person who injures another's body, liberty or reputation, or otherwise causes mental suffering, must also compensate for non-property damage, that is, compensation for emotional distress (위자료).

items.name: Civil Act Article 760(1) (Liability of joint tortfeasors)
items.text: When several people cause damage to another through a joint unlawful act, they are jointly and severally liable. The unfaithful spouse and the affair partner share liability together.

items.name: Civil Act Article 766 (Extinctive prescription of damage claims)
items.text: The claim lapses 3 years after the day the victim learned of the damage and the wrongdoer, or 10 years after the day of the unlawful act.

table.title: For the affair partner to be held liable
rows: Infidelity
That it was a relationship breaching the spouses' duty of fidelity, even if it did not go as far as sex
Chats with expressions of affection, lodging and travel records, photos taken together
Knowledge of the marriage
That the affair partner knew your spouse had a family when they saw each other
Chats mentioning your spouse's family, a profile showing a family photo, statements from acquaintances
Ongoing marriage
That the couple's shared married life was actually continuing at the time of the infidelity
Same registered address, transfers for living expenses, family event photos, childcare records
Emotional harm
That the plaintiff suffered because of the infidelity
Medical or counseling records, material showing changes in daily life
table.note: If the affair partner argues that the marriage had already broken down beyond repair at the time of the infidelity, the affair partner must prove it (Supreme Court Decision 2022므13504, 13511, rendered June 27, 2024).

sections.title: The affair alone does not win compensation
body: Legally, a compensation claim against an affair partner (상간자) is a claim for damages based on tort. The case name on the complaint (소장) is usually simply "damages." Even if your spouse's affair is clear, the court separately examines whether the affair partner acted intentionally and whether the marital relationship was actually continuing at the time.

So preparing the lawsuit begins with choosing evidence that matches the requirements the court will check. Even with several photos of the two entering a motel, the claim can be dismissed if there is no evidence that the affair partner knew of the marriage. Conversely, even without evidence of sex, infidelity (부정행위) is recognized if there are enough signs of an ongoing romantic relationship.

sections.title: You must show the affair partner knew
body: Case law does not go so far as to require people to check whether every partner they date has a spouse. So it is up to the claimant to show, with evidence, that the affair partner knew or could have known about the marriage.

The most common evidence is the conversations between the two. Mentions of your spouse's husband, wife or children, pressure to get a divorce, or remarks that contact is difficult because of a family trip all suggest knowledge of the marriage. If there are no such conversations, we gather indirect evidence, such as a messenger profile showing a family photo or a coworker's statement that the marriage was known at the workplace, and organize it by period.

sections.title: The amount is decided case by case
body: There is no fixed schedule for compensation for emotional distress (위자료). The court looks at the length of the marriage and whether there are children, the duration and extent of the infidelity, how clearly the affair partner knew of the marriage, their attitude after being found out, and the effect on the marriage. If you have already received compensation from your spouse, that amount may also be considered when assessing the total harm.

The amount claimed is set by attaching grounds to these circumstances. Records of the two continuing to meet after being found out, and messages mocking the plaintiff or demanding that the family be broken up, are grouped separately and submitted as aggravating circumstances for the amount.
bullets: Length of the marriage and childcare situation
Duration, frequency and extent of the infidelity
When and how clearly the affair partner knew of the marriage
Whether they ended the relationship or apologized after being found out
Changes in the marriage, such as separation or divorce

sections.title: First check the time limit and the other party's identity
body: A compensation claim lapses 3 years after the day you learned of the damage and the wrongdoer. Here, "learned" means not when you vaguely suspected, but when you concretely knew who the affair partner was and what kind of relationship it was. If time has passed while you were weighing a divorce, we first need to determine the starting date.

To file a complaint, you need the other party's name and address. Even if you only know a phone number, car plate number or bank account number, after filing the lawsuit their identity can be confirmed through the court's fact inquiry (사실조회) or a document production order (문서제출명령). These procedures also take time, so if little time remains, you need to move quickly.

sections.title: We plan all the way to actually getting paid
body: Even after a judgment, if the affair partner does not pay, you must seek compulsory execution against their bank deposits, salary or real estate. As a rule, one-half of a salary cannot be seized (Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 246), so you may not be able to collect everything at once.

If there is a risk the affair partner will dispose of assets, we consider a provisional attachment (가압류) before the lawsuit. Not every application for a provisional attachment is granted: you must show the need for preservation and are usually required to provide security, so we decide after first looking into the other party's financial situation.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Hearing your situation
items.desc: A managing partner personally hears how you found out about the affair and where your marriage stands now, and first checks whether the time limit for a claim is still open.

items.title: Organizing evidence by requirement
items.desc: We sort the material you have into infidelity, knowledge of the marriage and the ongoing marriage, and mark where gaps remain.

items.title: Setting the amount claimed
items.desc: We weigh the length of the marriage, the duration and extent of the infidelity, and the attitude after it came out, to set an amount with a clear basis. If there is a risk of assets being disposed of, we also consider a provisional attachment.

items.title: Filing the complaint and hearings
items.desc: We file the complaint with the evidence organized in date order. If the other party argues they didn't know or that the marriage had already broken down, we submit a rebuttal brief and further evidence.

items.title: Mediation or judgment, and enforcement
items.desc: In mediation, we decide with you whether to include a no-contact clause and a payment clause for breach. If no payment is made after judgment, we apply for compulsory execution.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Marital relationship certificate (혼인관계증명서) and resident registration certificate (주민등록등본)
Screenshots of chats between your spouse and the affair partner (keep the original chat rooms too; do not delete them)
Payment records related to lodging, travel and gifts
Whatever you know about the affair partner, such as name, phone number, workplace and car plate number
A note of the date and circumstances in which you found out about the affair
Records of any medical treatment or counseling you received

faqs.q: Can I sue without evidence of sex?
faqs.a: Yes. Case law views infidelity more broadly than adultery, covering any unfaithful conduct that breaches the spouses' duty of fidelity. Conversations of the kind exchanged between lovers, repeated one-on-one meetings and overnight stays, and travel records can together be recognized as infidelity. However, if the relationship was less intense, the amount may be set lower.

faqs.q: I don't know the affair partner's name, only their phone number.
faqs.a: You can start a lawsuit with just a phone number. After filing the complaint, the court can send a fact inquiry to the mobile carrier or issue a document production order to confirm the person's name and resident registration number; their address is then confirmed and the complaint is served. Confirmation takes time, so we check the time limit at the same time.

faqs.q: Will I get more compensation if I have psychiatric treatment records?
faqs.a: Treatment records are used to show that the emotional suffering was serious. However, the amount is not calculated so that it rises with the number of visits; it is judged together with the other circumstances. Before submitting the records, we first check that they do not contain sensitive information unrelated to the case.

faqs.q: We are in a de facto marriage. Can I claim against the affair partner?
faqs.a: A de facto spouse (사실혼 배우자) can also claim compensation from the affair partner. However, because the marriage was not registered, you need to show more carefully that you actually lived together as a married couple and that the affair partner knew this. Your shared address, visits between both families, and signs that you introduced each other as spouses can serve as evidence.

faqs.q: What happens if the two keep seeing each other during the lawsuit?
faqs.a: The fact that the relationship continued during the lawsuit can be seen as a lack of remorse and reflected in the amount. For newly confirmed meetings, write down the dates and places, gather the evidence, and submit it additionally. Even then, it is safer to respond through your legal representative than to confront them in person.

areaPages.areaName: Organizing and Preserving Evidence of Infidelity
areaPages.title: Organizing & Preserving Evidence of Infidelity
areaPages.lead: The outcome of an affair lawsuit depends heavily on what evidence you have and how you obtained it. If it was collected unlawfully, you may be unable to use it or may even be punished, so check the method before you act.

seo.title: Gathering Evidence for an Affair Lawsuit in Korea & CCTV Preservation | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: The types of evidence used in affair lawsuits in Korea, where the line between lawful and unlawful collection lies, how to secure material that will soon be erased (such as motel CCTV) through court evidence preservation, and how to organize evidence in time order. Message us through the chat on this page.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You saw suspicious chats on your spouse's phone and don't know how to keep a record of them
You saw the two enter a motel together but couldn't take a photo
You asked a lodging business to show you its CCTV and were refused
You are wondering whether to hire a private investigator
You already have a recording and don't know whether you can use it
Your materials are scattered everywhere and you don't know what matters

items.name: Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 375 (Requirements for preservation of evidence)
items.text: If it is recognized that evidence would be difficult to use unless examined in advance, the court may, on a party's application, examine it even before a lawsuit is filed.

items.name: Civil Procedure Act Article 376 (Jurisdiction for preservation of evidence)
items.text: Before a lawsuit is filed, the application goes to the district court with jurisdiction over the residence of the person holding the document or the place where the object to be inspected is located; after filing, it goes to the court of the instance in which the evidence will be used.

items.name: Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법) Articles 3, 14 and 16
items.text: No one may record or listen in on a private conversation between other people. Violators face 1 to 10 years' imprisonment and suspension of qualifications for up to 5 years. Content obtained this way cannot be used as evidence in court (Article 4 and Article 14(2) of the same Act).

items.name: Location Information Act (위치정보법) Articles 15(1) and 40
items.text: Collecting or using a person's location information without that person's consent is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million.

table.title: Common evidence and what to watch for when obtaining it
rows: Messenger chats and text messages
The nature of the relationship, knowledge of the marriage, how long it lasted
If obtained by secretly opening your spouse's phone, first review how it was obtained
Recordings of conversations or calls you took part in
Your spouse or the affair partner admitting the facts
Allowed only when you are a party to the conversation. Recording conversations between other people is prohibited
Photos, videos, dashcam footage
The place and time they were together
Focus on public social media posts and your own car's dashcam
Card and lodging payment records
How often and where they met
Without your spouse's cooperation, consider obtaining them through court procedures after filing
CCTV at lodging businesses or buildings
That they entered, and whether they were together
Apply for evidence preservation before it is overwritten
Written statements from people around you
What someone who knew of the relationship saw or heard
Keep a record of how the statement was written and prepare a copy of the writer's ID
table.note: Whether evidence is admitted and how much weight it is given is decided by the court in each case. For material you already have, review how it was collected before submitting it.

sections.title: Evidence gains strength when pieces are linked
body: In affair cases, a single decisive photo is rare. The court puts chats, payment records, movement records and statements side by side to judge when the relationship began and how long it continued. So once the material is collected, we build one table in date order and check where the gaps are.

Material is sorted by three questions: Were the two in a romantic relationship? Did the affair partner know about the marriage? Were you and your spouse living together at the time? In actual consultations, evidence is often concentrated on the first question while the other two are left empty.

sections.title: Where lawful ends and unlawful begins
body: Recording a conversation you take part in is not a violation of the Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법), even without the other person's consent. A recording made while discussing the affair with your spouse, or while on the phone with the affair partner, can be submitted as evidence. On the other hand, placing a recorder in your spouse's car or room to record the two of them is recording a conversation between other people: it is punishable and cannot be used in court.

Secretly installing a location-tracking app or GPS device, breaking into your spouse's account with their password, or entering the affair partner's home to film can also lead to problems under the Location Information Act (위치정보법), the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) or trespass laws. Unlawfully gathered material can also give the other side grounds to file a counter-complaint or to argue for reduced compensation.
bullets: Acceptable: recordings of conversations and calls you took part in, screenshots of public social media, your own car's dashcam, material your spouse showed you voluntarily
Avoid: secretly accessing your spouse's phone or accounts, recording conversations between other people, installing tracking devices, entering the other person's home

sections.title: CCTV that will soon be erased is secured through evidence preservation
body: CCTV at lodging businesses or buildings is often overwritten after a certain period, and businesses usually refuse to show footage, citing personal data. In that case, even before filing a lawsuit, you can apply to the court for evidence preservation (증거보전) and obtain a decision ordering the business to submit the footage to the court.

The application must state the other party, the facts to be proved, the evidence to be preserved and the reason for preservation, and you must make a prima facie showing of that reason (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 377). The more narrowly you specify the place, date and time of the recording, the more likely the application will be granted. You can apply even without knowing the affair partner's name, but if the dates in the application don't match the dates in the material, the court will ask for corrections, so it must be accurate from the start.

sections.title: What to check before hiring a private investigator
body: Many people turn to private investigation agencies to gather evidence of an affair. Getting a report on what was observed in public places and following someone to track their location or secretly recording conversations are viewed completely differently under the law. If the agency uses unlawful methods, not only can the results not be used, but the client can also get into trouble.

Before hiring anyone, first check what the material you have now proves and what is missing. If the gaps can be filled through a court fact inquiry (사실조회) or evidence preservation, there may be no need to hire an investigator at all.

sections.title: Leave the originals as they are
body: If you keep only screenshots and delete the original chat room, it becomes hard to respond when the other side claims they were edited or fabricated. Leave the chat room as it is, and save screenshots so the other person's name and the date appear together. Do not edit recordings; prepare the original file together with a transcript.
Also avoid telling the other side in advance that you have evidence. It gives the affair partner time to delete chats or get their story straight with your spouse.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles evidence

items.title: Reviewing your material
items.desc: A managing partner personally looks at the material you have now and first checks that there is no problem with how it was obtained.

items.title: Sorting by requirement
items.desc: We sort it into infidelity, knowledge of the marriage and the ongoing marriage, build a table in date order, and mark the periods where evidence is missing.

items.title: Evidence preservation and fact inquiries
items.desc: For CCTV at risk of being erased, we apply for evidence preservation; the other party's identity and communications records are obtained after filing, through fact inquiries and document production orders.

items.title: Preparing the evidence explanation
items.desc: We submit each item to the court with an explanation of what it proves. We also check the source of the other side's evidence and whether it has been edited.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Your phone with the screenshots and the original chat rooms still on it
The original, unedited recording files
A note of the suspected dates, places and times
Card statements and lodging or transport payment records
The memory card holding the dashcam footage
Names and contact details of anyone who saw what happened with you

faqs.q: How long until CCTV footage is erased?
faqs.a: It varies, because each business has different storage capacity and settings. Some places overwrite footage within a few days, so you should get a consultation as soon as you learn the date they went in. The evidence preservation application must state the place, date and time precisely, so bring your memories of that day along with any records.

faqs.q: Can I submit a private investigator's report as evidence?
faqs.a: If it reflects lawful observation in public places, it can be submitted together with other material. If it is the result of secretly tracking someone's location or recording conversations, it is hard to use as evidence and may cause criminal problems. Before you receive a report, confirm how the investigation was carried out.

faqs.q: My spouse wrote a statement admitting the affair. Does that help?
faqs.a: A pledge or statement of facts written by your spouse is important evidence that the infidelity happened. However, the affair partner may argue your spouse made it up alone, so the more specific it is about when and where they met and the affair partner's knowledge of the marriage, the better. Also keep a record of how it was written, so no one can say it was obtained under pressure.

faqs.q: Can I take screenshots of the affair partner's social media?
faqs.a: Capturing posts that are open to the public is usually not a problem. Entering a private account with someone else's account, or logging in after finding out the password, can violate the Information and Communications Network Act. When you take screenshots, make sure the posting date and the account name are visible.

faqs.q: Can I get call records through the court?
faqs.a: While a lawsuit is pending, you can apply to the court for a document production order or a fact inquiry to obtain communication confirmation data, such as call dates and times, from the mobile carrier. The court must accept that it is necessary, and the content of the calls cannot be obtained. Narrow the period you need when applying.

areaPages.title: Defending an Affair Lawsuit (Defendant)
areaPages.lead: Receiving an affair complaint does not mean you have to pay the amount claimed as it stands. If you separately examine whether you knew the other person was married, whether their marriage was still alive at the time, and whether the plaintiff's account matches the facts, the points you can contest become clear.

seo.title: Sued by Your Partner's Spouse in Korea? Defending an Affair Lawsuit | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What a defendant in a Korean affair lawsuit should check before filing an answer, when the arguments "I didn't know they were married" and "the marriage had already broken down" are accepted, how to respond when the plaintiff's account is untrue, what not to do, and what to prepare.
keywords: didn't know he was married Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You received an affair complaint from the court and don't understand what it says
When you met, you were told they were single or divorced
You believed them when they said they were separated and about to divorce
You were named as the affair partner when you are only a coworker
The period and nature of the relationship the plaintiff alleges differ from the facts
The other person's spouse keeps calling and threatening to tell your workplace

items.name: Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 256(1) (Duty to file an answer)
items.text: To contest the plaintiff's claim, the defendant must file an answer within 30 days of being served with the copy of the complaint. Service by publication is an exception.

items.name: Civil Procedure Act Article 257(1) (Judgment without hearing)
items.text: If no answer is filed, the court may treat the facts in the claim as admitted and rule without a hearing. This does not apply if an answer contesting the claim is filed before the judgment is delivered.

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 750 (Tort)
items.text: Tort liability requires intent or negligence. If you did not know, and could not have known, that the other person was married, liability may be denied.

table.title: Points the defendant can raise
rows: There was no infidelity
We were friends or coworkers, not in a romantic relationship
The overall flow of the conversations, evidence that meetings involved several people
I didn't know they were married
The other person lied about being single or divorced
Messages introducing themselves as single or divorced, records of ending the relationship right after finding out
The marriage had already broken down
The couple's shared married life had ended, for example through long-term separation before the relationship began
Evidence of when the separation began, records of divorce proceedings, signs that living expenses and childcare had stopped
The amount claimed is excessive
Liability is admitted, but the amount is large for the duration and extent
A short relationship, when it was ended, records of an apology
table.note: The defendant must prove that the marriage had already broken down (Supreme Court Decision 2022므13504, 13511, rendered June 27, 2024). A bare assertion will not be accepted.

sections.title: Read the complaint carefully before writing your answer
body: The complaint (소장) contains the relief sought, which states the amount claimed, and the cause of action, which sets out the facts the plaintiff alleges. Mark each point: the period of infidelity the plaintiff alleges, what evidence is attached, and the grounds for saying you knew of the marriage.

The amount in the complaint is only what the plaintiff wants; it is not an amount set by the court. However, if you do not file an answer (답변서), judgment may be entered for that exact amount, so first calculate the 30-day deadline from the day you were served.

sections.title: "I didn't know" must be shown with evidence
body: Knowledge of the marriage is, in principle, for the plaintiff to prove. Even so, in actual trials, the more concretely the defendant shows how they came not to know, the easier it is to persuade the court. The court wants to confirm three things: what words and actions deceived you, when you learned of the marriage, and how you acted after learning of it.

Key evidence includes messages in which the other person introduced themselves as single or divorced, conversations in which you asked whether they were married, and records showing you cut off contact right after learning the truth. If you kept meeting after finding out, liability may be recognized for the period after that, so check unfavorable records in advance as well.
bullets: Chats or recordings in which they introduced themselves as single or divorced
Evidence that, during the relationship, the other person lived as if they lived alone
The day you learned of the marriage and how
Messages cutting off contact or protesting right after that

sections.title: When "they were separated" works and when it doesn't
body: If the couple had been separated for a long time, so that their shared married life no longer existed in substance and was objectively beyond repair, a relationship after that point is not a tort. The test is not whether a divorce lawsuit was pending, but whether the breakdown had already become settled before that.

A marital quarrel or a brief period apart is not enough. If, even while separated, your partner kept sending living expenses, cared for the children together with their spouse, and attended family events with them, the breakdown argument is unlikely to be accepted. We organize evidence on when and why the separation began, whether living expenses and childcare stopped, and whether there are records of divorce being discussed.

sections.title: When the plaintiff's account is not true
body: Sometimes people are sued through a misunderstanding when they were actually only coworkers or friends. If you don't respond, the plaintiff's account may be accepted as it stands, so we submit the entire conversation in time order to show the nature of the relationship.

In other cases, the two did meet, but the plaintiff exaggerates the period or claims that payment records from other days are also connected to the defendant. We check whether the date and place of each piece of the plaintiff's evidence match the facts, and rebut the inconsistencies in a separate table.

sections.title: What not to write in your answer
body: Out of a sense of injustice, some defendants write at length about the plaintiff couple's private life or the plaintiff's faults. Accusations that the other person's spouse approached first, or that the plaintiff neglected the family, can look like shifting blame and may actually hurt you. The answer should be written around the facts and the law.

Claiming you didn't know when you actually did is also dangerous. If contrary evidence comes out, your other arguments become hard to believe too. In some cases, it is better to admit what should be admitted and put your weight behind the grounds for a reduction.

factors.title: Circumstances affecting liability and the amount
plus: Records of continuing to meet after learning of the marriage
Chats mentioning the spouse's family or pressing for a divorce
A long relationship with repeated cohabitation or travel
Contacting the plaintiff directly or blaming the plaintiff during the lawsuit
minus: Evidence that the other person lied about being single or divorced
Records of ending the relationship right after learning of the marriage
Objective evidence of long-term separation before the relationship began
A short relationship that has already ended
A written apology and a promise not to make contact again

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center builds your defense

items.title: Analyzing the complaint
items.desc: A managing partner personally reads the complaint and the attached evidence and separates the plaintiff's claims into what is true, what is untrue and what is exaggerated.

items.title: Building a timeline
items.desc: We fix the dates when the relationship began, when you learned of the marriage and when the relationship ended, and attach the evidence for each point.

items.title: Filing the answer
items.desc: Within the deadline, we decide whether to seek dismissal of the claim or to admit part of the liability and seek a reduction, and file the answer accordingly.

items.title: Hearings and mediation
items.desc: We submit rebuttal evidence against the plaintiff's witnesses or additional evidence, and in mediation we negotiate the amount along with confidentiality and no-further-claims clauses.

items.title: Resolving remaining issues
items.desc: If the plaintiff's side tells your workplace or threatens you, we consider a separate response, and after the compensation is paid we also look at reimbursement.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The complaint you received and the date you were served
All chats with the other person's spouse (keep them; do not delete them)
Records of the other person saying they were single or divorced
Chats or notes from the day you learned of the marriage
The date you ended the relationship and messages from around that time
Records of contact from the plaintiff or the plaintiff's side

faqs.q: The plaintiff contacted me before I received the complaint. Should I reply?
faqs.a: Messages in which you explain yourself or apologize directly to the plaintiff can be submitted as evidence just as they are. Words said in an emotional phone call are sometimes used as an admission that you knew about the marriage. If a reply is needed, it is safer to decide what to say first and send it through your legal representative.

faqs.q: I've been named as Defendant 2 in the other person's divorce lawsuit.
faqs.a: This means a compensation claim against the affair partner was filed together with the divorce lawsuit. If you don't respond because it's someone else's divorce, judgment may be entered as the plaintiff claims, so you must file your own answer. Which of the spouse and the affair partner led the relationship more actively is also a factor in dividing liability.

faqs.q: I keep getting messages saying they will tell my workplace.
faqs.a: Separately from the lawsuit, spreading the facts to your workplace or acquaintances can be defamation (명예훼손), and threatening to tell while demanding money can raise issues of threats (협박) or extortion (공갈). Do not delete the texts and call records you receive; keep them by date. Another option is to settle this with a confidentiality clause in mediation.

faqs.q: What if I can't finish the answer within 30 days?
faqs.a: You can first file an answer within the deadline stating that you contest the claim, and add specific arguments and evidence later in a brief (준비서면). As a rule, if you file an answer contesting the claim before judgment is delivered, the court will not rule without a hearing, but schedule things so that you don't miss the deadline.

faqs.q: Do I have to appear in court in person?
faqs.a: If you appoint a lawyer, your representative appears, so you may not have to face the plaintiff in court. However, the court sometimes wants to hear from you directly or requires you to attend a mediation session in person. We will let you know in advance about any hearing you need to attend.

areaPages.areaName: Reducing Compensation and Reviewing Reimbursement Claims
areaPages.title: Reducing Compensation & Reimbursement Claims
areaPages.lead: Even if you admit the infidelity, you can still contest the amount of compensation. After paying the compensation, you also need to look at whether you can seek reimbursement of their share from the other person's spouse, who should bear liability with you.

seo.title: Reducing Affair Compensation & Reimbursement Claims in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What affects a reduction of compensation in a Korean affair lawsuit, when the plaintiff's own conduct lowers the amount, how the right to reimbursement between joint tortfeasors works, why a plaintiff who stays married includes a waiver of reimbursement, and the deadline for appeal.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You did see the person, but the amount claimed is far too high
The relationship was short and you have already ended it
You paid all of the compensation yourself, while the other person's spouse bore no responsibility at all
You sued without divorcing and worry the affair partner will claim reimbursement from your husband
You think the first-instance award is excessive and are considering an appeal

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 760(1) (Liability of joint tortfeasors)
items.text: People who cause damage through a joint unlawful act are jointly and severally liable to the victim. Among those jointly liable, each person's share is determined, and this leads to the question of the right to reimbursement (구상권).

items.name: Civil Act Article 751 (Compensation for non-property damage)
items.text: Compensation for emotional distress (위자료) is also recoverable. The court sets the amount by considering all the circumstances that appear in the proceedings.

items.name: Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 396 (Period for appeal)
items.text: An appeal must be filed within 2 weeks of the day the written judgment is served. This is a peremptory period and cannot be extended.

table.title: When reimbursement becomes an issue
rows: The plaintiff divorces and sues both the spouse and the affair partner
The judgment often sets the joint liability of both
Check the operative part of the judgment and sort out the actual scope of payment
The plaintiff stays married and sues only the affair partner
After paying, the affair partner can claim their share from the plaintiff's spouse
For the plaintiff, consider adding a waiver of reimbursement in mediation or settlement
The affair partner pays all of the compensation
The issue is whether the amount paid beyond their own share can be recovered from the spouse
Payment records, the judgment or mediation terms, evidence that the spouse led the relationship
The settlement agreement includes a waiver of reimbursement
As a rule, it is hard to claim again
Before signing, confirm in writing the scope of what is being waived
table.note: The reimbursement ratio is not set by law; it is decided case by case by weighing the degree of responsibility of the two.

sections.title: A reduction means arguing the amount is excessive
body: If you knew they were married when you met, it is hard to avoid liability itself. In that case, the approach is to show with evidence that the amount the plaintiff claims is too large for the circumstances of the case. The court looks at the length of the relationship, how often you met and how deep the relationship was, the effect on the marriage, and your attitude afterward.

If the relationship was short and you cut off contact right after it came out, records showing that date are the most important. The fact that the plaintiff couple had long-standing conflict before the affair may also be considered, but using it to blame the plaintiff backfires, so it should be handled only with objective evidence.
bullets: The length of the relationship and how many times you actually met
The date you ended the relationship and the fact there has been no contact since
Objective evidence of the plaintiff couple's conflict before the affair
A written apology delivered to the plaintiff
A promise not to make contact again

sections.title: The plaintiff's own conduct can lower the amount
body: If the plaintiff took private revenge, such as causing a scene at the affair partner's workplace or posting the facts on social media, the suffering this caused the defendant may be considered when setting compensation. If the plaintiff is separately accused of defamation (명예훼손) or threats (협박), the case becomes more complicated.

Plaintiffs should also be careful about saying themselves that their marriage ended long ago. The affair partner will use those words to argue that the marriage had already broken down. Records of the plaintiff sending the affair partner sympathetic messages, such as "You must have been deceived too," are sometimes used against the plaintiff when the amount is set.

sections.title: The spouse and the affair partner share liability
body: Infidelity (부정행위) is a tort committed jointly by the spouse and the affair partner. The two are jointly and severally liable to the plaintiff, and between themselves each has a share. If one pays more than their own share, they can claim the excess from the other; this is called the right to reimbursement.

If the affair partner paid all of the compensation, we look at whether they can claim reimbursement from the plaintiff's spouse. However, if the court views the compensation it awarded as falling within the affair partner's own share from the start, reimbursement may not be accepted. The terms of the judgment or mediation and how much the spouse led the relationship must be looked at together.

sections.title: Why reimbursement matters for a plaintiff who stays married
body: If you sue only the affair partner without divorcing, and the affair partner then claims reimbursement from your spouse after paying, that money ultimately comes out of your own household. In effect, you hand back part of the compensation you received.

A judgment only decides whether to award compensation and how much; it does not settle the reimbursement issue. So a plaintiff who stays married should consider including, when ending the case through mediation or settlement, a clause that the affair partner will not claim reimbursement or any other money from the spouse. Getting this clause sometimes requires a concession on the amount, so the amount and the clause are decided together.

sections.title: Contesting the amount on appeal
body: If you think the first-instance award is excessive, you must appeal within 2 weeks of being served with the written judgment. On appeal, we go through the reasons in the judgment one by one to see what circumstances the first instance relied on to set the amount, and fill in missing circumstances or wrongly found facts with new evidence.

If the first instance proceeded by service by publication (공시송달) and you didn't even know a judgment had been entered, we look at whether you can file a late appeal (추후보완 항소) within 2 weeks of the day you learned of it (Civil Procedure Act Article 173). The period is short here as well, so you need to move quickly.

factors.title: Circumstances that decide whether the amount is reduced
plus: A long relationship with repeated cohabitation or travel
Continuing the relationship after it came out
Records of mocking the plaintiff or demanding that the family be broken up
Contacting the plaintiff directly during the lawsuit
minus: A short relationship that has already ended
Evidence that the other person's spouse led the relationship
Objective evidence of deep conflict in the plaintiff's marriage before the affair
Harm suffered from the plaintiff's public exposure or workplace visits
A written apology and a promise not to make contact again

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center reviews your case

items.title: Analyzing the basis of the claim
items.desc: A managing partner finds in the complaint the basis on which the plaintiff set the amount and checks, point by point, whether it matches the facts.

items.title: Organizing grounds for reduction
items.desc: We gather evidence that affects the amount, such as the length of the relationship, when it ended and the plaintiff couple's circumstances, and organize it in a table.

items.title: Mediation negotiations
items.desc: If mediation is better than a judgment for the case, we negotiate the amount, payment method, confidentiality and a no-further-claims clause together.

items.title: Assessing reimbursement
items.desc: After the compensation is paid, we look at the terms of the judgment or mediation and the spouse's degree of involvement, and judge whether a reimbursement claim is worthwhile.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The complaint or first-instance judgment, and the date you were served
Chats showing the beginning and end of the relationship
Evidence that there has been no contact since the relationship ended
Records of public exposure or contact with your workplace by the plaintiff's side (if any)
Transfer records of compensation payments (if considering reimbursement)
Any mediation record or settlement agreement already signed

faqs.q: How much can I get back through reimbursement?
faqs.a: There is no ratio set by law. The court determines each person's share by weighing what role the spouse and the affair partner each played in the relationship and who was more active. If the court views the compensation the affair partner paid as their own share from the start, reimbursement may not be recognized.

faqs.q: I wrote in the settlement agreement that I waive reimbursement. Can I still claim it later?
faqs.a: As a rule, a right you waived yourself is hard to exercise again. However, if the scope of the waiver is unclear from the wording, or another term that formed the basis of the agreement was not honored, there may be room to argue. It has to be judged by looking at the whole agreement.

faqs.q: If the plaintiff also had an affair, will the amount be reduced?
faqs.a: The fact that the plaintiff also bears responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage can be considered when setting the amount. The Supreme Court has held that when the responsibility of both spouses is equal and the compensation claim against the spouse is dismissed, a third party who took part in the infidelity cannot be held liable for damages on the ground of the divorce either (Supreme Court Decision 2023므16678, rendered June 27, 2024). That ruling concerns a case that ended in divorce, so the structure of your case must be checked first.

faqs.q: Doesn't writing an apology mean admitting fault?
faqs.a: In a case where you contest the infidelity itself, be careful with an apology letter. On the other hand, in a case where you admit liability and contest the amount, a sincere apology can be considered as a ground for reduction. We first decide on the direction of your response, then review the wording together.

faqs.q: Can I pay the compensation in installments?
faqs.a: A judgment usually orders payment in a lump sum, so if you want installments, they must be agreed through mediation or settlement. Installment terms often include a clause that if even one payment is late, the remaining balance becomes due at once, so make sure the schedule is one you can manage.

areaPages.title: Certified Letters & Settlement Agreements
areaPages.lead: If you want to resolve the matter without a lawsuit, a certified letter and a settlement agreement are the tools for it. Once signed, a settlement agreement is hard to change, so look at the wording before the amount.

seo.title: Affair Settlement Agreements & Certified Letters in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to include and what to avoid in a certified letter to your spouse's affair partner in Korea; the payment, no-contact, confidentiality, reimbursement and further-claims clauses in a settlement agreement; the difference between liquidated damages and a penalty for breach; and how to secure performance if the agreement is broken.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: A lawsuit feels like too much, and you want to give a warning by certified letter first
The affair partner contacted you first, proposing a settlement
The other side wants you to sign a draft settlement agreement they sent
The two are seeing each other again even after the settlement
The settlement money has not arrived by the agreed date
You would rather settle quietly than have a written judgment on record

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 398 (Predetermined damages)
