items.text: An agreed breach payment (위약금) is presumed to be liquidated damages (손해배상액의 예정) (paragraph 4), and if the predetermined amount is unreasonably excessive, the court may reduce it appropriately (paragraph 2).

items.name: Civil Mediation Act (민사조정법) Article 29; Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 59(2)
items.text: A mediation reached in court has the same effect as a judicial settlement, so compulsory execution can be carried out on the basis of the mediation record (조정조서).

items.name: Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 56, item 4
items.text: A notarial deed (공정증서) drawn up by a notary for payment of a fixed sum of money, stating that the debtor consents to compulsory execution, serves as a basis for compulsory execution even without a judgment.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 307(1) (Defamation)
items.text: A person who damages another's reputation by publicly alleging facts faces up to 2 years' imprisonment with or without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 5 million. This is why you should avoid sending a certified letter to someone's workplace or family.

table.title: Clauses to include in a settlement agreement
rows: Payment of compensation
Amount, due date, bank account, whether in installments, what happens if payment is late
Hard to collect promptly even after the deadline passes
Period covered
Up to what date the infidelity is being settled
Disputes over whether conduct after the settlement is also released
No further contact
Scope of the ban, such as calls, texts, social media and contact through others, and work-related exceptions
Renewed disputes over what counts as a breach
Payment on breach
Amount per breach and its nature (penalty for breach or liquidated damages)
Arguments for reduction or disputes over validity
Confidentiality
Who must not be told of the settlement and its terms, and exceptions such as submission to a court or investigators
Even unavoidable submissions could count as a breach
Reimbursement and further claims
Waiver of reimbursement claims against the spouse, and the scope of no further claims over this matter
Reimbursement suits or further lawsuits after the settlement
table.note: A settlement agreement signed only between the parties cannot be enforced directly, so if it has installment or breach-payment clauses, we also consider recording it in a notarial deed or a court mediation record.

sections.title: A certified letter is both a warning and a record
body: A certified letter (내용증명) is mail for which the post office certifies what document was sent, when and to whom. It does not by itself oblige the other person to reply or pay, but it formally puts on record that you know about the infidelity (부정행위) and intend to pursue legal liability. It is not unusual for the other person, now taking the prospect of a lawsuit seriously, to get in touch about a settlement.

The certified letter states that a marriage exists, the infidelity you have confirmed, your demands and a deadline for a reply. You don't need to reveal all your evidence. If you describe the types of evidence in detail, the other side can prepare its counterarguments in advance.

sections.title: What to avoid before sending
body: Avoid sending a certified letter to the person's workplace or parents' home, or including wording such as "If you don't comply, I will tell your company." Even if what you write is true, defamation (명예훼손) can become an issue once several people learn of it, and threatening to tell while demanding money can escalate into accusations of threats (협박) or extortion (공갈).

Insults or exaggerated wording will also be submitted by the other side as evidence in a lawsuit. Some affair partners who receive a certified letter say they will end the relationship and then delete their chats, so secure the evidence you need before sending.

sections.title: The wording decides what a settlement agreement means
body: If the agreement simply says no objections of any kind will be raised in future, a court may read it as a promise covering conduct up to the date the agreement was signed. That means meeting again after the settlement can be pursued separately as new infidelity. So write down the date up to which conduct is being settled, and make clear how conduct after that date will be handled.

A no-contact clause must specify the methods of contact that are prohibited. If the two work at the same place and cannot avoid seeing each other for work, set that exception in advance as well. If the scope is vague, you will end up arguing again over whether something is a breach.

sections.title: A breach payment and a penalty for breach are treated differently
body: In a clause stating that a certain sum will be paid if the promise is broken, if that sum is simply called a breach payment (위약금), the law presumes it to be liquidated damages (손해배상액의 예정). The court can reduce liquidated damages if they are unreasonably excessive. To make it a sanction for the breach itself, the wording must make clear that it is a penalty for breach (위약벌).

It is realistic to set the amount within what the other person can actually afford. An excessively large amount makes a settlement itself harder and can also give grounds to dispute its validity later.

sections.title: Prepare for the agreement not being kept
body: A settlement agreement signed only between the parties cannot be enforced directly, so if the money doesn't arrive, you have to go through a lawsuit or a payment order again. If there are installment or breach-payment clauses, consider making it a notarial deed (공정증서) with consent to compulsory execution or, if a lawsuit is pending, recording it in a court mediation record (조정조서).

Compared with a judgment, a settlement takes less time and can include terms that a judgment cannot set, such as no further contact, confidentiality and a waiver of reimbursement (구상권). On the other hand, not having a written judgment on record can be a drawback, so decide first what matters more to you and then choose the direction.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Deciding the result you want
items.desc: A managing partner first asks which matters most to you, the amount, ending the relationship or confidentiality, and sets the direction.

items.title: Sending after securing evidence
items.desc: After securing the evidence needed, we draft a certified letter in the lawyer's name and send it to the other person directly. We do not use methods that inform their workplace or family.

items.title: Negotiation
items.desc: Jisan Law, as your representative, negotiates the terms with the other person or their representative. You do not need to meet the affair partner yourself.

items.title: Drafting the settlement agreement
items.desc: We draft the payment, no-contact, breach payment, confidentiality, reimbursement and further-claims clauses, reviewing the wording line by line.

items.title: Securing performance
items.desc: If there are installment or breach clauses, we consider a notarial deed or mediation record; if payment is late, we move on to enforcement procedures.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The affair partner's name and address (if unknown, everything you do know)
Evidence showing the infidelity
Any settlement proposal or draft agreement the other side sent
Your thoughts on the amount and how it should be paid
Circumstances requiring exceptions to the no-contact clause (such as working at the same place)
Certified letters or messages already exchanged

faqs.q: I sent a certified letter, but there's been no reply.
faqs.a: A certified letter cannot force a reply. If there is still no answer after the reply deadline, we decide whether to move on to a lawsuit or a provisional attachment (가압류). The certified letter you sent can be submitted in the lawsuit as evidence of when you made what demands.

faqs.q: I don't know the affair partner's address, so I can't send a certified letter.
faqs.a: If the address is unknown, a lawyer can contact the person by phone and deliver a written notice with the same content. If no agreement is reached, after filing a lawsuit, their identity and address are confirmed through court procedures. Since this takes time, we also check the time limit for your claim.

faqs.q: The two met again after the settlement. Can I claim again?
faqs.a: Meeting after the settlement can be treated as new infidelity, so you can claim compensation separately, and if there is a payment-on-breach clause, you can claim that amount too. However, if the marriage is found to have already broken down in the meantime, liability may not be recognized, so you need evidence showing the state of the marriage.

faqs.q: Can I also get a written apology from the affair partner?
faqs.a: A written apology is sometimes made a condition of settlement. A judgment cannot compel an apology, so this is a term that can only be set by agreement. How the apology is kept and who it may be shown to should be decided together with the confidentiality clause.

faqs.q: What changes if the settlement agreement is notarized?
faqs.a: A notarial deed that contains a promise to pay money and states that the debtor consents to compulsory execution serves as a basis for compulsory execution even without a judgment. That is why it is often used for settlements that take time to perform, such as installment payments. Note that non-monetary promises, such as no further contact, cannot be enforced directly this way.

areaPages.title: Combining with a Divorce Lawsuit
areaPages.lead: If you have decided to divorce, you can bring your case against both your spouse and the affair partner together in the family court. Combining them is not always to your advantage, though, so the order and approach depend on your evidence and the result you want.

seo.title: Divorce Lawsuit and Affair Lawsuit Together in Korea: Court & Order | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: Which court hears a divorce lawsuit combined with a compensation claim against the affair partner in Korea, the requirements and order for joining them, the Supreme Court ruling that a claim against the affair partner also fails when both spouses are equally at fault, and how to keep your statements consistent in both cases.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You are divorcing your spouse and also want to hold the affair partner responsible
You filed an affair lawsuit first and decided on a divorce while it was in progress
You are in the middle of a divorce lawsuit and your spouse is seeing someone else
You found out about the affair after completing a divorce by agreement
The affair partner lives in another region and you don't know which court to file in

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 2(1)(i)(c)(2)
items.text: A claim for damages on the ground of divorce, including a claim against a third party, is a Category C family litigation case (다류 가사소송사건) within the exclusive jurisdiction of the family court.

items.name: Family Litigation Act Article 14 (Joinder of related cases)
items.text: Several family litigation cases whose claims are based on the same facts can be brought in a single lawsuit, and if they fall under different courts, they can be filed together in a family court that has jurisdiction over one of the claims.

items.name: Family Litigation Act Article 50 (Mediation first)
items.text: For Category B and Category C family litigation cases, mediation must be applied for first; if a lawsuit is filed without applying for mediation, the court as a rule refers the case to mediation.

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 840, item 1 (Grounds for judicial divorce)
items.text: If a spouse has committed an unchaste act, the other spouse can file for divorce with the family court.

table.title: Which court, depending on the approach
rows: Staying married and claiming only against the affair partner
Civil court (district court)
Claims emotional harm caused by the infidelity
Claiming against the spouse and affair partner together with a judicial divorce
Family court
One complaint naming the spouse as Defendant 1 and the affair partner as Defendant 2
Reaching divorce during an affair lawsuit and changing the cause of action
The case may be transferred to the family court
The test is whether the cause of action was changed to seek damages for the divorce as well
Claiming against the affair partner after completing a divorce by agreement
Depends on what is claimed
The court is decided by whether the claim is for harm from the infidelity itself or harm from the divorce it led to
table.note: The exact court depends on the parties' addresses and the progress of the case, so we confirm it before filing the complaint.

sections.title: First decide whether to combine or file separately
body: If the divorce lawsuit and the lawsuit against the affair partner are joined, the same panel of judges examines the same facts at once. The spouse's and the affair partner's liability are judged on the same evidence, which lowers the risk of conflicting conclusions, and witness examinations and fact inquiries can be done once.

On the other hand, a divorce case also involves division of property and child custody, so it tends to take longer. If you want to resolve the affair partner issue first, or haven't decided yet whether to divorce, you can file the lawsuit against the affair partner in a civil court first. If your evidence is thin, we also consider pursuing the divorce first and using material obtained in that process.

sections.title: If both spouses are equally at fault, the claim against the affair partner can fail too
body: The Supreme Court has held that when a compensation claim (위자료) against the spouse is dismissed because both spouses are equally responsible for the breakdown of the marriage, a third party who took part in the infidelity cannot be held liable for damages on the ground of the divorce either (Supreme Court Decision 2023므16678, rendered June 27, 2024). The reason is that divorce compensation is liability for the breakdown of the marriage, not for an individual act of infidelity (부정행위).

So when claiming against the affair partner together with a divorce, you must be prepared for your spouse to file a counterclaim (반소) alleging your own faults. If there are circumstances on your side that could be disputed, we carefully decide first what kind of harm the claim should be framed around.

sections.title: A relationship that began during the divorce lawsuit is viewed separately
body: If the affair began before the divorce lawsuit, we additionally submit the fact that the two kept meeting during the lawsuit so it is reflected in the compensation. This can be viewed as continuing the relationship despite knowing it was wrong.

It is different when your spouse began seeing someone new during the divorce lawsuit. If the marriage had already broken down beyond repair by then, that relationship is not a tort. However, it is not unusual for the relationship to have actually started before the lawsuit, so finding evidence of when the two first made contact is important.

sections.title: If you decide to divorce during an affair lawsuit
body: Many people decide to divorce while suing the affair partner as a married plaintiff. Filing a divorce lawsuit does not automatically move the pending lawsuit against the affair partner to the family court. To be compensated for the harm of the divorce as well, you must apply to change the cause of action in the existing lawsuit, and if the court regards it as a family case, it transfers the case to the family court (Supreme Court Decision 2024므12628, rendered July 16, 2026). When changed this way, the existing claim is as a rule treated as replaced by the new claim, and even if the change is made on appeal, the case does not start over from the first instance; a collegiate panel of the family court continues hearing it as the appellate court.

Changing the cause of action means you must newly prove the link between the affair partner's infidelity and the breakdown of the marriage. If the main cause of the divorce was financial problems or other conflicts, the amount may not increase as much as you expect, so we first assess whether the change is worthwhile.

sections.title: Keep your statements consistent across both cases
body: If you say in the divorce lawsuit that you found out about the affair recently and in the affair lawsuit that you have known for a year, both statements lose credibility. The date you learned of the affair is also tied to the starting point of the time limit, so once set, that date must stay the same in both cases.

Compensation from your spouse and from the affair partner is for the same harm, so an amount received from one side can affect the decision on the other. We first set the overall amount and then work out together how to claim it from each party.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Choosing the approach
items.desc: A managing partner hears about your evidence, your intention to divorce, and property and custody issues together, and decides whether to join the cases or file separately.

items.title: Confirming the court
items.desc: We check the addresses of the couple and the affair partner and any cases already pending, and decide which court to file the complaint in.

items.title: Drafting the complaint
items.desc: Naming your spouse as Defendant 1 and the affair partner as Defendant 2, we set out claims for divorce, compensation, division of property and custody, together with the claim against the affair partner, in one complaint.

items.title: Mediation and hearings
items.desc: In family court mediation, we negotiate terms with your spouse and with the affair partner separately; if no agreement is reached, we argue the case with evidence at the hearings.

items.title: Managing statements
items.desc: We keep a single fact table for the whole case so that the arguments and dates against both parties do not conflict.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Marital relationship certificate (혼인관계증명서) and family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서)
Addresses of the couple and the affair partner (as far as you know)
Evidence of the affair and a note of the date you found out
Asset records such as real estate, deposits, insurance and severance pay
Material showing the children's care arrangements
Case numbers and documents for any lawsuit already in progress

faqs.q: Can I receive full compensation separately from both my spouse and the affair partner?
faqs.a: The two are jointly liable for the same harm, so you cannot collect the full amount from each of them separately. Judgments often order them to pay jointly, and when one pays, the other's liability is reduced by that much. That is why the claim is organized around the overall amount.

faqs.q: Does a divorce lawsuit go straight to trial?
faqs.a: As a rule, divorce and compensation claims go through mediation (조정) first. If the divorce terms and the compensation from the affair partner are settled in mediation, the case ends without a trial; if not, it moves on to hearings. It's wise to prepare any evidence you want to use in mediation beforehand.

faqs.q: I found out about the affair after a divorce by agreement. Can I still claim?
faqs.a: If it is within 3 years of the day you learned of the infidelity and the affair partner, and within 10 years of the infidelity, you can claim compensation from the affair partner. You also need to check how compensation was settled with your spouse at the time of the divorce. If you agreed not to make further claims against each other, a claim against your spouse may be difficult.

faqs.q: Can I use financial records obtained in the divorce lawsuit for the claim against the affair partner?
faqs.a: If the cases are joined, material obtained through court procedures in the same lawsuit becomes evidence in that case. If your spouse's card records show payments for lodging or gifts, they also support the claim against the affair partner. If the cases proceed separately, how to submit material from another case is reviewed separately.

areaPages.title: Exposing an Affair & Defamation
areaPages.summary: Even if the affair is true, telling someone's workplace, family or social media about it can lead to a defamation complaint.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Article 307; Information and Communications Network Act Article 70
areaPages.lead: If you tell the affair partner's workplace, family or social media about the affair, you can face a criminal complaint for defamation even if what you said is true. What you need to do now differs depending on whether you are the one who told others or the one who was exposed.

seo.title: Exposed an Affair at Work or on Social Media? Defamation in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: How to respond if you told the affair partner's company, family or social media about the affair and were accused of defamation, or if you were the one exposed. Why true statements can still be punished in Korea, how "publicity" is judged, and the effect on the affair lawsuit.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You told the HR team at the affair partner's company about the affair
You sent messages to the affair partner's spouse or parents
You posted on a parenting forum or Blind without names, and then received a criminal complaint
The plaintiff spread news of the affair in a group chat at your company
You are in an affair lawsuit and the other side says it will file a defamation complaint against you

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 307 (Defamation)
items.text: Damaging a person's reputation by publicly alleging facts is punishable by up to 2 years' imprisonment with or without labor or a fine of up to KRW 5 million; if the facts are false, by up to 5 years' imprisonment, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. If the victim states that they do not want the offender punished, no indictment can be brought (Article 312(2)).

items.name: Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) Article 70(1) (Penalties)
items.text: Damaging a person's reputation by publicly revealing facts through an information and communications network with intent to disparage is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. False facts are punished more heavily, and if the victim states that they do not want the offender punished, no indictment can be brought.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 310 (Justification)
items.text: There is no punishment if the facts are true and solely in the public interest. Infidelity between spouses is a private matter, so this provision rarely applies.

sections.title: True statements can still be defamation
body: The Criminal Act (형법) punishes not only false statements but also revealing true facts. Even if the affair is real and you have evidence, defamation (명예훼손) becomes an issue if you conveyed something that lowers the affair partner's social standing in a way that many people could learn of it.
Investigators look at who you told, how and for what purpose. If your words show an intent to retaliate or include insults, an insult charge (모욕죄) may be added.

sections.title: Telling one person can count as public if it could spread
body: Defamation requires publicity (공연성). The Supreme Court maintains the rule that even if you told only a few people, publicity is recognized if those people could pass it on to others (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020도5813, rendered November 19, 2020).

On the other hand, if you conveyed only the facts to a single HR officer to ask that the two be separated at work, and it spread no further, there may be room to contest publicity or intent to disparage.
bullets: Company-wide emails, workplace group chats, internal bulletin boards
Posts on social media, Blind or local online communities (a problem if the person can be identified, even without a name)
Messages sent to the affair partner's parents, spouse or friends
Signs or banners in front of their workplace

sections.title: How exposure affects the affair lawsuit
body: A defamation complaint proceeds as a criminal case separate from the affair lawsuit. The other side can argue for reduced compensation because of the exposure, or separately claim damages for emotional harm.

A debt arising from an intentional tort cannot be set off against another claim (Civil Act (민법) Article 496). Neither side can unilaterally cancel out the affair compensation you are owed against the defamation damages you owe; settling both requires an agreement.

sections.title: If you were the one exposed
body: Even if you are the defendant in an affair lawsuit, you can file a criminal complaint if your reputation was damaged. Keep a record of who disclosed what, when and where, such as the post's URL, screenshots and statements from people who received the messages.

However, a criminal complaint easily ends up used as a bargaining chip in the affair lawsuit. It is better to decide first how the complaint fits with what you will contest in the lawsuit, and then act.

factors.title: Circumstances affecting the disposition and outcome
plus: Disclosed in places many people see, such as the workplace or social media
Repeated several times, or posts were not deleted
Included insults or sexual expressions
Used as pressure to extract settlement money
minus: A limited purpose, such as asking for separation at work
Disclosed narrowly, and it spread no further
Deleted the post and apologized right away
Settled with the victim and obtained a statement that they do not want punishment

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center responds

items.title: Confirming the facts
items.desc: We confirm, with the original text and dates, who was told what and by what means.

items.title: Preventing further harm
items.desc: With the originals stored separately, we decide whether to take down the posts, and cut off further contact.

items.title: Preparing for and attending questioning
items.desc: Before police questioning, we practice with likely questions, and a defense lawyer sits in on the questioning.

items.title: Written opinion and settlement
items.desc: We submit a written opinion on points to contest, such as publicity and intent to disparage, and also explore a settlement in which the victim states they do not want punishment.

items.title: Aligning with the affair lawsuit
items.desc: We assess how the criminal case may affect the compensation decision and keep your statements consistent across both cases.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The original posts and messages and screenshots (with dates visible)
Where the posts were made and the range of people who could see them
The criminal complaint or the police text message asking you to appear
Evidence of the affair and documents from the affair lawsuit
All conversations with the other side

faqs.q: I didn't use a real name, only something like 'K on the ○○ team.'
faqs.a: Even without a name, if people around them can tell who it is, the victim can be considered identified. This is even more likely if the team name, job title or part of a photo is included. Before taking the post down, save the original separately and get a consultation.

faqs.q: Is it still defamation if I told only the affair partner's spouse?
faqs.a: Even if you told one person, publicity can be recognized if that person might spread it to others. However, there may be room to argue that, given the close relationship, it was unlikely to spread. The judgment depends on what words you used and whether you also sent it to anyone else.

faqs.q: If I'm accused of defamation, will I lose my affair compensation?
faqs.a: Your right to claim affair compensation does not disappear. However, if the circumstances of the exposure come out at trial, the other side can raise them as a ground for reduction and separately claim damages. It is advisable to look at both cases together and decide how to resolve them.

areaPages.areaName: Threats & Stalking by an Affair Partner
areaPages.title: Threats & Stalking by an Affair Partner
areaPages.summary: If the affair partner shows up at your home or workplace or keeps contacting you, you can report it as stalking and seek a no-approach order.
areaPages.cardLaw: Stalking Punishment Act Article 18; Criminal Act Article 283
areaPages.lead: If, after the affair comes out, the affair partner turns up outside your home or keeps contacting you saying "I'll expose everything," this is not something to just put up with. The reverse also happens: messages you sent to the affair partner can lead to a complaint for stalking or threats.

seo.title: Affair Partner Threats & Stalking in Korea: Reporting and No-Approach Orders | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do when, after an affair is discovered, the affair partner comes to your home or workplace, keeps contacting you, or demands money while threatening to tell your spouse. Stalking penalties in Korea, emergency measures and provisional measures, the line for threats and extortion, and the records to prepare.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: The woman your husband broke up with is waiting outside your home
The man your wife had an affair with keeps contacting her and is sending photos to you too
You received a message saying, "Pay me or I'll tell your spouse"
They have come to your child's school or even your workplace
You have been reported for stalking over texts you sent to the affair partner

items.name: Act on the Punishment of Stalking Crimes (스토킹범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 18 (Stalking crimes)
items.text: Continuously or repeatedly approaching someone against their will, waiting near their home or workplace, or sending calls or messages is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million; carrying a dangerous weapon raises this to up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. A July 2023 amendment removed the rule that the case ends if the victim does not want punishment.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 283 (Threats) and Article 350 (Extortion)
items.text: Threatening a person is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 5 million, short-term detention or a petty fine. Obtaining money by intimidation is extortion, punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Stalking Punishment Act Articles 4 and 9 (Emergency measures and provisional measures)
items.text: In an emergency, the police can order the person to stay at least 100 meters away and not to make contact by telecommunications; the court can order a written warning, a no-approach order, an electronic monitoring device, or detention in a police cell or detention center.

sections.title: When contact becomes stalking
body: Stalking (스토킹) means, without a legitimate reason and against the other person's wishes, approaching them, waiting near their home or workplace, or sending calls and messages in a way that causes fear. Once is a stalking act; when it continues or is repeated, it becomes a stalking crime.
Approaching the person's household members or family is also included. If the affair partner goes not only to your spouse but also to your children or parents, that too can be a stalking act.

sections.title: Threatening to tell is a threat; demanding money is extortion
body: Frightening someone with words like "I'll tell your spouse everything" or "I'll tell your company" raises the crime of threats (협박). Demanding or obtaining money on that pretext can be punished heavily as extortion (공갈).

It is dangerous for the wronged spouse seeking compensation to say the same things. Even when exercising a right, if the method goes beyond what is socially acceptable, it can become extortion, so make your claim through a certified letter (내용증명) or a complaint (소장).

sections.title: Protection available when you report
body: If stalking is in progress, call 112 (the police emergency number) and the police will stop it on the spot and separate you. If it is likely to happen again, contact and approach can be blocked through police emergency measures (긴급응급조치) and court provisional measures (잠정조치).
Gathering records before reporting speeds up these measures. Note, by date, the times of contact, the places they came to, the locations of nearby CCTV and anyone who witnessed it.

sections.title: What to consider alongside the affair lawsuit
body: The affair partner's stalking or threats can be considered, as their attitude after being found out, when compensation is set. On the other hand, texts you sent in a moment of anger can become evidence for the other side, so cut off contact and say what needs to be said through your legal representative.

factors.title: Circumstances affecting the disposition and outcome
plus: Kept contacting after being refused
Came to the home, workplace or school
Demanded money or a meeting while threatening exposure
Made contact even after a no-approach order
minus: Contact was limited to once or twice
The purpose of contact was legitimate, such as returning belongings
Stopped contact and apologized right away
Settled with the victim

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center responds

items.title: Assessing the danger
items.desc: We hear what contact and visits have occurred and since when, and whether they are still going on, and decide on urgent measures first.

items.title: Organizing records
items.desc: We put the contacts and visits in date order and select the material to use in the report.

items.title: Criminal complaint and protective measures
items.desc: We file the criminal complaint and consider whether emergency or provisional measures are needed. Jisan Law accompanies you to your interview as a victim.

items.title: Reflecting it in the affair lawsuit
items.desc: We include the stalking and threats in the arguments and evidence of the affair lawsuit.

items.title: If you are the one accused
items.desc: If the contact you sent is at issue, we practice with likely questions before questioning and explain the circumstances in a written opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Screenshots of messages and call logs received (before blocking the number)
Notes of the dates and places they came, and footage from your door camera or dashcam
Records of 112 calls or the case report number
Evidence showing the affair
All the messages you sent (do not delete them even if they look unfavorable)

faqs.q: My husband blocked the other woman, and now she's contacting me instead.
faqs.a: Even if the person being contacted changes, repeated unwanted contact can be a stalking act. Don't reply; just keep screenshots. If there are threats or she comes to see you, it is better to report it right away.

faqs.q: I was reported over a text I sent the affair partner saying, 'I'll come to your house.'
faqs.a: A single emotional text and repeated approaches are viewed differently. Cut off contact from now on, and keep every text you sent so you are ready to explain the circumstances. It's a good idea to work out the direction of your statement with a lawyer before police questioning.

faqs.q: If a no-approach order is issued, can they still appear at the affair lawsuit hearings?
faqs.a: A no-approach order keeps the person away from the victim and their home and similar places; it does not bar them from attending court. Still, to avoid running into each other or making contact outside the courtroom, it is safer to move with your legal representative on hearing days.

areaPages.areaName: Criminal Complaints over Illegal Evidence Gathering
areaPages.title: Criminal Complaints over Illegal Evidence Gathering
areaPages.summary: Secretly recording other people's conversations cannot be used as evidence in an affair lawsuit, and the person who recorded can be punished.
areaPages.cardLaw: Protection of Communications Secrets Act Article 16; Location Information Act Article 40
areaPages.lead: If, while gathering evidence of an affair, you opened your spouse's phone or put a recorder or location tracker in their car, you may end up facing a criminal complaint yourself. In 2026, the Supreme Court held that recordings obtained this way cannot be used as evidence even in an affair lawsuit.

seo.title: Secret Recording & Location Tracking for Affair Evidence: Penalties in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: How to respond if you were accused after using a car recorder, location tracker or your spouse's phone to gather evidence of an affair. Penalties under Korea's Protection of Communications Secrets Act and Location Information Act, and admissibility in affair lawsuits after the 2026 Supreme Court ruling.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You put a recorder in your spouse's car and recorded their conversations with the affair partner
You attached a GPS tracker to your spouse's car
You unlocked your spouse's phone and took photos of KakaoTalk chats
You hired a private investigator to follow someone, and that agency is now under investigation
Your spouse has filed a criminal complaint against you under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act

items.name: Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법) Article 16(1) (Penalties)
items.text: Recording or listening in on a private conversation between other people is punishable by 1 to 10 years' imprisonment and suspension of qualifications for up to 5 years. There is no fine option, and content obtained this way cannot be used as evidence in court (Articles 4 and 14(2)).

items.name: Location Information Act (위치정보법) Article 40, item 4 (Penalties)
items.text: Collecting, using or providing personal location information without the consent of the person concerned is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million.

items.name: Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) Article 71(1), item 14 (Penalties)
items.text: Infringing or leaking another person's secrets processed or stored through an information and communications network is punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (violation of Article 49).

sections.title: The test is whether you were part of the conversation
body: Secretly recording a conversation you take part in does not violate the Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법). The same applies when one of three people in a conversation records it (Supreme Court Decision 2006도4981, rendered October 12, 2006).

The problem is a conversation you were not part of. Placing a recorder in a car or home to record your spouse talking with the affair partner is recording a conversation between other people, and it is treated seriously: only imprisonment is prescribed, with no fine option.

sections.title: What the 2026 Supreme Court ruling made clear
body: The Supreme Court held that recording files and transcripts obtained by secretly installing a recorder in a spouse's car are inadmissible as evidence in a lawsuit for affair compensation under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act (Supreme Court Decision 2024다222212, rendered April 30, 2026). In effect, a recording obtained at the risk of punishment cannot be used at trial.

The same ruling said that material with no specific rule barring its use as evidence, such as photos of messages on a mobile phone, is judged individually by weighing how it was collected, the degree of privacy intrusion and the need for the evidence. However, the plaintiff in that case had also been finally convicted under the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) for photographing the phone.

sections.title: Location tracking, private investigators and trespass
body: Attaching a location tracker to your spouse's car without consent, or secretly installing a location-sharing app on their phone, violates the Location Information Act (위치정보법). If a private investigation agency used unlawful methods and the client requested them or hired the agency knowing about them, the client can also be investigated as an accomplice.
Entering the affair partner's home or a lodging room to check the scene can raise the issue of trespass (주거침입).

sections.title: If a complaint has already been filed against you
body: We sort out, act by act, when each device was installed, the actual extent of recording or listening, and whether you were part of the conversation. Even within the same case, some acts may not be crimes.

The affair lawsuit is restructured around whether it can be won without that evidence. We look for substitute evidence through court procedures, such as evidence preservation (증거보전) of lodging CCTV and fact inquiries (사실조회) to mobile carriers and card companies.

factors.title: Circumstances affecting the disposition and outcome
plus: Recorded or listened in real time to conversations you were not part of
Left the device installed for a long time
Spread what you obtained to others
Directly asked a private investigator to track location or record
minus: Most of the recordings were made as a party to the conversation
No recording actually took place, or its scope was narrow
Did not disclose the content to anyone
Removed the device right away

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center responds

items.title: Separating each act
items.desc: We separate recording, location tracking, accessing the phone and entering premises, and look at which law is at issue for each.

items.title: Managing the material
items.desc: We leave the originals as they are and make sure the material does not spread beyond what the investigation needs.

items.title: Practice and attending questioning
items.desc: We practice with likely questions before questioning, and a defense lawyer sits in to explain how the material was collected.

items.title: Written opinion
items.desc: We submit a defense lawyer's written opinion on the parts that are not crimes and on favorable mitigating circumstances.

items.title: Rebuilding the affair lawsuit
items.desc: We secure lawful evidence to replace the problematic evidence through evidence preservation and fact inquiries.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The type of device installed and the dates of installation and removal
A list of recording and photo files (do not send their content to anyone)
The contract with the private investigator and messages exchanged
The criminal complaint and summons
Documents from the affair lawsuit and other evidence

faqs.q: Are photos taken by a private investigator a problem too?
faqs.a: Even if the photos were taken in public places, if unlawful methods such as a location tracker were used while following the person, both the agency and the client can be in trouble. Decide whether to submit them as evidence after confirming how they were collected. It's a good idea to keep the contract and messages that show what methods the agency used.

faqs.q: I already knew my spouse's phone password.
faqs.a: Knowing the password does not by itself mean you were allowed to look. The judgment can depend on whether you normally shared the phone and whether your spouse allowed you to look at it. In the Supreme Court case above, photographing messages on the phone was punished as a violation of the Information and Communications Network Act.

faqs.q: Can I avoid punishment if I delete the recording?
faqs.a: Deleting the file does not undo the recording you already made. Destroying material during an investigation can actually look worse, so don't delete anything on your own. You must immediately stop sending it to others or making it public. Disclosing or leaking the content of a recording is also punished separately.

areaPages.areaName: Infidelity in a De Facto Marriage
areaPages.title: Infidelity by a De Facto Spouse
areaPages.summary: Even without a registered marriage, if a de facto marriage is recognized, you can claim compensation from the unfaithful partner and the affair partner.
areaPages.lead: Even if you never registered your marriage, living together as a married couple is protected as a de facto marriage. You must first show it was a de facto marriage, and then that the affair partner knew about that relationship.

seo.title: Affair in a De Facto Marriage (Unregistered Marriage) in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether you can claim compensation from your partner and the affair partner when your de facto spouse in Korea, with whom you lived without registering the marriage, had an affair. Evidence for recognition of a de facto marriage, the affair partner's knowledge, bigamous de facto marriages that are not protected, and time limits.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You held a wedding but kept putting off registering the marriage
You have lived together for years and were introduced to both families as a married couple
Your de facto spouse started seeing someone else and moved out
The affair partner says, "I thought they were just living together"
Your partner turned out to have a legally registered spouse

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 750 and 751 (Tort; non-property damage)
items.text: A person who unlawfully causes damage, intentionally or negligently, must compensate for it, and emotional suffering is also compensable. Compensation claims against a de facto spouse and an affair partner also start from these provisions.

items.name: Civil Act Article 766 (Extinctive prescription of damage claims)
items.text: The claim lapses 3 years after the day the victim learned of the damage and the wrongdoer, or 10 years after the day of the unlawful act.

sections.title: First show that it was a de facto marriage
body: A de facto marriage (사실혼) is a relationship in which two people, intending to marry, actually lived together as a married couple. It is not decided by the length of cohabitation alone; the court looks at whether people around you treated you as spouses and whether you ran your lives together.

If it is judged to be cohabitation while dating, it is difficult to claim compensation (위자료) from either your partner or the affair partner. So in de facto marriage cases, evidence showing the substance of the relationship matters as much as evidence of infidelity (부정행위).
bullets: Wedding photos, wedding invitations, records of the families' formal first meeting
Records of attending both families' holidays, weddings and funerals together
Bank records of sharing living expenses or loans
Hospital or school documents listing your partner as spouse or guardian
Records of moving in at the same address, lease agreements

sections.title: The affair partner must have known about the de facto marriage
body: Because the marriage was not registered, affair partners often argue, "I didn't know they were a married couple." You need evidence that the affair partner knew the two of you lived together, or that you had held a wedding.

Useful evidence includes chats in which your partner referred to you as "my wife" or "my husband" to the affair partner, records of meeting near your shared home, and wedding photos posted on social media.

sections.title: Some de facto marriages are not protected
body: A de facto marriage with someone who has a separate legal spouse does not, absent special circumstances, receive protection comparable to a legal marriage. Case law holds the same even when the legal spouse had left home long ago (Supreme Court Decision 96므530, rendered September 20, 1996).
Conversely, if you are the legal spouse and your spouse is living with someone else as if in a de facto marriage, that person can be held liable as the affair partner.

sections.title: Ending the relationship and compensation are considered together
body: A de facto marriage can be ended without any filing, so when an affair comes out, ending the relationship, compensation and property issues are often disputed all at once. You need to decide whether to proceed against your de facto spouse only, the affair partner only, or both.
A compensation claim must be made within 3 years of the day you learned of the damage and the wrongdoer. Keep a record of the date the relationship ended and the date you learned of the affair.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Assessing the relationship
items.desc: We hear when you began living together, about the wedding and how living expenses were managed, and first judge whether a de facto marriage is likely to be recognized.

items.title: Sorting the evidence
items.desc: We organize evidence showing the substance of the relationship separately from evidence of infidelity.

items.title: Choosing whom to sue
items.desc: We decide whether to proceed against the de facto spouse, the affair partner or both, and whether to dispute property issues at the same time.

items.title: Lawsuit and mediation
items.desc: If the other side denies the de facto marriage, we rebut with witnesses and documents; in mediation, we negotiate compensation and the division of property together.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Photos of the wedding or the families' first meeting, wedding invitations
Records showing the same address, such as a resident registration abstract (주민등록초본)
Bank records of sharing living expenses or loans
Messages in which family or friends treated you as a married couple
Evidence of infidelity and the affair partner's personal details

faqs.q: We lived together for 2 years without registering the marriage. Is that a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: It is not decided by length alone. The court looks together at whether there was an intention to marry, whether both families and people around you knew you as a married couple, and whether you ran your lives together. If it looks like cohabitation while dating, it is hard to get the protection given to de facto marriages.

faqs.q: We lived apart because of our jobs. Can it still be a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: Even if you lived apart because of your respective jobs, a de facto marriage can be recognized if you held a wedding, attended family events together and lived as a married couple. Prepare material showing why you lived apart and how often you visited each other.

faqs.q: Can I claim against the affair partner only?
faqs.a: Yes. However, even in a lawsuit against the affair partner alone, you must still prove that it was a de facto marriage and that the affair partner knew about that relationship.

areaPages.title: Same-Sex & Online Infidelity
areaPages.summary: Even without sex, and even if the other person is the same sex, a relationship like that of lovers can be found to be infidelity.
areaPages.lead: Infidelity is a broader concept than adultery. Even if the other person is the same sex, or the two only met online, if they had a relationship like that of lovers, you can examine whether the affair partner can be held liable.

seo.title: Same-Sex or Online Affair: Can You Sue in Korea? | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether it counts as infidelity under Korean law when your spouse had a romantic relationship with someone of the same sex, or kept up a relationship only through chats and video calls. How far case law extends infidelity, what evidence is needed, and how to identify someone whose name you don't know.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You saw messages showing your husband behaving like a couple with another man
Your wife used pet names with a female friend and exchanged photos of physical intimacy
Your spouse exchanges expressions of love every day with someone met on a chat app
They say they never met, but video calls and gifts were exchanged
The affair partner claims they are "just friends"

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 840, item 1 (Grounds for judicial divorce)
items.text: If a spouse has committed an unchaste act, the other spouse can file for judicial divorce. Case law interprets an unchaste act more broadly than adultery, as any conduct that falls short of a spouse's duty of fidelity (Supreme Court Decision 92므68, rendered November 10, 1992).

items.name: Civil Act Article 760 (Liability of joint tortfeasors)
items.text: A third party who engages in infidelity with one spouse and thereby infringes on the couple's shared married life in principle commits a tort and is jointly liable with that spouse (Supreme Court Decision 2013므2441, rendered May 29, 2015).

sections.title: It can be infidelity even without sex
body: Not being able to prove sex directly does not block an affair lawsuit. The court looks at the degree and circumstances of the relationship, and if expressions of affection and meetings of the kind lovers have continued, it can find infidelity (부정행위).

Conversations with pet names and repeated "I love you" or "I miss you," records of traveling or staying overnight together alone, and photos of physical contact are used as material for this judgment.

sections.title: The same applies if the other person is the same sex
body: Infidelity does not depend on the other person's sex. If your spouse had a romantic relationship with someone of the same sex, the same standards as for an opposite-sex affair apply to whether it was infidelity and whether the other person knew of the marriage.

Between people of the same sex, the explanation "we're just close friends" comes up easily. Expressions not used between friends, signs of trying to hide the relationship, and records of meeting after lying to you are important.

sections.title: Relationships carried on only online
body: A relationship involving only chats, video calls and gifts may also be found to be infidelity, depending on its content and duration. However, the scope of recognition is narrower than when there are actual meetings, and even if recognized, compensation (위자료) may be set lower.

In online relationships, you often don't know the other person's real name or address. First secure clues that can identify them, such as account IDs, phone numbers, money transfer records and gift delivery addresses.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Reviewing the conversations
items.desc: A managing partner personally looks at whether the messages read as a romantic relationship and which parts are weak.

items.title: Identifying the other person
items.desc: We identify the other person through accounts, phone numbers and transfer records, and if needed apply to the court for a fact inquiry.

items.title: Building the argument
items.desc: We write the complaint by combining the duration and degree of the relationship with evidence that the other person knew of the marriage.

items.title: Mediation and judgment
items.desc: If the other side argues they were just friends, we submit rebuttal evidence, and in mediation we also negotiate a no-contact clause.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Chat screenshots (including the surrounding context, with dates visible)
Photos and videos and the dates they were taken
The other person's account ID, phone number and transfer records
Chats or a written statement in which your spouse admitted the relationship
Payment records for lodging and travel

faqs.q: My spouse is strangely close to a same-sex friend, but the evidence is unclear.
faqs.a: Meeting or contacting each other often is not enough on its own. The test is whether there are expressions used between lovers, physical contact, or signs that they met while deceiving you. Lay out the material you have now in date order and start by checking where the gaps are.

faqs.q: My spouse had an online romance with someone living abroad. Can I sue?
faqs.a: It may be found to be infidelity, but if the other person lives abroad, service and enforcement are difficult, so you need to weigh whether it is worthwhile. We also consider raising the infidelity as a ground for divorce in a divorce lawsuit against your spouse.

faqs.q: We are a same-sex couple. Can I claim against my partner's affair partner?
faqs.a: Under current law, it is difficult for same-sex couples to receive the same protection as a legal or de facto marriage. Depending on how long you lived together and what your life together looked like, there may be room to argue, but there is no established standard yet, so it must be reviewed individually with the evidence you have.

areaPages.areaName: Defense: Marriage Had Already Broken Down
areaPages.title: Defense: Marriage Had Already Broken Down
areaPages.summary: If the plaintiff's marriage had already broken down beyond repair when you met, liability is denied, but the defendant must prove it.
areaPages.lead: If, at the time of the infidelity, the couple's marriage had already broken down in substance and could not be restored, the affair partner has not committed a tort. However, the affair partner must prove this, and the fact of separation alone is not enough.

seo.title: Dating Someone Separated or Mid-Divorce: The Marriage Breakdown Defense in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: If you received an affair complaint but the other couple was already separated or in a divorce lawsuit when you met, are you free of liability? The Supreme Court's standard for breakdown, the defendant's burden of proof, evidence that shows breakdown, and arguments for a reduced amount.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: When you met, you were told they had been separated for years
You dated someone whose divorce lawsuit was in progress
You started seeing each other during the cooling-off period for a divorce by agreement
The plaintiff was seeing someone else first
The plaintiff's side says they were "just apart for a while"

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 750 and 751 (Tort; non-property damage)
items.text: For a third party's infidelity to be a tort, it must have infringed on the couple's shared married life. In a marriage that had already broken down, there is no shared life left to infringe, so liability is denied (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2011므2997, rendered November 20, 2014).

items.name: Civil Act Article 826(1) (Duties between spouses)
items.text: Spouses must live together and support and cooperate with each other, but where they temporarily live apart for a legitimate reason, they must bear with each other. This is the starting point for distinguishing temporary separation from breakdown.

sections.title: When the breakdown defense is accepted
body: The Supreme Court holds that even if a couple has not yet divorced, if their shared married life had broken down in substance and could not be restored, a third party who then has a sexual relationship with one of the spouses does not commit a tort.
The standard is "beyond repair." Leaving home briefly after a quarrel, living apart because of work, or merely having discussed divorce are usually not regarded as a breakdown.

sections.title: The affair partner must prove it
body: The third party who argues that the marriage had already broken down at the time of the infidelity (부정행위) must prove it (Supreme Court Decision 2022므13504, 13511, rendered June 27, 2024). This means the plaintiff does not need to prove that the marriage had not broken down.
What the other person's spouse told you is unlikely to count as proof. It is common for people having affairs to say "We're getting divorced soon" or "We've slept in separate rooms for ages."

sections.title: Evidence that shows breakdown
body: On the other hand, if the spouse kept sending living expenses or went on family trips even during the separation, breakdown is likely to be denied. Prepare for the plaintiff to submit such evidence by matching everything up period by period.
bullets: Records of a divorce lawsuit being filed, or of an application for confirmation of intent to divorce by agreement
Records of the date the separation began and of the change of address
Material showing the period when living expenses and contact stopped
Signs of the plaintiff's own relationship with someone else

sections.title: Even short of breakdown, it can be a ground for reduction
body: Even if a complete breakdown is not recognized, the fact that the marriage had already deteriorated considerably can be considered when compensation (위자료) is set. That is why answers often include both an argument for dismissal and an argument for reduction.
If the relationship began during a divorce lawsuit, the court also looks at what stage the lawsuit was at, whether mediation had failed, and whether there was any chance of the couple reconciling.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center builds your defense

items.title: Matching the timeline
items.desc: We line up, in a single table, the date your relationship began and the dates of the plaintiff couple's separation and lawsuit.

items.title: Finding evidence
items.desc: We look for public records and conversations that show breakdown, and also check what evidence the other person's spouse holds.

items.title: Filing the answer
items.desc: We put together an argument for dismissal and an alternative argument for reduction, and file within 30 days.

items.title: Hearings and mediation
items.desc: We rebut the contrary evidence submitted by the plaintiff, and in mediation we negotiate confidentiality and no-further-claims clauses.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The complaint and the date you were served
Chats in which the other person's spouse described the separation or divorce
The other person's spouse's change-of-address records or divorce case number
The first contact, showing the date your relationship began
Photos of the plaintiff couple at events together (check them even if unfavorable)

faqs.q: We met after a divorce lawsuit had already been filed. Am I still liable?
faqs.a: Filing a lawsuit does not by itself establish a breakdown. The court also looks at how far the lawsuit had progressed, whether the couple still lived together and whether there was room for reconciliation. Start by matching the filing date against the date your relationship began.

faqs.q: The other person said they were divorced and even showed me documents.
faqs.a: This is closer to arguing that you didn't know about the marriage than to the breakdown defense. If there were circumstances that would deceive anyone, intent or negligence may be denied, so keep photos of the documents shown to you and the related chats.

faqs.q: The plaintiff was also having an affair.
faqs.a: The plaintiff's affair can support the claim that the marriage had already broken down, or be a ground for reducing compensation. However, it does not by itself make your liability disappear, so you need to show its timing and extent with evidence.

areaPages.title: Affairs Between Two Married People (Cross Lawsuits)
areaPages.summary: If both people in the affair are married, both wronged spouses can sue each other, so first weigh what you would actually gain and in what order to act.
areaPages.lead: If both people in the affair are married, while you claim against the affair partner, that person's spouse can also claim against your spouse. When the two lawsuits interlock, you must calculate what money is actually left for each household, and confidentiality too.

seo.title: When Both Affair Partners Are Married: Cross Affair Lawsuits in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: How it works when your spouse's affair partner is also married and both wronged spouses sue each other in Korea, why the judgments come out separately, how to calculate gains and losses per household, mutual settlements and reimbursement, and service issues for a married defendant.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: The woman your husband had an affair with was also married
The wife of the man your wife had an affair with has sent your wife a complaint
You are married too, the other person's spouse has sued you, and your own spouse doesn't know yet
Both couples have decided not to divorce
The other side has proposed, "Let's not sue each other"

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 760 (Liability of joint tortfeasors)
items.text: The two people who committed infidelity are jointly liable as joint tortfeasors to each wronged spouse, and that liability is an "untrue" joint and several obligation (부진정연대채무) (Supreme Court Decision 2013므2441, rendered May 29, 2015).

items.name: Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 184 (Reporting a place for service)
items.text: A party or their legal representative may designate a place other than their address as the place to receive service and report it to the court.

sections.title: The two lawsuits proceed separately
body: If A's husband and B's wife had an affair, A can claim against B's wife and B can claim against A's husband. These are separate cases with different plaintiffs and defendants, so the judgments also come out separately.

Even for the same infidelity (부정행위), you cannot assume the two judgments will award the same amount. They can differ depending on each household's length of marriage, children, whether there is a divorce, and who was more active.

sections.title: Calculate what is left per household
body: If both couples stay married, the compensation (위자료) you receive from the affair partner and the compensation your spouse pays to the other spouse move in and out of the same household budget. Once litigation costs are added, sometimes almost nothing is left.

So the two couples sometimes settle by agreeing not to claim against each other and only promising that the two will not meet and that everything stays confidential. Such an agreement should be signed by all four people involved to avoid later disputes.

sections.title: If your spouse doesn't know yet
body: A married person who becomes a defendant in an affair lawsuit first worries about documents arriving at home. Appointing a legal representative or reporting a place for service lets you change where later documents are received.
However, focusing only on hiding it delays your response. Decide the order of steps keeping in mind that your own spouse also has a right to claim against the other affair partner.

sections.title: Reimbursement gets tangled in too
body: An affair partner who paid compensation under a judgment can claim reimbursement (구상) from the person they had the affair with, up to that person's share. In an affair between two married people, this reimbursement also ultimately comes out of the other household's budget.
When ending the matter by settlement, include both a clause that neither side will exercise the right to reimbursement and a no-further-claims clause so you don't end up disputing again later.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Understanding both households
items.desc: We sort out both couples' intentions regarding divorce, the lawsuits already filed and those that could be filed.

items.title: Calculating gains and losses
items.desc: We compare, in one table, the amount to be received, the potential amount to be paid, reimbursement and costs.

items.title: Choosing litigation or settlement
items.desc: We decide whether to go to court or settle mutually, and negotiate with the other side.

items.title: Drafting the settlement agreement
items.desc: We put the mutual waiver of claims, the ban on meeting, confidentiality and the waiver of reimbursement into one document.

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: Any complaint or certified letter you received
Personal details of the affair partner and their spouse
Evidence of the infidelity and when it happened
Your thoughts on your own marriage (staying together or divorcing)
Any settlement proposal from the other side

faqs.q: Do the lawsuit the other man's wife filed against my wife and the lawsuit I filed against that man cancel each other out?
faqs.a: The two lawsuits have different plaintiffs and defendants, so the court does not cancel them out on its own. Each gets its own judgment and each must be paid separately. To withdraw both or trade payments, a separate agreement is needed.

faqs.q: If both couples decided not to divorce, is there any point in suing?
faqs.a: You can sue, but if the marriage continues, compensation may be set lower and a counter-suit may come from the other household. If your goal is ending the relationship and preventing it from happening again rather than money, a settlement agreement may be the better choice.

faqs.q: I'm married too, and I'm worried the complaint will come to my home.
faqs.a: The first complaint is often served at your registered address, but for later documents you can change where they are received by appointing a legal representative or reporting a place for service. If you are still at the certified-letter stage before receiving a complaint, you can also designate your representative as the contact for replies.

areaPages.title: Workplace Affairs and Company Discipline
areaPages.summary: An affair with a coworker can lead to discipline, but private life alone is hard to treat as a legitimate ground for discipline.
areaPages.cardLaw: Labor Standards Act Article 23; State Public Officials Act Article 63
areaPages.lead: If your spouse's affair partner is a coworker at the same company, the issue of company discipline comes along separately from the affair lawsuit. Whether you are the one wanting to tell the company or the one facing discipline, you need to know where private life ends and workplace order begins before you act.

seo.title: Workplace Affair, Discipline and Dismissal in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether you can tell the company when your spouse's affair partner works there, and whether discipline or dismissal for a workplace affair is justified in Korea. The Supreme Court's standard for disciplining private misconduct, public officials' duty to maintain dignity, and deadlines for challenging discipline.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: Your husband and the other woman still work in the same department
You want to tell the company so the affair partner is moved to another department
The other person's spouse came to the company and an HR investigation has begun
You were notified of a suspension because of a workplace affair
You are a public official and have been referred to a disciplinary committee for violating the duty to maintain dignity

items.name: Labor Standards Act (근로기준법) Articles 23(1) and 28 (Restrictions on dismissal; application for remedy)
items.text: An employer may not dismiss, place on leave, suspend, transfer, reduce the pay of, or otherwise discipline an employee without just cause. If you consider it unfair, you can apply to the Labor Relations Commission for a remedy within 3 months of the date of the action.

items.name: State Public Officials Act (국가공무원법) Articles 63 and 78 (Duty to maintain dignity; grounds for discipline)
items.text: Public officials must not engage in conduct that damages their dignity, whether on or off duty, and conduct that damages their honor or prestige is a ground for discipline.

sections.title: Private life alone rarely justifies discipline
body: The Supreme Court holds that an employee's misconduct in private life is a legitimate ground for discipline only if it is directly related to business activities or risks harming the company's public reputation (Supreme Court Decision 93누23275, rendered December 13, 1994). An affair itself is a private matter, so a dismissal based on that alone leaves ample room to challenge it.

However, the judgment can change if the two kept meeting during working hours or business trips and work was disrupted, if they used company facilities, or if gossip in the office disturbed workplace order. If a superior used their position in the relationship, it can also become a matter of workplace sexual harassment or bullying.

sections.title: Public officials and public institutions face stricter standards
body: Public officials can be disciplined for violating the duty to maintain dignity even for conduct outside their duties. Public institutions and some companies also have dignity clauses in their rules of employment, so the risk of discipline is greater than at ordinary companies.

In disciplinary proceedings, you are given an opportunity to explain. It's advisable to set out in writing how the relationship came about, that it did not affect your work, and that you have already ended it.

sections.title: If you are the spouse wanting to tell the company
body: Telling the company may seem like a way to separate the two, but depending on how widely and in what way you tell, you could face a criminal complaint for defamation (명예훼손) or obstruction of business (업무방해). Posting in a group chat or on a bulletin board seen by many employees is especially risky.

If separating them at work is truly necessary, adding clauses such as no contact outside work or efforts toward a department transfer to an affair-lawsuit mediation or settlement agreement carries less legal risk.

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Family Law Center handles your case

items.title: Understanding the situation
items.desc: We check the rules of employment, the statement of disciplinary grounds and the progress of the company's investigation.

items.title: Preparing your explanation
items.desc: Jisan Law writes the explanation to submit to the disciplinary committee and organizes the supporting material. If the company allows a representative to attend, we also appear before the disciplinary committee with you.

items.title: Aligning statements
items.desc: We align what you say so that statements made in the disciplinary process are not used against you in the affair lawsuit.

items.title: Considering a challenge
items.desc: If the discipline is unfair, we apply to the Labor Relations Commission for a remedy within 3 months; Jisan Law writes the application and attends the hearing with you. If you are a public official, Jisan Law also handles your appeal to the Appeals Commission (소청심사).

checklist.title: Helpful materials to prepare before the consultation
items: The disciplinary notice, statement of grounds and rules of employment
Any statement you wrote during the company's investigation
Documents from the affair lawsuit
Material showing the relation to work, such as the division of duties chart
Information on who told the company and how

faqs.q: The company says it will fire both me and the other woman.
faqs.a: A dismissal based solely on the affair can be challenged as lacking just cause. We examine whether the grounds and procedure for dismissal comply with the rules of employment and whether work was actually affected. At workplaces that regularly employ 4 or fewer workers, the dismissal restrictions may not apply, so check the size of the company too.

faqs.q: Is there a way to separate the two without telling the company?
faqs.a: You can put clauses such as no contact outside work, no meeting alone and a penalty for breach (위약벌) into an affair-lawsuit mediation or settlement agreement. If they are in the same department and contact cannot be avoided, the parties sometimes negotiate a promise that the affair partner will request a transfer or resign.

faqs.q: The company says it will close the matter without discipline if I submit a resignation letter.
faqs.a: If you resign, it is not a dismissal, so it becomes hard to challenge it later as an unfair dismissal. If the grounds for discipline are weak, don't rush; weigh the terms of leaving and the disadvantages before deciding.

areaPages.areaName: Renouncing an Inheritance and Limited Acceptance
areaPages.title: Renunciation and Limited Acceptance
areaPages.lead: If nothing is done, a deceased person's debts pass to the heirs. You must file with the family court within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began, and until then the first priority is not to touch the deceased's bank accounts or property.

seo.title: Renouncing an Inheritance or Limited Acceptance in Korea: Deadlines and Steps | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do, and by when, to avoid inheriting a parent's debts in Korea. Covers when the 3-month period starts, the difference between renunciation and limited acceptance, next-in-line heirs, actions that count as simple acceptance, the settlement process after limited acceptance, and special limited acceptance.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: My father has died, and I do not know how much he owed on credit cards and loans
There are some assets and some debts, and I cannot tell which is larger
I heard that if all the children renounce, the debts go to the grandchildren or an uncle
I withdrew money from the deceased's account to pay for the funeral and worry this is a problem
Court papers arrived saying a relative I had lost touch with has died
The 3 months have already passed, and I received a collection notice from a private lender

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1019 (Period for acceptance or renunciation)
items.text: An heir may accept the inheritance simply, accept it with limits, or renounce it within 3 months from the day they learned that the inheritance began, and the family court may extend this period at the request of an interested party or a prosecutor. If the heir did not know, without gross negligence, that the debts exceeded the assets and the inheritance was treated as simply accepted, the heir may take limited acceptance within 3 months from the day they learned that fact (paragraph 3).

items.name: Civil Act Article 1026 (Deemed simple acceptance)
items.text: An heir is treated as having simply accepted the inheritance if they disposed of estate property, if they did not take limited acceptance or renounce within 3 months, or if after limited acceptance or renunciation they hid estate property, used it wrongfully or intentionally left it out of the list of the estate.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1028 and 1030 (Limited acceptance)
items.text: Limited acceptance means accepting the inheritance on the condition of paying the deceased's debts and bequests only up to the value of the property inherited. It must be filed with the court together with a list of the estate.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1041 to 1043 (Renunciation)
items.text: Renunciation must be filed with the family court within 3 months, and it takes effect back to the time the inheritance began, so the person is treated as never having been an heir. The share of the person who renounced goes to the other heirs.

table.title: How Renunciation and Limited Acceptance Differ
rows: Effect
You are treated as never having been an heir
You remain an heir but pay debts only up to the value of what you received
Do the debts pass to the next in line?
They can (next-in-line heirs must renounce separately)
They are settled with the person who took limited acceptance
What to submit when filing
Filing form, family relationship documents, certificate of seal impression
The documents on the left plus a list of the estate
What to do after filing
Keep the written decision; show it if collection demands arrive
Settlement: public notice, notice to creditors, payment in proportion to claims
Suits cases where
The debts clearly exceed the assets and next-in-line heirs can be dealt with
You do not know which is larger, or there are many next-in-line relatives
