table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 1019 and 1028 to 1043. In practice, families often combine the two depending on the family structure and the state of the estate.

sections.title: The 3 Months Run From the Day You 'Learned'
body: The deadline starts not on the day of death but on the day you learned that the inheritance began. The courts read this as the day you learned both that the person had died and that you had become an heir as a result. A child who was at a parent's bedside usually counts from the date of death, but the starting point is different if you learned of an estranged father's death months later, or if you became an heir because everyone ahead of you renounced.

Learning about the debts late does not by itself restart the 3 months. If you already knew of the death and that you were an heir, the deadline keeps running, and if you only discovered the debts later, you have to turn to special limited acceptance (특별한정승인).

If the asset search is not finished and it is hard to decide, you can ask the family court to extend the period before the 3 months run out. The filing only needs to be received within 3 months; the court's decision to accept it does not have to be issued within that time.

sections.title: If You Renounce, the Debts Go to the Next Person
body: Renunciation of inheritance (상속포기) does not wipe out the debts; it takes you out of the position of heir. The share of the person who renounced goes to the other heirs of the same rank, and if everyone of that rank drops out, it passes to the next rank. The order is children (including grandchildren), parents, siblings, and collateral blood relatives within the fourth degree.

According to Supreme Court case law, if the spouse and children were heirs together and only the children all renounced, the spouse becomes the sole heir and nothing passes to the grandchildren. That is why a common approach is for the spouse to take limited acceptance (한정승인) and the children to renounce. If there is no spouse, or the spouse also needs to renounce, consider having one of the children take limited acceptance.
The court does not notify next-in-line heirs. To avoid uncles or cousins being shocked by collection notices months later, it is wise to decide in one go, for the whole family, who will do what.

sections.title: Withdrawing From Accounts or Disposing of Property Can Count as Simple Acceptance
body: If an heir disposes of estate property, they are treated as having simply accepted the inheritance (단순승인). Typical examples are withdrawing the deceased's deposits for living expenses, selling the car or changing its registration, or collecting a lease deposit and splitting it. If this happens, a renunciation or limited acceptance filed later may not be accepted.

There is case law holding that paying funeral costs within a socially reasonable range from the estate is not a disposal, but you must be able to show the amount and its use with receipts. From September 11, 2026, financial transactions in the deceased's name are blocked from the day after the death is reported, so for urgent funeral and hospital costs it is safer to use the financial institution's exceptional withdrawal and have the money sent directly to the hospital or funeral home.

You must stay careful even after renouncing or taking limited acceptance. Hiding estate property, using it wrongfully or deliberately leaving it out of the list is treated as simple acceptance (Civil Act Article 1026, item 3). Even a person who renounced must keep managing the property as it is until the next heir can manage it.

sections.title: With Limited Acceptance, What Comes After Filing Matters More
body: Receiving the court's decision accepting limited acceptance is not the end. Within 5 days of the limited acceptance, you must publish a notice, for example in a newspaper, telling creditors to report their claims within a period of at least 2 months, and you must notify known creditors individually. Until that period ends you can refuse to pay, and after it ends you pay from the remaining property in proportion to the amounts claimed.

If you skip this order and pay only the creditor who contacted you first, you may have to compensate other creditors for their loss (Civil Act Article 1038). If real estate must be sold to pay debts, it is sold by auction under the Civil Execution Act (민사집행법). Because you remain an heir even with limited acceptance, you may have to file an inheritance tax return, and tax issues can arise when real estate is sold, so check this in advance.

sections.title: If the Deadline Has Passed, Look at Special Limited Acceptance
body: If the 3 months passed and the inheritance became a simple acceptance, and you later learned that the debts exceed the assets, you can take limited acceptance within 3 months from the day you learned this, provided you did not know it without gross negligence. An heir whose inheritance became a simple acceptance while they were a minor can do so within 3 months from the day they learn of it after becoming an adult (Civil Act Article 1019(4)).

If you have already disposed of any estate property, you must also submit a list of it with its value, and you must pay debts up to an amount that includes that value. Note also that at this stage you cannot renounce; only limited acceptance is available.

items.desc: We put the Safe Inheritance search results, collection notices and guarantor documents into a table, and assess the chance of private loans or surety debts that the search does not show.

items.title: Planning for the whole family

items.title: Preparing the filing and the list of the estate
items.desc: We match the list of the estate with the attached documents, file with the competent family court, and respond promptly to any order to correct.

items.title: Settlement and dealing with creditors
items.desc: After limited acceptance, we carry out the public notice, notices to creditors and proportional payment in order, and we answer any lawsuits filed after the acceptance.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The deceased's basic certificate (기본증명서), detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) and resident registration abstract of a deregistered person (말소자 주민등록초본)
Text messages or printouts of the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service (안심상속 원스톱서비스, a government service that searches a deceased person's assets and debts in one application) results
Any collection notices, complaints or payment orders you received, with their envelopes (to confirm the date received)
Copies of the deceased's bankbooks and transactions after the death
Receipts for funeral and hospital costs
A simple family tree (including siblings, nephews and nieces, and cousins)

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court in person to file a renunciation of inheritance?
faqs.a: You can go in person or file through the electronic litigation system (전자소송). The competent court is not the one for your address but the family court that has jurisdiction over the deceased's last address. With electronic filing, each filer must sign electronically with a digital certificate, so if family members are filing together, each should prepare in advance.

faqs.q: Our family signed a written statement renouncing the inheritance. Is that enough?
faqs.a: No. A written statement among family members, or an agreement that 'I won't take anything', is only an agreement on dividing the estate; it is not a renunciation that frees you from debts as against creditors. To avoid inheriting debts, you must file with the family court within 3 months and have the renunciation accepted.

faqs.q: Do minor children also have to renounce?
faqs.a: Yes, if the children are in the rank that becomes heirs. The parent with parental authority files on the child's behalf. If the parent and child renounce together, there is usually no problem, but if the parent inherits and only the child renounces, their interests conflict and a separate special representative (특별대리인) may have to be appointed. The period runs from the day the parent with parental authority learned that the inheritance began (Civil Act Article 1020).

faqs.q: I renounced the inheritance and then found out there were more assets. Can I cancel it?
faqs.a: You cannot cancel it because you changed your mind (Civil Act Article 1024(1)). You can challenge it only if there is a ground for cancellation under the general provisions of the Civil Act, such as being deceived or coerced by another heir, and you must do so within 3 months from the day you could ratify it and within 1 year from the day you renounced.

faqs.q: My renunciation was accepted, but creditors keep contacting me.
faqs.a: It is common for debts to be sold several times, so a new creditor contacts you without knowing about the renunciation. Sending a copy of the written decision in response to calls or mailed demands usually resolves it. However, if you ignore a complaint or payment order (지급명령) from the court, a judgment against you can become final, so you must file an answer or an objection within the deadline, attaching the written decision.

areaPages.title: Division of the Estate
areaPages.lead: Until it is divided, an estate is co-owned by all the heirs. A division agreement has no effect if even one heir is left out, and if the heirs cannot agree, the family court divides the estate through mediation and then adjudication.

seo.title: Division of an Estate in Korea: Agreement, Mediation and Court Adjudication | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: For siblings who cannot settle how to divide an estate in Korea. Covers the requirements for division by agreement and drafting the agreement, minor or unreachable heirs, registration by statutory shares, mediation and adjudication on division of the estate, division methods and tax deadlines.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: One of my siblings will not stamp the division agreement
My eldest brother lives in our parents' house and refuses to sell it or divide it
Some of the heirs are minors or people we have lost contact with
Someone registered the property in statutory shares without any agreement
My remarried father has died, and we have to divide the estate with our stepmother
I was handed a division agreement and do not know whether it is safe to sign

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 1006 and 1009 (Co-ownership and statutory shares)
items.text: When there are several heirs, the estate is co-owned, and heirs of the same rank receive equal shares. A spouse who inherits together with lineal descendants or lineal ascendants receives an additional 50% of their share.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1013 (Division by agreement)
items.text: Unless the method of division was set by will, the co-heirs may divide the estate by agreement at any time, and if they cannot agree, they may ask the court to divide it.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1015 (Retroactive effect of division)
items.text: Division takes effect back to the time the inheritance began, but it cannot harm the rights of third parties.

items.name: Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Articles 2 and 50
items.text: Claims for division of the estate and for a contribution share are non-contentious family cases of category 'ma' (마류) handled by the family court, and mediation must come before a request for adjudication.

table.title: Three Ways to Divide an Estate
rows: Division by will
The estate is divided as the deceased set out in the will
Check that the will is in a valid form and does not infringe the forced heirship share
Division by agreement
All heirs agree on who gets what
Invalid if even one heir is left out. Minors need a special representative
Division by adjudication
The family court decides by adjudication after mediation
Divided by specific shares that reflect special benefits and contribution shares
table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 1012 and 1013 and Family Litigation Rules (가사소송규칙) Articles 110 to 116.

sections.title: Every Heir Must Sign the Agreement
body: Division by agreement (협의분할) is valid only if all the co-heirs take part. They do not have to meet in one place: one person can draw up the agreement and pass it around for each heir to sign and stamp with their registered seal. However, an agreement that leaves out even one heir, or that one heir did not consent to, is void, and any registration based on it can be challenged.

The agreement should list every heir's name and resident registration number and state specifically who takes each asset. All heirs then stamp it with their registered seals and attach a certificate of seal impression (인감증명서). Real estate should be described down to the lot number and area, and deposits down to the bank and account number, so the agreement can be used as it is for registration and banking. Adding a clause on assets not listed, such as 'any remaining assets and debts follow the statutory shares', reduces new disputes over assets found later.

sections.title: If an Heir Is a Minor or a Sibling Cannot Be Reached
body: When a parent and child are heirs at the same time, for example a mother and her minor children, the mother cannot negotiate on the children's behalf. A special representative (특별대리인) must be appointed by the family court for each child and take part in the agreement (Civil Act Article 921). If there are two children, each needs a separate special representative.

If an heir has lost contact and their whereabouts are unknown, ask the family court to appoint an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인). With the court's permission, the administrator takes part in the agreement or becomes a party to the adjudication. Keep in mind that if you put things off for years waiting for one heir's consent and another heir dies in the meantime, that heir's spouse and children also become parties to the agreement.

sections.title: Registration by Statutory Shares Is Not the Same as Division
body: Even without an agreement, one heir can apply to register the property in all the heirs' names according to their statutory shares. This puts the registration in a co-owned state for now, but it also registers the shares of heirs who did not consent, and it does not complete a final division reflecting special benefits or contribution shares.

The Supreme Court views co-heirs as provisionally co-owning the estate in their statutory shares until division, with ownership of each asset settled only when the estate is divided according to each heir's specific share, taking special benefits and similar factors into account. So the fact that someone registered the statutory shares first does not settle the outcome, and the shares can be adjusted again in the division adjudication.

sections.title: Without Agreement, the Case Goes to Mediation and Adjudication
body: One or more heirs request an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할) against all the remaining heirs (Family Litigation Rules Article 110). Because mediation must come first, the case usually begins with a mediation date, and if mediation fails, the court holds a hearing and issues an adjudication. To claim a contribution share (기여분), you must file a petition to determine it together with the request for division, and if the court sets and announces a period for such claims, you must file within it (Article 113 of the same Rules).

The court divides all the property subject to division at once. For property that is hard to divide, such as a home, the court may give it to one person and have that person pay the other heirs the difference in cash (Article 115 of the same Rules), or order it sold at auction and the proceeds divided. Including mediation, this usually takes around a year, and longer if real estate appraisals or financial transaction inquiries drag on.

sections.title: Keep the Tax Timeline in View
body: There is no statutory deadline for dividing an estate, but inheritance tax must be reported within 6 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began, and some deductions, such as the spousal inheritance deduction, apply only if the division is completed within a set period. If a division adjudication is under way, there is a way to state this when filing the tax return, so if the negotiations look likely to take a long time, coordinate the schedule with a tax accountant in advance. We can also work together with a tax accountant who cooperates with Jisan Law.

steps.title: How Our Family Law Center Handles Your Case

items.title: Confirming the heirs
items.desc: Using the certificate of removed family register (제적등본) and family relationship documents, we confirm every heir, including those from a remarriage, children born outside marriage and heirs by representation.

items.title: Listing the estate and lifetime gifts
items.desc: We make a table of the assets and debts as of the date of death and who received what during the deceased's lifetime, with market price data attached.

items.title: Calculating specific shares
items.desc: We include special benefits and contribution shares to calculate each person's actual share, and set the range you can accept in negotiations.

items.title: Reviewing or drafting the agreement
items.desc: If agreement is possible, we draft an agreement that includes the description of each asset and a clause on assets not listed, and we review any agreement the other side sends before you sign.

items.title: Requesting mediation and adjudication
items.desc: If agreement fails, we file the division request together with a contribution share claim, and confirm the estate through financial transaction inquiries and appraisal requests.

items.title: Completing registration and settlement
items.desc: Once the mediation or adjudication becomes final, we follow through to inheritance registration and payment of the settlement money.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The deceased's certificate of removed family register, basic certificate (기본증명서) and detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서)
Real estate registry certificates and officially assessed price or market price data
Search results for deposits, stocks and insurance
Transfer records and registry documents for money or homes your siblings received during the deceased's lifetime
If you provided support or care, materials showing the period and costs
Any draft agreement or messages the other side sent

faqs.q: If one sibling will not stamp the agreement, can we not register the inheritance?
faqs.a: You cannot register a division by agreement, but one heir can apply to register the inheritance in all the heirs' names according to their statutory shares. However, this only makes you co-owners by share; it does not complete the division. To divide the estate finally, you must negotiate again or ask the family court for an adjudication on division.

faqs.q: By when must the estate be divided?
faqs.a: The law sets no deadline. However, considering the inheritance tax filing deadline, the risk of more parties if another heir dies, and the burden of managing real estate and paying taxes, the longer you wait, the harder it gets. Some claims do have their own periods, such as a claim for payment of value by a person who became an heir through acknowledgment or a court judgment after the inheritance began.

faqs.q: What if assets we did not know about turn up after the agreement is signed?
faqs.a: If the agreement does not say how unlisted assets are handled, you must negotiate again or request division for those assets alone. If some heirs hid assets at the time of the agreement, we also consider whether the validity of the agreement can be challenged.

faqs.q: Does my stepmother also inherit from my father?
faqs.a: If she was his legal spouse with a registered marriage, she is a co-heir together with the children and receives 1.5 times one child's share. A de facto spouse whose marriage was never registered is not an heir; only when there are no other heirs at all can she ask, as a person with a special relationship to the deceased, to be granted part of the estate.

faqs.q: Another heir requested a division adjudication, and I was told to appear in court. Do I have to go?
faqs.a: All heirs are parties to the adjudication, so you receive notice even if you do not intend to take anything. If you cannot attend, submit a written explanation with the case number, and it is wise to state in writing the division method or views you want. If you submit nothing, the case may be decided mainly on the other heirs' arguments.

areaPages.title: Forced Heirship Share Claims
areaPages.lead: Even if a will or lifetime gifts sent the estate to one person, the law reserves a minimum share for children, spouses and parents. The claim must be made within 1 year from the day you learned of the gift or bequest.

seo.title: Forced Heirship Share (Yuryubun) Claims in Korea: Calculation, Deadlines and the 2026 Amendment | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to claim a forced heirship share in Korea when a parent's estate went to one sibling, and how to respond if a claim is made against you. Covers who is entitled and in what proportion, calculating the base estate, the 1-year and 10-year limits, the 2026 rule of returning value in money, gifts in return for contribution, and the abolition of siblings' forced heirship share.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: Just before he died, my father gave the house to my youngest sibling
There is a notarized will leaving the entire estate to the eldest son
I wonder whether the apartment my brother received 20 years ago is counted
My mother left a will donating all her property to a charitable organization
My younger sibling sent me a complaint demanding a forced heirship share
I received a house in return for caring for our parents and do not know whether I must give it back as a forced heirship share

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1112 (Persons entitled and amount of the forced heirship share)
items.text: Lineal descendants and spouses receive one half of their statutory share, and lineal ascendants one third. Item 4, which set a forced heirship share for siblings, was deleted following the Constitutional Court's 2024 ruling that it was unconstitutional.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1113 and 1114 (Calculation and gifts to be counted)
items.text: The calculation takes the property at the start of the inheritance, adds gifted property and deducts the full amount of debts. As a rule, only gifts made in the year before the inheritance began are included, but gifts made earlier are also included if both sides knew they would harm a person entitled to a forced heirship share.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1115 (Preservation of the forced heirship share)
items.text: If gifts and bequests leave a forced heirship share short, the person may claim payment of the value of that property to the extent of the shortfall, with interest added from the date of the claim. This applies to inheritances that began on or after March 17, 2026.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1116 to 1118
items.text: Gifts are claimed only after bequests have been returned. The right to claim expires 1 year after learning of the start of the inheritance and of the gift or bequest to be returned, or 10 years after the inheritance began. The provisions on special benefits (Article 1008) and others apply to the forced heirship share.

table.title: How the Forced Heirship Share Is Calculated
rows: ① Base estate
Property at the start of the inheritance + gifts counted - all debts
Under case law, gifts to co-heirs are counted even if made more than 1 year earlier
② My forced heirship share
Base estate × my statutory share × forced heirship ratio
Children and spouse one half, parents one third
③ Shortfall
Forced heirship share - gifts and bequests I received - my net share of the inheritance
If much of the estate remains, there may be no shortfall
④ Who must return it
Recipients of bequests first, then recipients of gifts
If there are several, divided in proportion to the value each received
table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 1113 to 1118 and case law. As a rule, gifted property is converted to its value at the start of the inheritance.

sections.title: Who Can Claim, and How Much
body: Only people who would be heirs have a forced heirship share (유류분). If there are children, the children and spouse are entitled; if there are no children, the parents and spouse are. The forced heirship share of siblings lost its effect after the Constitutional Court ruled it unconstitutional on April 25, 2024, and the provision has been deleted, so the deceased's siblings cannot make a claim on this ground.

The ratio is one half of the statutory share for children and spouses, and one third for parents. For example, if three children are the heirs and there is no spouse, each statutory share is one third, and the forced heirship share is half of that, one sixth. Multiply this by the base estate and subtract what you have already received to get the amount you can actually claim.

sections.title: Which Gifts Are Counted
body: The Civil Act counts gifts made within 1 year before the inheritance began, but under case law, gifts received by co-heirs are treated as special benefits (특별수익) and counted regardless of when they were made. So an apartment your brother received 20 years ago can be included. Gifts to people who are not heirs are counted only if made within that year, or if both sides knew the gift would harm the forced heirship share.

As a rule, gifted property is valued as of the start of the inheritance. Real estate is valued by appraisal at market prices around the time of death, and cash given long ago is converted to reflect changes in prices. Even if the recipient has already sold the property, it is still included in the calculation.

sections.title: What Changed in March 2026
body: The Civil Act amended on March 17, 2026 provides that a forced heirship shortfall is returned as value, that is, in money, with interest added from the date of the claim. This applies to inheritances that began after the amendment took effect, so if the person died before then, the rule under earlier case law is return of the property itself. Even under that rule, if the recipient has already sold the property, you claim return of its value.

In addition, gifts or bequests received as compensation for specially supporting the deceased, such as living with and caring for them for a considerable period, or for specially contributing to maintaining or increasing their property, are no longer treated as special benefits to the extent that matches the contribution (Civil Act Article 1008, proviso). This also applies to the forced heirship share and to inheritances that began on or after April 25, 2024. If you received property in return for caring for a parent, you should actively raise this point when a claim is made against you.

An heir who seriously failed in their duty of support loses their forced heirship share as well if a court declares that they have lost their inheritance rights. Since the 2026 amendment, this can also apply to children and spouses.

sections.title: One Year Is Shorter Than You Think
body: The right to claim a forced heirship share expires 1 year after you learned that the inheritance began and that there was a gift or bequest to be returned, or 10 years after the inheritance began. Under case law, 'learned' means knowing not merely that a gift was made but also that it could be subject to return, yet disputes often turn on the day you obtained the registry record or saw the will.

If preparing a lawsuit is taking time, one option is to first state clearly that you are claiming return by certified mail with proof of contents (내용증명). You still have to file the lawsuit on time afterwards, so it is safest to keep a record of the dates and start preparing immediately.

sections.title: What the Person Facing a Claim Can Dispute
body: Receiving a forced heirship share complaint does not mean you must pay the amount stated. We examine, point by point, whether the time limit has passed, whether the plaintiff also received something during the deceased's lifetime, whether the plaintiff still has a share to inherit, whether the value of gifted property has been inflated, and whether the estate's debts were left out. The fact that a gift was received in return for supporting a parent can now also be reflected in the calculation.

A forced heirship share lawsuit is a civil lawsuit, so you must file an answer within 30 days from the day you received the copy of the complaint. If you do not, judgment may be entered as the plaintiff claims, without a hearing.

steps.title: How Our Family Law Center Handles Your Case

items.title: Checking the time limit
items.desc: We use documents to confirm the date the inheritance began and the day you learned of the gift or bequest, and calculate the period in which you can claim.

items.title: Gathering gift records
items.desc: We collect registry records, financial transaction records and notarized wills, and during the lawsuit we look for missing gifts through orders to submit financial transaction information and fact-finding inquiries.

items.title: Calculating the forced heirship share
items.desc: We calculate the base estate and the shortfall to set the amount of the claim, and determine whether return is in money or in kind depending on whether the amended law applies.

items.title: Negotiation or filing suit
items.desc: If the other side may be willing to talk, we send the basis of our calculation and negotiate; if not, we file suit and dispute the amount through appraisals and inquiries.

items.title: Defending against a claim
items.desc: We write the answer and briefs based on the time limit, the plaintiff's special benefits, gifts in return for contribution and the valuation standards.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The deceased's family relationship certificate and documents confirming the date of death
Registry certificates for the gifted real estate (to confirm the cause and date of transfer)
A copy of the will or the notarized will
Materials showing how and when you first learned of the gift
Records of money or property you received during the deceased's lifetime
Any complaint or certified letter you received (if a claim was made against you)

faqs.q: I heard the deadline for a forced heirship share claim is 2 years. Is that right?
faqs.a: No. It is 1 year from the day you learned of the start of the inheritance and of the gift or bequest to be returned, and 10 years from the start of the inheritance (Civil Act Article 1117). If either period passes, you can no longer claim, so if more than a year has passed since the death, start by checking when you learned of the gift.

faqs.q: I also received tuition and wedding money while my father was alive. Can I still claim a forced heirship share?
faqs.a: You can, but the gifts you received are also counted as special benefits, which reduces your shortfall. Ordinary support for tuition or living costs is often excluded from special benefits, while wedding money or housing funds are often included, so the amounts and timing need to be examined.

faqs.q: My brother who received the house has already sold it. Can I not get anything back?
faqs.a: You can. If the inheritance began on or after March 17, 2026, you claim payment of value from the start, and even for an earlier inheritance, if return of the property itself is impossible, you claim its value. If the buyer knew the purchase would harm the person entitled to the forced heirship share, you may in some cases be able to claim against the buyer.

faqs.q: Is property transferred through a will substitute trust also subject to the forced heirship share?
faqs.a: Whether property transferred through a will substitute trust is counted in the forced heirship share calculation can depend on when the trust was set up and whether the beneficiary is a co-heir or a third party, so it must be examined case by case. First secure the trust agreement, the beneficiary designation and the date the trust was created.

areaPages.title: Wills: Drafting, Court Inspection and Invalidity
areaPages.lead: A will is valid only if it follows one of the five forms set out in the Civil Act. Even if it reflects the deceased's true wishes, it is void if the form is wrong, and even a will in proper form can be challenged if the person lacked mental capacity.

seo.title: Wills in Korea: Handwritten Will Requirements, Court Inspection and Challenging a Will | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: For people who want to make a will in Korea, and for those who have found a will or want to challenge one. Covers the requirements for handwritten, recorded, notarized, sealed and oral wills, disqualified witnesses, court inspection and opening of a will, grounds for invalidity and proving mental capacity, and how wills relate to the forced heirship share.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: I want to write a will now to prevent disputes among my children
A will in an envelope turned up in my father's drawer
There is a notarized will made after a dementia diagnosis
The handwriting on the will does not look like my mother's
The will is missing an address or a date
I want to register property as the will says, but another sibling objects

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 1060 and 1065 (Formal requirements and types of wills)
items.text: A will has no effect unless it is made in a form set by the Civil Act. The five forms are a handwritten will, a recorded will, a notarized will, a sealed (secret) will and an oral will.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1066 (Handwritten will)
items.text: The testator must personally write the full text, the year, month and day, their address and their name, and affix a seal. Any insertion, deletion or correction must also be handwritten and sealed by the testator.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1068 and 1072 (Notarized wills and witnesses)
items.text: For a notarized will, the testator states the substance of the will before a notary in the presence of 2 witnesses, the notary writes it down and reads it aloud, and the testator and witnesses confirm it and sign it or write their names and affix seals. Minors, persons under adult or limited guardianship, and people who benefit from the will and their spouses and lineal blood relatives cannot be witnesses.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 1091 and 1092 (Court inspection and opening)
items.text: A person who keeps or finds a written will or recording must submit it to the court without delay after the testator's death and request a court inspection. Notarized and oral wills are exempt from this inspection, and a sealed will is opened by the court in the presence of the heirs or others.

table.title: Requirements by Type of Will
rows: Handwritten will
Full text, date (year, month, day), address and name handwritten + seal
Required
Recorded will
Testator states the substance, name and date + attending witness states that it is accurate and gives their own name
Required
Notarized will
2 witnesses present, stated before a notary, written down and read aloud, confirmed, then signed or name written and sealed
Not required
Sealed will
Sealed document presented to 2 or more witnesses, date and signatures on the envelope, certified date stamp within 5 days
Required
Oral will
Urgent circumstances such as illness, 2 or more witnesses present, stated, written down, read aloud and confirmed
Separate inspection within 7 days from the end of the urgent circumstances
table.note: Based on Civil Act Articles 1066 to 1070 and 1091. A person under 17 cannot make a will (Article 1061).

sections.title: A Handwritten Will Is Void If Even One of Five Elements Is Missing
body: A handwritten will (자필증서 유언) costs nothing and can be written alone, so it is the most common type, but it also leads to the most disputes over validity. The whole text must be written by hand, so a document printed from a computer and only signed has no effect. The date must include the year, month and day, so leaving out the day, as in 'October 2026', makes it void.

The address must also be handwritten. Courts have held a will without an address void, and have not recognized a will that was only signed instead of sealed. The seal does not have to be a registered seal, and a thumbprint counts as a seal. Any correction must also be handwritten and sealed at the corrected spot, so if many changes are needed, it is better to write a new will.

sections.title: If You Expect a Dispute, We Recommend a Notarized Will
body: With a notarized will (공정증서 유언), the notary questions the testator directly and keeps the original, so there are fewer claims of forgery, and after the death it can be used for registration and banking right away without a court inspection. Two witnesses are needed, and children who will receive property or their spouses cannot be witnesses, so find people with no interest in the will in advance.

Naming an executor at the same time makes it clear who will handle registration and the transfer of deposits after the death. A will can be revoked at any time, and where an earlier and a later will conflict, the conflicting part of the earlier will is treated as revoked (Civil Act Articles 1108 and 1109). When deciding how to distribute your property, also keep in mind that the other heirs' forced heirship share (유류분) remains even if you make a will.

sections.title: If You Find a Will, Keep the Original Intact and Request a Court Inspection First
body: For handwritten, recorded and sealed wills, the person who keeps or finds the will must request a court inspection (검인) from the family court without delay after the death. The competent court is the one where the inheritance began, usually the family court for the deceased's last address. The court sets an inspection date and notifies the heirs, and on that day it checks the form, handwriting and seal of the will and records them in a written record.

A will sealed in an envelope must be submitted as it is; the family must not open it. The court inspection is only a procedure to prevent forgery or alteration and to preserve the will's condition; it is not a trial that confirms the will is valid. So if another heir states at the inspection that 'this is not father's handwriting', the matter is often blocked at the registration stage or the will's validity has to be fought out in a separate lawsuit.

sections.title: Invalidity Is Argued on Form and Mental Capacity
body: A lawsuit to confirm that a will is invalid mainly turns on two issues. One is a breach of form: for example, a handwritten element is missing, or when a notarized will was made, the testator did not state it personally but simply nodded at a document prepared in advance. The other is mental capacity: whether, at the time of the will, the person could understand and judge who was getting what.

A dementia diagnosis alone does not make a will void. The court looks at medical and nursing records from around the time of the will, cognitive test results, the questions and circumstances when the will was notarized, and whether the content fits the person's usual wishes. If the handwriting is suspicious, collect samples of the deceased's handwriting from their lifetime and request a handwriting examination.

Separately from the claim of invalidity, the time limit for a forced heirship share claim keeps running. In case the will is found valid, it is safer to file a forced heirship share claim at the same time.

steps.title: How Our Family Law Center Handles Your Case

items.title: Checking the form of the will
items.desc: Whether it is a will you want to make or one you have found, we first identify its form and check each requirement.

items.title: Advice on drafting
items.desc: For those making a will, we look at the description of assets and wording, the effect on the forced heirship share and taxes, and the appointment of an executor.

items.title: Requesting a court inspection
items.desc: For a will you have found, we request a court inspection while preserving the original, and make sure the views of other heirs on the inspection date are recorded.

items.title: Reviewing grounds for invalidity
items.desc: We gather medical records, notarization materials and handwriting samples to review breaches of form and mental capacity.

items.title: Lawsuit alongside a forced heirship share claim
items.desc: When filing a lawsuit to confirm the will is invalid, we also consider an alternative claim so you do not miss the deadline for a forced heirship share claim.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The original will (if sealed, unopened) and photos of it
For a notarized will, the authenticated copy or certified copy
Medical records, nursing records and long-term care grade documents from around the time of the will
Letters, notebooks or contracts in the deceased's handwriting
Registry certificates for real estate transferred under the will
Contact details of people who know how the will was made

faqs.q: Is a will void if there is no court inspection?
faqs.a: The will itself does not become void just because it was not inspected. However, registering property or withdrawing deposits under a handwritten will often requires the inspection record, so in practice you need the court inspection to carry out the will.

faqs.q: Is a video will recorded on a mobile phone valid?
faqs.a: It is valid if it meets the requirements for a recorded will. The recording must show the testator stating the substance of the will, their name and the date, and an attending witness stating that the will is accurate and giving their own name. A video recorded alone without a witness is likely to be found not to meet the required form.

faqs.q: Can we siblings divide the estate differently from what the will says?
faqs.a: It is generally accepted that if all the heirs, including those who receive property under the will, agree, they can divide the estate by agreement differently from the will. However, cases where there is an executor or a bequest to a third party need separate review, and the tax consequences should also be checked.

faqs.q: My brother is hiding our father's will.
faqs.a: A person who forges, alters, destroys or hides a will concerning inheritance cannot be an heir (Civil Act Article 1004, item 5). However, the person making this claim must prove the hiding, so first secure statements or messages showing that someone saw the will. If it is a notarized will, you can ask the notary office, as an heir, to confirm it.

areaPages.title: Contribution Share and Special Benefits
areaPages.lead: The basic rule is that a person who specially supported a parent receives more, and a person who received property in advance receives that much less. However, simply saying 'I took care of them' or 'they got money' is not enough; the period and amounts must be shown with documents to be reflected in the calculation.

seo.title: Contribution Share and Special Benefits in Korean Inheritance | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The requirements for a contribution share for a child who lived with and cared for a parent, and the evidence needed; when lifetime gifts and wedding money count as special benefits; calculating each heir's specific share; and the 2026 amendment excluding gifts given in return for contribution from special benefits.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: I lived with my parents for over 10 years and even paid their hospital bills, but my siblings want to split everything equally
I worked in my parents' shop for many years without pay
Our parents bought my brother a home when he married, and he does not want it counted
I have been paying off my mother's apartment loan on her behalf
My sibling is claiming a contribution share, and I do not know whether it would be recognized
I received a house in return for caring for our parents, and my siblings say it is a special benefit

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1008-2 (Contribution share)
items.text: A co-heir who specially supported the deceased, for example by living with and caring for them for a considerable period, or who specially contributed to maintaining or increasing their property, receives their share calculated after first deducting the agreed contribution share from the estate, plus the contribution share. If no agreement is reached, the family court decides at the contributor's request, and the contribution share cannot exceed the estate minus the value of bequests.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1008 (Share of an heir who received special benefits)
items.text: A co-heir who received gifts or bequests has a share only to the extent that what they received falls short of their share. The amendment of March 17, 2026 created an exception, to the extent matching the contribution, for gifts or bequests received as compensation for special support or for specially contributing to maintaining or increasing the property.

items.name: Family Litigation Rules (가사소송규칙) Articles 110 to 113
items.text: A petition to determine a contribution share is joined to and heard together with the case for division of the estate. The court may set and announce a filing period of at least 1 month, and a petition filed after that period may be dismissed.

table.title: Example: Calculating Specific Shares
columns: Example (children A, B and C; estate of KRW 600 million)
rows: ① Deduct contribution share
Estate - contribution share
A's contribution share KRW 60 million → KRW 540 million
② Add special benefits
① + lifetime gifts (special benefits)
Gift received by B, KRW 90 million → KRW 630 million
③ Apply statutory shares
② × each heir's statutory share
One third each = KRW 210 million
④ Specific share
③ - own special benefits + own contribution share
A KRW 270 million, B KRW 120 million, C KRW 210 million
table.note: A simplified example to aid understanding. In practice the calculation varies with the valuation date, the contribution share ratio and whether there are bequests.

sections.title: A Contribution Share Requires 'Special' Support
body: Supporting one's parents is also a legal duty for children, so courts recognize a contribution share (기여분) only for special support that goes beyond that duty. Under case law, it must be shown that the heir specially supported the deceased, or specially contributed to maintaining or increasing their property, to a degree that requires adjusting the shares for fairness among the co-heirs.

Circumstances that make recognition more likely include living together for a long time and providing care personally without a hired caregiver, paying a substantial part of hospital and living costs, other siblings being barely involved, working unpaid in the parents' business for a long time, and protecting the property by paying off loans on their behalf. Holiday visits, occasional pocket money or a few days of hospital care are precious as filial devotion, but they are hard to have recognized as a contribution share.

sections.title: A Contribution Share Is Proved With Documents
body: The caregiving period can be shown through resident registration history, guardian signatures on inpatient and outpatient records, and records of long-term care services. For costs, the most reliable evidence is transfers from your account to hospitals or care homes and card payment records. If you paid in cash, gather at least the receipts and messages from that time.

Contributions that increased the property are documented with the money paid toward buying real estate, the principal and interest of loans repaid on the parent's behalf, and work records for the period of unpaid work. Note also that if there is no agreement, a contribution share must be claimed together with an adjudication on division of the estate, and it cannot be claimed separately in a forced heirship share lawsuit.

sections.title: A Special Benefit Is a 'Share Received in Advance'
body: Not every lifetime gift is a special benefit (특별수익). Under case law, the question is whether, considering the deceased's assets, income, standard of living and family situation, the gift can be seen as giving a future heir part of the estate in advance. Funds to buy a home, business funds and large wedding costs are often treated as special benefits, while ordinary support for tuition or living costs is often excluded.

Special benefits are added back to the estate for the calculation and then subtracted from the recipient's share. So if your brother received a lot during your parent's lifetime, he may have little or no share of the remaining estate. You need to show the transfer records at the time of the gift, the cause of registration and the size of your parent's assets at that time.

sections.title: 2026 Amendment: Gifts in Return for Contribution Are Excluded From Special Benefits
body: The Civil Act amended on March 17, 2026 added a proviso to Article 1008: if a gift or bequest was made as compensation for specially supporting the deceased or specially contributing to maintaining or increasing their property, it is not treated as a special benefit to the extent that matches the contribution. This rule also applies to inheritances that began on or after April 25, 2024.

In the past, even if you received a house in return for caring for a parent, it was hard to argue back when other siblings called it a special benefit and demanded a deduction. Now, if you prove that the gift was compensation, that portion is not counted as a share received in advance, and the same principle applies to the forced heirship share calculation. Keeping records of the support and of how the gift came about has become important.

steps.title: How Our Family Law Center Handles Your Case

items.title: Timeline of support and contribution
items.desc: We set out year by year when and how you cared for your parent and who paid how much, and also note how involved the other siblings were.

items.title: Gathering evidence
items.desc: We collect transfer records, medical and nursing records, resident registration history, long-term care records and loan repayment records.

items.title: Investigating special benefits
items.desc: We confirm lifetime gifts to siblings through registry records and financial transaction data, and during the case we apply for orders to submit financial transaction information.

items.title: Calculating specific shares
items.desc: We prepare a calculation table including contribution shares and special benefits and use it as the basis for a settlement proposal or the amount claimed.

items.title: Claiming a contribution share
items.desc: If agreement fails, we file the adjudication on division of the estate together with a petition to determine the contribution share, keeping to the filing period set by the court.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: A resident registration abstract showing the period you lived with your parent
Account transfer records for hospital, care and living costs you paid
The guardian entries in medical records and the long-term care grade decision
Materials showing work at your parent's business
Registry records and transfer records for gifts your siblings received
Family messages showing the support or how gifts came about

faqs.q: How much is a contribution share usually?
faqs.a: There is no fixed ratio. The court decides at its discretion, looking at all the circumstances, such as the timing, method and extent of the contribution and the size of the estate. Rather than the ratios circulating online, what matters is showing with documents how special your support was compared with your siblings'.

faqs.q: Can a spouse also receive a contribution share?
faqs.a: A spouse who is a co-heir can also claim a contribution share. However, spouses have a mutual duty of support to begin with, so living together and providing care for a long time is not enough on its own; the spouse must show that the care was special in degree. The Supreme Court has held that long-term cohabitation and care alone do not automatically justify a contribution share.

faqs.q: Does living money I gave my parents count toward a contribution share?
faqs.a: If the monthly money effectively covered your parents' living costs, it may be seen as a contribution, but if it was at the level of pocket money, that is difficult. The answer depends on the period, the amounts and whether your parents had other income.

faqs.q: How can I find out what gifts my brother received?
faqs.a: For real estate, you can check the cause and date of transfer on the registry certificate. Cash gifts are confirmed by searching your parent's account history through the court after filing an adjudication on division of the estate or a forced heirship share lawsuit. Even before a lawsuit, heirs can obtain transaction records after the death, or for a certain period, from financial institutions, so check those first.

areaPages.title: Estate Search and Claims to Recover an Inheritance
areaPages.lead: To settle an inheritance, you first need to know what is left and what has gone. If someone has taken your share as well as theirs, you must claim recovery within 3 years from the day you learned of the infringement.

seo.title: Finding a Deceased Person's Assets in Korea, Withdrawals Before and After Death, and Recovering an Inheritance | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to find assets through the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service and the heir's financial transaction inquiry; how to recover money a sibling withdrew before or after the death or property registered in one sibling's name; the 3-year and 10-year limits for a claim to recover an inheritance; disqualification of heirs and the 2026 expansion of the declaration of loss of inheritance rights; and criminal complaints for embezzlement between relatives.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: My mother's bank account was almost empty just before she died
After our father died, my brother withdrew money using his card and PIN
Without my knowledge, the inheritance was registered in another sibling's name
I think someone secretly used my registered seal to make a division agreement
A parent who left when I was young is demanding my late sibling's death insurance money and estate
Nobody knows where the deceased's assets are or how much there is

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 999 (Right to claim recovery of inheritance)
items.text: If inheritance rights are infringed by a person falsely claiming to be an heir, the rightful heir can file a lawsuit to recover the inheritance. This right expires 3 years after learning of the infringement, or 10 years after the infringing act.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1004 (Grounds for disqualification of heirs)
items.text: A person who intentionally killed or attempted to kill the deceased or certain others, who prevented a will or caused one to be made by fraud or duress, or who forged, altered, destroyed or hid a will cannot be an heir.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1004-2 (Declaration of loss of inheritance rights)
items.text: For an heir who seriously breached the duty of support, committed a serious crime or treated the deceased in a grossly unjust way, the executor (if the deceased expressed this wish in a notarized will) or, if there is no will, the co-heirs may ask the family court to declare loss of inheritance rights within 6 months from the day they learned that person became an heir. Since the amendment of March 17, 2026, this applies to all heirs, not only lineal ascendants.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 328 (Crimes between relatives and complaints)
items.text: Under the amendment of December 31, 2025, embezzlement, fraud and similar crimes between relatives are no longer exempt from punishment but can be prosecuted only upon a complaint, and this applies to offenses committed on or after June 27, 2024. The complaint must be filed within 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 230).

table.title: Ways to Find Assets
rows: Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service

table.note: Based on Government24 and Financial Supervisory Service guidance (October 2026). Processing times differ by agency, so national taxes, financial accounts and pensions may take around 20 days, and financial search results can be viewed on the Financial Supervisory Service website for 3 months from the application date.

sections.title: The Asset Search Starts When You Report the Death
body: Apply for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service (안심상속 원스톱서비스, a government service that searches a deceased person's assets and debts in one application) at the community service center (주민센터, your local district office) when you report the death, or through Government24 (the government's online portal). You can apply within 1 year from the last day of the month of death, and heirs of the first to third rank, heirs by representation and some others are eligible. However, online applications through Government24 are open only to first- and second-rank heirs, so siblings and heirs by representation must visit a community service center. Some results, such as vehicles, come right away, but each agency reports financial and tax results separately by text message, so print the details from each agency's site as soon as you receive the messages. Financial search results can be viewed on the Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원) website only for 3 months from the application date.

The search results often show only that an account exists and its approximate balance. You must apply separately, as an heir, to each financial institution for deposit and withdrawal records from before and after the death, and where money went into another sibling's account is confirmed through the court after filing a lawsuit.

sections.title: Separate Withdrawals Made Before the Death From Those Made After
body: Money taken out before the death still belonged to your parent, so the issues are whether your parent allowed it and what it was used for. If it is confirmed that the money went to hospital or living costs, it is hard to challenge. If it was moved to a sibling's account and used, it is treated as a gift and included in the calculation of special benefits or the forced heirship share, or, if it was taken without permission, you claim its return.

Money taken out after the death already belonged to all the heirs jointly. If one person withdrew and spent other heirs' shares as well, you can claim return of unjust enrichment or damages, and it may also amount to criminal embezzlement or computer-related fraud. For offenses on or after June 27, 2024, the offender can be punished on a complaint even within the family, but there is a 6-month complaint period from the day you learned who the offender was.

sections.title: Claims to Recover an Inheritance Have Strict Time Limits
body: Typical cases for a claim to recover an inheritance (상속회복청구) are where someone who is not an heir acts as an heir and takes the property, or where one co-heir shuts out the others and registers the property in their sole name. Under case law, a co-heir can also be a false heir for the part that exceeds their own share.

This claim cannot be made once 3 years have passed from the day you learned of the infringement, or 10 years from the infringing act. However, where a person who became an heir through acknowledgment or a court judgment after the inheritance began claims the value of an already divided estate (Civil Act Article 1014), the Constitutional Court ruled the 10-years-from-infringement limit unconstitutional on June 27, 2024 (2021헌마1588), so only the 3 years from learning apply. A claim to cancel a registration made with a forged division agreement may also be treated as a claim to recover an inheritance and be subject to these limits, so record the date you checked the registry and act immediately. If the other side is trying to sell the real estate, first apply for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal.

sections.title: When the Right to Be an Heir Itself Is Disputed
body: A person who falls under Civil Act Article 1004, such as someone who forged or hid a will or harmed a parent, automatically cannot be an heir, without any court ruling. By contrast, a person who seriously failed in the duty of support or treated the deceased in a grossly unjust way loses inheritance rights only when the family court's declaration of loss of inheritance rights (상속권 상실 선고) becomes final.

Since the amendment of March 17, 2026, the declaration of loss of inheritance rights has been extended from parents to all heirs, including children and spouses. Co-heirs must file within 6 months from the day they learned that person became an heir, and the court decides by looking at the circumstances and seriousness, the relationship and how the property was built up. A long break in contact alone is not enough; you must show with documents, for example, that the person never paid child support or abandoned the deceased during a long illness.

steps.title: How Our Family Law Center Handles Your Case

items.title: Mapping the estate
items.desc: We gather the Safe Inheritance search results, registry records and transaction records and put the assets, debts and missing money on a single page.

items.title: Analyzing withdrawals
items.desc: We split transactions at the date of death and separate those with a confirmed use, such as hospital costs, from those that need explaining.

items.title: Preservation measures
items.desc: We first freeze real estate or deposits at risk of being disposed of, through provisional injunctions and provisional attachments.

items.title: Choosing the right claim
items.desc: We compare division of the estate, a forced heirship share claim, a claim to recover an inheritance and return of unjust enrichment in terms of time limits and burden of proof, and choose the claim that fits.

items.title: Considering criminal proceedings
items.desc: Where there is also a criminal issue, such as a forged division agreement or unauthorized withdrawals after the death, we decide whether and when to file a complaint in step with the civil proceedings.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Safe Inheritance search results and the detailed records from each financial institution
Transaction records of the deceased's accounts from before and after the death
Real estate registry certificates (to confirm the cause and date of transfer)
Copies of the division agreement or power of attorney (if forgery is suspected)
Messages with siblings about withdrawals or registration
If you are seeking a declaration of loss of inheritance rights, materials showing unpaid child support or abuse

faqs.q: Can I search my cousin's assets through the Safe Inheritance service if I am a fourth-rank heir?
faqs.a: Collateral blood relatives of the fourth rank are not eligible for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service. In that case, you must apply separately to each agency's service, such as the Financial Supervisory Service's inquiry into an heir's financial transactions.

faqs.q: My brother managed our mother's bank account while she was alive and spent her money. Can we get it back?
faqs.a: If he used it for personal purposes without our mother's consent, the claim she had against him for its return is inherited, and each heir can claim their share. If our mother allowed it, the argument is that it was a gift to be counted as a special benefit or in the forced heirship share calculation. Either way, the first step is to organize the timing and use of the withdrawals from the transaction records.

faqs.q: If someone is declared to have lost their inheritance rights, do their children inherit in their place?
faqs.a: Yes. The Civil Act amended on March 17, 2026 provides that the lineal descendants of a person who cannot be an heir because of a declaration of loss of inheritance rights inherit in that person's place (inheritance by representation, 대습상속, Article 1001). However, that person's spouse does not inherit by representation. The same amendment also bars the spouse of a disqualified heir from inheriting by representation (Article 1003(2)).

faqs.q: The tax office has asked me to explain withdrawals made before the death.
faqs.a: If, for each type of property, KRW 200 million or more was withdrawn within 1 year before the inheritance began, or KRW 500 million or more within 2 years, and its use is unclear, it is presumed to have been inherited and is added to the taxable value for inheritance tax (Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (상속세 및 증여세법) Article 15). A tax accountant who cooperates with Jisan Law handles the tax explanation, and if the money turns out to have gone to a sibling, it also affects the division of the estate or the forced heirship share, so it is wise to deal with both together.

areaPages.areaName: Death Insurance, Severance Pay and Survivor Pensions
areaPages.title: Death Insurance, Severance Pay, Survivor Pensions and Inheritance
areaPages.summary: Insurance money and survivor pensions often have a designated recipient, so the rules for dividing them differ from those for the estate.
areaPages.cardLaw: Commercial Act Article 733, National Pension Act Article 73
areaPages.lead: Not all money that comes in after a death is part of the estate. How the insurance contract and the law designate the recipient determines how the money relates to renunciation of inheritance and in what proportions the family shares it.

seo.title: Death Insurance, Severance Pay and Survivor Pensions in Korea: Are They Part of the Estate? | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether death insurance money is part of the estate in Korea depends on who was named as beneficiary. Covers how it is divided when 'legal heirs' are named, insurance paid to someone else and the forced heirship share, the order of recipients for survivor pensions and industrial accident survivor benefits, and accident compensation.
keywords: life insurance forced heirship share Korea

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: The insurance beneficiary is listed only as 'legal heirs', and we siblings disagree about how to split it
A few years before he died, my father changed the insurance beneficiary to someone else
One family member took the whole death severance pay from the company
I am confused about who receives the National Pension survivor pension and whether it is the same as the heirs
My family member died in a traffic accident, and with so much debt I do not know what happens to the compensation if we renounce

items.name: Commercial Act (상법) Article 733 (Right to designate or change the beneficiary)
items.text: The policyholder may designate or change the beneficiary. If the insured event occurs before the policyholder exercises this right, the heirs of the insured person or of the beneficiary become the beneficiaries (paragraph 4).

items.name: National Pension Act (국민연금법) Article 73 (Scope of survivors)
items.text: The survivor pension is paid only to the highest-ranking survivor among those who depended on the insured person for their living at the time of death, in this order: spouse, children (under 25 or with a disability), parents (60 or over or with a disability), grandchildren (under 19 or with a disability) and grandparents. Under this Act, a spouse includes a de facto spouse (Article 3(2)).

items.name: Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act (산업재해보상보험법) Article 65 (Order of survivors entitled to benefits)
items.text: Lump-sum survivor compensation and similar benefits go first to the spouse, children, parents, grandchildren and grandparents who shared a household with the worker at the time of death, and if several people are in the same rank, they share equally. If the worker designated a survivor by will, that designation is followed.

sections.title: Start by Checking Who Is Named as Beneficiary
body: The nature of death insurance money depends on who is written in the beneficiary field of the policy. If a specific person, such as the spouse or a child, is named as beneficiary, the insurance money is that beneficiary's own property. Even if the beneficiary is written only as 'heirs', or the insured event occurred without any beneficiary being named, case law treats the money as the heirs' own property received directly under the insurance contract (Supreme Court Decision 2000다31502 of December 28, 2001; Supreme Court Decision 2003다29463 of July 9, 2004).

So, as a rule, this kind of insurance money can be received regardless of renunciation of inheritance (상속포기), and the deceased's creditors cannot take it as part of the estate. On the other hand, if the beneficiary is the deceased themselves, the insurance money becomes the deceased's property and part of the estate. If you do not have the policy, check the contract terms separately with the insurers shown in the Safe Inheritance (안심상속) search results.

sections.title: If 'Legal Heirs' Are Named, the Money Is Split by Inheritance Shares
body: For accident insurance where the beneficiary was written only as 'legal heirs', the Supreme Court held that, unless there are special circumstances, each heir can claim the portion of the insurance money that corresponds to their inheritance share (Supreme Court Decision 2015다236820 of December 22, 2017). For a mother and two children, for example, the split would be 1.5 to 1 to 1.

If one sibling collected the full amount from the insurer, you can claim back the part that exceeds their share. If a family member renounced the inheritance, whether that person is counted in the proportions may be disputed depending on the policy terms and the case, so check this before claiming from the insurer.

sections.title: If Someone Else Received It, Look at the Forced Heirship Share and Special Benefits
body: Where a father paid the premiums and then changed the beneficiary to someone who is not an heir, and that person received the insurance money, case law treats this as a gift to that person that can be counted in the forced heirship share (유류분) calculation. The amount of the gift is not necessarily the full insurance payout; it can be calculated by multiplying the payout by the proportion of the premiums paid that the father paid (Supreme Court Decision 2020다247428 of August 11, 2022).

If only one of the siblings was named as beneficiary, the dispute is whether that insurance money counts as a share received in advance (special benefit, 특별수익). Documents showing who paid the premiums, when the contract was made and when the beneficiary was changed are important.

sections.title: Severance Pay, Survivor Pensions and Accident Compensation Are Assessed Separately
body: For the National Pension survivor pension and industrial accident survivor benefits, the law sets who receives them and in what order. The test is whether the person shared a household or depended on the deceased, so the recipients may differ from the heirs, and sometimes a de facto spouse receives them. These are not part of the estate, so they can be received even after renouncing the inheritance.

Whether death severance pay is the survivors' own money or part of the estate depends on whether the company's rules or collective agreement provide for it to be paid directly to survivors. If the death was caused by an accident, the deceased's own compensation for emotional distress and lost future income, claimed from the person responsible, is part of the estate, while each survivor's own compensation for emotional distress belongs to that survivor. If you renounce because of debts, you cannot receive the compensation belonging to the deceased, so you need to decide in the right order.

steps.title: How We Sort It Out

items.title: Securing the policy and payment records
items.desc: We obtain the insurance policy, beneficiary change history and the insurer's payment records, and check the rules under which severance pay and pensions are paid.

items.title: Classifying each payment
items.desc: We sort the money into estate property, the beneficiary's own property and statutory survivor benefits in a table, and look at how each affects renunciation or limited acceptance.

items.title: Calculating proportions and refunds
items.desc: We compare the money to be split by inheritance shares with what one person has already taken, and calculate the amount to be returned.

items.title: Reviewing the forced heirship share and special benefits
items.desc: If a third party or one sibling received insurance money, we prepare a forced heirship share or special benefit argument based on the premium payment records.

items.title: Agreement or a claim
items.desc: If a family agreement is difficult, we resolve it through a claim for return or within the division of the estate proceedings.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Insurance policies and the results of an insurance policy search
The beneficiary change history and payment records from the insurer
The company's severance pay rules or collective agreement and the severance pay statement
Survivor benefit decision notices from the National Pension Service or other bodies
Materials on how the accident happened and records of contact with the other side's insurer
A detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) based on the deceased

faqs.q: My brother was the insurance beneficiary, so he received the money alone. Do I have no rights at all?
faqs.a: The insurance money itself is your brother's own property as beneficiary, so it is hard to demand that it be split directly. However, if your father paid the premiums, it may be counted as a share your brother received in advance in the division of the estate, or you may be able to examine whether your forced heirship share was infringed. Start by checking who paid the premiums and how much.

faqs.q: Does my mother have to share her National Pension survivor pension with us children?
faqs.a: No. The survivor pension is paid only to the highest-ranking survivor in the order set by law, and it is not part of the estate (National Pension Act Article 73). While the spouse is receiving it, nothing is paid to the children.

faqs.q: The other side in the accident is offering a settlement, but we are thinking of renouncing because of debts.
faqs.a: The damages belonging to the deceased are part of the estate, so receiving and spending them may count as simple acceptance (단순승인), and if you renounce, you cannot receive them. Each survivor's own compensation for emotional distress can be received separately. Compare the debts with the amount of compensation, decide first whether renunciation or limited acceptance (한정승인) is better, and only then agree to a settlement.

areaPages.title: Transferring Title to Inherited Real Estate and Inheritance Registration
areaPages.summary: There is no deadline for registration itself, but acquisition tax must be paid within 6 months, and if the heirs cannot agree, the registration method changes from the start.
areaPages.cardLaw: Registration of Real Estate Act Article 23, Local Tax Act Article 20
areaPages.lead: Transferring a parent's home into an heir's name is not difficult if the documents are in order. But if one sibling will not stamp the documents, or there is a loan on the home, getting the order wrong costs extra time and tax.

seo.title: Inheritance Registration and Transferring Title to Inherited Property in Korea When Heirs Disagree | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: To transfer title to inherited real estate in Korea, you first decide between registration by division agreement and registration by statutory shares. A step-by-step guide covering the acquisition tax deadline, heirs who will not stamp the agreement, settling the loan on a mortgaged home, and sole registration after a court adjudication.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: We want to put the house in our mother's name, but one sibling will not send their certificate of seal impression
I heard there is a fine if we put off registration, and I am worried
There is still a loan on my father's house, and I do not know whether to register first or take over the debt first
Another sibling registered the property in statutory shares without asking me
The adjudication on division of the estate is over, but I do not know how to register the property

items.name: Registration of Real Estate Act (부동산등기법) Article 23 (Applicants for registration)
items.text: As a rule, the person acquiring the right and the person obliged to register apply together, but registration based on universal succession, such as inheritance, is applied for by the person acquiring the right alone (paragraph 3). Registration based on a judgment can also be applied for by the winning party alone (paragraph 4).

items.name: Local Tax Act (지방세법) Article 20 (Reporting and payment)
items.text: Acquisition tax on real estate acquired by inheritance must be reported and paid within 6 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began, or 9 months if an heir has an address abroad.

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1015 (Retroactive effect of division)
items.text: Division of the estate takes effect back to the time the inheritance began, but it cannot harm rights acquired by third parties in the meantime.

sections.title: First Decide on the Registration Method
body: There are two main types of inheritance registration (상속등기). One is registration by division agreement, where all the heirs agree on who takes how much. The other is registration by statutory shares, where all the heirs' names are entered in the proportions set by law. Registration by division agreement requires an agreement on division of the estate and certificates of seal impression (인감증명서) from all the heirs, while one heir can apply for registration by statutory shares in all the heirs' names.

Registration by statutory shares is a way to secure the rights for now when there is no agreement, but afterwards, selling the home or taking out a loan again requires the consent of all the co-owners. If you later reach agreement and correct the registration, separate tax issues can arise, so get tax advice in advance.

sections.title: There Is No Registration Deadline, but There Is an Acquisition Tax Deadline
body: No provision sets a deadline for inheritance registration, so registering late does not by itself lead to a fine. The Act on Special Measures for the Registration of Real Estate, which sets registration deadlines for contracts such as sales, does not apply to inheritance either.

However, acquisition tax must be reported and paid within 6 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began, and a penalty tax is added after that. Also keep in mind that if another heir dies while you wait, both the paperwork and the number of parties increase.

sections.title: If an Heir Will Not Stamp the Agreement
body: If even one heir does not stamp the agreement with their registered seal, registration by division agreement is not possible. In that case, apply to the family court for mediation on division of the estate (상속재산분할), and once the mediation or adjudication becomes final, apply for registration in the chosen person's name using the mediation record or written decision.
