If an heir cannot be reached, an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인) must be appointed first, and if an heir is a minor, a special representative (특별대리인). A person whose renunciation has been accepted is left out of the agreement, and the written decision on the renunciation is attached to the registration application.

sections.title: Settle a Mortgaged Home Together With the Bank
body: The deceased's loans pass to the heirs according to their inheritance shares, separately from the home. Even if the siblings agree that the person who takes the home will also take on the whole loan, the other siblings remain liable to the bank unless the bank consents (Civil Act Article 454).

So you need to coordinate with the bank in advance on the order of registration and assumption of the debt. If there is a tenant, the obligation to return the lease deposit is also inherited, so state in the agreement who will bear it.

steps.title: How We Take You Through to Registration

items.title: Confirming heirs and shares
items.desc: We confirm every heir through the certificate of removed family register (제적등본) and family relationship documents, and calculate the statutory shares.

items.title: Deciding the registration method
items.desc: We decide whether to go with division by agreement or to register statutory shares first, looking at taxes and plans for later sale together.

items.title: Drafting the agreement or applying for mediation
items.desc: If there is agreement, we draft it so the property descriptions match the registry; if not, we apply for mediation on division of the estate.

items.title: Acquisition tax return and registration application
items.desc: We file the acquisition tax return within the deadline and apply for registration with the agreement or written decision attached. Jisan Law also handles the registration application.

items.title: Settling loans and leases
items.desc: We decide who will assume the mortgage loan and the obligation to return the tenant's deposit, and notify the bank and the tenant.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: A full certificate of the real estate registry
The deceased's basic certificate (기본증명서), detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) and certificate of removed family register
For division by agreement, certificates of seal impression and resident registration certificates (주민등록등본) of all the heirs
If any heir renounced, the written decision on the renunciation
A loan balance certificate and the lease agreement
Text or KakaoTalk messages with siblings about the agreement

faqs.q: If we register by statutory shares, do we not need an agreement?
faqs.a: Correct. One heir can apply for registration by statutory shares in all the heirs' names, and the other heirs' certificates of seal impression are not required. However, keep in mind that acquisition tax must be paid on all the heirs' shares, and that selling the home or using it as collateral later requires everyone's consent.

faqs.q: My sibling registered the property in statutory shares, including my share. Is that invalid?
faqs.a: Any heir can register according to statutory shares, so that registration is not invalid in itself. Your share is also in your name, so the actual shares can be decided later in a division agreement or adjudication. However, if your share was left out or the agreement was fabricated, you can claim cancellation of the registration, and we also consider criminal issues.

faqs.q: Can we do the inheritance registration ourselves?
faqs.a: Yes. Heirs can apply at the registry office themselves. However, when there are many heirs, or a mix of heirs by representation, minors and people who renounced, orders to correct are common, so having the list of heirs and the share calculation checked in advance saves time.

areaPages.areaName: Selling Co-inherited Real Estate and Partition of Co-owned Property
areaPages.title: Selling Co-inherited Real Estate and Partition of Co-owned Property
areaPages.summary: Before the estate is divided, you go to the family court for division of the estate, not a partition lawsuit; after division, an auction is also possible.
areaPages.lead: A home left in the joint names of siblings cannot be sold if even one of them objects, and conflict grows when one of them moves in. Which court you go to depends on whether the estate has not yet been divided or whether the property remains co-owned after division.

seo.title: Selling Jointly Inherited Property in Korea and Partition of Co-owned Property | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when you want to sell real estate inherited in siblings' joint names but a sibling objects, or one sibling is living there alone. Covers the difference between an adjudication on division of the estate and a lawsuit for partition of co-owned property, when the property is divided by auction, claiming a usage fee, and provisional injunctions.
keywords: sibling refuses to sell inherited house Korea

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: Our parents' apartment is in the joint names of three siblings, and one refuses to sell
My brother moved into the inherited house alone and pays nothing for using it
Property tax and maintenance fees keep going out, but the sale has been stuck for years
We siblings do not know how to divide a single plot of rural land
My sibling says they will sell their share to a stranger

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1013 (Division by agreement)
items.text: Co-heirs may divide the estate by agreement at any time, and if they cannot agree, the court divides it, applying Article 269 on the method of partitioning co-owned property.

items.name: Civil Act Article 265 (Management and preservation of co-owned property)
items.text: Matters concerning the management of co-owned property are decided by a majority of the co-owners' shares, and each co-owner can carry out acts of preservation alone.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 268 and 269 (Claim for partition and method of partition)
items.text: A co-owner may claim partition of the co-owned property, and if there is no agreement, may ask the court. If the property cannot be divided in kind, or dividing it is likely to greatly reduce its value, the court may order an auction.

sections.title: Before Division, Go to the Family Court
body: If the heirs have not yet agreed on a division, you cannot single out one house and file a lawsuit for partition of co-owned property (공유물분할). The Supreme Court has held that in this case you can only ask the family court for an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할) (Supreme Court Decision 2015다18367 of August 13, 2015). This is so even if the property has been registered in statutory shares.

In an adjudication on division of the estate, the court looks not only at that house but also at deposits, other real estate and lifetime gifts together, and decides who gets what. It may give the house to one person and have them pay the other siblings the difference in money, or have it sold and the proceeds divided.

sections.title: Co-ownership After Division: A Partition Lawsuit
body: Once the siblings have agreed on joint ownership, or the shares have been fixed by adjudication, it becomes an ordinary co-ownership. You then file a lawsuit for partition of co-owned property, and for apartments or small plots of land that are hard to divide, the judgment often orders a sale by auction with the proceeds divided by share.

Because an auction may sell below market price, the case is sometimes settled during the lawsuit by one person buying the other siblings' shares. Applying for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal of the other side's share before the lawsuit prevents that share from passing to a third party in the meantime.

sections.title: If One Person Is Using It Alone
body: Each co-owner may use the whole of the co-owned property in proportion to their share (Civil Act Article 263). If one sibling is using the house alone beyond their share, the other siblings first consider claiming a usage fee for their share as unjust enrichment.

However, under a Supreme Court en banc decision, a sibling with a minority share cannot demand that another sibling with a minority share hand over the entire house. Instead, they can demand that the other stop preventing shared use (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2018다287522 of May 21, 2020). Also keep in mind that decisions on management, such as renting the house out, can be made by a majority of the shares.

steps.title: How We Resolve Joint Ownership

items.title: Before or after division
items.desc: We look at the cause of registration and whether there is a division agreement, and first determine whether you are at the division of the estate stage or in ordinary co-ownership.

items.title: Market value and current use
items.desc: We organize market price data, who actually lives there, and who has paid the taxes and maintenance fees.

items.title: Considering a provisional injunction
items.desc: If the other side may sell or mortgage their share, we first apply for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal or an interim measure (사전처분).

items.title: Mediation, adjudication or a lawsuit
items.desc: Before division, we pursue mediation and adjudication in the family court; after division, a partition lawsuit and a claim for a usage fee.

items.title: Sale and settling shares
items.desc: Depending on the outcome, we complete the purchase of shares, or the sale or auction and the distribution of the proceeds.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: A full certificate of the real estate registry and documents showing the cause of registration (agreement or written decision)
Recent actual transaction prices or market price data
Records of property tax and maintenance fee payments and who actually paid
If a sibling lives there, when they moved in and how the property is used
Text or KakaoTalk messages about the sale

faqs.q: Does a partition lawsuit always end in an auction?
faqs.a: No. The court orders an auction when the property cannot be divided in kind or dividing it would greatly reduce its value. Property that is hard to divide, such as a single apartment, often goes to auction, but cases are also settled by one person buying the other shares.

faqs.q: What happens if my sibling sells their share to someone else?
faqs.a: A co-owner is free to dispose of their share, so there is little legal basis for stopping it (Civil Act Article 263). The buyer becomes a new co-owner and may file for partition, so if a dispute seems to be starting, consider a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal. If the estate has not yet been divided, you can also apply for an interim measure together with the request for division.

faqs.q: I live in the house and have paid the property tax and maintenance fees. Can I be reimbursed?
faqs.a: Co-owners bear management costs and other obligations in proportion to their shares (Civil Act Article 266), so if you paid other siblings' shares, you can ask for reimbursement. On the other hand, they may argue that you should pay a usage fee for the benefit of living there alone, so the two need to be calculated together.

areaPages.title: Inheriting a Family Business and Disputes Over Control
areaPages.summary: With a corporation, it is the shares that are inherited, not the company's property, and until the shares are divided, even deciding who votes them can stall.
areaPages.cardLaw: Commercial Act Article 333, Civil Act Articles 1008-2 and 1013
areaPages.lead: If your parent ran a shop or a company, the scope of the estate and the debts, and who will carry on the business, all come into play at once. What is inherited differs from the start depending on whether it was a sole proprietorship or a corporation.

seo.title: Inheriting a Family Business or Company Shares in Korea: Control and Sibling Disputes | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Issues that arise in Korea when inheriting a parent's sole proprietorship or corporate shares. Covers business debts and limited acceptance, the representative for co-owned shares, gaps in leadership, the contribution share of a child who built up the company, and shares held in other people's names.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: We do not know how much my father's restaurant owes suppliers and lenders
My brother, who actually ran the company, says he will take all the shares
Because the shares have not been divided, the shareholders' meeting cannot choose a new representative director
I found out that some of my father's company shares were held in an employee's name
My siblings want to split everything equally between me, who helped build the company, and those who did not

items.name: Commercial Act (상법) Article 333 (Co-owned shares)
items.text: When shares are co-owned by several people, the co-owners must choose one person to exercise the shareholder's rights, and if there is no such person, the company need only give notice to one of the co-owners.

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 1008-2 (Contribution share)
items.text: A co-heir who specially supported the deceased for a considerable period, or who specially contributed to maintaining or increasing the deceased's property, can have a contribution share recognized by agreement or by a family court decision.

items.name: Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (상속세 및 증여세법) Article 18-2 (Family business succession deduction)
items.text: When a small or medium-sized business or similar enterprise that the deceased ran continuously for 10 years or more is inherited, a certain amount is deducted from the taxable value for inheritance tax. There are separate requirements for the heirs and for post-inheritance compliance.

sections.title: What Is Inherited Differs for Sole Proprietorships and Corporations
body: If your parent was a sole proprietor, business assets such as the shop deposit, stock and equipment pass to the heirs, and so do debts such as unpaid supplier invoices, business loans and unpaid wages. The books are often not in order, so if you do not know how much is owed, consider limited acceptance (한정승인) within 3 months as well.

With a corporation, the company's building and deposits belong to the company, and what is inherited is the shares the deceased held. If the representative director acted as joint and several surety for company loans, those surety obligations are inherited, so the company's financial condition must also be examined.

sections.title: Voting Rights Are Frozen Until the Shares Are Divided
body: Inherited shares are co-owned by the heirs until division, and voting rights on co-owned shares can only be exercised once one person has been chosen to exercise them. If the siblings cannot agree on that person, electing a new representative director or making important decisions at the shareholders' meeting can come to a halt.

That is why agreements that give the shares to the person who will carry on the company and settle with the other heirs through real estate or cash are common. If no agreement is reached, the family court decides the method of division by looking at the nature of the assets, the relationship among the heirs and the state of the business. For unlisted shares, even the valuation method becomes a point of dispute, and since who takes over the company is tied to the requirements for the family business succession deduction, it is wise to get a tax review at the same time.

sections.title: Contribution to Building the Company and Shares in Other People's Names
body: A child who helped their father build up the company and increase its value can claim a contribution share (기여분). The court looks at whether the child was paid a proper salary, whether they put personal money into the company and what roles the other siblings played. Conversely, if a child received a high salary or shares from the company in advance, these may be counted as special benefits (특별수익).

If the deceased placed shares in the name of an employee or relative, you must show that the deceased was the real owner, using records of payment for the shares or the flow of dividends, and include the shares in the estate. If the named holder will not return them, a separate lawsuit is needed.

steps.title: How We Handle an Inheritance Involving a Business

items.title: Identifying business assets and debts
items.desc: We gather the books, business bank accounts, tax filings, receivables, payables and surety records to estimate the net assets.

items.title: Deciding on acceptance or renunciation
items.desc: If the debts may be larger, we decide on limited acceptance or renunciation within 3 months, and then whether to keep running the business or wind it up.

items.title: Preventing a management gap
items.desc: For a corporation, we choose the person to exercise the rights of the co-owned shares and check the articles of incorporation and shareholder register to set up how decisions will be made for now.

items.title: Preparing a division proposal
items.desc: We combine shares, real estate and cash to calculate the shares of the person taking over the company and those to be paid out.

items.title: Mediation, adjudication and follow-up lawsuits
items.desc: If agreement fails, we pursue an adjudication on division of the estate and a contribution share claim, and if needed, a lawsuit to recover shares held in another person's name.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The business registration certificate, and tax returns and financial statements for the last few years
The articles of incorporation, shareholder register and records of changes in shareholding
Business bank accounts and loan and surety documents
Lists of receivables and payables with business partners
The staff list and records of wage and severance pay
Salary and investment records of family members involved in running the company

faqs.q: If I carry on running my father's shop, can I no longer renounce the inheritance?
faqs.a: Using or disposing of the shop's assets as an heir can be treated as simple acceptance (단순승인), after which renunciation or limited acceptance may be blocked. If you do not know how large the debts are, consider limited acceptance before continuing the business, and think about the effect before disposing of stock or equipment as well.

faqs.q: While he was alive, my father transferred all his company shares to my brother. Can I claim a forced heirship share?
faqs.a: If you are his child, you can. For inheritances that began on or after March 17, 2026, the rule is that you receive the value in money rather than the shares themselves. How the unlisted shares are valued will decide the amount, so first secure the company's financial records.

faqs.q: My father, the representative director, was a surety for the company's loan. Isn't it fine as long as the company repays it?
faqs.a: Surety obligations are inherited, so if the company cannot repay, the heirs may be asked to pay. If the company is in poor financial shape, weigh the value of the shares against the surety risk and consider limited acceptance.

areaPages.areaName: Lifetime Gift Disputes and Filial Support Contracts
areaPages.title: Invalidating or Reclaiming Lifetime Gifts, and Filial Support Contracts
areaPages.summary: A gift already registered in the recipient's name is hard to undo just because the giver changed their mind; whether the gift came with conditions is the turning point.
areaPages.lead: When the relationship sours after parents transfer property to a child, or there is suspicion that a gift was made while a parent's judgment was impaired, the question is whether the gift can be undone. When the gift was made, on what conditions and in what state of mind decides the outcome.

seo.title: Reclaiming a Lifetime Gift, Cancelling a Filial Support Contract, and Gifts by Parents With Dementia in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether a parent in Korea can get back a gift made to a child. Covers rescinding an unwritten gift, the recipient's ingratitude and the 6-month period, the limits once a gift has been performed, cancelling a filial support contract, and challenging a gift made by a parent with dementia as invalid.
keywords: gift cancellation duty of support Korea
gift by parent with dementia invalid Korea

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: I transferred my house to my son, and since then he has not called or sent living money
I made the gift after he promised to live with and look after me, but he has not kept that promise
I found out late that my mother's building was gifted to my older brother after her dementia began
My child is demanding money I only promised verbally
I think a sibling forged documents with our parent's registered seal to transfer land

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 555 (Gifts not made in writing and rescission)
items.text: If the intention to give was not expressed in writing, either party may rescind the gift.

items.name: Civil Act Articles 556 and 558 (Recipient's conduct and rescission; rescission and performed parts)
items.text: If the recipient commits a crime against the giver or the giver's spouse or lineal blood relatives, or fails to perform their duty of support toward the giver, the giver may rescind the gift. This right lapses 6 months after the giver learns of the cause, or if the giver forgives the recipient, and such rescission does not affect parts already performed.

items.name: Civil Act Article 561 (Gift with a burden)
items.text: For a gift that places a burden on the recipient, the provisions on bilateral contracts apply in addition to those on gifts.

sections.title: Property Already Transferred Is Hard to Recover Through Ordinary Rescission
body: A gift promised only verbally, without anything in writing, can be rescinded if it has not yet been carried out. A gift can also be rescinded if the child commits a crime against the parent or abandons their duty of support, but this must be done within 6 months from the day the parent learned of the cause.

The problem arises once the registration has been transferred or the money handed over. The law provides that even when these grounds for rescission exist, they do not affect parts already performed (Civil Act Article 558), so it is difficult to get back a house whose registration has already been transferred on the basis of these provisions alone.

sections.title: A Gift With Conditions Is a Different Story
body: A gift made on condition that the child lives with the parent or pays hospital bills is a gift with a burden (부담부증여). The Supreme Court has held that if the recipient fails to perform that obligation, the giver can cancel the contract even if the gift has already been carried out, and Articles 555 and 558 do not apply in that case (Supreme Court Decision 97다2177 of July 8, 1997).

However, the giver must show that there was a condition. What matters is whether the gift contract sets out the support specifically, and whether there are text messages or records of living-money transfers showing the promise was broken. A vague phrase such as 'I will be a good child' is hard to use as a standard.

sections.title: A Gift Made While Judgment Was Impaired Can Be Challenged as Invalid
body: If, at the time of the gift, the parent could not understand what they were doing because of dementia or a similar condition, the gift is void for lack of mental capacity. The key evidence is medical records, cognitive test results and care records from around the time of the gift, and what matters is the person's condition on that day rather than the diagnosis.

As a rule, while the parent is alive, the other children have no right to challenge the gift directly. If the parent cannot challenge it themselves, you apply for adult guardianship (성년후견) so that the guardian can sue on their behalf. After the parent dies, the heirs take over that right, and even if the gift is not void, the calculation is redone through special benefits or the forced heirship share.

steps.title: How We Handle Gift Disputes

items.title: Confirming how the gift was made
items.desc: We use the registry, the gift contract and account transfer records to confirm what was transferred, when and on what conditions.

items.title: Gathering evidence of the parent's condition
items.desc: We obtain medical records, cognitive tests and care records from around the time of the gift, and see whether mental capacity can be challenged.

items.title: Choosing the claim
items.desc: Among cancelling a gift with a burden, invalidity for lack of mental capacity and rescission for ingratitude, we choose the route that fits the deadlines and available evidence.

items.title: Provisional injunction and lawsuit
items.desc: We apply for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal so the property is not sold on, and claim cancellation of the ownership transfer registration or similar relief.

items.title: Linking to settlement after the inheritance
items.desc: If the parent has died, we continue by resolving the matter through the special benefit and forced heirship share calculations.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The real estate registry and the gift contract
The parent's medical records, dementia diagnosis and long-term care recognition documents from before and after the gift
Text messages or recordings of the child's promise of support
Bank records showing when living-money transfers stopped
A copy of the gift tax return (if any)

faqs.q: Our filial support contract was not notarized. Is it still valid?
faqs.a: Notarization is not a requirement for validity. A contract signed by the parties is enough to support a gift with a burden. However, how it was made or whether the signatures are genuine may be disputed later, so notarizing it makes proof easier.

faqs.q: If the gift is cancelled and returned, will tax be charged again?
faqs.a: Depending on when and how the property is returned, gift tax issues can arise again. We decide the timing and method of return together with a review by a tax accountant who cooperates with Jisan Law.

faqs.q: My brother took our father's registered seal and secretly registered a gift to himself.
faqs.a: If our father had no intention of making a gift, there was no gift at all, so the registration has no valid cause. Our father himself or his guardian can claim its cancellation, and if documents were fabricated to register it, we also consider criminal issues such as forgery of private documents or false entries in an authenticated original document.

areaPages.areaName: Children Born Outside Marriage, Acknowledgment Claims and Inheritance
areaPages.title: Inheritance by Children Born Outside Marriage and Acknowledgment Claims After the Father's Death
areaPages.summary: After the father has died, a child must file an acknowledgment claim against the prosecutor within 2 years from the day they learned of the death to become an heir.
areaPages.lead: A child born outside marriage receives the same share as any other child once they are legally established as the father's child. But if the father has already died, an acknowledgment claim has a deadline, and if the estate has already been divided, the claim becomes one for money.

seo.title: Inheritance Rights of a Child Born Outside Marriage in Korea: Acknowledgment Claims and DNA Testing | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: In Korea, a child born outside marriage must file an acknowledgment claim within 2 years from learning of the father's death to become an heir. Covers how DNA testing works, claiming the value of an estate already divided, and what the other heirs should check when such a child comes forward, from both sides.
keywords: child born outside marriage inheritance Korea
claim for value of inheritance share Korea
illegitimate child forced heirship share Korea

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: Someone I had never seen came to my father's funeral and said they were also his child
My father is not listed in my family relationship register, but I heard my biological father has died
My paternity was only confirmed after my siblings had already divided the estate
We were asked to take a DNA test, but my father's family will not cooperate
I found records showing my father sent money to a child born outside marriage while he was alive

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Articles 863 and 864 (Action for acknowledgment; death of a parent and action for acknowledgment)
items.text: A child, the child's lineal descendants or legal representative may file an action for acknowledgment against the father or mother, and if the parent has died, the action must be filed against the prosecutor within 2 years from the day the death became known.

items.name: Civil Act Article 860 (Retroactive effect of acknowledgment)
items.text: Acknowledgment takes effect back to the child's birth, but it cannot harm rights a third party has already acquired.

items.name: Civil Act Article 1014 (Claim of an acknowledged child after division)
items.text: A person who becomes a co-heir through acknowledgment or a final court judgment after the inheritance began may, if the other co-heirs have already divided or disposed of the estate, claim payment of the value corresponding to their share.

sections.title: The Child Must Be Legally Established as the Father's Child
body: The legal relationship with the mother arises from giving birth, but the relationship with the father arises only when he registers an acknowledgment (인지) or it is established by a court judgment. Once acknowledged, the child has the same rank and the same share in the inheritance as a child born within marriage.

While the father is alive, an acknowledgment claim (인지청구) can be made at any time, but after his death, the action must be filed with the family court against the prosecutor within 2 years from the day the child learned of the death. This deadline is sometimes missed while talks about the estate drag on, so check the dates first.

sections.title: DNA Testing Is Done With the Father's Blood Relatives
body: If the father has already died, paternity is confirmed through DNA testing with his blood relatives, such as half-siblings or the father's parents or siblings. If they refuse, you can ask the court for an order to submit to testing, and the court can order testing when it is hard to decide on other evidence (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 29).

Apart from the test, records of child support or living money sent by the father, photos and letters together, and statements from people who knew them are supporting evidence. Because of the 2-year deadline, prepare to gather evidence and file the action at the same time.

sections.title: An Estate Already Divided Is Claimed as Value
body: If the other heirs divided or sold the estate before the acknowledgment became final, rather than having the division declared void, the child claims payment of money corresponding to their share. This claim must be made within 3 years from the day the child learned of the infringement, and the 10-years-from-infringement limit does not apply, because on June 27, 2024 the Constitutional Court ruled it unconstitutional as applied to this claim (2021헌마1588).

If you are on the side where such a child has come forward, it is safer to settle who the heirs are before rushing a division agreement. If the estate is settled while the acknowledgment lawsuit is pending, you will later face a claim for value, and the date for valuing the property also becomes a point of dispute. If the father gave money to the child born outside marriage during his lifetime, you can argue that it was a special benefit (특별수익).

steps.title: How We Handle Acknowledgment and Inheritance

items.title: Calculating the deadlines
items.desc: We confirm the day you learned of the father's death and set out the 2-year deadline for the acknowledgment claim and the 3-year deadline for a claim for value.

items.title: Gathering evidence
items.desc: We collect family relationship documents, child support transfer records, photos, letters and contact records.

items.title: Filing the acknowledgment claim
items.desc: We file the action with the family court against the prosecutor and decide who should take the DNA test and whether to ask for a testing order.

items.title: Taking part in the inheritance
items.desc: Once the acknowledgment is final, you take part in the division agreement or adjudication as an heir, and if there are debts, we also consider renunciation or limited acceptance.

items.title: Claim for value and forced heirship share
items.desc: For an estate already divided, we claim payment of value, and if gifts were concentrated on one person, we also claim the forced heirship share.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Your basic certificate (기본증명서) and detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서)
Text messages or other contact showing the father's death and the day you learned of it
Records of child support or living money transfers
Photos, letters and messages with the father
Contact details of the father's relatives who might cooperate with a DNA test

faqs.q: If the court acknowledges me as his child, do I also inherit my father's debts?
faqs.a: You become an heir, so debts also pass to you in proportion to your share. Consider renunciation or limited acceptance within 3 months from the day you learned you became an heir. If the debts may exceed the assets, check the state of the estate from the acknowledgment lawsuit stage.

faqs.q: If a child born outside marriage becomes an heir, how much does my share shrink?
faqs.a: Children's shares are equal, so each share shrinks as the number of children grows. If an inheritance shared by a spouse and two children gains one more child, it is redivided at a ratio of 1.5 for the spouse and 1 for each child.

faqs.q: My birth mother, who did not raise me, has died. Am I one of her heirs?
faqs.a: The parent-child relationship with a mother arises from birth, so you are an heir without any separate acknowledgment. If the mother-child relationship is not recorded in the family relationship register, you may first need to resolve it through a procedure such as an action to confirm the existence of a biological parent-child relationship.

areaPages.areaName: Heirs Living Abroad and Foreign Assets
areaPages.title: Heirs Living Abroad, Foreign Nationality and Inheriting Overseas Assets
areaPages.summary: The deceased's nationality decides which inheritance law applies, and heirs abroad need documents authenticated differently, so they should start counting the deadlines earlier.
areaPages.cardLaw: Act on Private International Law Articles 77 and 78
areaPages.lead: If one of the heirs lives abroad, the deceased held a foreign nationality, or there are assets in another country, the first questions are which country's law applies and how to prepare the documents. The deadlines run the same way even if you are abroad.

seo.title: Inheritance in Korea for Heirs Living Abroad, Foreign Nationals and Overseas Assets | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Inheritance when an heir lives abroad, or the deceased had a foreign nationality or overseas assets. Covers which country's law applies (Act on Private International Law Article 77), authentication at Korean diplomatic missions and apostilles, reporting a foreign national's inheritance of Korean real estate, and procedures for overseas assets.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: My brother, a US citizen, is inheriting our parents' property in Korea together with us
My sibling in Canada does not know what is needed to sign the division agreement
My father, who had become a foreign national, died leaving land in Korea
My mother had a foreign bank account and a house overseas in her name
Living abroad, I am worried I will miss the deadline to renounce the inheritance

items.name: Act on Private International Law (국제사법) Article 77 (Inheritance)
items.text: Inheritance is governed by the law of the deceased's home country at the time of death. However, if the deceased expressly chose, in a form that applies to wills, the law of their habitual residence or, for real estate, the law of the place where it is located, that law applies.

items.name: Act on Private International Law Article 78 (Wills)
items.text: The form of a will is valid if it meets any one of the following: the law of the testator's nationality, the law of their habitual residence, the law of the place where the will was made, or, for real estate, the law of the place where it is located (paragraph 3).

items.name: Act on Report on Real Estate Transactions (부동산 거래신고 등에 관한 법률) Article 8 (Report of acquisition and holding of real estate by foreigners)
items.text: A foreigner or similar person who acquires real estate or similar property in Korea by inheritance must report it to the competent authority within 6 months from the date of acquisition (paragraph 2).

sections.title: First, Which Country's Law Applies
body: Who the heirs are and how much each receives is decided by the law of the deceased's nationality at the time of death. If the deceased was a Korean national, the Korean Civil Act (민법) applies whether an heir is a US citizen or lives in Japan, and an heir's nationality does not change their share.

If the deceased held a foreign nationality, that country's law applies in principle. However, if that country's law in turn refers back to Korean law, Korean law may apply (Act on Private International Law Article 22), and the deceased may have chosen the law of the place where real estate is located in a will, so each case must be examined.

sections.title: Overseas Assets Go Through That Country's Procedures Separately
body: Even after Korean law has decided the heirs and their shares, transferring a foreign bank account or foreign real estate often requires going through a court or agency in that country. Some countries require a procedure in which a court-appointed administrator settles the estate before distributing it, so plan the schedule together with a local lawyer.

Whether a Korean judgment or adjudication on division of the estate is recognized as it is abroad also differs by country. If the overseas assets are large, deciding at the start which country's procedure to go through first reduces costs.

sections.title: Documents and Deadlines for Heirs Abroad
body: Korean nationals living abroad usually have their signature on the division agreement or power of attorney authenticated at a Korean embassy or consulate in their country of residence, in place of a certificate of seal impression (인감증명서). Foreign nationals need local notarization plus an apostille or consular confirmation, and a translation, and should also prepare documents showing that their Korean name and the name in their foreign passport belong to the same person.

The 3-month period for renunciation (상속포기) and limited acceptance (한정승인) runs the same way even if you are abroad. Authenticating documents can take several weeks, so consider appointing a representative in Korea by power of attorney or asking for an extension of the period. For acquisition tax and inheritance tax, the filing deadline is extended to 9 months if an heir has an address abroad.

steps.title: How We Prepare an Inheritance With an Overseas Element

items.title: Confirming nationality and where assets are
items.desc: We set out in a table the deceased's nationality at the time of death, each heir's nationality and country of residence, and the countries where assets are located.

items.title: Reviewing the applicable law
items.desc: We look at which country's law decides the heirs and shares, and whether any will is valid in form.

items.title: Deciding on document formats
items.desc: For each heir, we decide and explain whether they need authentication at a Korean mission, local notarization and an apostille, or a translation.

items.title: Proceedings in Korea
items.desc: We handle the division agreement, renunciation or limited acceptance, inheritance registration and the report of a foreigner's acquisition of real estate within the deadlines.

items.title: Coordinating with overseas procedures
items.desc: For overseas assets, we check whether local procedures are needed and decide which documents will carry the Korean outcome over.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The deceased's nationality and residence history (passport, record of loss of Korean nationality)
Each heir's passport and documents showing their address in their country of residence
A list of overseas accounts and real estate, and the local documents
If there is a will, the original and the country where it was made
Korean family relationship documents and the certificate of removed family register (제적등본)

faqs.q: Does my sibling with foreign nationality also inherit our parents' house in Korea?
faqs.a: Yes. The inheritance of parents who were Korean nationals follows the Korean Civil Act, and an heir's nationality does not affect their inheritance rights. However, a foreigner who acquires real estate in Korea by inheritance must report it within 6 months.

faqs.q: I live abroad. Can I renounce the inheritance without going to Korea?
faqs.a: Yes. A common method is to authorize a representative in Korea with authenticated documents to file with the family court. Getting documents authenticated takes time, so count back from the 3-month deadline and start early.

faqs.q: Is a will written abroad valid in Korea?
faqs.a: The form of a will is valid if it meets the law of the testator's nationality, habitual residence or the place where it was made, or, for real estate, the law of the place where it is located (Act on Private International Law Article 78(3)). A will written in a foreign form can be valid, but carrying it out in Korea may require separate steps such as a court inspection or translation and authentication.

areaPages.areaName: Adult Guardianship and Managing the Assets of a Parent With Dementia
areaPages.title: Adult Guardianship and Disputes Over Managing the Assets of a Parent With Dementia
areaPages.summary: A dementia diagnosis alone does not give a child the authority to act on a parent's behalf; the family court chooses the guardian on its own authority and supervises them.
areaPages.lead: When dementia makes it hard for a parent to manage their own property, disputes among siblings begin even before any inheritance: who will handle the bank accounts and the house, and what to do about money that has gone missing in the meantime. The path the law provides is guardianship through the family court.

seo.title: Adult Guardianship in Korea: Managing a Parent's Assets With Dementia and Sibling Disputes | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: To protect the assets of a parent with dementia in Korea, you need to know whether adult, limited or specific guardianship fits, who can apply and how the court chooses the guardian. Covers psychiatric evaluation, the list of assets, court permission to sell the home the parent lives in, and changing the guardian.

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: My older brother manages our mother's bank account while she has dementia, and money keeps disappearing
I heard my brother is trying to sell our father's house
We were told to appoint a guardian to admit our parent to a care hospital and handle bank matters
Two siblings are fighting over who will be the guardian
My parents want to choose someone in advance to manage their property before their judgment declines

items.name: Civil Act (민법) Article 9 (Adjudication commencing adult guardianship)
items.text: For a person who persistently lacks the capacity to handle their affairs because of mental limitations caused by illness, disability, old age or similar reasons, the family court commences adult guardianship at the request of the person, their spouse, relatives within the fourth degree, a prosecutor, the head of a local government or others, and must take the person's wishes into account.

items.name: Civil Act Article 936 (Appointment of an adult guardian)
items.text: The family court appoints the adult guardian on its own authority, taking into account the person's wishes, health, living situation and finances, and the candidate's occupation, experience and any conflict of interest.

items.name: Civil Act Article 959-14 (Guardianship contract)
items.text: In preparation for a time when their judgment may weaken, a person can make a guardianship contract by notarial deed with someone who will manage their property and personal care. It takes effect from the time the family court appoints a supervisor of the voluntary guardian.

sections.title: There Are Four Types of Guardianship
body: If the capacity to handle affairs is persistently absent, you apply for adult guardianship (성년후견); if it is insufficient, limited guardianship (한정후견); and if help is needed only for specific matters, specific guardianship (특정후견). There is also voluntary guardianship (임의후견), where, while their judgment remains, the person makes a guardianship contract by notarial deed with someone they trust.

The application is made to the family court for the parent's address. As a rule, the court asks a doctor for a psychiatric evaluation and also hears from the person (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Articles 45-2 and 45-3). It is not a procedure that starts immediately on a single medical certificate, so a decision can take several months.

sections.title: The Child Who Applies Does Not Automatically Become Guardian
body: The court chooses the guardian on its own authority. If siblings are fighting over who will take the role, or a candidate has been involved in transactions tangled up with the parent's property, the court may appoint someone outside the family as guardian or add a guardianship supervisor.

Within 2 months of appointment, the guardian must prepare a list of the parent's property (Civil Act Article 941), and family court permission is needed to sell, rent out or mortgage the home the parent lives in (Article 947-2(5)). If the guardian does not act for the parent's benefit, relatives can ask for the guardian to be changed (Article 940).

sections.title: Money Already Taken and Inheritance Disputes
body: While the parent is alive, the other children have no right to directly demand the return of the parent's property. Once guardianship begins, the guardian can, on the parent's behalf, claim back money a sibling took, or decide whether a criminal complaint is needed.

The list of assets and transaction records organized during the guardianship become the basic evidence later, when the inheritance begins, for disputes over special benefits, the forced heirship share and the scope of the estate. Gifts or wills the parent made before guardianship began are challenged separately on whether the parent had mental capacity at the time.

steps.title: How We Handle a Guardianship Application

items.title: Choosing the type of guardianship
items.desc: Based on the medical certificate and the parent's daily condition, we decide whether to apply for adult, limited or specific guardianship.

items.title: Preparing the application and attachments
items.desc: We gather family relationship documents, the medical certificate, information on the assets, and opinions or consent from other family members.

items.title: Proposing a guardian and supervision
items.desc: If there is conflict in the family, we explain why we recommend a particular candidate and why a supervisor is needed.

items.title: Responding to evaluation and investigation
items.desc: In line with the schedule for the psychiatric evaluation and the family court investigation, we explain the parent's condition and how their property is actually being managed.

items.title: Follow-up after appointment
items.desc: We continue with preparing the list of assets, claiming back money wrongfully taken, and applying for permission to dispose of property.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The parent's dementia diagnosis, cognitive test results and long-term care grade documents
Registry records for real estate in the parent's name and a list of accounts you know of
Who currently manages the property and how
Family relationship documents of the proposed guardian
Other siblings' views and whether they consent

faqs.q: Do we need a guardian to withdraw hospital costs from our parent's account when they have dementia?
faqs.a: It depends on the bank, but if the account holder's own wishes cannot be confirmed, banks often refuse withdrawals or account closures even for family members. If you only need help with a specific matter such as hospital costs, you can apply in a narrower form, such as specific guardianship, so start by deciding what scope you need.

faqs.q: My brother became the guardian and seems to be spending our parent's money as he likes.
faqs.a: At the request of relatives or others, the family court can investigate the parent's financial situation and order the guardian to take necessary measures (Civil Act Article 954). Request an investigation with concrete evidence such as bank statements, and if the situation is serious, ask for a guardianship supervisor to be appointed or for the guardian to be changed.

faqs.q: Once adult guardianship begins, can our parent no longer make a will?
faqs.a: They can make a will only when their mental capacity has recovered, and in that case a doctor must add to the will a note of that recovered state and sign and seal it (Civil Act Article 1063). A will made without that procedure is very open to challenge.

areaPages.title: Withdrawals After Death, Forged Documents and Other Inheritance-Related Crimes
areaPages.summary: Property crimes within the family committed on or after June 27, 2024 can be punished on a complaint, and there is no family exception for forging documents.
areaPages.lead: Withdrawing money with a deceased person's card, or fabricating a division agreement with a sibling's registered seal, is not just a civil dispute; it becomes a criminal case. Since the Criminal Act was amended in December 2025, property crimes between family members can be punished if a complaint is filed.

seo.title: Criminal Complaints Over Inheritance in Korea: Withdrawals After Death and Forged Division Agreements | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The offenses and penalties that apply in Korea to unauthorized withdrawals before or after a parent's death, use of the deceased's card, forging a division agreement or will, and misuse of a registered seal; the provisions on crimes between relatives as amended on December 31, 2025 and the complaint period; and how to respond if a complaint is filed against you.
keywords: misuse of registered seal inheritance Korea

situations.title: When You Should Get Advice
items: The day after our father died, my brother withdrew all the cash using his card
The house had been transferred to my younger sibling using a division agreement stamped with my registered seal
My sister, who looked after our mother, transferred tens of millions of won from her account while she was alive
I moved money from our father's account to pay for the funeral, and my sibling says they will file a complaint
The handwriting on the will does not look like our father's, and I want to file a complaint for forgery

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 328 (Crimes between relatives and complaints)
items.text: If a person who obstructs the exercise of rights is a relative of the victim, prosecution requires a complaint, and in this case a complaint may also be filed against one's own or one's spouse's lineal ascendants. This also applies to theft, fraud, computer-related fraud, embezzlement, breach of trust and others (Articles 344, 354 and 361). The provisions amended on December 31, 2025 apply to crimes first committed on or after June 27, 2024 (Addenda Article 2).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 347-2 (Computer-related fraud), Article 355 (Embezzlement)
items.text: Obtaining a financial benefit by entering information without authority is punishable by imprisonment of up to 20 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million, and embezzling another person's property in one's keeping is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Articles 231 and 234 (Forgery of private documents; use of forged private documents)
items.text: Forging another person's document concerning rights or duties for the purpose of using it, or using a forged document, is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Causing a false entry in the registry through a false report also raises the crime of false entry in an authenticated original document (Article 228).

sections.title: Which Crimes Are Involved
body: Taking money out after the death using the deceased's debit card or mobile banking can be computer-related fraud, and withdrawing at a bank counter with the deceased's bankbook and seal can be fraud or forgery of a private document. If a child who managed a parent's account while the parent was alive used the money for themselves without permission, that is embezzlement.

Secretly using a sibling's registered seal to make an agreement on division of the estate amounts to forgery and use of a private document and misuse of a seal, and if the agreement was used for registration, false entry in an authenticated original document and its use are also considered. A person who forges a will concerning inheritance loses the right to be an heir, separately from criminal punishment (Civil Act (민법) Article 1004, item 5).

sections.title: Even Family Members Can Be Punished
body: In the past, theft, fraud and embezzlement between close family members such as parents, children and spouses were exempt from punishment. After the Constitutional Court found this incompatible with the Constitution, the Criminal Act was amended on December 31, 2025, so now prosecution is possible between relatives if the victim files a complaint, and filing a complaint against a parent is also allowed. These provisions apply to crimes first committed on or after June 27, 2024, so first check the dates the money was taken.

The rules on crimes between relatives apply only to property crimes; there is no such exception for forging documents or misusing a seal. In a case where someone put the deceased's bankbook into an ATM and transferred money to another account, the Supreme Court treated the bank as the victim and did not apply the rules on crimes between relatives (Supreme Court Decision 2006도2704 of March 15, 2007).

sections.title: Complaint Period and Procedure
body: For crimes that require a complaint, such as property crimes between relatives, the complaint must be filed within 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 230). If the crime was committed while your parent was alive and your parent has since died, the spouse, lineal relatives or siblings can file a complaint, but not against the parent's expressed wishes (Article 225(2)).

The complaint is filed with the police. From October 2, 2026, after the police investigate and refer the case, a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) decides whether to indict and, if needed, requests a supplementary investigation. Criminal proceedings do not get your money back, so civil proceedings such as a claim for return or division of the estate must be pursued alongside.

sections.title: If a Complaint Has Been Filed Against You
body: If the money was spent for the deceased, such as on funeral or hospital costs, organize where it went using receipts and transfer records, and gather signs that the other heirs knew about it. Whether the amount stayed within your own inheritance share, and whether any money has already been settled or returned, also affect the outcome.

Before appearing at the police, make a table of where the money went by transaction date and check your statement against likely questions. Jisan Law responds with practice before questioning, attendance at the questioning and a written defense opinion, and looks at the civil settlement and the criminal proceedings together to decide on a direction.

factors.title: Circumstances That Affect the Decision and Sentence
plus: Large amounts taken repeatedly
Withdrawals while the deceased was unconscious or in intensive care
Fabricating an agreement or power of attorney and using it for registration or withdrawals
Hiding it from other heirs, or closing accounts to erase the traces
Refusing to settle or return the money even after the complaint
minus: Receipts confirm that the money was spent for the deceased, such as on funeral or hospital costs
The amount was within your own inheritance share and the other heirs also knew
You returned the money before the investigation, or agreed to settle it in the division of the estate
There is evidence that the deceased clearly gave permission while alive

steps.title: How We Handle an Inheritance Involving Criminal Issues

items.title: Organizing dates and amounts
items.desc: We split the transaction records into before and after the death and set out in a table how the money was withdrawn and which accounts received it.

items.title: Confirming the applicable rules
items.desc: Depending on whether the crime was on or after June 27, 2024, and whether it is a property crime or a document crime, we work out whether a complaint is needed and the deadline.

items.title: Preparing a complaint or a defense
items.desc: For the complaining side, Jisan Law drafts the complaint and submits it with the evidence; for the side facing a complaint, we prepare records of how the money was used and the statement.

items.title: Handling questioning
items.desc: Before police questioning we practice likely questions, and a lawyer attends the suspect's questioning and raises objections to improper questions on the spot. For the complaining side, we attend the complainant's questioning together.

items.title: Resolving it together with civil claims
items.desc: We pursue a claim for return, division of the estate and a lawsuit to cancel registration alongside, and consider whether a settlement is possible.

checklist.title: Helpful Documents to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Transaction records of the deceased's accounts from before and after the death
The issuance history of certificates of seal impression, and copies of the disputed agreement or power of attorney
The registry and the results of inspecting the registration application documents
Records of the deceased's condition at the time, such as hospital admission records
If a complaint was filed against you, receipts for funeral and hospital costs
Text and KakaoTalk messages within the family

faqs.q: Is there no point filing a complaint over money taken before June 2024?
faqs.a: The amended provisions apply to crimes first committed on or after June 27, 2024, so earlier crimes must be assessed separately under the previous provisions and the effect of the Constitutional Court's decision. Even if criminal punishment is difficult, you can still claim the money back in a civil case or have it settled in the division of the estate.

faqs.q: I heard that the amendment included a special rule allowing complaints within 6 months. Does it still apply?
faqs.a: There was a special rule allowing complaints, for crimes committed between June 27, 2024 and the effective date of the amendment, for 6 months from December 31, 2025, the date the amended law took effect (Addenda Article 3). By calculation, that period ended at the end of June 2026, so now the general rule of 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was applies.

faqs.q: If we siblings settle, does the case end?
faqs.a: For property crimes between relatives that require a complaint, prosecution cannot proceed once the complaint is withdrawn. A complaint can be withdrawn only before the first-instance judgment is pronounced, and once withdrawn, it cannot be filed again (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232). For crimes that do not require a complaint, such as forging documents, the investigation can continue even after a settlement.

guides.stage: I've decided to divorce but don't know where to start
guides.title: What to sort out first once you've decided to divorce
guides.lead: There are things to do before you bring up divorce. If you first organize the assets, the evidence and your children's daily lives, you will have more room to choose between agreement and a lawsuit.

seo.title: Preparing for Divorce in Korea: Steps, Organizing Assets and Gathering Evidence | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do once you have decided to divorce in Korea, how to judge whether divorce by agreement or a lawsuit is right for you, how to list assets and gather evidence lawfully, and the procedure ahead and deadlines that are easy to miss, in order.
keywords: divorce by agreement vs lawsuit Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Before you bring up divorce, take just a few days to organize things in the order below. The more you do before your spouse notices, the more useful it will be.
bullets: Write down, one line per event and in date order, everything that has happened from when the problems first started until now.
Make a list of any real estate addresses, each spouse's banks and securities firms, insurance, and your spouse's workplace and length of service. You don't need to know the amounts.
Back up the KakaoTalk and text messages you received, and recordings of conversations you took part in, in their original form somewhere else.
If you have children, mark on a calendar who has handled school drop-offs and pick-ups, doctor visits and school meetings, and keep photos.
If there is violence or threats, getting yourself to safety comes before anything on this list.

sections.title: Whatever you do, don't do these
body: Things done while preparing often end up as evidence for the other side later.

In particular, material obtained by secretly opening your spouse's phone is hard to use in a lawsuit and can turn into a criminal matter. It is safer to obtain records in your spouse's name through court procedures after the lawsuit begins.
bullets: Unlocking your spouse's phone or secretly logging into their accounts
Secretly recording conversations you are not part of
Criticizing your spouse in front of the children or making the children choose whom to live with
Leaving home without a word and cutting off living expenses
Suddenly moving deposits in your name into someone else's name

sections.title: First consider whether you can reach an agreement
body: If your spouse also wants a divorce and there are no major disagreements about assets and the children, a divorce by agreement (협의이혼) saves time and cost. However, in a divorce by agreement the court does not confirm property division (재산분할) or compensation for emotional distress (위자료), so you need to write a separate, careful agreement.

If your spouse refuses to divorce, will not tell you what assets they have, or both of you want to raise the children, you should consider mediation (조정) or a lawsuit. If you tell us in the consultation how far you think you can agree, it is easier to set a direction.

Even if a divorce by agreement seems right, if you are worried your spouse will not pay child support properly or will delay transferring assets, you can also proceed through mediation. Mediation has no cooling-off period, and once it succeeds, the mediation record (조정조서) can be used for compulsory execution of money and child support.

sections.title: How to gather the asset list and evidence
body: Once divorce comes up, some spouses start moving assets. Even if you do not know the exact amounts, just writing down where things are lets you check them after the lawsuit begins through an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and an asset inquiry (재산조회). Also write down money received from either family at the wedding and the balance in your own account before the marriage.

If you were assaulted, tell the hospital plainly that your spouse hit you and get a medical certificate. Records of 112 (police) reports are also important material. Save KakaoTalk conversations so the context before and after is visible, rather than cropping a single line of abuse, so the other side cannot easily take issue with the context.

If you know your spouse's workplace, their severance pay and pension can later be checked through a fact inquiry (사실조회), and you can also apply for a direct payment order (직접지급명령) to receive child support straight from their wages. Write down at least the name of the workplace and roughly the year they joined.

sections.title: The procedure ahead
body: In a divorce by agreement, you apply to the court together and receive the guidance, go through a cooling-off period (숙려기간) of 3 months if you have minor children or 1 month if not, receive the confirmation, and report the divorce within 3 months, and it is done.

A lawsuit starts with a mediation application or complaint, goes through mediation sessions and, if needed, a family investigation (가사조사) and asset inquiries, and ends in a judgment. The first instance usually takes about 6 months to a year, and many cases end in mediation along the way.

If you plan to sue on the ground of an affair, a divorce cannot be claimed on that ground once 6 months have passed since you learned of the infidelity, or 2 years since it occurred (Civil Act (민법) Article 841), so first write down the date you found out. Property division must be claimed within 2 years of the date of divorce.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner handles consultations personally. If you bring your dated notes and asset list, we will look together, on the spot, at whether agreement or a lawsuit fits and whether a provisional attachment (가압류) should come first. It's fine if you haven't decided yet.

Consultations are available at our main office in Seoul and our branch offices in Incheon, Hongseong and Songpa, and we explain fees after the consultation. If it is hard to set a time, send us a message through the chat on this page first.

faqs.q: Can I separate first, before bringing up divorce?
faqs.a: A separation with a reason, such as by agreement or to escape violence, is not a disadvantage. However, leaving the children behind can affect the custody decision, and leaving without a word and cutting off living expenses can support a claim of desertion. Before you leave, first decide what will happen with the children and living expenses.

faqs.q: Can I secretly print out my spouse's bank statements?
faqs.a: Organizing records of accounts in your own name or that you managed jointly is fine, but secretly checking with your spouse's digital certificate or password can be a problem. Assets in your spouse's name can be checked through an asset disclosure order and asset inquiry once the lawsuit begins, so just writing down the names of the banks where they have accounts is enough.

faqs.q: If I have a consultation, will my spouse find out?
faqs.a: Lawyers have a duty to keep consultations confidential, so nothing is disclosed to the other spouse. If you tell us in advance the times and methods that are convenient for you to be contacted, we will contact you accordingly.

guides.stage: I received a divorce complaint from my spouse
guides.title: When you receive a divorce complaint
guides.lead: Your answer is due within 30 days of the day you received the copy of the complaint. Whether or not you want a divorce, you need to decide your position on each claim within that time.

seo.title: Received a Divorce Complaint in Korea? Preparing Your Answer and Counterclaim | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do when you receive a divorce complaint from your spouse in Korea, the 30-day deadline for an answer and how to write it, how to respond if you do not want a divorce or only dispute the terms, counterclaims and pre-trial measures, and preparing for the first mediation session.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Once you have opened the envelope, do these four things first, before your emotions settle.
bullets: Write the date you received it on the envelope and on your calendar. The 30-day deadline for the answer is counted from that day.
Keep all the documents that came with the complaint in one place. If an application for a pre-trial measure or a provisional attachment decision came with it, it must be responded to separately.

In the relief sought, find and mark the amount of compensation, the property division demanded and the demands about the children (person with parental authority and custodial parent, child support, visitation).
Underline the parts of your spouse's claims that are not true, and note beside them where the material to refute them can be found.

sections.title: What not to do after receiving the complaint
body: Things done in the heat of the moment are used as evidence in the lawsuit just as they are.
bullets: Moving deposits or disposing of real estate (this can be suspected as hiding assets and be subject to revocation)
Suddenly moving with the children or cutting off contact with your spouse
Sending your spouse messages containing abuse or threats
Posting about the lawsuit or your spouse on social media
Secretly opening your spouse's phone or logging into their accounts

sections.title: File your answer within 30 days
body: To dispute the plaintiff's claims, you must file an answer (답변서) within 30 days of being served with the copy of the complaint (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 256; Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 12). The rule on deemed admission does not apply to judicial divorce (재판상 이혼), so not filing an answer does not automatically mean the divorce is granted. Even so, if you miss the deadline, the court will see only the plaintiff's side first, and you may be at a disadvantage on the money claims.
If you have not gathered all the material yet, file an answer with your basic position first and supplement the rest with briefs.

In the answer, respond separately to the relief sought and to the grounds of the claim. Separate the facts in the plaintiff's claims that you admit, those you do not know, and those that are untrue, and attach supporting material as evidence for the untrue parts.
If the case is being handled through electronic litigation, you can check the other side's filings and hearing notices directly on the electronic litigation website, so check the case history often.

sections.title: If you don't want a divorce, or only disagree on the terms
body: If you do not intend to divorce, you need to state specifically that there is no legal ground for divorce and that the plaintiff's claims are untrue. Efforts to repair the relationship, your daily life up to recently, and messages that contradict the claims help. If the plaintiff is mainly responsible for the breakdown, also argue that it is a claim by the spouse at fault (유책배우자).

If you agree to the divorce but disagree on compensation for emotional distress (위자료), property division (재산분할) or custody, separate, item by item, what you accept and what you dispute. If you should receive compensation or want to be the custodial parent, an answer alone is not enough; you must file a counterclaim (반소).

As for the children, the court decides the person with parental authority (친권자) and the custodial parent (양육자) on its own authority, but if you want to raise them, you should clearly state that wish and your parenting plan. Describe specifically who is caring for the children now, and where you will live and who will help after the divorce.

sections.title: The procedure ahead
body: After you file the answer, a mediation session is usually scheduled. If you organize your list of assets and loans and the children's care situation beforehand, it is easier to judge which terms you can accept in mediation. If your spouse applied for a pre-trial measure (사전처분), a hearing on it may be scheduled first.

If custody is disputed, a family investigation (가사조사) may take place, so think about your parenting plan in advance. If you are worried about living expenses or child support being cut off during the lawsuit, apply for a pre-trial measure together with your answer or counterclaim, and if your spouse seems to be moving assets, consider a provisional attachment (가압류) at this point as well.
If mediation fails, the case goes through hearings to a judgment. The first instance usually takes about 6 months to a year, and longer if property or custody is heavily disputed.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner reads the complaint personally and decides with you what to admit, what to dispute, and whether a counterclaim is needed. We prepare the answer, the counterclaim and written opinions on pre-trial measures within the deadline.
Even if the compensation amount in the complaint is large, it is not automatically awarded, so don't panic and rush into a settlement.
If the deadline is close, take photos of the complaint and send them to us first through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: I've received the complaint. Can I keep living in the same home?
faqs.a: Continuing to live in the same home during the lawsuit is not a problem. However, if the conflict escalates, verbal abuse or clashes can become new evidence. If you end up moving out, leave a message recording the date and the reason.

faqs.q: Can I file the answer without a lawyer?
faqs.a: You can file it yourself. However, facts you admit in the answer are hard to reverse later, and people sometimes miss a needed counterclaim. Even if you write it yourself, it is a good idea to have what you admit and what you dispute checked once before filing.

faqs.q: Can the deadline for the answer be extended?
faqs.a: The 30 days is only the period in which an answer is requested, not a cutoff after which you can file nothing, so you can still file late before the judgment. But the court will see only the plaintiff's side first in the meantime, so if you have not gathered all the material, file an answer with your basic position first and supplement the rest with briefs.

guides.title: When you think your spouse is hiding assets
guides.lead: If money has been drained from deposits or your home has been listed for sale since divorce came up, you need to move quickly. Even with a judgment, if no assets remain in your spouse's name, your options for collecting narrow.

seo.title: Hidden Assets in a Korean Divorce: Provisional Attachment and Asset Inquiries | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do when your spouse seems to be disposing of or hiding assets before a divorce in Korea: provisional attachment and injunctions against disposal, asset disclosure orders and asset inquiries, and revoking fraudulent transfers to recover assets moved into other names, in order.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Suspicion alone is hard to bring before a court. Start by keeping material that shows what moved and when.
bullets: Write down the date and details of any unusual activity you saw. For example: 'September 3: our home listed for sale on a real estate app.'
Take screenshots of the sale listing, messages with real estate agents, and records of large sums withdrawn from a joint account.
Get a certified copy of the home's register from the Internet Registry Office (the court's online property register service) and check the owner and any mortgages.
Make a list of the names of the banks, securities firms and insurers your spouse uses, their workplace and their vehicles.
If you will apply for a provisional attachment, think ahead about how to raise the cash or surety bond premium to be provided as security.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Secretly checking accounts using your spouse's digital certificate or password
Telling your spouse in advance that you will apply for a provisional attachment (they may move more assets before you apply)
Retaliating by moving your own assets into family members' names
Secretly opening mail addressed to your spouse

sections.title: Provisional attachment and injunctions against disposal
body: A provisional attachment (가압류) is not a procedure for taking the assets but for freezing them in their current state until the judgment. To protect compensation for emotional distress (위자료) or property division (재산분할) to be settled in money, you file for provisional attachment; to receive a specific apartment, you file for an injunction against disposal (처분금지가처분). These can be filed with the family court even before a divorce lawsuit (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 63).

The application must show that you have a right to claim and that it will be hard to collect later unless the assets are frozen now. If you only state that the assets exist and cannot show a risk of disposal, it is unlikely to be granted, so concrete signs such as a sale listing matter. The court often orders you to provide security through a cash deposit or a surety bond, and once the case ends, you apply to get the security back.

After a provisional attachment is granted, if your spouse asks the court to order you to file the main lawsuit, you must file within the period the court sets, or the provisional attachment may be cancelled. If you have already filed for divorce mediation, that counts as filing the main case (Family Litigation Act Article 63(3)). If the home already has large senior mortgages, a provisional attachment may be of little practical value, so we check the register first.

sections.title: When you don't know where the assets are
body: Once the lawsuit begins, you can apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) requiring your spouse to submit a list of assets. Failing to submit without a valid reason or submitting a false list leads to an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (Family Litigation Act Articles 48-2 and 67-3).

If the list is not enough, you apply for an asset inquiry (재산조회) to check assets in your spouse's name with financial institutions and public agencies (Article 48-3 of the same Act). Deposit and withdrawal records at a specific bank are checked through an order to submit financial transaction information, and severance pay or pensions at the workplace through a fact inquiry (사실조회). The more specifically you identify which institution to ask about what, the more likely it is to be granted, so even writing down a single bank name helps.

Asset disclosure orders and asset inquiries can only be used while a divorce lawsuit or property division claim is pending in court. So if you know very little about your spouse's assets, these are often applied for at the same time as the complaint or mediation application.

sections.title: If assets have already been moved into someone else's name
body: If your spouse transferred assets to a parent or acquaintance knowing it would avoid property division, you can ask for that act to be revoked and the assets restored (Civil Act (민법) Article 839-3).
