This must be filed within 1 year of learning the grounds for revocation and within 5 years of the transfer, so be sure to write down the date you learned of the change in title.

If the title has not changed but money has been drained, you argue for that money to be included in the division calculation by showing when, where and how much went out. The more unusual the spending, such as money sent to an affair partner or large withdrawals just before the divorce, the more weight it carries.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, we look at the material showing signs of disposal in the consultation and decide whether to file for provisional attachment first or together with the complaint or mediation application. During the lawsuit, we choose together which institutions and what scope to apply for in asset disclosure orders, asset inquiries and production orders.
The application for a provisional attachment must identify the specific assets, so the more accurate the register and account information, the faster the decision.
If your home is already listed for sale, let us know first through the chat on this page, even on a weekend.

faqs.q: If I get a provisional attachment, do I take those assets?
faqs.a: No. A provisional attachment freezes the assets so your spouse cannot sell or transfer them at will. You actually receive money or real estate only after property division is set by a judgment or mediation and goes through the enforcement procedure.

faqs.q: What if my spouse says the withdrawn money was spent on living costs?
faqs.a: The court looks at whether the amount matches actual living costs and when and where the money went. Withdrawals far above normal living costs, or transfers made right after divorce came up, give grounds to demand an explanation. That is why it is important to get the joint account records in advance.

faqs.q: How much security is needed for a provisional attachment?
faqs.a: The court sets it by looking at the assets and the amount claimed, so it is hard to say exactly in advance. In many cases it can be provided with a surety bond instead of a cash deposit, which reduces the burden. Once the case ends, you apply to cancel the security and get it back.

guides.title: When your ex won't pay the child support set at the divorce
guides.lead: While you wait, the overdue child support just keeps growing. If you have the underlying documents, there are several procedures to collect it without a new lawsuit.

seo.title: Unpaid Child Support in Korea: Performance Orders, Direct Payment Orders and Advance Payment | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away when you are not receiving the child support set at your divorce in Korea, checking your documents, direct payment orders from wages and seizure, performance orders, fines and detention, driver's license suspension, travel bans and public disclosure of names, and the advance payment requirements that change in 2026.
keywords: child support direct payment order Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Any procedure can begin only once the following four things are ready.
bullets: Find out whether you have a judgment, a mediation record or a child support protocol. If you divorced by agreement, you will have the child support protocol you received from the court.
Make a monthly table of the agreed payment dates and amounts and the money actually received. Download your bank statements for the period as a PDF from your banking app.
Write down your ex's workplace and address, and any accounts and vehicles you know of. Knowing the workplace opens the way to receiving payment straight from wages.
Take screenshots of text messages asking for payment and your ex's replies, and make future requests by text rather than by phone.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Refusing to let your ex see the child because they don't pay (visitation is a separate obligation, so you could become subject to a performance order)
Going to your ex's home or workplace and causing a scene
Agreeing only verbally to reduce the overdue amount
Waiting for years, hoping they will pay someday
body: If you threaten your ex over child support or start contacting their family, you could end up being the one facing a criminal complaint.

sections.title: Your starting point depends on your documents
body: If you have a judgment, mediation record, ruling or child support protocol (양육비부담조서), you can apply directly for compulsory execution or a performance order (이행명령) without a separate lawsuit. If there was only a verbal promise or an agreement written between the two of you, you must first ask the family court for a ruling on child support to fix the amount.

In a child support ruling, you can claim not only future child support but also past child support you paid alone. The amount is set based on the Child Support Guidelines (양육비 산정기준표), reflecting the parents' incomes and the child's age.

If preparing the documents on your own is difficult, you can also apply to the Child Support Enforcement Agency (양육비이행관리원) for representation in a child support lawsuit, legal support for enforcement, or collection support (Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments (양육비 이행확보 및 지원에 관한 법률) Article 11).

sections.title: Collecting straight from wages, and seizure
body: If your ex receives wages from a company, a direct payment order (직접지급명령) is the most reliable route. If payment has been missed twice or more without a valid reason, the court orders the company to deduct child support from the wages and send it directly (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 63-2). If your ex changes jobs, the company must notify the court within 1 week.

If your ex is self-employed or has no wages, we consider a security order (담보제공명령) requiring security to be provided and, if that is not followed, a lump-sum payment order (일시금지급명령) requiring the child support to be paid all at once (Article 63-3 of the same Act). Money already overdue is collected by seizing deposits or real estate.

sections.title: From performance orders to administrative sanctions
body: A performance order is a procedure in which the court orders payment within a set period. If it is violated, an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million can be imposed, and if three or more regular child support payments are missed, you can apply for detention (감치) for up to 30 days (Articles 64, 67 and 68 of the same Act). Detention is a means of pressure and does not collect the money for you, so it is used together with seizure.

If, despite a performance order, the overdue child support is KRW 30 million or more or three or more payments are missed, the matter can go through review to driver's license suspension, a travel ban and public disclosure of the name (Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments Articles 21-3 to 21-5). Failing to pay within 1 year after a detention order is subject to criminal punishment (Article 27 of the same Act).

sections.title: Advance payment from the government
body: You can apply for advance payment (선지급) if you have the underlying documents; the average child support received in the 3 months, or the 3 consecutive payments, before applying is less than the advance payment amount; and you have applied for legal or collection support from the Child Support Enforcement Agency or gone through a procedure such as a performance order. The government recovers the money it paid in advance from your ex.

For cases decided by October 28, 2026, household income must be no more than 1.5 times the standard median income, and from cases decided on or after October 29, this income requirement no longer applies. Even if you applied earlier, if the decision is made on or after October 29, it may be decided regardless of income. Under current government guidance, the amount is KRW 200,000 per minor child per month, does not exceed the child support set in the judgment or record, and can be received until the child becomes an adult. Detailed requirements can be checked with the Child Support Enforcement Agency (1644-6621).

While receiving advance payments, you must notify the Agency if your ex pays child support directly or the amount changes (Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments Article 21-7(4)). If your ex pays even part of it, the advance payment may be reduced or stopped.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, we first check how your ex earns income and decide the order of a direct payment order, seizure and a performance order. If you do not have the underlying documents, we prepare a child support ruling with you first.
If you learn new information about your ex's workplace or assets, let us know through the chat on this page before you forget.

faqs.q: My ex uses a bank account in someone else's name. Can it be seized?
faqs.a: An account in someone else's name is that person's property, so it is hard to seize directly. Instead, if your ex's workplace is identified, you can receive payment from wages through a direct payment order, and after a performance order you can apply pressure through sanctions such as driver's license suspension or a travel ban. Assets in your ex's own name can be checked through an asset disclosure order or asset inquiry.

faqs.q: Can I apply for a performance order with only a child support protocol?
faqs.a: Yes. The Family Litigation Act lists the child support protocol, along with judgments, rulings and mediation records, as a basis for a performance order (Family Litigation Act Article 64). You can use the protocol the court drew up at your divorce by agreement as is.

faqs.q: My ex says they lost their job and can't pay.
faqs.a: Simply saying they lost their job does not end the duty to pay. The court looks at their actual income and assets, whether they tried to pay at least part, and whether they formally asked for a reduction. If your ex wants a reduction, they must ask the court for a change, and until then, the set amount keeps building up.

guides.stage: My spouse keeps verbally abusing or assaulting me
guides.title: When your spouse's verbal abuse or violence continues
guides.lead: Before any divorce procedure, take care of your own safety and your children's. For divorces involving domestic violence, the law provides special protection procedures.

seo.title: Domestic Violence Divorce in Korea: Restraining Orders and Victim Protection Orders | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do when a spouse's verbal abuse or violence continues in Korea: police emergency and temporary measures after a 112 report, victim protection orders, waiver of the cooling-off period in divorce by agreement and what changes in a divorce lawsuit, and how to organize evidence of verbal abuse.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: If you are in danger now, act in the order below. Evidence comes after you are safe.
bullets: If you are in danger, call 112 (police) right away. The police will stop the violence on the spot and separate the offender, and if you wish, take you to a counseling center, shelter or hospital.
If you are injured, tell the hospital plainly that your spouse hit you and get a medical certificate. Photograph your injuries so the date is visible.
Take screenshots of abusive messages showing the conversation before and after, and back up recordings of calls or conversations you took part in, in their original form, somewhere else.
Keep the things you would need if you had to leave in a hurry, such as ID, bankbooks, a phone charger and your children's medicine, together in one place.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Hitting back or swearing back (this can turn into a claim that you assaulted each other)
Secretly looking at your spouse's phone or logging into their accounts
Leaving the children behind without a word. If circumstances forced you to, leave a message explaining why.
Getting back together after receiving a written pledge or apology and deleting the records up to then. Pledges and apology messages are also evidence, so keep them.

sections.title: Protective measures provided by law
body: Police who receive a report take emergency measures (응급조치) on the spot to stop the violence and separate you, and if there is a high risk of further violence, they can use emergency temporary measures (긴급임시조치) to remove the offender from the home or block contact. The victim can ask the police to apply for temporary measures (임시조치) from the court (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence Crimes (가정폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Articles 5, 8 and 8-2). Temporary measures include removal from the home, a ban on coming within 100 meters of the home or workplace, and a ban on contact by phone or message.

The victim can also apply directly to the family court for a victim protection order (피해자보호명령). In addition to a restraining order, you can ask for restrictions on the offender's exercise of parental authority and visitation. The period is set at up to 1 year, and with extensions it can last up to 3 years in total (Articles 55-2 and 55-3 of the same Act). Violating a protection order or temporary measure is subject to criminal punishment.

A protection order is a procedure separate from the divorce lawsuit, so you can apply even before filing for divorce. If needed, the court may first issue a temporary protection order before deciding (Article 55-4 of the same Act).
Among the court's temporary measures, removal from the home and restraining orders cannot exceed 2 months, but they can be extended up to twice if needed (Article 29(5) of the same Act).

sections.title: What changes in the divorce process
body: In a divorce by agreement (협의이혼), you can show that violence makes waiting difficult and have the cooling-off period (숙려기간) shortened or waived (Civil Act (민법) Article 836-2(3)). In a lawsuit, you claim both the ground for divorce of extremely unfair treatment by your spouse and compensation for emotional distress (위자료).

If it is hard to face your spouse in mediation or the family investigation (가사조사), you can ask the court to proceed separately, and during the lawsuit you can also apply for pre-trial measures (사전처분) such as a restraining order or designation of a temporary custodial parent.

If there was violence in front of the children, you can ask for visitation to be restricted or its method changed (Civil Act Article 837-2(3)). If you are worried about your current address becoming known to your spouse, decide first, before filing the complaint, which address to use for receiving court documents.

sections.title: If you were never hit, only verbally abused
body: Verbal abuse can also be a ground for divorce if it was repeated and went on long enough to destroy the marriage. Rather than a single instance of severe swearing, it is important to show a pattern of the same thing repeated over years.

Group KakaoTalk messages by period, and for recordings, note separately the date and the time stamps where the key statements occur. If you also swore during arguments, do not delete it; leave it as it is. Deleting only part creates a new dispute about hiding things.

If threats to cut off living expenses or being thrown out of the house were repeated along with the verbal abuse, write that down too. Financial control and threats are circumstances that show how severe the verbal abuse was.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, and we decide together in what order to file the application for a protection order, the divorce complaint and applications for pre-trial measures. We also make the necessary requests in mediation and the family investigation so that you do not have to face your spouse.

If your spouse's side asks you to withdraw the complaint or settle, do not answer alone. Jisan Law receives that contact as the victim's representative and negotiates the settlement terms, and if a criminal complaint is needed, we write it and accompany you to the victim interview.
If you are in danger now, call 112 first. Once you have reached a safe place, contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: If I report it, will my husband be punished right away?
faqs.a: Domestic violence cases are sometimes sent to domestic protection proceedings instead of criminal punishment, where protective dispositions such as a restraining order or counseling are imposed. Either way, the report records and medical certificates become important material in the divorce lawsuit. Regardless of punishment, you can apply directly for a protection order.

faqs.q: Can I take my children and go to my parents' home to escape?
faqs.a: If you left with your children to escape violence, that alone is not a disadvantage. Keep a record of the date you left and the reason, and if your spouse tries to take the children during the lawsuit, you can apply for a pre-trial measure designating a temporary custodial parent.

faqs.q: After the protection order, my spouse keeps contacting me.
faqs.a: Violating a protection order or temporary measure is subject to criminal punishment (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence Crimes Article 63). Do not delete the contact records; take screenshots and report them to the police.

guides.title: If you can't attend the confirmation hearing for divorce by agreement
guides.lead: Missing a confirmation hearing once does not end a divorce by agreement. But if you miss both, the application is treated as withdrawn, so first check what stage you are at.

seo.title: Missing the Confirmation Hearing in a Korean Divorce by Agreement: Reapplying and Withdrawing | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What happens, with the relevant provisions, when one spouse does not appear at the confirmation hearing for a divorce by agreement in Korea, when you reapply after the application is withdrawn for missing two hearings, when the other spouse deliberately stays away, and when you change your mind after the confirmation.

sections.title: Two confirmation hearings are scheduled
body: When you apply for a divorce by agreement (협의이혼), you are usually told about two confirmation hearings (확인기일) at once, both set after the cooling-off period (숙려기간) ends. If one of you could not attend the first hearing, you do not need to reapply; just check the date of the second hearing.

Both spouses must attend the confirmation hearing together with their ID. One spouse cannot attend alone to receive the confirmation, and a lawyer cannot attend on your behalf. If you want to change the date, do not just show up on another day; ask the court handling the case first.

At the confirmation hearing, the judge asks whether you intend to divorce, and if there are minor children, checks the agreement. If the agreement does not serve the child's welfare, the court may issue a correction order (보정명령), and if you do not comply, it will not issue the confirmation (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 규칙) Article 78(1), proviso).

Notice of the confirmation hearing may come by simple means such as phone or fax, so do not change the contact details you wrote on the application (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 73(6)).

sections.title: If you miss both
body: If either spouse fails to appear twice after receiving notice, the application for confirmation is treated as withdrawn (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 77(2)). This does not mean you are divorced or that the divorce was refused; the application process has simply ended.

If you both still want a divorce, you can simply apply again. The previous case is not revived, so check with the court how the cooling-off period and confirmation hearings will be set in the new application. If you have minor children, you also submit the agreement again. An application is also treated as withdrawn if you do not receive the divorce guidance within 3 months of applying (Article 77(3) of the same Rules).

It is hard to say in advance whether the cooling-off period starts over when you reapply or whether the earlier period is taken into account. If there are urgent circumstances such as violence, ask again for shortening or waiver in the new application.

sections.title: If your spouse is deliberately not showing up
body: If your spouse is not attending because they no longer want a divorce, reapplying for divorce by agreement any number of times will not solve it. A divorce by agreement is a procedure that requires both spouses to intend to divorce.

In that case, you need to file for divorce mediation (조정) or go to a lawsuit. Mediation has no cooling-off period, and once mediation succeeds, the record can be used for compulsory execution of property and child support. If your spouse seems to be moving assets while dragging things out by avoiding the confirmation hearing, we also consider a provisional attachment (가압류).

Conversely, if you are the one who has changed your mind and does not want to attend, it is cleaner to withdraw the application before the confirmation than to skip the hearings. You can withdraw the application at any time until the confirmation is given (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 77(1)).
bullets: Do not delete messages in which your spouse said they refuse the divorce; save them.
The existing settlement agreement and the agreement on the children also serve as reference material in mediation.
If you want to divorce on the ground of infidelity, there is a 6-month period from when you learned of it, so check the dates (Civil Act (민법) Article 841).

sections.title: After you receive the confirmation
body: Even after receiving the court's confirmation, you are not divorced yet. You must report the divorce (이혼신고) to the city hall, district office, or town or township office within 3 months of receiving the certified copy of the confirmation, and once this period passes, the court's confirmation loses its effect (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률) Article 75). Either spouse may file the report.

If you change your mind before the report, you can submit a withdrawal of intent to divorce (이혼의사철회서) with the certified copy of the confirmation attached. However, if your spouse files the divorce report first, that report is accepted (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 80).
If you have minor children, you write the person with parental authority set by agreement on the divorce report (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 74).

sections.title: If one spouse is abroad or in prison
body: If one spouse is a Korean national living abroad or is in a prison or detention center and cannot attend, the spouse in Korea can attend alone to apply, and the court entrusts the confirmation to a Korean embassy or consulate or the correctional facility (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Articles 73(2) and 74(2)). If both spouses live abroad, they can apply together at a Korean embassy or consulate.

If the hearing is close and your spouse has cut off contact, send us a message through the chat on this page. At Jisan Law, the managing partner hears you personally, and we decide together whether to wait for the next hearing or switch to mediation.

faqs.q: I forgot the first confirmation hearing. Do I have to submit the application again?
faqs.a: Missing it once does not immediately withdraw the application. You and your spouse just need to attend the second confirmation hearing you were told about when you applied. If you do not remember the second date, ask the family court where you applied, using the case number.

faqs.q: Will the judge also ask about property division at the confirmation hearing?
faqs.a: At the confirmation hearing, the court confirms the intent to divorce and the agreement on custody and the person with parental authority for minor children. Property division and compensation for emotional distress are not confirmed, so they must be settled separately in a written agreement.

guides.title: If you've received notice of a family investigation
guides.lead: A family investigation is not about grilling you on who was at fault; it is a procedure in which the court checks what the family is really like, which is hard to tell from documents. What you say there goes into a report that the court refers to when deciding.

seo.title: Family Investigations in Korean Divorce Cases: Questions, Preparation and Cautions | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When you receive notice of a family investigation during a divorce lawsuit in Korea: what the family investigator asks, what material to bring, what to watch for in child interviews and home visits, what to be careful about when giving statements, and how the investigation report is used at trial.

sections.title: What a family investigation is
body: If the presiding judge or the head of the mediation committee considers it necessary, they order a family investigator (가사조사관) to conduct a family investigation (가사조사). The investigator looks into the parties' living conditions, finances, health and home environment, and submits a report with the results and their opinion to the court (Rules on Family Litigation (가사소송규칙) Articles 8, 9 and 11).

It is not done in every divorce case. It is mainly ordered when who will raise the children is disputed, or when the accounts of responsibility for the breakdown or how the assets were built differ sharply. An interview at the court is the basic format; depending on the case it may end in one session or require several, and home visits or interviews with the children may be added if needed.

sections.title: Commonly asked questions
body: In actual interviews, the following are generally asked. If you organize your answers in advance, you will not lose your train of thought even if you are nervous.
bullets: How you met and married, and when the relationship started to go wrong
Why you want a divorce and whether you are open to repairing the relationship
How the assets were built and what each of you did, and why any debts arose
Your child's daily routine, homeroom teacher, doctors and favorite foods
Where you will live after the divorce, and who will look after the child while you work
Your thoughts on how the other parent will see the child
How housework and childcare have been shared
How you plan to work out matters concerning the child with the other parent going forward

sections.title: Material worth bringing
body: Bring a one- or two-page timeline listing the major events in date order. It is important to check in advance that it does not contradict what you wrote in the complaint, answer or briefs. You don't need to bring all the evidence; just mark the key items among the evidence already submitted.
If custody is at issue, material that shows you have actually been caring for the child helps, such as notices from the daycare or school, medical records and plans for after-school care.

If assets are at issue, prepare a list of assets, loan records, and a table of the money each of you brought into the marriage. Also organize the terms you want after the divorce and what you can concede, so you will not waver if the investigator asks about the possibility of an agreement.

sections.title: Things to be careful about when answering
body: Calmly describing when, where and what happened gets across much better than words blaming the other parent. For example, rather than saying 'they have no interest in the children', say 'they spent most weekday evenings and weekends on work'.

Rather than hiding facts unfavorable to you, admit them and explain the reasons and what you are doing now. Even if you are encouraged to settle during the investigation, you do not have to answer on the spot; you can state your position after thinking it over.

Lies or exaggerations are easily exposed when checked against other material, and once you lose credibility, your other statements are doubted too. Bringing up the other parent's private life more than necessary can also create new disputes.

sections.title: Child interviews and home visits
body: The investigator may meet the child separately to hear what the child has to say. If the child is 13 or older, the court must in principle hear the child's opinion before deciding the person with parental authority (친권자) and the custodial parent (양육자) (Rules on Family Litigation Article 18-2). Coaching a child on what to say or getting the child to speak badly of the other parent is obvious to the investigator and works against you when the custodial parent is decided.

If a home visit is scheduled, simply show naturally what the child's room and study space are like and who the supporting caregivers are. It is better for everyday life to show than a staged appearance.
Explain to the child why they are meeting the investigator in a way that does not burden them, but do not tell them what to say. Also avoid pressing the child afterward about what they said.

sections.title: After the investigation
body: Once the report is submitted to the court, check through your lawyer how much of it can be viewed, and if anything is recorded incorrectly, submit a brief asking for it to be corrected. The report is only one piece of material for the decision; it does not become the judgment as is.

If the situation has changed after the investigation, for example because you moved or the child changed schools, inform the court in writing and explain the difference between the report and the current situation.

At Jisan Law, we go over likely questions with you before the investigation to check the flow of your answers. If a date for the family investigation has been set, contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't go to the family investigation?
faqs.a: If you do not cooperate with the investigation, your circumstances will not be included in the report, and it may be written mainly from the other side's statements. If you truly cannot make the date, contact the investigator in advance to rearrange the schedule.

faqs.q: I don't want to be interviewed together with my spouse.
faqs.a: If there was domestic violence or there are reasons it is hard to be in the same room, you can ask the investigator to interview you separately. It is a good idea to make the request well before the investigation date.

faqs.q: My spouse told a lot of lies. Will the investigator notice?
faqs.a: The investigator cross-checks both sides' statements, the material submitted and what the child said in the interview. Rather than rebutting the other side's untrue claims emotionally, it is more effective to point to the material that shows the truth on those points.

guides.title: What to know before a divorce mediation session
guides.lead: A mediation room is closer to a meeting room than a courtroom. Even so, a record you sign there has the same force as a judgment, so decide in advance what you will accept before you go in.

seo.title: Divorce Mediation Sessions in Korea: Procedure, Questions and Wording of the Mediation Record | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How a divorce mediation session in Korea runs, what the judge and mediators ask, the wording to check in the mediation record before signing, and how to respond, and by when, if mediation fails or a decision in lieu of mediation is issued.
keywords: decision in lieu of mediation Korea

sections.title: How the mediation room works
body: You arrive at the family court, wait, and enter the mediation room when your case number is called. It is set up like a meeting room, where you sit across a large table from the judge or mediators, and there are usually two mediators. At first, both sides' basic positions are checked together, and then each side is often called in separately to narrow down the terms.

It is common for it not to end in one session. If asset records have not all come in or matters concerning the children remain, the next session is scheduled after a family investigation (가사조사) or asset inquiry (재산조회).

Arrive a little earlier than the time on the notice, and be sure to bring your ID. Several cases may be scheduled for the same time slot, so the wait can be long. If it is hard to wait in the same space as your spouse, let the court know in advance.

sections.title: What is usually asked
bullets: Whether both of you agree to divorce
What you think of the reasons for the breakdown your spouse gives, and how much compensation for emotional distress you want
Whether any assets are missing, and what division ratio you think is fair
Who will raise the children, and how child support and visitation will work
body: The judge and mediators are more interested in what you want than in how much your spouse was at fault. Practice answering each question briefly with the outcome you want and the reason.

sections.title: What to decide before going in
body: Mediation (조정) is a place where both sides give a little. Decide in advance, in numbers, what you must keep, what you can concede, and the bottom line below which you will not sign. If you sign on the spot because you are swept along by the atmosphere or want to finish today, it is very hard to undo later.
Things said in mediation sometimes remain in the record and become an issue in a later lawsuit. Be careful not to make sweeping statements about the children or about fault in the heat of the moment.

It is easier to explain if you bring material supporting your numbers summarized on one page, such as a list of assets, loan balances and a child support calculation. Calculate the child support amount in advance using the Child Support Guidelines (양육비 산정기준표).

sections.title: Check the wording of the record before signing
body: A mediation record (조정조서) has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 59), so it is enforced exactly as written. Look especially carefully at the following wording.
Read the draft record aloud once and check that the numbers and dates match what you have in mind. If any wording is ambiguous, ask for it to be corrected right then.
bullets: By when and to which account money will be paid, and what happens if it is late
The date real estate will be transferred, who will repay the loan, and what happens if the bank refuses to let the loan be taken over
The child support amount, the monthly payment date, and until when it will be paid
The frequency, times and places of visitation, whether the child stays overnight, and how vacations will work
A clause stating that neither side will make any further claims regarding property (this may block claims even if hidden assets come to light later)

sections.title: If no agreement is reached
body: If mediation fails, the lawsuit is treated as filed when mediation was requested, and the case moves to litigation (Civil Conciliation Act (민사조정법) Article 36). You do not need to write a new complaint, but if you receive a correction order (보정명령) to pay the shortfall in stamp fees, you must pay it before the deadline.

The court may also issue a decision in lieu of mediation (조정을 갈음하는 결정). If no objection is filed within 2 weeks of being served with the original copy of the decision, it becomes final and has the same effect as mediation; if an objection is filed, the entire decision loses its effect and the case goes to litigation (Family Litigation Act Article 49; Civil Conciliation Act Article 34).
Your preparation is not wasted just because mediation failed. The issues and the other side's positions revealed during mediation tell you what needs to be proved in the lawsuit that follows.

sections.title: Do I have to attend in person?
body: In principle, you must attend mediation sessions in person, and if there are special circumstances, only your lawyer may attend with permission (Family Litigation Act Article 7). If the person who applied for mediation fails to attend twice, the application is treated as withdrawn (Civil Conciliation Act Article 31), so be sure to keep the dates.
In cases involving children, you may be told to attend parenting education or counseling before mediation, so read the notice carefully.
Even if your spouse keeps not showing up, that does not mean you cannot divorce. The court can issue a decision in lieu of mediation, or end mediation and send the case to litigation.

At Jisan Law, we decide with you before mediation the bottom line you will accept and the wording of the record, and we attend the mediation session with you to check the wording. If you have received notice of a mediation session, contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: The mediator is pushing me to sign, saying this is good enough.
faqs.a: Mediation succeeds only with agreement. If you are not sure, do not sign; you can ask for time to review or request another session. Once mediation succeeds, it has the same effect as a judgment, so it is hard to challenge even if you regret it later.

faqs.q: If mediation succeeds, do I still have to report the divorce?
faqs.a: When mediation succeeds, the divorce takes effect at that moment, and you report the divorce within 1 month, attaching a certified copy of the mediation record. The report is the procedure for recording it in the family relationship register.

guides.title: When your ex won't let you see your child (visitation)
guides.lead: If every scheduled day brings the reply that the child is sick or busy, it may be refusal rather than circumstance. Even if you are angry, following the steps set by law is the faster way back to seeing your child.

seo.title: Refused Visitation in Korea: Performance Orders and Fines | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When your ex won't let you see your child after a divorce in Korea: how to keep records and responses to avoid, performance orders and fines for visitation, the procedure when you only have a written agreement, changing the visitation arrangement when the child refuses to meet, and changing the custodial parent.
keywords: ex won't let me see child Korea

sections.title: Start by keeping records
body: Every procedure starts with records. Write down the following by date.

If you keep hearing that the child does not want to come, do not write down only that remark; also record how the child seemed the last time you met. Any gap between the reasons your ex gives for refusing and how the child actually behaves helps the court decide later.
bullets: Messages and call attempts requesting visitation, and the replies or lack of response
Photos and location records from days you went to the meeting place and the child did not come
The visitation provisions in the judgment, mediation record or agreement
Photos and conversations from the last time you saw your child

sections.title: Responses to avoid
body: Showing up unannounced at your ex's home or your child's school gives your ex a pretext for refusing ('the child is anxious'), and in serious cases can even lead to a restraining order. Bombarding your child with direct messages also drags the child into the middle of an adult dispute.

The most common mistake is stopping child support. Visitation (면접교섭) and child support (양육비) are separate obligations, so the moment you stop paying, you become subject to a performance order and sanctions.

Also avoid speaking badly of your ex to the child on visitation days or quizzing the child about life at the other parent's home. It makes the child feel burdened by the visits and gives your ex an excuse to refuse.

sections.title: Performance orders and fines
body: If visitation is set in a judgment, ruling or mediation record and is not followed without a valid reason, you can apply to the family court for a performance order (이행명령) (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 64(1)3). The court summons your ex, hears the circumstances and orders them to let you see the child as set. If visitation was written only in the agreement at a divorce by agreement, that agreement is not a basis for a performance order, so you may first need to obtain a visitation ruling from the family court.

If the performance order is also violated, you can apply for an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (Article 67 of the same Act). Unlike child support, there is no detention provision for failure to allow visitation, so the fine is the last sanction at the court stage. That is why, when applying for a performance order, it is a good idea to also ask the court to reset specific dates, times and handover locations that can actually be kept going forward.

Before applying for a performance order, sending a certified letter (내용증명) that restates the set visitation terms and demands compliance leaves a record that you made a formal demand. Sometimes that alone changes the other parent's attitude.

sections.title: If your child truly does not want to meet
body: If you keep hearing that the child refuses, start by looking at why. The response differs depending on whether the child feels unfamiliar, finds overnight stays a burden, or actually had an unpleasant experience. The court can restrict visitation or change its method if needed for the child's welfare (Civil Act (민법) Article 837-2(3)).

If you are the custodial parent, do not stop the visits on your own because the child doesn't want to go; keep records of the child's reactions and health and ask the court to change the method. If you are the non-custodial parent, proposing to start again with short daytime visits may actually be faster. Some family courts run spaces and programs that support visitation, so ask the court handling your case.
A request to change the visitation arrangement is filed with the family court by one parent against the other (Rules on Family Litigation (가사소송규칙) Article 99(2)).

sections.title: If your ex keeps blocking visits
body: If, despite a performance order and a fine, your ex prevents you from seeing your child for a long time, one option is to ask for a change of custodial parent (Civil Act Article 837(5)). However, blocking visitation alone does not immediately lead to a change; you must show that the current arrangement is harmful to the child and that a change would be better for the child.

If your ex took the child and did not bring the child back, you can apply for a performance order for handing over the child (유아인도), and if the child is still not returned within 30 days after a fine is imposed, you can even apply for detention (감치) (Family Litigation Act Article 68(1)2).

At Jisan Law, we use your records to prepare the application for a performance order together with a new visitation arrangement. If it has been a long time since you last saw your child, message us through the chat on this page first.

faqs.q: My ex says I can see our child if I pay more child support.
faqs.a: A condition trading visitation for child support is not legally accepted. Keep sending the set child support, and demand visitation separately through a performance order. Save any messages setting such conditions as evidence.

faqs.q: We're still in a lawsuit, so visitation hasn't been set yet.
faqs.a: Even during the lawsuit, you can apply for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) asking the court to set visitation temporarily (Family Litigation Act Article 62). Specifying the frequency, times, places, whether the child stays overnight and even video calls reduces disputes after the decision.

faqs.q: Can grandparents also see their grandchild?
faqs.a: If the non-custodial parent has died, or cannot see the child because of illness, living abroad or similar circumstances, that parent's lineal ascendants can also ask the family court for visitation (Civil Act Article 837-2(2)).

guides.title: Is a home bought before marriage, or money from parents, also divided?
guides.lead: Even if an asset is in your name and was acquired before the marriage, it is not always protected as is; conversely, even if an asset is in your spouse's name, you may be recognized as having a share. The test is how the asset was maintained and grew during the marriage.

seo.title: Separate Property in a Korean Divorce: Pre-Marital Homes and Gifts from Parents | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether a home or savings acquired before marriage, money contributed by parents, and assets inherited during the marriage are included in property division in a Korean divorce; if they are, how they are reflected in contribution; the records to secure in advance; and the reference date for property division.

sections.title: The rule is that it belongs to each spouse
body: Property division (재산분할) is a system for dividing assets the spouses built together during the marriage (Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2). So assets owned before the marriage, and assets one spouse received by inheritance or gift even during the marriage, are called separate property (특유재산) and are in principle excluded from division.

However, if the other spouse actively contributed to keeping that asset, preventing it from shrinking or increasing its value, it is exceptionally included in the division. The longer the marriage and the more the assets were mixed, the harder it becomes to set it apart as separate property.

Even for the same home, the ratio differs depending on the length of the marriage, how the assets were built and whether both spouses worked, so other people's cases cannot simply be applied to yours. Also remember that the division ratio is set for all the assets as a whole, not for a single home.

Assets whose ownership is unclear are presumed to be jointly owned by the spouses (Civil Act Article 830(2)). If the spouse claiming separate property cannot show it with records, the asset may be treated as built together during the marriage.

sections.title: If you lived together in a home bought before the marriage
body: If you lived together in a home you bought in your name before the marriage and your spouse helped repay the loan or paid maintenance fees, taxes or repair costs, a contribution may be recognized to that extent. If the marriage was short and you repaid it alone, it may be excluded from division or the contribution may be valued as small.

It is different if money you saved before the marriage became the seed money for a home bought after the marriage. That home is an asset acquired during the marriage, so the whole of it is subject to division, and the money you put in is often reflected as a factor that raises your contribution when the division ratio is set. The calculation is not done by first deducting the pre-marital money and splitting only the rest in half.

If you sold your pre-marital home and used the money to buy another home after the marriage, it is easier to have it recognized as your contribution if you show with transfer records that the flow of money is continuous.

sections.title: Money from parents
body: Money one side's parents contributed toward buying a home is usually seen as given to their own child and is assessed as that child's contribution. However, the assessment differs if there are circumstances showing it was given to both spouses, or if it was a loan that must be repaid.

Assets inherited during the marriage are also in principle separate property, but if the other spouse helped repay the loan on an inherited home or managed it for a long time, a contribution may be recognized.

Wedding gifts to the in-laws, wedding presents and household items exchanged at the wedding are a separate issue. If the marriage lasted a considerable time, they are often hard to get back, so check this separately.
If loans were repaid with your parents' money, keep those transfer records too.

sections.title: Records to secure in advance
body: The spouse claiming that an asset is separate property must show it with records. These become harder to obtain over time, so get them now.
bullets: Transaction records showing your account balance just before the marriage
The home sale contract and transfer records showing which account the deposit and balance were paid from
Records of money sent by your parents and messages exchanged at the time
Records showing whose account loan repayments were made from
For inherited assets, inheritance documents and the registered ground of transfer
Records showing the loan balance around the time of the marriage (a loan reduced during the marriage may be argued to have been repaid jointly)

sections.title: Severance pay and pensions
body: Severance pay and retirement pensions accumulated during the marriage can be subject to division regardless of whose name they are in. If your spouse has not yet retired, the amount of retirement benefits expected if they retired around the close of the hearings in the divorce lawsuit is subject to division (Supreme Court en banc decision of July 16, 2014, 2013므2250). If it is a job held since before the marriage, that period may be considered when assessing contribution, so check both the start date of employment and the date of marriage.

sections.title: As of when are assets divided?
body: In a judicial divorce, the assets and their values for property division are in principle set as of the close of the final hearing on the facts. So if home prices rise during the lawsuit, the new market price is reflected. However, assets one spouse newly built up alone during a long separation may be excluded from division.
The value of real estate is set through appraisal or market price data, so if prices are moving sharply, you also need to decide in advance how to submit market price evidence.

At Jisan Law, we organize in a table in the consultation when and with whose money each asset came about, and separate what to argue as separate property from what to argue as contribution. If it is hard to bring all the records at once, message us through the chat on this page to discuss first.

faqs.q: We've been married 2 years. Is the home split 50/50?
faqs.a: The shorter the marriage, the more weight is given to the assets each spouse brought in, so the split is often not 50/50. Who put in how much and who repaid the loan after the marriage are the key records for setting the ratio.

faqs.q: Can a home in my spouse's parents' name also be divided?
faqs.a: If the title is in the name of your spouse's parents, it is in principle not the couple's asset and is not subject to division. However, if it is proved that the couple actually paid for it and only borrowed the parents' name, there may be room to dispute it.

guides.title: Breaking up after living together without a marriage report
guides.lead: Even if you never filed a marriage report, if you lived as a married couple, you can claim property division and compensation for emotional distress when you separate. First you need to show it was a de facto marriage, not simply living together.

seo.title: Ending a De Facto Marriage in Korea: Property Division, Compensation and Evidence | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When breaking up after living together without a marriage report in Korea: what separates a de facto marriage from simple cohabitation, the evidence that shows a de facto marriage, deadlines for property division and compensation claims, the documents to keep when settling by agreement, the limits when a de facto spouse dies, and matters concerning children.
keywords: de facto marriage property division Korea

sections.title: De facto marriage or cohabitation?
body: To be recognized as a de facto marriage (사실혼), the two of you must have intended to live as a married couple and actually lived together as one. A long time living together is not enough on its own; the court looks at everything together, including whether you held a wedding, whether you introduced each other as spouses to both families and others, and whether you ran the household finances together.

Unlike a legal marriage, there is no divorce report procedure, so the relationship ends once one partner ends it. If there is a dispute, you claim property division and compensation for emotional distress arising from the end of the de facto marriage in the family court, and if needed also file a lawsuit to confirm that a de facto marital relationship existed.

If you broke up after the families met and a wedding date was set, it may be seen as an engagement. When an engagement is broken off, the way you dispute the return of wedding gifts and damages is different, so first decide how the relationship should be characterized.
Even if you did not register at the same address, it can be recognized if other material shows a shared life as a married couple.

sections.title: Material that shows a de facto marriage
bullets: The wedding venue contract, wedding invitations, and photos and videos of the ceremony
Resident registration records showing you moved in at the same address
Photos of visiting both families on holidays, and messages exchanged with both families
Conversations using terms couples use, such as 'honey', 'husband', 'wife' or 'mother-in-law'
A joint account for living costs, and records of jointly paying a jeonse deposit or buying appliances and furniture

sections.title: What you can claim, and the deadlines
body: Case law applies the property division (재산분할) provisions by analogy to the end of a de facto marriage. Assets built while living together are divided according to contribution regardless of whose name they are in, and the claim must be made within 2 years of the day the relationship ended. Even for a home in your partner's name, if you contributed to the deposit or helped repay the loan, you can claim a share to that extent.

If the relationship broke down because of your partner's affair, verbal abuse or violence, you can claim compensation for emotional distress (위자료) for wrongfully ending the de facto marriage. This is a tort damages claim, so it must be made within 3 years of learning of the damage and the person responsible (Civil Act (민법) Article 766). You can also make a separate claim against the affair partner.

Property division covers assets formed or maintained together during the de facto marriage, and assets each partner had before that are in principle excluded. Even for a car bought in your partner's name, if you made the installment payments, those transfer records show your contribution.

If your partner cut off contact unilaterally and moved their belongings out, that day may be argued to be the day the relationship ended. Keep a record of your last conversation and the date the belongings were moved out.

sections.title: Points that are easy to miss
body: A de facto spouse has no right to inherit. Case law does not allow a property division claim when the de facto marriage ended because the partner died. If you intend to end the relationship, settle the property issues while your partner is alive.

If you have a child, first check whether the father has acknowledged the child (인지). If not, also file a claim for acknowledgment, and set the person with parental authority, the custodial parent and child support by the same standards as in a legal marriage. Since you are not married, there is no divorce-by-agreement procedure, so if you cannot agree, you petition the family court for a ruling.
If you lived together while your partner had a separate legal spouse, it is in principle hard to be protected as a de facto marriage. If this applies, first check the scope of what you can claim.

Child support for a child born during a de facto marriage is set using the same Child Support Guidelines, and if it is not paid once set, the same procedures, such as performance orders and direct payment orders, can be used.

sections.title: When settling by agreement
body: If you settle without a lawsuit, put in writing who takes what, how much will be paid and when, and how any deposit will be divided. Ending a de facto marriage has no court confirmation procedure, so the agreement is the only record that remains. If money is to be received later, making it into a notarized deed (공정증서) with a clause consenting to compulsory execution allows enforcement without another lawsuit.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: If your partner seems likely to deny that there was a de facto marriage at all, we group the material by period before filing the complaint so that it shows when the relationship began and how it continued.

At Jisan Law, we first check whether there is enough material to show a de facto marriage, organize the records of your contributions to the assets, and set the scope of the claim. The deadlines depend on when the relationship ended, so write down the date you separated and message us through the chat on this page to arrange a consultation.

faqs.q: We didn't have a wedding, but we lived together for 5 years. Is that a de facto marriage?
faqs.a: Even without a wedding, it can be recognized as a de facto marriage if there was an intention to live as a married couple and you actually lived like one. Contact between both families, signs that you presented yourselves as a couple to others, and records of managing living costs together are important. On the other hand, if you lived together sharing living costs with no intention of marrying each other, it is hard to see it as a de facto marriage.

faqs.q: Can I take the car and appliances I bought with my own money?
faqs.a: Even for things bought while living together, if most of the money was yours, you can argue in property division that they should be counted as your share. Collect payment records and receipts. For appliances and furniture, the parties often agree that whoever actually uses them keeps them and the difference is settled in money.

guides.title: Is it okay to move out before the divorce?
guides.lead: Moving out first does not by itself put you at a disadvantage in a divorce. What matters is why you left and how you handled the children and living expenses after leaving.

seo.title: Separating Before Divorce in Korea: Does Moving Out Hurt Your Case? Living Expenses | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether you can move out first before a divorce in Korea, when it counts as malicious desertion, what to take before leaving, what to watch for when leaving with children, living expenses and property division during separation, and the risks of seeing someone else while separated.

sections.title: The reason matters more than the fact that you left
body: The Civil Act (민법) sets malicious desertion of a spouse as a ground for divorce (Civil Act Article 840, Item 2), but case law holds that this means abandoning, without a valid reason, the duties to live together, help each other and provide support. If you left to escape verbal abuse, violence or ongoing conflict, you do not bear responsibility for the breakdown just because you left first.

Conversely, if you cut off contact and even living expenses without any explanation, the risk of being accused of desertion grows. The law also states that spouses must accept each other temporarily living apart for a justifiable reason (Civil Act Article 826(1)).
A long separation is sometimes treated as a sign that the marriage has broken down beyond repair, but there is no rule that it is automatically considered broken down after a certain number of years.

sections.title: What to take care of before leaving
bullets: Send your spouse a short message explaining why you are leaving. It becomes a record that you did not simply vanish.
Write down the date the separation began. It will be used later when property division and the time of breakdown are examined.
Take photos of records that will be hard to see again once left at home, such as the home's register, loans, bank statements and insurance policies.
Take your ID, your children's documents, bankbooks and cards in your name, and medication.
If there is a joint account or family card, agree by message on rules for using it so that spending after you leave does not become a dispute.

sections.title: If you leave with your children
body: It is usually not a problem for the parent who has actually been caring for the children to leave with them. However, if you completely block the other parent from seeing them, you may later be seen as an uncooperative parent when the custodial parent is decided. It is better to set how they will meet.

Suddenly changing schools or daycare disrupts the children's lives, so be careful. If your spouse tries to take the children, you can file a lawsuit and apply for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) designating a temporary custodial parent.
If circumstances forced you to leave alone without the children, keep in steady contact asking how they are and arranging to visit. This becomes a record showing your will to raise them.
Moving the children's registered address may change their school assignment, so think about the timing of the move-in report too.

sections.title: Living expenses and property during separation
body: Even living apart, spouses have a duty to support each other and share living costs (Civil Act Articles 826 and 833). If your spouse has cut off living expenses, you can claim spousal support (부양료) or marriage expenses (혼인생활비용), or, during a lawsuit, ask for temporary living expenses and child support to be set through a pre-trial measure.

Leaving the home does not end your right to property division (재산분할) of that home. However, assets one spouse built up alone during a long separation may be excluded from division, so the date the separation began matters.
If you have kept sending living expenses, those transfer records show you fulfilled your duty of support. If you did not, you need to be able to explain why.
If you are not considering a lawsuit, you can also petition for a spousal support ruling on its own.

sections.title: If you are the one who stayed
body: If your spouse left home, record the date they left and what they said at the time. If contact has been cut off and no living expenses are coming, your records of living costs during that period support a claim of desertion and a spousal support claim. Throwing out your spouse's belongings or changing the door code to keep them out can lead to new disputes, so arrange the removal of belongings on a set date and keep a record by message.

sections.title: If you see someone else during the separation
body: Even during a separation, as long as you are legally married, a relationship with someone else can be treated as infidelity. The judgment may differ if the marriage had already broken down beyond repair, but disputes easily arise over when that point was reached. It is safer to be careful until the divorce is settled.

Conversely, if you learn your spouse is seeing someone else during the separation, keep the dates and material separately. They are used when responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage is examined.

At Jisan Law, we work out with you what to leave in place when you separate and how to settle living expenses and matters concerning the children. If you want to talk it over once before leaving, contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: After several years of separation, are we automatically divorced?
faqs.a: Separation alone does not result in divorce. A long separation is considered as one sign that the marriage has broken down beyond repair, but the court also looks at how the separation came about, contact and visits, efforts to reunite, and the financial relationship. To divorce, you must go through the agreement or court procedure.

faqs.q: Since I moved out, do I have to give the home to my spouse who lives there?
faqs.a: Who lives in the home and property division are separate matters. The home remains subject to division, and in a lawsuit it is in principle valued at the market price around the close of the hearings.

guides.title: When your foreign spouse leaves home and cuts off contact
guides.lead: When a spouse who came to Korea on a marriage migrant visa suddenly disappears, it is upsetting, and with the marriage still registered, both remarrying and putting your life in order are blocked. You can divorce even if you cannot reach your spouse, so start by steadily keeping the records you will need later.

seo.title: Foreign Spouse Left Home or Out of Contact: How to Divorce in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When a foreign spouse leaves home and cuts off contact in Korea: what to do first, such as filing a missing-person report and confirming personal details, what not to do, a divorce lawsuit by service by public notice and considering nullity of marriage, and reporting the divorce after the judgment, in order.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Doing the following in order will give you the records you need for the lawsuit.
bullets: File a missing-person report at the police station for your address and get a record of its receipt. Even if your spouse is not found, it becomes an official record showing their whereabouts are unknown.
Send your spouse messages asking them to come back or get in touch, and save screenshots. They become a record that you tried to continue the marriage.
Find copies of their residence card or passport and the documents submitted when you reported the marriage, and check their name in Roman letters, date of birth and passport number.
Organize the belongings your spouse left behind, records of money transfers, and the date of last contact.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Avoid contacting your spouse's family or acquaintances in their home country in a way that could seem threatening. It could later give your spouse grounds to claim they left because of verbal abuse. Do not throw away or sell your spouse's belongings on your own either.
You cannot register a marriage with someone else while your current marriage has not been dissolved. If you are thinking of a new relationship, first finalize the divorce.

Some people end things by signing only an agreement with the marriage broker, along the lines of 'we will not make an issue of it in return for a refund', but that agreement does not dissolve the marriage. Treat issues with the broker and dissolving the marriage as separate matters.

sections.title: The divorce proceeds as a lawsuit
body: A divorce by agreement (협의이혼) requires both spouses to appear at court together, so it cannot be used when your spouse has disappeared. If your spouse left home without a valid reason and cut off contact, you claim a judicial divorce (재판상 이혼) on the ground of malicious desertion or another serious reason making it difficult to continue the marriage (Civil Act (민법) Article 840, Items 2 and 6).

If there are clear signs that the marriage was reported from the start as a means of entering Korea without any intention to marry, nullity of the marriage (혼인무효) is also considered. If nullity is recognized, the marriage is treated as never having existed, and the record is different from that of a divorce.

Either way, the length of time you lived together after the wedding, who paid the living costs, and what your spouse said and did before leaving become the basis for the decision. Write these down by date before your memory fades.

sections.title: The lawsuit goes all the way even without an address
body: In the complaint, you state that your spouse's address is unknown, and immigration records and the address are checked through the court. If it is then shown that your spouse still cannot be found, the case proceeds by service by public notice (공시송달) (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 194).

The first service by public notice takes effect 2 weeks after it is posted, and service by public notice on a person to be served abroad takes effect after 2 months (Article 196 of the same Act). Even if your spouse does not appear, a judgment can be issued after the hearings.

Even in a case proceeding by service by public notice, the judge does not grant the divorce just by hearing the plaintiff's side. Organize and submit how the marriage came about, how long you lived together, and records of attempts to make contact after your spouse left, and if needed, prepare written statements from family members or neighbors.

sections.title: The procedure ahead
body: The case proceeds in this order: filing the complaint, correcting the address and fact inquiries, service by public notice, hearings and judgment. Once the judgment is final, you must report the divorce to the city, district, town or township office within 1 month for it to be reflected in the family relationship register.

If you have a child, the court sets the person with parental authority and the custodial parent together with the divorce judgment. If you are worried that your spouse may leave the country with the child, also consider a pre-trial measure (사전처분) concerning the child's care when you file the lawsuit.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, organizes your spouse's personal details from the remaining documents, and judges with you whether divorce or nullity is the right fit. We prepare the lawsuit documents, including the address correction, fact inquiries and the application for service by public notice. Consultations are available at our main office in Seoul and our branch offices in Incheon, Hongseong and Songpa.

faqs.q: I think my spouse has gone back to their home country. Can I still divorce in Korea?
faqs.a: For a Korean spouse living in Korea, Korean courts usually have jurisdiction and Korean law applies (Private International Law Act Articles 56 and 66). A separate procedure in the other country may be needed to have it reflected in that country's records too.

faqs.q: How long does the lawsuit take?
faqs.a: Because the address search and the service by public notice period are added, it tends to take longer than a case in which the other spouse appears. If service abroad has to be attempted, it can take even longer, so securing accurate personal details from the start is the way to shorten the time.

guides.title: When the spouse who had an affair files for divorce
guides.lead: If the spouse at fault sends you a divorce complaint first, the sense of injustice comes first. The court in principle does not accept a divorce claim from the spouse who broke up the marriage, so before reacting emotionally, decide what outcome you want.

seo.title: When a Cheating Spouse Files for Divorce in Korea: How to Respond | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to check first when a spouse who broke up the marriage through an affair or leaving home files for divorce in Korea, how to respond if you do not want a divorce or would agree if the terms are right, how to show your intention to continue the marriage, and what not to do.

sections.title: What to check first
body: When you receive the complaint, start by organizing the following.

The complaint contains only your spouse's side, so it is natural to get angry reading it. Rather than sending a text rebutting it right away, it is better to mark the untrue parts and put them in your answer. If a notice of a mediation session came with it, check the date too.
bullets: Write down the date you received the complaint. Your answer is due within 30 days of being served.
Mark the parts of the complaint where your spouse claims you were at fault, and note by date what is untrue.
Keep the messages, photos and card records showing the affair in their original form.
Think through whether you do not want a divorce, or whether you could agree if the terms are right. Your answer will differ depending on this choice.

sections.title: If you don't want a divorce
body: The Supreme Court in principle does not allow a divorce claim by the spouse mainly responsible for the breakdown of the marriage (en banc decision of September 15, 2015, 2013므568). However, an exception may be recognized if it appears that the other spouse also has no intention of continuing the marriage.

So simply saying 'I won't agree to a divorce' is not enough. In a decision of June 16, 2022 (2021므14258), the Supreme Court said that the intention to continue the marriage should be judged by actual words and conduct, not by what is said in the lawsuit. There needs to be a record of efforts to maintain the relationship, such as agreeing to couples counseling recommended by the court, keeping in contact about the children, and asking for living expenses.

Even small things, such as messages asking for living expenses or records of suggesting you attend a child's birthday or school event together, add up and matter. Conversely, posting criticism of your spouse on social media during the lawsuit or refusing all contact can be used as grounds that you have no intention of continuing the marriage.

If the court recommends couples counseling or a family investigation (가사조사), cooperate as far as possible. If your spouse keeps seeing the affair partner even during the lawsuit, record that as well to show that their responsibility is still heavy.

sections.title: If you could accept a divorce on the right terms
body: If you accept the divorce itself but want to dispute the terms, you file a counterclaim (반소) for compensation for emotional distress (위자료), property division (재산분할), designation of the person with parental authority and the custodial parent, and child support. If your spouse wants a quick divorce, there is room to negotiate the terms in mediation.

You can also claim compensation from the affair partner. Whether to bring the claim together in the same family court case or as a separate civil lawsuit is decided by looking at the evidence and the affair partner's address.

When filing a counterclaim, you need to organize the list of assets, records of your contributions, and who has been caring for the children. Your share does not shrink just because your spouse sued first, so do not rush; weigh the terms carefully.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Sending a message in anger saying 'Fine, I'll give you a divorce'. It can be used as grounds that you have no intention of continuing the marriage.
Secretly opening your spouse's phone or installing a location-tracking app. This can become a separate criminal matter.
Telling the affair partner's workplace or posting about it on their social media. It can turn into a defamation dispute.
Speaking badly of your spouse to the children or blocking visits. It works against you when the custodial parent is decided.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, decides with you whether to keep the marriage or dispute the terms, and prepares the answer and counterclaim accordingly. In mediation, we check even the wording of the record so that you do not lose the outcome you want. Contact us through the chat on this page before 30 days pass from receiving the complaint.

faqs.q: If I don't file an answer, will the divorce just go through?
faqs.a: In family litigation, not filing an answer does not immediately lead to a judgment as your spouse claims, but you miss the chance to tell the court your side. If you do not want a divorce, state that clearly, with your reasons, within the deadline.

faqs.q: We're separated, and my spouse has been sending living expenses for years. Does that still mean no divorce?
faqs.a: The fact that the spouse at fault faithfully sent living expenses and child support during the separation can be considered in their favor when an exception is judged. In the end, the court weighs the intention to continue the marriage together with all the circumstances, so it is important to organize what you have done to repair the relationship.

guides.title: Can a homemaker receive property division?
guides.lead: Even if you never earned a salary, you can receive a share of the assets built together during the marriage. The same is true even if everything is in your spouse's name, so to avoid shrinking your share, start by gathering material that shows your contribution.

seo.title: Property Division for Homemakers in a Korean Divorce: Recognition of Contribution | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How the contribution of a homemaker who handled housework and childcare without income is assessed in property division in a Korean divorce, the circumstances that shape the ratio, easily missed severance pay, pensions and insurance, and what not to do and what to gather before divorce.

sections.title: What to secure first
body: Before you move out or bring up divorce, gather the following.
bullets: Certified copies of the registers for your home and any land, and the loan balances
The names of the financial institutions for any of your spouse's bank, insurance and securities accounts you know of
Your spouse's workplace and years of service (needed to calculate severance pay)
When and why you stopped working after the marriage, and how long you raised the children
The flow of money you brought into the marriage or received from your own family

sections.title: Contribution is recognized even without income
body: Property division (재산분할) is a system for dividing assets built through both spouses' cooperation during the marriage (Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2). Taking on housework and childcare so your spouse could focus on work, saving by cutting living costs and repaying loans, and managing the home and rental properties all count as cooperation.
So whose name an asset is in is only a starting point. The court looks at how the assets were built and who did what.

Material showing contribution does not have to be impressive. Household account books, living-expense bank records, daycare and medical records for the children, the period you cared for your in-laws, and traces of helping in your spouse's business can all be used. Even if the records are old, don't throw them away; keep them together.

sections.title: Circumstances that shape the ratio
body: There is no fixed formula. The general view in practice is that the longer the marriage, the more weight tends to be given to contributions through housework and childcare, but the ratio is not set by length alone.

Assets your spouse owned before the marriage or inherited are in principle not divided. However, if you helped protect them or increase their value, you can argue for them to be included in the division. Conversely, if there is a dispute claiming you wasted living expenses, you also need to prepare an explanation for that.

If you worked for a few years along the way or added to living costs through a side job, also organize your income for those periods. The fact that your career was interrupted for childcare can also be considered in relation to your ability to support yourself after the divorce.

sections.title: Assets that are easy to miss
bullets: Severance pay not yet received. Even while your spouse is still employed, the retirement benefits expected if they retired now are subject to division (Supreme Court en banc decision 2013므2250).
Civil service pensions and the National Pension. For the National Pension, a split pension is claimed separately from the National Pension Service after the divorce.
Surrender values of insurance policies, interests in your spouse's business, and cars
Deposits moved into the names of children or your spouse's relatives
body: It is fine if you do not know all the assets in your spouse's name. If you apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회) in the lawsuit, you can check assets in your spouse's name held at financial institutions and public agencies (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Articles 48-2 and 48-3).
