Any bank or company names you know help define the scope of the inquiry.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Do not sign a pledge saying 'I don't need any assets' just to end the conflict quickly. Leaving bank statements, insurance policies and registration documents behind when you move out is also a common mistake. On the other hand, secretly moving your spouse's assets into your name will only work against you.

Even if your spouse says 'you never earned any money, so you get nothing', do not set the terms based on that. Even when settling by agreement, writing the agreement after both of you have checked the list of assets reduces the chance of fighting again later.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally and organizes the list of assets and the material on your contribution on one page. Unknown assets are checked through asset disclosure orders and asset inquiries in the lawsuit, and for assets at risk of disposal, we start by applying for provisional attachment (가압류). We explain fees after the consultation, tailored to your case.

faqs.q: We've only been married 5 years. Can I still receive a share?
faqs.a: Yes. If the marriage is short, pre-marital assets carry more weight and there is less time to show contribution, so the ratio may be lower, but assets built together during that time are subject to division.

faqs.q: We lived in an apartment my husband received from his family.
faqs.a: Inherited or gifted assets are in principle separate property, but if you helped repay the loan or managed it for a long time so its value was maintained, it can be subject to division. Gather records of loan repayments and of paying maintenance fees and repair costs.

guides.title: When your spouse cuts off living expenses during separation
guides.lead: If living expenses stopped once you started living apart, you can claim them through the court even before divorce. But past living expenses are calculated from when you asked for them, so make a record of your request today.

seo.title: No Living Expenses During Separation in Korea: Claiming Spousal Support | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When your spouse cuts off living expenses during separation in Korea: what to do first, such as keeping a record of your request; what not to do; spousal support mediation and rulings, and pre-trial measures during a divorce lawsuit; and performance orders and detention when support is still not paid after the decision.
keywords: husband not paying living expenses Korea
living costs during divorce lawsuit Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Doing these in order moves forward the date from which you can claim.

If you have the children with you, keep separate notes of the money spent on the children and your own living costs. You can use them as is later when claiming child support and spousal support separately.
bullets: Send a request for living expenses by text or KakaoTalk. State the amount needed, the account to send it to and the date, and save a screenshot.
If there is no reply, send the same content once more by certified letter (내용증명).
Make a table of the date living expenses stopped, the amount you received before, and what you actually spend each month.
Write down any leads for checking your spouse's income, such as their workplace, payday and business address.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Withdrawing all the money from a joint account at once. This can escalate the dispute over property division.
Contacting your spouse's company to tell them about the living expenses problem
Demanding living expenses in exchange for letting your spouse see the children. Visits with the children and living expenses are handled separately.
body: Also avoid retaliating in kind if your spouse has frozen your card. Resolving living expenses through records and procedures is faster in the end, and emotional responses can be used against you when each side's faults are weighed in a divorce lawsuit.

sections.title: Why a record of your request matters
body: Spouses have a duty to support each other even when living apart (Civil Act (민법) Article 826). However, in a decision of August 25, 2017 (2014스26), the Supreme Court held that past living expenses can be claimed only for the period after they were requested but not paid.
Even if you put up with it for years, if there is no trace of a request, it will be hard to receive support for that period. The message you send today becomes the starting point of your claim.

When making the request, rather than 'please send some living money', it is better to state the amount and date clearly, for example: 'From this month, please send KRW ___ to this account by the ___ of each month.' If there are particular costs, such as the children's tutoring or medical bills, include the reason as well.

sections.title: How to claim through the court
body: Before divorce, you claim spousal support (부양료) from the family court. It is a Category Ma non-contentious family case, so it starts with mediation (조정), and if no agreement is reached, the court sets the amount by looking at both spouses' incomes, assets and standard of living. If you do not know your spouse's income, you can apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회).

If a divorce lawsuit is already under way, apply for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) ordering living expenses to be paid first until the judgment (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 62). Failing to follow a pre-trial measure can lead to an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million.

When the amount is being set, it helps to show by item what you actually spend, such as rent or maintenance fees, food, phone bills and the children's education. If your spouse seems to be hiding income, also submit material showing their card spending or standard of living.

sections.title: If they still don't pay after the decision
body: If the spousal support ruling is final and payment still is not made, you apply for a performance order (이행명령). If three or more monthly payments are missed, you can apply for detention (감치) for up to 30 days (Family Litigation Act Articles 64 and 68). Compulsory execution, such as seizing wages or deposits using the ruling, is also possible.

If your spouse works for a company, seizing wages is often the most effective; if they are self-employed, deposits and real estate are found through an asset inquiry and seized. Violating a performance order can also lead to a separate administrative fine.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, works out the wording of your written request with you, and decides in what order to file the spousal support claim, the divorce lawsuit and any pre-trial measure. We also prepare applications to check your spouse's income.

faqs.q: Can I claim the children's living costs and my own together?
faqs.a: Yes. The children's share is often set as child support and the spouse's share as spousal support, so keep separate records of the children's costs and your own living expenses.

faqs.q: I was the one who left home. Can I still receive support?
faqs.a: The reason you left matters. If you left because of verbal abuse, violence or severe conflict, it can be seen as a justifiable reason, but if you left for no reason and cut off contact, your claim may be limited. Keep material showing how you came to leave.

guides.title: If you divorced without property division
guides.lead: Even if you rushed through a divorce by agreement without discussing property, it may not be too late. The right disappears 2 years after the date of divorce, so first check when it expires.

seo.title: How to Claim Property Division After Divorce in Korea and the 2-Year Deadline | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When you divorced by agreement without property division, or assets were left out of the judgment, in Korea: confirming the date of divorce and calculating the deadline, what not to do, the order of the claim and provisional attachment, and the Supreme Court decision on hidden assets found later.
keywords: property division after divorce by agreement Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Start with what you can do today.

If fewer than three months remain until the deadline, file first rather than gathering more material. The claim can be filed with just the assets you know of, and the rest is supplemented within the procedure.
bullets: Get a detailed marriage relationship certificate (혼인관계증명서 상세) and check the date the divorce was reported or the judgment became final. Mark on your calendar the day 2 years from that date.
Write down the assets in your ex-spouse's name as far as you know them. Even without exact amounts, bank names or the apartment building and unit number are enough.
If you wrote an agreement or pledge at the divorce, find it.
If you hear that your ex-spouse has listed the home for sale or is moving deposits, write it down with the date.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Even if your ex-spouse says 'I'll share it with you later', do not just take their word for it and wait. The 2-year period does not stop because you made a demand, so it can run out while an agreement drags on.
Picking only a few certain assets to claim first is also risky. If the period passes while you are trying to add the remaining assets later, you cannot receive that part.

Also be careful about announcing 'I'll sue' when contacting your ex-spouse about dividing property. They may dispose of or move the assets in the meantime. If there are assets you are worried will be disposed of, it is safer to apply for provisional attachment (가압류) together with the claim.

sections.title: The order of the claim
body: The deadline is met only if a mediation application or petition for a ruling on property division (재산분할) is filed with the family court (Civil Act (민법) Article 839-2(3)). For a claim after a divorce by agreement, the assets to be divided and their values are set as of the time the divorce took effect.

If you do not know your ex-spouse's assets, apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회), and if there is a risk of disposal, first secure a provisional attachment or an injunction against disposal (처분금지가처분). If little time remains, file first even if you have not gathered all the material, and supplement it later.

If your ex-spouse handed over some assets at the divorce by agreement, those are also part of the settlement. Your share must be calculated out of all the assets, combining what you have already received and what you will receive, so write down every payment and item exchanged at the divorce.

If agreement is reached in mediation, the mediation record (조정조서) should clearly state the assets to be transferred, the amount to be paid and the payment deadline. Vague wording leads to new disputes later at the enforcement stage.

The claim is filed with the family court with jurisdiction over the other party's address (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 46). If your ex-spouse has moved, you need to confirm the current address with a resident registration abstract, which you can obtain within the lawsuit procedure through the court's correction order.

sections.title: If hidden assets come to light later
body: According to a Supreme Court decision of June 22, 2018 (2018스18), if assets that were not dealt with at all in the property division proceedings are discovered later, an additional division can be claimed. However, that additional claim must also be made within 2 years of the date of divorce.

The same decision held that if only some assets were claimed within the 2 years, the right to claim the remaining assets disappears once the period passes. That is why you must list every asset you know of when you first file.

If your ex-spouse transferred assets into the names of family members or acquaintances ahead of the divorce, a lawsuit to revoke the disposal as a fraudulent act (사해행위취소) can also be considered (Civil Act Article 839-3). It cannot be filed once 1 year has passed since you learned of the disposal, so record the date you found out.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, calculates the deadline, and sets the order of filing and preservation measures based on the time remaining. When the asset inquiry results come in, we expand the claim so that no assets are left out.

faqs.q: Our agreement says 'neither party will make claims about property'.
faqs.a: That clause alone does not block every claim. Its effect may be judged differently depending on whether it simply waived the right in advance before the divorce or whether the assets were all reviewed and accounts settled. Organize how it came to be written and what assets you knew of at the time, and get advice.

faqs.q: I was awarded property division in the judgment, but my ex-spouse won't pay.
faqs.a: You can enforce it with the judgment or mediation record, and if it is an obligation to pay money, you can also apply for a performance order (이행명령). For real estate, the judgment allows you to apply for registration on your own (Real Estate Registration Act Article 23(4)).

guides.title: When child support needs to go up or down
guides.lead: A few years after child support is set, the children have grown and the parents' circumstances have changed. Child support can be reset when circumstances change, but it does not change by one parent deciding alone and giving notice.

seo.title: How to Request an Increase or Decrease in Child Support in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When child support needs to be raised after divorce in Korea because of the child's schooling or medical costs, or lowered because of job loss or business closure: what to check first, the changes in circumstances the court recognizes, what happens if you reduce payments on your own, the mediation and ruling procedure, and the material to prepare.
keywords: change in circumstances child support Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: Whichever side you are on, start by organizing the following.
bullets: Check whether the document setting child support is a judgment, a mediation record or a child support protocol.
Write down what has changed between then and now: the child's grade at school, any treatment, both parents' incomes and jobs, new family members and so on.
Get your latest income documents (withholding tax receipt, certificate of income amount).
First talk with the other parent about whether you can agree in writing. If you agree, you can record it in a mediation record.

sections.title: When you can ask for an increase
body: If education costs have increased because the child moved up to a higher school, a serious illness has brought medical costs, or so much time has passed that prices have risen sharply, you can ask for an increase. A large rise in the other parent's income since the original decision is also a relevant circumstance.

Check the amount that fits the child's current age and both parents' incomes in the Child Support Guidelines (양육비 산정기준표) the court uses, and show actual spending with receipts for tutoring and medical bills.

If the amount was set low because the child was young at the divorce, the key is showing that actual spending rose sharply as the child moved on to elementary and middle school. Dated material works well for spending records, such as tutoring receipts, records of buying school uniforms and textbooks, and medical receipts.

sections.title: When you can ask for a decrease
body: If your income has dropped sharply through no fault of your own, for example because you were laid off for business reasons, your business closed, or a serious illness left you unable to work, you can ask for a decrease. If you quit voluntarily or appear to be hiding income, it is unlikely to be accepted.
Remarriage alone does not lead to a decrease. Explain how long the reduced income is expected to last, and show with material your efforts to find work again.

Along with material showing why your income dropped, such as records of unemployment benefits, a certificate of business closure or a medical certificate, you need to organize how your current living costs are spent. If you have steadily paid child support until now, records of that also add credibility.

sections.title: What not to do
body: If the paying parent reduces or stops payments without a court decision, the difference from the original amount becomes overdue child support as is. They may face sanctions such as a performance order, detention or suspension of their driver's license.
The receiving parent also must not block visits with the child because a request for more support is not accepted. Visitation and child support are separate obligations.

Even if you got the other parent's understanding by phone to 'send less just this month', it will become a dispute later if that promise is not recorded. If something comes up, leave a record by message, and if it is a long-term problem, ask for a change right away.

sections.title: How the procedure works
body: Changing child support is a change of a disposition on the child's upbringing and is a Category Ma non-contentious family case (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 2). You file for mediation (조정) with the family court, and if no agreement is reached, it is decided by a ruling. Until the decision comes out, the original amount must continue to be paid.
The decision also sets from when the changed amount applies, so if circumstances have changed, file without delay.

Even if you agree on an amount with the other parent, if it is recorded only in messages or a pledge, it is hard to enforce later. If you file for mediation and record it in a mediation record (조정조서), you can use that record to apply for a performance order or a direct payment order. It is also a good idea to settle costs after adulthood, such as university tuition, at the same time.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally and calculates the amount to claim by comparing the guideline amount, actual spending and changes in income. If agreement is reached in mediation, we clearly record in the record everything from the payment date and account to the sharing of large costs such as university tuition.

faqs.q: After filing for a change, how much do I have to pay until the decision?
faqs.a: Until the decision is made, the originally set amount remains your obligation. If you reduce payments in advance because you filed for a decrease, the difference builds up as overdue child support.

faqs.q: How can I find out whether the other parent's income has increased significantly?
faqs.a: After filing, you can apply to the court for an asset disclosure order or asset inquiry to check the other parent's income and assets (Family Litigation Act Articles 48-2 and 48-3).

guides.title: Moving abroad with your child after divorce
guides.lead: If you plan to live abroad with your child for study, a new job or remarriage, first sort out the other parent's rights. Leaving without consent can trigger international proceedings to have the child returned.

seo.title: Moving Abroad with Your Child After Divorce in Korea: Passport Consent | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: When moving abroad with your child after a divorce in Korea: checking who holds parental authority and getting a passport, the cooperation needed under joint parental authority, family court procedures when the other parent objects, Hague Convention child return issues if you leave without consent, and readjusting visitation.
keywords: moving abroad with child after divorce Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: Before making plans, look at the following.

When you tell the other parent about the plan also matters. If you give notice just before leaving, the other parent may apply first for a pre-trial measure or register an objection to the passport being issued, and the court may also see you as not having respected the process. Give written notice well in advance.
bullets: Check who is listed as the person with parental authority on your child's basic certificate. The procedure differs depending on whether it is sole or joint.
Reread the visitation provisions in the judgment or mediation record. The frequency and places will have been set on the assumption that you live in Korea.
Check whether the country you are moving to is a party to the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction.
Put in writing your child's living plan after the move, such as school, housing and work.

sections.title: Under joint parental authority, you need the other parent's cooperation
body: If parental authority remains joint after the divorce, both parents often need to agree on important decisions such as issuing the child's passport and leaving the country long-term. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also runs a system under which, if one joint holder of parental authority registers an objection to the child's passport being issued, the other cannot obtain the passport.

If the other parent ultimately refuses to consent, you can ask the family court to change the person with parental authority (친권자) or make a disposition on child-rearing and have the court decide. You need to show both why the move is necessary for the child and how the child's relationship with the other parent will be maintained.

If you reach an agreement, put in writing the destination country and duration, when the child will visit Korea, and how visitation (면접교섭) will work, and record it in a mediation record (조정조서). Verbal consent easily becomes a 'that never happened' dispute later.

sections.title: What happens if you take the child without consent
body: If a child is taken to a Convention country in breach of one parent's custody rights, the parent left behind can request the child's return through that country's Central Authority. Korea has the same procedure under the Act on the Implementation of the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction.

Criminal issues depend on the case. In an en banc decision of June 20, 2013 (2010도14328), the Supreme Court held that it was not abduction where a parent who had been peacefully caring for the child left the country with the child, but the conclusion may differ if the other parent's custody was disrupted by assault, threats or unlawful force. Leaving the country without consent can also be grounds for a request to change the custodial parent.

The parent who took the child faces return proceedings in the other country's court, and the child may have to come back before even adjusting to the new environment. In the end the heaviest burden falls on the child, so moving through the proper procedure is the path that serves the child.

sections.title: Visitation must be set again
body: Once you move abroad, it is hard to keep the existing visitation arrangement as is. Setting new terms for regular video calls, the child's stays in Korea during school vacations, sharing airfare, and the currency and method for sending child support, and recording them in a mediation record, reduces disputes later.

If you are the parent staying in Korea with the child leaving, consider applying for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) and registering an objection to the passport being issued as soon as you learn of the other parent's plan to move.

Set the days and times for video calls with the time difference and school schedules in mind, and write down in advance who will look after the child and where while the child is in Korea. Small issues, such as who buys the plane tickets, often turn into conflicts.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, the managing partner consults with you personally, checks the status of parental authority and the plan to move, and prepares a proposed agreement with the other parent or a petition to the family court. If you are the parent whose child would be leaving, we also consider procedures to prevent the departure.

faqs.q: I'm the sole person with parental authority and the custodial parent. Do I still need the other parent's consent?
faqs.a: As the sole person with parental authority, you can apply for the passport alone. However, the other parent's right of visitation remains, so if the move makes visitation practically impossible, the arrangement has to be set again and the other parent may raise an objection.

faqs.q: Do I need the other parent's permission even for a short trip abroad?
faqs.a: Under joint parental authority, cooperation may be needed from the passport application onward. It helps to write in the record at the divorce that short trips only require notice while long stays require a separate agreement.

guides.title: What to take care of after the divorce is final
guides.lead: Receiving the judgment does not mean everything is over. Tasks with deadlines remain, such as reporting, registration, your children's documents and pension claims, so sort them out in one go.

seo.title: What to Do After a Divorce Judgment Becomes Final in Korea: Reporting the Divorce | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: After a divorce judgment or mediation becomes final in Korea: reporting the divorce and the person with parental authority within 1 month, registering property division and settling loans and insurance, documents for your children, deadlines for splitting the National Pension and civil service pensions, and the procedures when the other spouse does not comply.

sections.title: Within one month
body: Count from the date the judgment became final or the date mediation succeeded.
bullets: For a judicial divorce, report the divorce within 1 month of the date it became final, attaching a certified copy of the judgment and a certificate of finality. The other spouse may also file the report.
If there was a decision setting the person with parental authority, also report the person with parental authority within the same period.
Obtain several copies of the judgment, the certificate of finality and the original mediation record. You will keep using them for registration, at banks and at schools.
Reporting late can lead to an administrative fine of up to KRW 50,000.

sections.title: Settling property
body: If the judgment or mediation record sets a transfer of real estate, you can apply for the ownership transfer registration on your own using that record (Real Estate Registration Act Article 23(4)). If you delay and the other spouse acquires other creditors in the meantime, things get complicated.

The name on a loan does not change by the judgment alone; the financial institution's approval is needed. Also change the policyholder and beneficiary on insurance, the name on vehicles, and automatic payments for utilities.

If property division (재산분할) is to be paid in installments, record the date and amount each time money comes in. If a payment is late even once, making a written demand right away helps later compulsory execution. Real estate received through property division may be taxed differently when you sell it later, so check before selling.

sections.title: Documents concerning the children
body: Notify the other parent in writing of the account for receiving child support (양육비), and keep a separate record of deposits. If you tell the school and daycare about the change of guardian and contact details, and the hospital about the change of legal representative, you will avoid trouble over consent later.
For visitation (면접교섭), schedule the first visit as written in the record, and keep a record of later schedules and changes by message.

If the children are still registered as dependents under the other parent's health insurance, ask the National Health Insurance Service whether they can be moved to the parent actually raising them. If there are bank accounts or insurance in the children's names, also settle who will manage them.

sections.title: Claims with deadlines
bullets: If property division was not decided, it must be claimed within 2 years of the date of divorce.

For a split National Pension (분할연금), if you divorced before reaching the pension age, you can file an advance claim within 3 years of the divorce, and once all requirements are met, you must claim within 5 years.
A split civil service pension is claimed within 3 years of meeting the requirements.
body: Pension claim deadlines feel far off at the time of the divorce, so they are easy to miss. Print your pension coverage records and keep them with your divorce documents, and note when your former spouse is expected to retire. If a separate division ratio was set, you must also keep that record to report it to the pension service.

sections.title: If the other spouse does not follow the judgment
body: If money is not paid, you can seize deposits and wages using the judgment or record, and you can also apply for a performance order (이행명령). For child support, there are direct payment orders and detention, and if the other parent will not let you see your child, there is a performance order for visitation. See also our guides 'When your ex won't pay the child support set at the divorce' and 'When your ex won't let you see your child (visitation)'.

Having a certificate of execution attached to the original judgment speeds up applications for seizure. If the other spouse hides assets, apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and asset inquiry (재산조회) to first find the assets to seize.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, we organize the reporting and pension claim schedule that remains after the judgment, and also handle applications for ownership transfer registration based on the judgment or record. If the other spouse does not comply, we continue with compulsory execution and performance orders. If questions come up after the judgment, contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: Does a divorce by agreement also have to be reported within 1 month?
faqs.a: A divorce by agreement has a different deadline. It must be reported within 3 months of receiving the certified copy of the court's confirmation, and once this period passes, the confirmation loses its effect and you have to apply again from the beginning.

faqs.q: Our case ended in mediation. Do we still have to report the divorce?
faqs.a: When mediation succeeds, it has the same effect as a judgment, but to have it reflected in the family relationship register, you must report the divorce within 1 month of the date mediation succeeded, attaching a certified copy of the mediation record.

guides.stage: I found out my spouse is having an affair
guides.title: When you find out your spouse is having an affair
guides.lead: What you do in the first few days after confirming an affair can change the outcome of a later lawsuit. Here, in order, is what to do first and what not to do.

seo.title: Found Out Your Spouse Is Cheating in Korea? What to Do First | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: How to keep records right after discovering your spouse's affair in Korea, why you shouldn't contact the affair partner right away, what not to do, how to secure material that may be erased, and how to decide whether to pursue a divorce or an affair lawsuit first.
keywords: what to do after discovering affair Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: The first few days after confirming an affair are when you are most shaken. Even so, if you take the steps below in order, you won't lose out whatever you decide later.

These five things are things you can do on your own today. Whether to divorce, or to hold only the affair partner (상간자) responsible, can be decided calmly after you have done them; it won't be too late. If you reverse the order and confront them first, it is hard to take back.
bullets: Write down in a notes app the date you found out and how. Include what you saw and what your spouse said at the time.
Leave the material in front of you as it is, and keep separate screenshots. Make sure the date and the other person's name appear on the same screen.
Write down everything you know about the affair partner: name, phone number, KakaoTalk ID, workplace, car plate number, even the neighborhood they live in.
Check whether there is material that will soon be erased, such as motel or parking-lot CCTV, and if so, note the date and place separately.
Mark on your calendar the date 3 years from the day you found out. This is the basis for the time limit on a claim against the affair partner.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Wanting to confront them and get an apology right away is natural. But early contact gives the affair partner time to delete chats and get their story straight with your spouse. It can also lead them to prepare the argument that they never knew your spouse was married.

Going to their workplace, posting on social media or telling their family can be defamation (명예훼손) even if it is true. Installing a location-tracking app on your spouse's phone, leaving a recorder in their car or secretly accessing your spouse's accounts can also be punished, and such material is hard to use as evidence. Texts containing insults will be used later when the other side files a counter-complaint or argues for a reduced amount.
bullets: Contacting the affair partner right away
Telling their workplace, family or social media
Installing a location-tracking app or a recorder
Secretly accessing your spouse's accounts
Seeing someone else out of anger

sections.title: Material that may be erased is secured through court procedures
body: CCTV at lodging businesses or buildings is overwritten over time. In most cases the business won't show you the footage even if you ask directly, so we consider applying to the court for evidence preservation (증거보전), specifying the date and place.
Keep the memory card from your own car's dashcam separately before it is overwritten. Taking or opening the device in someone else's car can be a separate problem.

sections.title: Next steps: divorce or an affair lawsuit first?
body: You can claim compensation for emotional distress (위자료) from the affair partner whether or not you divorce. If you plan to stay married, we consider claiming only against the affair partner while settling the right to reimbursement (구상권) through mediation or settlement; if you have decided to divorce, we consider claiming against both your spouse and the affair partner in the family court.

If you haven't made up your mind yet, there is no need to rush. However, you cannot claim once 3 years have passed from the day you learned of the affair partner and the infidelity, and a divorce claim on the ground of infidelity cannot be made once 6 months have passed from the day you learned of it or 2 years from the day it happened (Civil Act (민법) Article 841). Keep track of these deadlines, at least.

sections.title: How to organize your material
body: Once you have dozens of screenshots, it gets confusing which is from when. Save them with the date at the front of the file name, like "2026-03-14 KakaoTalk," and keep them in one folder. For card or bank transactions, it's convenient to set the period in the app and download them as a PDF.

If you upload them to a cloud or shared album you use with your spouse, your spouse could see and delete them. Keep them in storage only you use. Moving material from your spouse's phone to yours can be a problem depending on how it's done, so talk with us first.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Before anyone contacts the affair partner, Jisan Law first looks at the material you have now together with you. We decide together what is already sufficient and what is missing, whether evidence preservation is needed, and whether to start with a certified letter (내용증명) or file a lawsuit right away. A managing partner handles the consultation personally. We don't hide behind office managers or associate lawyers; we go through the material you bring from the start, together with you. We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have heard the details of the case and the scope of work.
If you discover something late at night and can't sleep, you can send us a message through the chat on this page right then.

faqs.q: My spouse admitted the affair and promised never to see them again. Can I still sue?
faqs.a: Forgiving your spouse and holding the affair partner responsible are separate matters. You can claim compensation from the affair partner while staying married. If your spouse is cooperative, getting a written statement describing the affair, or related material, will help the lawsuit.

faqs.q: I have almost no evidence. Is it still worth getting a consultation?
faqs.a: You can get a consultation even if you have little material. We will check together what can be obtained through court procedures and whether evidence preservation is needed. We explain the fees after the consultation.

faqs.q: The affair partner contacted me first. What should I do?
faqs.a: Don't delete the messages and call records you received; keep them. If anything the affair partner said shows they knew about the marriage, it becomes important evidence. If a reply is needed, it's wise to keep it short, along the lines of asking them to contact your legal representative.

guides.stage: I've been sued by my partner's spouse over an affair
guides.title: When you receive an affair complaint
guides.lead: The deadline for your answer starts running from the day the complaint is served on you. Here, in order, is what to check and prepare during the first 30 days.

seo.title: Served with an Affair Lawsuit in Korea: From Service to Your Answer | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do when you receive a complaint in an affair lawsuit in Korea: confirming the service date and the answer deadline, five things to check in the complaint, material you must not delete and contact to avoid, how to choose the direction of your answer, and the mediation and hearing steps that follow, in order so you don't miss a deadline.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: When you receive a complaint, your hands shake and you can't focus on anything. For today, just do these five things.
bullets: Write down the date you received the complaint. If a family member received it for you, it's the date they received it.
Mark the 30th day from that date on your calendar. That is the deadline for your answer (답변서).
Keep the envelope, notice, complaint (소장) and attached evidence in one place. They show the case number and court division.
Don't delete your chats, photos or call records with the other person's spouse; leave them as they are.
Don't contact the plaintiff or the other person's spouse. Even if you want to explain, wait.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Many people panic and delete chat rooms. Those chats also contain material in the defendant's favor, such as records of the other person saying they were single. Messages apologizing or explaining directly to the plaintiff can be submitted as the plaintiff's evidence, and contact to get your story straight with the other person's spouse later makes your entire account hard to believe.

Ignoring the complaint is not an option either. If you don't file an answer within the deadline, the court can treat the plaintiff's claims as admitted and rule without a hearing (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Articles 256 and 257).
Also be careful about venting to people around you about the case. What you say may reach the plaintiff's side and come back as a written witness statement.

sections.title: Five things to check in the complaint
body: A complaint is only the plaintiff's account; nothing in it has been established as fact. As you read, mark what is true, what is untrue and what is exaggerated, and you will save time in the consultation.

It is common for the plaintiff to state a longer period than the real one or to inflate the number of meetings. We rebut those points one by one with objective material, such as evidence that you were elsewhere on that date or records of periods when contact had stopped. If a screenshot attached to the complaint cuts out only part of a conversation, submitting the surrounding messages is another option.
bullets: The amount claimed (relief sought)
The period and places of the relationship the plaintiff alleges
The grounds for saying you knew of the marriage
The list of attached evidence (갑 제○호증, Plaintiff's Exhibits)
Whether any other procedure, such as a provisional attachment, is running alongside

sections.title: Next steps, starting with the direction of your answer
body: There are three broad directions for an answer: seeking dismissal by contesting the infidelity or your knowledge of the marriage; arguing that the marriage had already broken down when the relationship began; or admitting liability but contesting the amount. If you claim you didn't know and evidence then shows you did, even your argument for a reduced amount loses force, so we check the evidence first and then decide the direction. If time is short, file an answer stating that you contest the claim within the deadline, and supplement it later with a brief (준비서면).

Once you file the answer, the parties exchange arguments in briefs, and if the court refers the case to mediation (조정), the amount and terms are negotiated at the mediation session. If mediation succeeds, no written judgment is left on record, and terms such as confidentiality and no further claims can also be set. If not, the case goes through hearings to a judgment; if you disagree, you can appeal within 2 weeks of receiving the written judgment.

sections.title: If a provisional attachment or pressure came with it
body: Sometimes a provisional attachment (가압류) order arrives before the complaint. It means the plaintiff has frozen your deposits or salary before judgment; the money does not go to the plaintiff right away. If you think the attachment is excessive, you can contest it by filing an objection (Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 283).

Sometimes the plaintiff gets in touch saying they will tell your company or family. Keep such messages rather than deleting them, and don't respond in kind. The response to the pressure and the compensation issue are handled separately.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law lines up the complaint, the attached evidence and your chats with the other person's spouse in date order, and separates what to contest from what to admit. If the plaintiff is pressuring you by threatening to tell your workplace or family, we look at how to respond to that as well. A managing partner handles the consultation personally. We don't hide behind office managers or associate lawyers; we go through the material you bring from the start, together with you. We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have heard the details of the case and the scope of work.
If only a few days remain before the deadline, you can start by sending us a photo of the complaint through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: A provisional attachment order arrived before the complaint.
faqs.a: This means the plaintiff placed a provisional attachment on your deposits or salary before the lawsuit. A provisional attachment freezes assets until judgment, so the money does not go to the plaintiff right away. If the attachment is unjustified, we look at whether you can contest it by filing an objection.

faqs.q: A family member received the complaint for me. When does the deadline start?
faqs.a: As a rule, even when a family member living with you received it, service is treated as made on that day. Count 30 days from that date. If there are grounds to dispute whether service was properly made, bring the envelope and notice to the consultation.

faqs.q: Can I file the answer on my own, without a lawyer?
faqs.a: You can file it yourself. However, how you describe in the answer when you learned of the marriage and the nature of the relationship affects the entire process that follows. Even if you write it yourself, we recommend having it reviewed once before filing.

guides.title: When you want to claim compensation from the affair partner
guides.lead: Once you've decided to make a claim, there are things to take care of before the complaint. Here, in order, are the time limit, evidence, the other person's details and how you will actually collect.

seo.title: Suing Your Spouse's Affair Partner in Korea: How to Prepare | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do before filing a complaint if you want to claim compensation from your spouse's affair partner in Korea: calculating the time limit, grouping your evidence, what to do if you don't know their name or address, choosing between a certified letter and a lawsuit, provisional attachment, and a sense of how long it takes.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: From the day you decide to make a claim, there isn't much to do. You just need to keep to the order.
bullets: Confirm the day you found out about the affair, and write the date 3 years later on your calendar.
Gather KakaoTalk screenshots, photos, card statements and receipts in one folder in date order. It's convenient to download transaction histories as PDFs from your bank and card apps.
Write down on one page what you know about the affair partner (상간자), such as name, phone number, workplace and car plate number.
If there is CCTV that will soon be erased, note the date and place, and look into evidence preservation (증거보전) first.
Write down your current thinking on whether you will divorce or stay married. Which court you file in depends on this.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Before filing, avoid calling the affair partner to confront them or waiting outside their company. It only gives them time to delete chats and prepare to claim they didn't know. Sending a certified letter (내용증명) to their workplace or writing "affair" on the envelope also invites accusations of defamation (명예훼손).

Be careful, too, about putting a large claim amount out of anger. A bigger claim means higher court stamp fees (인지대), and if only part is granted, the plaintiff may have to bear part of the litigation costs (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 101).

sections.title: The two things the court looks at
body: To hold the affair partner liable, two things must be shown: that there was an unfaithful relationship between your spouse and the affair partner that breached the spouses' duty of fidelity, and that the affair partner knew or could have known your spouse had a family.

Infidelity (부정행위) is not narrowly limited to cases where sex is proven. It is sometimes recognized when conversations like those between lovers, overnight stays together and frequent meetings add up. Conversely, even with plenty of evidence, the claim can fail if the affair partner appears not to have known of the marriage, so you need to gather evidence of their knowledge separately.

So before writing the complaint, it helps to split your material into two bundles: one showing the relationship between the two, and another showing that the affair partner knew your spouse had a family. If the second bundle is empty, that is what must be filled first.

sections.title: Next steps
body: If there is room for a settlement, first send the amount and a deadline by certified letter; if not, file a complaint (소장). If you stay married and claim only against the affair partner, you file in the district court; if you claim together with a divorce, in the family court. If the other person seems likely to hide assets, you can also place a provisional attachment (가압류) on their deposits or salary before the lawsuit.

Once the complaint is served, the defendant files an answer within 30 days. Mediation or hearing dates follow, and the first date is usually set a few months after filing. If the other side does not contest, it can end within a few months; if the facts are hotly disputed, the first instance alone can take over a year. If they still don't pay after judgment, you collect through an asset disclosure order (재산명시) and seizure.

sections.title: What changes depending on whether you stay married
body: If you stay married and claim only against the affair partner, it proceeds as a civil case in the district court, and the amount tends to be set lower than where the marriage ended in divorce. If the affair partner pays compensation and then seeks reimbursement from your spouse, that money may come out of your household, so it is important to obtain, in mediation or settlement, a condition that they will not exercise the right to reimbursement (구상권).

If you are also considering divorce, you can claim against both your spouse and the affair partner in the family court. The same facts are judged by one court, so you don't have to submit evidence twice. If you haven't made up your mind, you can start with the claim against the affair partner and decide on divorce later. However, keep in mind that a divorce claim on the ground of infidelity cannot be made once 6 months have passed from the day you learned of it or 2 years from the day it happened (Civil Act (민법) Article 841).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Using the material you have gathered, Jisan Law first sorts out what will show the infidelity and what will show knowledge of the marriage. For the gaps, we consider whether they can be filled through court procedures such as evidence preservation or fact inquiries (사실조회), and if you are staying married, we also settle the reimbursement issue in advance. A managing partner handles the consultation personally. We don't hide behind office managers or associate lawyers; we go through the material you bring from the start, together with you. We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have heard the details of the case and the scope of work.
It's fine if your material isn't organized. Send us a message through the chat on this page and start by telling us your situation. You can message us on weekends and public holidays too.

faqs.q: My only evidence is a few KakaoTalk screenshots. Should I still sue?
faqs.a: It depends on the content and time span of the screenshots. If the conversations continued on the premise of a romantic relationship, that alone is sometimes enough; if not, material such as card statements or communication records can be added through court procedures. First check whether the original conversations behind the screenshots still exist.

faqs.q: The other woman is just starting her career and says she has no money. Is there any point in suing?
faqs.a: A claim confirmed by judgment remains enforceable for 10 years (Civil Act Article 165), and if she is employed during that time, her salary can be garnished. Even if there are no assets to collect right now, obtaining a judgment has value. Still, we weigh costs and time and also compare resolving it through a certified letter or settlement.

faqs.q: If I file an affair lawsuit, will my spouse also be called to court?
faqs.a: If you claim only against the affair partner, your spouse is not a party to the lawsuit. However, either the plaintiff or the defendant can ask for your spouse to be called as a witness. The outcome can shift depending on which side your spouse takes and what they say, so we think this through in advance.

guides.title: When you didn't know they were married
guides.lead: If the other person hid that they were married, you may not be held liable for compensation. But simply saying you didn't know is not enough. Here is what you can use to show it.

seo.title: Didn't Know He or She Was Married? Your Liability in a Korean Affair Lawsuit | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to check if you met someone without knowing they were married and have been, or may be, sued in an affair lawsuit in Korea: evidence that you didn't know, how you acted after finding out, when courts say you could have known, and what you can do about the person who deceived you.
keywords: didn't know he was married Korea
didn't know she was married Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: You may feel wronged and want to confront the other person, but first take care of the following.
bullets: Find messages in which the other person said they were single, divorced or separated, and take screenshots with the dates visible.
Note the day you first met, the day you first learned they were married and the day you ended the relationship.
Gather signs that made it reasonable to believe they were single, such as a dating app profile, conversations about getting married, or records of plans to meet your parents.
Don't leave or delete the chat room with the other person; leave it as it is.
If you have already received the complaint, write on your calendar the date 30 days from the day you received it.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Avoid contacting the other person's spouse first with long messages explaining "I was deceived too." A single phrase you use in the process can be read as a sign you knew. Deleting the whole conversation out of anger at the other person also hurts you, because the records of them saying they were single are in there.
Continuing to meet after finding out is the thing to avoid most. Even if you didn't know at first, liability can be recognized for meetings after you found out.
Also avoid hitting back emotionally at messages from the other person's spouse. Replies containing insults or accusations can be used against you when the amount is set.

sections.title: Evidence that you didn't know
body: Case law does not go so far as to require people to check whether every partner they date has a spouse. So if the other person actively hid the marriage and it was hard to find out, liability for compensation (위자료) may be denied. The court looks at the circumstances at the time rather than what you say now.
The more evidence the better, but evidence that contradicts itself actually does harm. Put it in time order and first check that it is consistent.
bullets: Messages in which they introduced themselves as single or said they were divorced
Conversations about marriage, living together or meeting each other's families
Records of meeting freely even on weekends and holidays
Having visited their home and seen no trace of a family
Statements from acquaintances who knew you both

sections.title: When courts say you could have known
body: If you worked at the same place and could have heard about their family, if their social media had photos of children, or if contact cut off every night or weekend, you are likely to be judged to have been able to know. If you met after hearing "I've filed divorce papers" or "We're separated," whether that was true and whether the marriage had actually broken down are disputed as separate issues. Simply having believed what you were told is often not enough.

The plaintiff usually gathers and submits every circumstance from which the defendant could have known. If the defendant first says they didn't know and then, once the chat records appear, changes their story to "I found out partway through," the rest of their arguments become hard to believe too. So before writing your answer (답변서), it is safer to reread the entire chat history and find any expressions that could have suggested the marriage. Knowing the unfavorable parts first and preparing an explanation leads to a different result than seeing them for the first time when the other side produces them.

sections.title: Next steps
body: If you have received a complaint (소장), state in your answer, with dates and evidence, when and from what you learned of the marriage and what you did after learning. If you didn't know for part of the period and did know for another part, one option is to contest the amount limited to the period when you knew.

We also look at whether you can hold the person who deceived you separately liable. There are lower-court decisions that granted compensation for emotional harm to someone who was in a relationship with a person who hid their marriage, but outcomes differ from case to case. If you end up paying compensation, we also consider whether you can claim reimbursement (구상) from that person.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law reads your chat history from start to finish in date order and uses the evidence to separate "the period when you didn't know" from "the point when you found out." Based on that evidence, we decide how far to contest and where to settle on the amount. A managing partner handles the consultation personally. We don't hide behind office managers or associate lawyers; we go through the material you bring from the start, together with you. We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have heard the details of the case and the scope of work.
If quite a while has passed since you received the complaint, the deadline must be checked first. Let us know right away through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: How do I prove I didn't know he was married?
faqs.a: You prove it with evidence of the circumstances at the time, such as messages in which he said he was single, conversations premised on marriage, and records of meeting freely even on weekends. It is stronger when several pieces of evidence point in the same direction rather than just one.

faqs.q: I didn't know at first, found out partway through, and couldn't end it right away.
faqs.a: Liability is likely to be recognized for the period after you found out. However, you can contest the amount by separating it from the period when you didn't know, and efforts you made to end it after finding out may also be considered. Be sure to keep the conversations that show the day you found out.

faqs.q: They said they had filed for divorce, and I believed it, but it was a lie.
faqs.a: If you have a record of being told this, it is important evidence. However, the court also looks at whether the marriage had actually broken down and whether there were reasons to believe what you were told. Gather circumstances such as whether they showed you a photo of the papers or were living separately.

guides.title: When you're asked to sign a settlement agreement
guides.lead: Once signed, a settlement agreement is hard to change. If you're being pressed to sign, here is what to look at, clause by clause.

seo.title: Before Signing an Affair Settlement Agreement in Korea: Clauses to Check | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: The clauses to check first if you're asked to sign an affair settlement agreement in Korea: the settlement amount and payment method, no contact and confidentiality, penalties for breach, no further lawsuits and waiver of reimbursement, and notarization and pre-suit settlement. Useful whether you are receiving or paying.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Even if you're told to sign by the end of today, don't rush. Start with the following.
bullets: Get the draft agreement as a photo or file. Don't sign the original on the spot.
Highlight the amount, due date, penalty amount and scope of the no-contact clause.
Check exactly who is party to the agreement, including whether the unfaithful spouse also signs.
Note how far wording such as "no civil or criminal objections of any kind will be raised" extends.
Agree on a signing date with the other side, and have the wording reviewed before then.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Even if the other side presses you to sign by threatening to tell your company or family, don't sign because of that pressure alone. Threatening exposure while demanding money can amount to threats (협박) or extortion (공갈) (Criminal Act (형법) Articles 283 and 350), so keep such messages rather than deleting them.

Also avoid withdrawing a pending lawsuit before the money comes in. If you are the one receiving, confirm the deposit first. Remember, too, that if you withdraw a lawsuit after a judgment on the merits, you cannot bring the same lawsuit again (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 267(2)).

sections.title: Amount, no contact and confidentiality
body: For the amount, state whether it is a lump sum or installments, and if installments, whether the remaining balance becomes due at once if even one payment is missed. For no contact, list calls, texts, social media and in-person meetings one by one, and separately set out an exception for unavoidable work contact if the two work at the same place.

For the confidentiality penalty for breach (위약벌), look at the balance of the amounts. If the confidentiality penalty is much smaller than the settlement amount, the party who received the money loses little by paying the penalty and spreading rumors anyway, so the clause loses its force.

Also write down the bank account and account holder for the settlement payment and how the deposit will be confirmed. The parties should sign in person, and getting a copy of each other's ID reduces later disputes that someone else signed. Make two copies of the agreement with identical content, and each side keeps one.

sections.title: A penalty for breach and a breach payment are treated differently
body: If the agreement just says "breach payment" (위약금), it is presumed to be liquidated damages (손해배상액의 예정), and the court can reduce it if it finds it unreasonably excessive (Civil Act (민법) Article 398). To make clear that the money is imposed as a penalty, write "penalty for breach." However, even a penalty for breach can be partly invalidated if it is excessively heavy, so setting a realistic amount actually increases the chance that you can collect it.

You also need to decide whether the penalty is "a certain amount per contact" or "a lump sum upon breach." A per-contact penalty requires proving how many contacts there were, while a lump sum attaches a large amount even to minor breaches and easily leads to disputes. Either way, what counts as a breach must be clearly stated in writing.

sections.title: Next steps: no further lawsuits, reimbursement and enforceability
body: A no-further-lawsuits clause (부제소 합의) is a promise not to sue again over this matter. If you are the one receiving, write down the period of infidelity covered by the settlement, so that relationships newly discovered after the settlement or renewed meetings can be claimed separately. A waiver of reimbursement (구상권) clause means the paying side gives up the right to recover money from their affair partner, so the paying side should weigh it together with the amount before signing.

With only a settlement agreement, if the other side doesn't pay, you have to sue again. If you make it a notarial deed (공정증서) with consent to compulsory execution (Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 56, item 4) or a court pre-suit settlement (제소전화해) (Civil Procedure Act Article 385), the monetary part can be enforced immediately. If a lawsuit is pending, resolving it with a mediation record (조정조서) or settlement record (화해조서) has the same effect.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law rereads each clause of the draft agreement from the perspective of both the receiving and the paying side, and marks missing clauses and wording likely to cause disputes later. We also look at how far the amount offered differs from the range a judgment would be expected to award. A managing partner handles the consultation personally. We don't hide behind office managers or associate lawyers; we go through the material you bring from the start, together with you. We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have heard the details of the case and the scope of work.
Even if you're due to sign tomorrow, you can send us a message through the chat on this page tonight.

faqs.q: What changes if the settlement agreement is notarized?
faqs.a: If you make a notarial deed that includes consent to compulsory execution, then if the other side doesn't pay, you can enforce it directly, for example by seizure, without a lawsuit (Civil Execution Act Article 56, item 4). Promises such as no contact are not directly enforced this way, so a breach is dealt with by claiming the penalty for breach.

faqs.q: Can I withdraw the lawsuit once I receive the settlement money?
faqs.a: The safe order is to withdraw only after confirming the money has actually arrived. If a lawsuit is pending, instead of withdrawing, you can also resolve it through mediation or a court settlement and leave a record. The record has the same effect as a judgment, so it can be enforced if the promise is broken.

faqs.q: I think the two are seeing each other again after the settlement.
faqs.a: If there are no-contact and penalty clauses, gather evidence of the breach and claim the penalty. If it is a relationship newly continued after the period covered by the settlement, we also look at whether you can claim compensation separately for that part.

guides.title: Motel CCTV: How to secure it before it's erased
guides.lead: If you ask a business to show you its CCTV, most will refuse, citing personal data. The procedure for this situation is court evidence preservation. Here is when to apply and what to prepare.

seo.title: Motel CCTV Evidence Preservation in Korea: How to Apply | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: How to secure CCTV footage from a motel or parking lot your spouse and the affair partner entered, through court evidence preservation in Korea: narrowing the date and time, what to write in the application, responding to correction orders, and the problems with getting the footage yourself.

sections.title: Footage is erased sooner than you think
body: CCTV at motels, officetels and apartment parking lots overwrites the oldest footage first once storage is full. Retention periods vary by business, but many keep footage for a few weeks to about a month. If quite some time has already passed since you confirmed signs of the affair, you need to act as soon as possible, even a day earlier.

In most cases, the owner won't show you the footage even if you explain the situation, because it also shows other guests and raises personal data issues. An affair is not a criminal case, so the police won't secure the footage for you either.
The day you find a receipt or payment text may be the last chance for the footage to still exist. Write down the business name, address and payment time that same day.

sections.title: Evidence preservation means the court examines evidence in advance
body: Evidence preservation (증거보전) is a procedure in which the court examines, even before a lawsuit, evidence that would be difficult to use later unless examined in advance (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 375). Before filing a lawsuit, you apply to the district court with jurisdiction over where the footage is; after filing, to the court hearing the case (Article 376 of the same Act).

You can apply even if you don't yet know the affair partner's name. In that case, the court can appoint a special representative (특별대리인) for the person who will be the other party (Article 378 of the same Act). The footage may be erased while you spend time finding out the name, so at this stage the date and place are more urgent than the name.

sections.title: Narrow the date and time before applying
body: Courts rarely grant broad applications. If you ask for a whole month of footage, you will get a correction order (보정명령) to narrow the scope. Narrow the date and time as much as possible by matching receipts, card payment texts, your own car's dashcam and the excuses your spouse gave. The application must state the other party, the facts to be proved, the evidence to be preserved and why it must be preserved now, and you must make a prima facie showing of that reason (Article 377 of the same Act).

Even getting the date wrong by one day costs time while the correction is made. If you submit screenshots of the receipt or card app showing the payment time and the business location along with the application, the court can decide quickly.
bullets: The business name and address, and where the entrance and parking lot are
The suspected date and time (e.g., from 22:00 on ○○ to 02:00 the next day)
Payment records or messages supporting that date
Your spouse's car plate number and what they wore that day
The circumstances showing the footage will soon be erased

sections.title: What to do after the decision
body: If you receive a correction order, narrow the scope or fix the date and resubmit within the deadline. Sometimes the court suggests corrections by phone, so don't miss calls from the court. Once the footage is submitted, put the scenes showing the two together in time order and submit them in the main lawsuit.

As a rule, the other party is also notified of the evidence examination date; notice can be omitted only in urgent cases (Article 381 of the same Act). If you are worried your spouse will find out, this point should also be considered at the application stage.
Keep the footage file you receive in its original form and work from a copy.

sections.title: Problems with getting it yourself
body: If you know the owner and film the footage on your phone or are handed the file, both the person who handed it over and the person who received it can face criminal complaints over personal data. There are also cases where CCTV screenshots submitted in an affair lawsuit led the other side to file a complaint, turning it into a criminal case.

The same goes for removing the memory card from someone else's dashcam or putting a camera outside the other person's home. If one piece of evidence turns the matter into a criminal case, it also weakens your position in negotiating compensation (위자료). The more urgent it is, the more the court procedure turns out to be the faster route.

sections.title: Material to gather along with the CCTV
body: A single video does not prove everything. Its meaning becomes clear only when combined with the messages the two exchanged that day, the lodging payment record and where your spouse said they were that day.

Even if you obtain the footage through evidence preservation, faces may be blurry or it may show only the entrance. So before applying, if you work out what your existing material can show and what the footage will add, you can also write the reasons in the application more concretely.
bullets: KakaoTalk chats or texts from the same day
Payment records for lodging and meals
Your own car's dashcam footage
The excuse your spouse gave for that day (business trip, work dinner, etc.)

faqs.q: Can I still check motel CCTV from the end of last year?
faqs.a: If several months have passed, it has most likely already been erased. However, retention periods differ by business, so it's worth checking, and if there is no footage, we look for other ways to show movements on that day, such as card payment records or communication records.

faqs.q: If evidence preservation is granted, does a criminal investigation start?
faqs.a: No. Evidence preservation is a civil procedure that only secures the footage in advance. An affair itself is not a crime, so it does not lead to an investigation.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to the motel to get the footage?
faqs.a: This is not a procedure in which the applicant goes to the business alone and demands the footage. Following the court's decision, the custodian submits the footage or the court examines the evidence in the manner it sets. The specific method follows what is written in the decision.

guides.title: When you don't know the affair partner's name or address
guides.lead: In many cases, you can start a lawsuit knowing just one number you saw on your spouse's phone. Here is the order in which the other person is identified through the court.

seo.title: Suing an Affair Partner Whose Name or Address You Don't Know in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: For those hesitating to sue because they don't know the affair partner's name or address in Korea: fact inquiries to mobile carriers using a phone number, other clues such as bank account and car plate numbers, service by publication when service fails, and the risks of investigating on your own.
keywords: sue affair partner phone number only Korea

sections.title: The complaint must say who the other party is
body: A lawsuit begins when the court sends the complaint (소장) to the defendant. So, as a rule, the complaint states the defendant's name and address. But few people know the affair partner's resident registration number or home address. Most come to a consultation knowing a name and phone number, or just a number.
You don't need to know everything from the start. Even one clue that distinguishes the person from others can be the starting point.
If you have several clues, write them all down. If one leads nowhere, you can search another way.
bullets: Mobile phone number
KakaoTalk ID or profile
Bank account number left in transfer records
Car plate number
Workplace name and location
Social media accounts

sections.title: With a phone number: a fact inquiry to the mobile carrier
body: You file the lawsuit naming the defendant by the name you know or as "name unknown" (성명불상), and apply to the court for a fact inquiry (사실조회) to the mobile carrier. The court can ask public agencies or organizations to look into necessary matters (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 294), and the carrier replies with the subscriber's name, address and other details. Once the reply arrives, the defendant's name and address are corrected and the complaint is sent again.

At this stage, you do not get to see the content of calls or messages. The procedure only confirms who uses the number. If it's a budget carrier (MVNO) line or a number registered in someone else's name, the reply may not identify the person, so we prepare other clues as well.
A reply to a fact inquiry can take several weeks. In the meantime the person sometimes changes their number, so it's good to keep a record of when you learned the number and of contacts made with it.

sections.title: Clues to use when you don't have a number
body: If there are records of your spouse sending money to the affair partner, a fact inquiry can be sent to that account's bank to confirm the account holder. Car plate numbers, messenger IDs and workplace information can also be used to identify the person. What can be asked of which institution depends on the clue, so we go through them one by one.

If you know their workplace, service can be attempted at their place of work even without a home address (Article 183(2) of the same Act). However, since the documents go to the company, keep in mind that the other person may react badly or the mood for a settlement may change.

sections.title: When service fails even with an address
body: Even with an address, service fails if no one is ever home or the person has moved. In that case, we reconfirm and correct the address or apply for service at night or on holidays. If that still fails, you can apply for service by publication (공시송달) (Article 194 of the same Act); the first service by publication takes effect 2 weeks after it is carried out (Article 196 of the same Act).

Because of this process, cases where you don't know the other person's details can take an extra few weeks to a few months before the trial really gets going. If little time remains on your time limit, it is safer to file with just the clues rather than waiting until you have all their details.
If the case proceeds by service by publication, the other person may receive a judgment without knowing a trial was held. As a result, finding their assets after the judgment can take time again.

sections.title: Be careful investigating on your own
body: Secretly finding out someone's address or contact details is prohibited by law, so if you hire an agency to do it, even you as the client can get into trouble. Secretly opening your spouse's phone or logging into their accounts to find information about the affair partner can also be punished.
Information obtained through court procedures must be used only for the lawsuit. Using that address to go to their home or to inform their family creates other disputes.

Looking up the affair partner's social media is not itself a problem, but approaching them with a fake account to dig for information or impersonating an acquaintance invites other disputes. Stop at saving public posts with the dates visible.

sections.title: What to prepare for each clue
body: To apply for a fact inquiry, you must specify what the court should ask. Also prepare material showing where the clue came from. Rather than submitting just the number, the need for the inquiry becomes clear when there are records of that number being used to contact your spouse.
bullets: For a phone number: call logs or message screens between it and your spouse
For a bank account number: a transaction statement showing the transfers
For a car plate number: a photo showing the plate and the date it was taken
For a workplace: the company name mentioned in chats, or a photo of a business card

faqs.q: I only know the name, phone number and bank account number. Do I need their resident registration number and address?
faqs.a: With clues like these, after filing the lawsuit you can confirm the address through a fact inquiry to the mobile carrier or bank. You don't need to know the resident registration number in advance to file a lawsuit.

faqs.q: I only know their KakaoTalk ID. Is that enough?
faqs.a: Applying for a fact inquiry to the messenger company is one option that is discussed, but depending on what information the company keeps, it may not identify the person. Also look for other clues mentioned in chats, such as their workplace, neighborhood or car.

faqs.q: If a judgment is entered after service by publication, can I get paid?
faqs.a: You can obtain a judgment, but if you can't find the other person's assets, it's hard to actually collect. After the judgment, we continue with procedures to find assets, such as an asset disclosure order (재산명시) or an asset inquiry (재산조회). A claim confirmed by judgment remains enforceable for 10 years.

guides.title: How much compensation is awarded in affair cases?
guides.lead: This is the first question asked in most consultations. There is no fixed table, but we can look at what the court considers when setting the amount and which circumstances push it up or down.

seo.title: How Much Is Affair Compensation in Korea? What Courts Consider | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: For anyone wondering how much compensation is awarded in a Korean affair lawsuit: what courts consider when setting the amount, circumstances that raise or lower it, the difference when the marriage continues, how to set the amount claimed, and late-payment damages.

sections.title: The judgment amount is not simply what you claim
body: Compensation for emotional distress (위자료) awarded by judgment in affair cases varies widely from case to case. If the relationship was short and less serious, it is set low; if the circumstances are serious, such as a long relationship or continuing to meet after being found out, it is set high. Because the amount is decided by the combination of circumstances listed below, it is hard to apply the figure from someone else's case directly to yours.

Writing KRW 100 million in the complaint does not raise the amount that much. The court sets the amount case by case, without a fixed table, by combining various circumstances. So it makes sense to look first at which circumstances are present in your case rather than at the number.
