Most of the large amounts you see online come from cases with special circumstances or from amounts set by settlement. If you expect a figure without looking at what your case has in common with those cases and how it differs, you are likely to be disappointed even after winning a judgment.

sections.title: Circumstances that raise the amount
body: When the following circumstances are shown by evidence, they work toward a higher amount.
bullets: A long marriage with young children
A relationship that lasted a long time or was repeated
The affair partner knew of the marriage from the start
The two kept meeting after being found out
Mocking or insulting messages were sent to the plaintiff
The marriage ultimately ended in separation or divorce

sections.title: Circumstances that lower the amount
body: Conversely, the following circumstances are grounds for arguing for a reduction. As always, they must be shown with evidence, not just asserted.

The plaintiff's own conduct also affects the amount. If the plaintiff went to the affair partner and assaulted them or told their workplace, that may be considered, and it can also become a separate criminal matter.
bullets: The relationship was short and mostly by messages
The affair partner didn't know at first and ended it soon after finding out
The couple's marriage had already been badly shaken before that
The unfaithful spouse actively made the first approach
The plaintiff has already received compensation from the spouse
The affair partner sincerely apologized and ended the relationship during the lawsuit

sections.title: Amounts tend to be lower when the marriage continues
body: If you claim only against the affair partner and stay married, courts often view the marriage as less harmed than where it ended in divorce and set a lower amount. On top of that, if the affair partner pays and then claims reimbursement (구상) from the unfaithful spouse, that money may ultimately come out of your household. This is why a plaintiff who stays married also obtains, in mediation, a condition that the right to reimbursement (구상권) will not be exercised.
Conversely, if you divorce during the lawsuit, that is taken into account and the amount may change, so inform the court promptly if circumstances change while the case is ongoing.

sections.title: The amount claimed and late-payment damages
body: A larger claim means higher court stamp fees (인지대), and if only part is granted, the plaintiff may bear part of the litigation costs (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 101). So it's better to claim an amount suited to the case, with grounds.

The judgment adds late-payment damages (지연손해금) to the compensation. From the day after the complaint is served on the other party, a statutory rate of 12% per year applies (Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법) Article 3 and its implementing rules). The longer the lawsuit goes on, the more the defendant owes, which can give the defendant's side a reason to push for mediation.

sections.title: Evidence of emotional suffering
body: Compensation is money for emotional suffering, so evidence showing how severe that suffering was helps. If you saw a doctor for insomnia or depression after learning of the affair, the medical records can be used, and written statements from family or friends describing the changes they saw can also be taken into account.

However, medical records do not raise the amount by a set figure. The court looks first at the nature and duration of the infidelity, and treats such material as supporting that judgment. Rather than visiting a hospital just to create records, it's better to keep an honest record of what you actually went through.

sections.title: How compensation from your spouse fits in
body: The unfaithful spouse and the affair partner are jointly liable to the plaintiff. So if you received compensation from your spouse in the divorce, that amount may be taken into account in the lawsuit against the affair partner, reducing what the affair partner must pay. However, receiving compensation from your spouse does not by itself eliminate the affair partner's liability.

If the money from your spouse was for reasons other than the affair, such as verbal abuse or refusal to care for the children, it's good to make that clear. How the grounds for compensation are written in the divorce mediation record or agreement will matter later.

faqs.q: If I claim a large amount, will I get more?
faqs.a: No. The court sets the amount based on the circumstances of the case, not the amount claimed. A larger claim means higher court stamp fees, and if only part is granted, you may bear part of the litigation costs.

faqs.q: If the affair partner says they have no money, will the amount go down?
faqs.a: Assets or financial circumstances are sometimes mentioned as a factor, but having no money does not by itself remove liability. Once you obtain a judgment, it remains enforceable for 10 years from the date it becomes final, so you can enforce it later if they earn income.

faqs.q: Is the settlement amount set close to the expected judgment amount?
faqs.a: The expected judgment amount serves as a benchmark, but it doesn't have to be the same. Depending on whether one side wants to finish quickly or wants to avoid a written judgment on record, it can be set higher or lower.

guides.title: When you receive a certified letter or settlement demand over an affair
guides.lead: Often a demand for settlement money arrives by certified letter or text before any complaint. Here is what to check before replying and what not to do.

seo.title: Received an Affair Demand Letter or Settlement Demand in Korea? | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: For those who received a certified letter or a text demanding settlement money over an affair in Korea: what a certified letter does and doesn't do, what to check before replying, why an admitting reply becomes evidence, how to handle threats to tell your company or family, and choosing between settlement and a lawsuit.

sections.title: A certified letter is not a judgment
body: A certified letter (내용증명) is mail for which the post office certifies what document was sent and when. It has no binding force on its own. Not sending money by the deadline it states does not mean your bank account will be seized right away.

That doesn't mean you should take it lightly. It signals that the sender is preparing a lawsuit, and if you ignore it, a complaint is likely to follow. Whether or not you reply, now is the time to work out your response.

If the sender is a lawyer, it's fair to assume the lawsuit is fairly well prepared. If the plaintiff wrote it personally, it may be very emotional, so read it focusing on the demands rather than the wording.

sections.title: What to check before replying
body: First read the document calmly and note the following.
In particular, if there is wording about telling your workplace or family, mark it. It will be important material when deciding how to respond later.
bullets: Whether the sender is the plaintiff personally or a lawyer
The amount demanded and the deadline
Whether the alleged period and nature of the relationship match the facts
The evidence the other side says it has
Whether there is wording about telling your workplace or family

sections.title: An admitting reply becomes evidence as it stands
body: Out of remorse, many people send a long apology saying "It's all my fault." That text is submitted as the plaintiff's evidence in the lawsuit just as it is. Conversely, a reply denying everything is also risky. If evidence comes out later, your other statements become hard to believe too.
Even if you apologize, decide the scope of the facts you are admitting and choose your words before sending. Not replying does not mean you have admitted the content, so there is no need to rush.
Also be careful with requests to talk by phone. The other person can record the call, and a recording made by a party to the conversation can be used as evidence.

sections.title: If you are being pressured with threats to tell your company or family
body: Demanding money while threatening to tell your company or spouse can amount to threats (협박) or extortion (공갈) (Criminal Act (형법) Articles 283 and 350). Actually spreading it at your company or on social media can be defamation (명예훼손) even if true (Criminal Act Article 307). Keep such messages and call records rather than deleting them.

That said, it does not make your liability for the affair disappear. The response to the pressure and the compensation (위자료) issue must be handled separately. If you work at the same place, it is also important to designate a place for service and a point of contact so documents don't go to the company.

sections.title: Settle, or wait for a lawsuit?
body: If the amount demanded is not far from what a judgment would be expected to award and ending it quietly matters to you, a settlement may be better. When settling, set out a no-further-claims clause, confidentiality and how reimbursement (구상권) will be handled, so you are not harassed again over the same matter.

If the amount demanded is excessive or the facts are different, you can also decline and contest it in a lawsuit. Either way, avoid contacting the other person's spouse separately to get your stories straight. The conversations you have now can also become evidence later.

When setting the settlement amount, also factor in the late-payment damages added if it goes to judgment and the time a lawsuit takes. Even if a judgment looks better on the amount alone, settlement can be the better choice once you consider the burden of exchanging briefs for close to a year.

sections.title: If you do reply
body: If you decide to reply, keep it short and calm. Rather than a long emotional message, it is safer to stop at the following. If you have hired a lawyer, it is enough to say that further contact should go to your representative.
bullets: That you have received the document
That you are reviewing its content
The point of contact going forward (yourself or your representative)
A request not to contact your workplace or family

sections.title: When the other person's spouse offers to pay for you
body: Sometimes the married person you had the affair with says, "I'll take care of it" or "I'll pay the settlement money." That person is also jointly liable to the plaintiff, so regardless of who actually pays, what matters is who is named as a party in the settlement agreement.

If it's settled only verbally and your name is left out of the agreement, the plaintiff may still claim against you separately later. Conversely, if you pay everything and want to recover that person's share later, you must not waive your right to reimbursement. Put in writing who pays how much and who gives up what.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore the certified letter?
faqs.a: Not replying to a certified letter doesn't cause any immediate disadvantage. However, the sender is likely to file a lawsuit, and once the complaint arrives, you must file an answer within 30 days. Even if you ignore it, organize your material in advance.

faqs.q: They say if I don't pay KRW 30 million by the deadline, they'll double it and tell my company.
faqs.a: Saying they will raise the amount has no legal effect in itself. The part where they demand money while threatening to tell your company can amount to threats or extortion, so keep the messages. Rather than giving in right away, decide your response by comparing it with the amount a judgment would be expected to award.

faqs.q: I'm married too, and I'm afraid my spouse will find out.
faqs.a: The court does not separately inform your family about a lawsuit. However, if a complaint is delivered to your home, a family member may receive it, so we consider appointing a representative to receive documents on your behalf, or resolving the matter by settlement.

guides.title: Claiming reimbursement after paying the compensation
guides.lead: Infidelity is something two people do together, so if you paid all the compensation yourself, you can ask the other person to return their share. Here is when you can claim and when you can't.

seo.title: Reimbursement After Paying Affair Compensation in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: For those who paid affair compensation alone and want to claim reimbursement from their affair partner in Korea: why the right to reimbursement arises, why you must pay first, what share you can recover, when reimbursement is barred, and why plaintiffs raise the reimbursement issue.

sections.title: Why the right to reimbursement arises
body: Infidelity by a spouse and the affair partner is treated as a tort they committed together (Civil Act (민법) Article 760). Case law views their liability as an "untrue" joint and several obligation (부진정연대채무) (Supreme Court Decision 2013므2441, rendered May 29, 2015). The plaintiff can claim the full compensation (위자료) from either of the two, and once one pays in full, the relationship with the plaintiff ends.
Next comes settling up between the two. The person who paid everything can claim from the other the part exceeding their own share. This is the right to reimbursement (구상권).
Plaintiffs often claim only against the affair partner and not against their own spouse, so this settling-up issue comes up frequently.

sections.title: You must pay before you can claim
body: Reimbursement can be claimed only after you have actually paid. If you have only a judgment and haven't paid yet, you can't start with a reimbursement claim. The starting point is that you actually paid more than your share, so be sure to keep transfer records and receipts.
If you are paying in installments, once the amount paid exceeds your share, you claim the excess. Keeping a table of when you paid how much makes this easier.

If you deliberately delay paying the compensation to get reimbursement, late-payment damages keep accruing on the plaintiff's side. Paying the plaintiff as required and then preparing the reimbursement claim results in less loss in the end.

sections.title: How much can you get back?
body: The court decides each person's share based on their degree of responsibility. If responsibility seems similar, it is often put at around half, but it varies with who led the relationship more actively and whether someone hid their marriage when approaching the other. If the unfaithful spouse lied about being married, you can argue that their share is larger.

If you paid less than your share as set by the court, there is nothing to reimburse. For example, if the total compensation is KRW 20 million and the two shares are half each, you can claim the part you paid beyond KRW 10 million.

sections.title: When reimbursement is barred
body: In the cases below, you cannot claim reimbursement or the amount is greatly reduced. Be sure to check before signing a mediation or settlement agreement.

If the mediation record (조정조서) only says "no further claims will be made in relation to this case" and says nothing about reimbursement, interpretations may differ on whether that wording settles only the relationship with the plaintiff or also bars reimbursement from the spouse. Make the scope clear before signing.
bullets: You agreed in mediation or a settlement agreement not to exercise the right to reimbursement
The judgment limited the compensation to the defendant's own share
The unfaithful spouse has also already paid compensation to the plaintiff
You have no records proving that you paid

sections.title: Why plaintiffs raise the reimbursement issue
body: For a plaintiff who stays married, reimbursement is an awkward problem. Even if they receive compensation from the affair partner, if the affair partner then seeks reimbursement from the plaintiff's spouse, that money goes back out of the household. So plaintiffs sometimes accept a slightly lower amount in mediation in exchange for a promise not to exercise the right to reimbursement, and defendants use this as a bargaining point.

From the defendant's point of view, waiving reimbursement means bearing the full compensation in practice. Before signing a waiver clause, compare the amount you could recover later with the amount being knocked off now.

If the plaintiff and the affair partner agree in mediation that "the defendant will not exercise the right to reimbursement," the spouse, who is not a party to that mediation, also benefits. Conversely, if a judgment is issued without such a clause, the affair partner can seek reimbursement from the spouse, so the terms are set with the plaintiff couple's household finances in mind.

sections.title: How to claim reimbursement
body: First, demand it by certified letter (내용증명), stating the amount you paid and the amount to be returned; if the other person doesn't comply, file a lawsuit for reimbursement. It proceeds as a civil case regardless of whether the other person has divorced.

In the lawsuit, you submit the judgment or mediation record on which the compensation was paid and the transfer records showing you actually sent the money. If you have evidence that the other person led the relationship or hid their marriage, you can argue that their share should be considered larger.
bullets: The compensation judgment or mediation record
Transfer records or receipts for payments to the plaintiff
Chats showing who led the relationship
Signs that the marriage was hidden

faqs.q: The other woman says she will exercise her right to reimbursement against my husband. What does that mean?
faqs.a: It means that after paying all the compensation, she will claim back your husband's share of it. If you are staying married, that money may ultimately come out of your household, so a condition that the right to reimbursement will not be exercised is often agreed in mediation or settlement.

faqs.q: The judgment was issued, but I haven't paid it all yet. Can I claim reimbursement first?
faqs.a: You can claim after you have actually paid more than your share. If you are paying in installments, keep a record of when you paid how much, and once you exceed your share, claim that part.

faqs.q: Is there a time limit for reimbursement claims too?
faqs.a: Yes. A separate limitation period for the right to reimbursement runs from the time you actually paid the compensation. If it has been a long time since you paid, first check whether time remains.

guides.title: When they won't pay the compensation after judgment
guides.lead: Even after winning, if the other side doesn't send the money of their own accord, you need to find a way to collect. Here, in order, are the procedures used after judgment.

seo.title: Affair Partner Won't Pay After Judgment? Enforcement in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: For those who won an affair lawsuit in Korea but haven't been paid: enforceable titles and provisional execution, asset disclosure orders and asset inquiries, salary and bank account garnishment, what to do if assets were hidden or there are none right now, and what not to do.

sections.title: The judgment is your basis for collecting
body: A final judgment, a mediation record (조정조서) or a final recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정) serves as the basis for compulsory execution. If the operative part of the judgment includes a provisional execution (가집행) clause, you can start enforcing without waiting for the judgment to become final, even if the other side appeals (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 213). In that case, the other side can post security and apply to stop enforcement.
To enforce, you need to obtain a certificate of enforcement (집행문) for the judgment. First check whether the judgment is final and whether you have a certificate of service (송달증명).
If you have lost the judgment, you can get it reissued by the court. Enforcement requires an authenticated original of the judgment, so check in advance if you only have a copy.

sections.title: Start by finding assets
body: If you don't know the other side's assets, apply for an asset disclosure order (재산명시) (Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 61). Once the court orders it, the other side must submit a list of assets, and if they fail to appear on the date or refuse to submit the list without a legitimate reason, they can be placed in detention for contempt (감치) for up to 20 days (Article 68 of the same Act).

If the disclosure procedure is not enough, you can apply for an asset inquiry (재산조회), in which financial institutions and public agencies are asked about assets in the other side's name (Article 74 of the same Act). If they still haven't paid 6 months after the judgment becomes final, you can also apply to have them entered in the register of defaulters (채무불이행자명부) (Article 70 of the same Act).

Sometimes the other side gets in touch as soon as the asset disclosure order is served on them. If they propose installment payments at that point, decide whether to accept and whether to put the terms in writing.

sections.title: Garnishing salary and bank deposits
body: If the other side is employed, garnishing their salary is the most realistic option. However, one-half of the salary cannot be seized, and a separate threshold reflecting living costs also applies, so you cannot take the full amount (Article 246 of the same Act). The garnishment order goes to their employer, which often prompts them to get in touch.

For bank deposits, the money in the account at the time of seizure is what can be seized. If the balance is near zero, there is little to collect, so we also look at regular income such as salary. If the asset disclosure reveals real estate or shares, we proceed with a compulsory auction for real estate and seizure for shares.

If the other side leaves their job, there is no more salary to collect from that company, so you must apply again once you learn of their new employer. One-half of severance pay is also exempt from seizure, but the rest can be seized (Civil Execution Act Article 246).

sections.title: If assets were moved, or there are none right now
body: If the other side moved assets into family members' names during the lawsuit or right after the judgment, we consider a lawsuit to revoke the fraudulent transfer (사해행위취소). This is why placing a provisional attachment (가압류) from the start matters.

Even if there are no assets right now, don't give up. A claim confirmed by judgment has a 10-year limitation period (Civil Act (민법) Article 165), and before it runs out you can file a lawsuit to extend it. If the other side gets a job or acquires assets in the meantime, you seize them then.

A fraudulent transfer action requires showing that the other side moved assets and that this left them with too little to pay, so we first check property registers and transaction records. There is also a time limit: it must be filed within 1 year of learning of the grounds for revocation and within 5 years of the disposal (Civil Act Article 406(2)).

sections.title: What not to do
body: Out of frustration, sending a certified letter to their company with "affair compensation claim" written on the envelope, or posting the judgment on social media, can raise defamation (명예훼손) issues (Criminal Act (형법) Article 307). This is true even with a judgment in hand. Applying pressure through procedures set by law, such as salary garnishment, is safer, and in practice the other side often gets in touch sooner.
Also avoid demanding that their family pay on their behalf. A judgment binds only the defendant, and pressuring family members creates other disputes.

sections.title: The order of enforcement procedures
body: After judgment, the procedures usually go in the following order. If you already know the other side's assets, you may skip the asset disclosure and go straight to seizure. Cases that ended with a mediation record or a final recommendation for settlement can be enforced the same way.
bullets: Confirm the judgment is final and obtain a certificate of service
Apply for a certificate of enforcement
Apply for an asset disclosure order and asset inquiry
Garnish salary or deposits and collect; compulsory auction of real estate
If still unpaid, apply for entry in the register of defaulters

faqs.q: The other side appealed. When can I get the money?
faqs.a: If the first-instance judgment includes a provisional execution clause, you can begin enforcement even during the appeal. The other side can post security and apply for a stay of execution (집행정지), in which case you must wait for the appeal result.

faqs.q: They listed real estate and shares in the asset disclosure. What's next?
faqs.a: The next step is to apply for a compulsory auction of the real estate and seizure of the shares. If the real estate has a lot of prior security interests, there may be nothing left even after an auction, so we check the property register first.

faqs.q: It's been several years since I got the judgment. Can I still collect?
faqs.a: If 10 years have not passed since the judgment became final, you can enforce it. As the 10 years approach, we file a lawsuit to extend the limitation period.

guides.title: When you've already told the affair partner's family or company
guides.lead: If, in anger, you told the affair partner's company or family about the affair, from now on you need to stop it from spreading further and prepare for a possible criminal complaint. Your right to claim compensation from the affair partner remains intact.

seo.title: Told the Affair Partner's Company or Family? Defamation Response in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away, and what not to do, if you've already told the affair partner's company, family or social media about the affair in Korea; what to examine to see whether it is defamation; and, in order, the steps after a complaint and how to resolve it together with the affair lawsuit.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: You can't undo what's been done, but what you do next changes how serious the case becomes. In particular, for anything posted in a group chat or on social media, first check how far it has spread before others screenshot it and pass it on.
bullets: Don't send anything more. Stop all further messages, comments and calls
Take screenshots of what you posted and sent, with dates visible, and keep them separately
After saving the original text, consider taking the posts down
Don't delete protest messages or warnings of a criminal complaint from the other side; keep them
Write down on one page who you told, when and what

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Replying, "If you file a complaint, I'll spread it further" (this can be a threat)
Reposting elsewhere or asking acquaintances to share it
Calling the affair partner's company again to ask how they handled it
Sending photos of the affair to others as "evidence"

sections.title: When replying to the other side
body: If you receive a warning of a criminal complaint or a demand for settlement, don't reply right away; keep it as it is. Apologies or explanations sent at this stage are sometimes used later as an admission of the offense.

If you want a settlement, it's better to set out the amount and terms and convey them through a legal representative. Direct contact easily becomes emotional, and the other side may make an issue of that contact too.

sections.title: What to examine to see whether it's defamation
body: Even telling the truth can be defamation (명예훼손). However, depending on the circumstances below, there may be points you can contest. If even a little untrue content was mixed in, it can be treated more severely as defamation by false statements, so recheck every line you sent.

Defamation under the Criminal Act (형법) and under the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) cannot be punished if the victim states that they do not want punishment. So once a complaint is filed, whether a settlement is reached greatly affects the outcome. Insult (모욕죄) can be punished only if the victim files a complaint.
bullets: How many people could learn of it, and whether those told were likely to spread it further
Whether the purpose was limited, such as asking for separation at work
Whether you used a real name or information identifying the person
Whether insults or offensive expressions were included
Whether it was a real-name space or an anonymous board

sections.title: Next steps
body: If the affair partner files a complaint, you will be questioned by the police as a suspect. The appearance date can be adjusted if you explain your circumstances, so coordinate the schedule with your defense lawyer before attending. You need to separate in advance what you will admit and what you will contest, and decide the direction of your statement before questioning.

The affair lawsuit can still go ahead. However, the other side can argue for reduced compensation (위자료) because of the exposure or separately claim damages, so settlement terms are often designed with both cases in view. Sometimes the affair compensation and the defamation settlement are resolved in a single agreement. A victim's wish not to have the offender punished is effective only if expressed before the first-instance judgment is delivered (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 232), so don't delay settlement talks.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law first confirms what was disclosed and how widely, and looks for points to contest on whether defamation is established. Before police questioning, we rehearse with likely questions, and a defense lawyer sits in on the questioning and objects on the spot to leading or improper questions. We look at the affair lawsuit and the criminal case together to work out settlement terms, and Jisan Law handles settlement contact with the other side on your behalf.

A managing partner handles the consultation personally, and we explain the fees after the consultation. Even before you receive a complaint, you can reach us through the chat on this page at any time.

faqs.q: I deleted the post right away. Can I still face a complaint?
faqs.a: Even if it was up only briefly, defamation can be an issue if someone saw it or took a screenshot. However, the short posting time and prompt deletion can be considered in your favor in the disposition.

faqs.q: The affair partner is demanding settlement money. Can it be offset against the compensation I'm owed?
faqs.a: The court will not cancel out the two debts on its own, because a debt arising from an intentional tort cannot be set off against another claim (Civil Act (민법) Article 496). To settle the money owed in each direction, you need a settlement agreement signed by both sides.

guides.title: When the affair partner threatens you or comes to your home
guides.lead: After an affair is discovered, the affair partner sometimes won't let your spouse go, or even contacts you and turns up in person. Rather than confronting them alone, it is safer to keep records and use the protective measures set by law.

seo.title: Affair Partner Coming to Your Home or Threatening You in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away, and what not to do, when after an affair is discovered the affair partner comes to your home or workplace, keeps contacting you, or demands money while threatening exposure in Korea. Reporting stalking, no-approach orders, and handling it together with the affair lawsuit.

sections.title: What to do right now
bullets: If you feel in danger, call 112 (the police emergency number) right away. Police will stop stalking that is in progress on the spot
Before blocking the number, take screenshots of texts, KakaoTalk messages and call logs received
Note the dates, times and places they came, and save footage from your door camera or dashcam
Tell your child's school or your workplace about the situation and ask them to contact you if a stranger shows up
Ask your spouse to cut off contact with the affair partner and to hand over any messages they received
body: Even if it isn't urgent, start keeping records today. If you try to recall everything at once later, the dates and order become blurred.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Meeting them in person to have it out
Replying with insults or lines like "You'll regret this"
Going to the affair partner's home or workplace in return
Posting public warnings in comments on the affair partner's social media
Paying money to make it quietly go away (once you pay, more demands may follow)

sections.title: How to keep records
body: Stalking (스토킹) requires showing repetition, so the record gains strength as each incident is added. Note briefly, on the same day, the date, time, method, content and how threatened you felt.

Gather the contacts made to your spouse as well. If your spouse keeps responding to the contact, it may be harder to treat it as stalking, and in an affair lawsuit it becomes a sign the relationship is continuing. In that case, you first need to decide what to do about your relationship with your spouse before a response strategy can be set.
bullets: Screenshots of messages and call logs showing the other person's number and the time
Door camera and dashcam footage saved separately as original files
Notes on the locations of CCTV near where they came (retention periods are short)
Names and contact details of neighbors or coworkers who witnessed it

sections.title: Protection under the law
body: Unwanted approaches and contact that continue or are repeated become a stalking crime. It is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and since a July 2023 amendment, the offender can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment.

With the victim's consent, the police can refer the victim on the spot to a counseling center or shelter, and if repetition is likely and the situation is urgent, they can order the person to stay at least 100 meters away and not to call or message. The court can order provisional measures (잠정조치) including a written warning, a no-approach order, an electronic monitoring device and even detention in a police cell.
Words like "I'll tell your spouse" or "If you don't pay, I'll spread it" can amount to threats (협박) or extortion (공갈). Be sure to keep any message demanding money.

sections.title: Next steps
body: Once you file a criminal complaint, the police interview you as the victim. Submitting your organized records in date order speeds up the investigation, and if protective measures are needed, request them along with the complaint. If contact continues after the complaint, submit those records as well. Once the police investigation is complete, a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) decides whether to indict.

If you are also preparing an affair lawsuit, the stalking and threat records can be submitted as evidence of the affair partner's attitude after being found out. We decide when to file the lawsuit while watching how the criminal case progresses.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law organizes the record of contacts and visits with you, writes the criminal complaint, and considers whether emergency measures (긴급응급조치) or provisional measures are needed. Jisan Law accompanies you to your interview as a victim and continues on to handle the affair lawsuit. A managing partner handles the consultation personally.
If you are in danger now, call 112 first, then contact us through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: The other woman goes to my husband's company and causes scenes. Is this stalking too?
faqs.a: Waiting near or going to the other person's workplace is also a stalking act. If she disrupted the company's work, obstruction of business (업무방해) may also be an issue. As a rule, your husband, as the victim, files the complaint, but anyone can call 112.

faqs.q: The man my wife had an affair with sent me photos of the two of them.
faqs.a: If he sent them repeatedly to torment you, this may raise stalking or the offense of sending fear-inducing content under the Information and Communications Network Act. If the photos are sexual, other crimes also need to be considered. Don't delete the photos; save them so the date received is visible.

guides.title: If you've already secretly recorded or tracked your spouse
guides.lead: If you have already used a recorder or location tracker to confirm an affair, check your risk of punishment before asking whether you can submit the material as evidence. In 2026, the Supreme Court held that conversations secretly recorded by a third party cannot be used as evidence in an affair lawsuit.

seo.title: Secretly Recorded or Tracked Your Spouse for Affair Evidence in Korea? | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: If you gathered affair evidence with a car recorder, location tracker or by accessing your spouse's phone in Korea: what to check first, the penalty provisions for each method, admissibility after the 2026 Supreme Court ruling, what not to do, and how to rebuild the affair lawsuit with lawful evidence.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Whether you were part of the recorded conversations or not
Whether the device is still installed (if so, stop using it)
Who you have sent the recordings or photo files to
If you hired a private investigator, what methods the agency used
Whether your spouse or the affair partner knows about this
body: Your risk of punishment and the order of your response vary greatly depending on these five points. Write them down with dates as well as you can remember.

sections.title: Which laws apply to each method
body: Recording a conversation you take part in is not a violation of the Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법). Recording a conversation in which you confront your spouse about the affair is not a problem. The problems are the cases below. Even if you went through a private investigator, the same laws may apply depending on what you asked for.
bullets: Recording or listening to a conversation you were not part of: violation of the Protection of Communications Secrets Act, 1 to 10 years' imprisonment and suspension of qualifications for up to 5 years (no fine option)
Attaching a location tracker or installing a location app without consent: violation of the Location Information Act (위치정보법), up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million
Unlocking your spouse's phone and reading or photographing messages: may raise violation of the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) or violation of secrecy (비밀침해)
Entering the affair partner's home or a lodging room: may raise trespass (주거침입)

sections.title: Can it be used as evidence?
body: Under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act, conversations secretly recorded by a third party cannot be used as evidence in court. The Supreme Court held that recording files and transcripts obtained by putting a recorder in a spouse's car are inadmissible in a lawsuit for affair compensation (Supreme Court Decision 2024다222212, rendered April 30, 2026).

Other unlawfully gathered material is not automatically excluded in civil lawsuits; it is judged by weighing how it was collected, the degree of privacy intrusion and the need for the evidence. Even if it is used as evidence, the criminal liability of the person who gathered it remains separately. In effect, you take on a criminal case for material that may not even be usable, so it is safer to use court procedures from the start.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Playing the recordings to family, acquaintances or people around the affair partner (disclosure and leaking are also punishable)
Leaving the device installed
Destroying files and devices on your own after an investigation has begun
Hiring a private investigator for further investigation
body: In particular, playing the recordings to the affair partner's family or company can raise both disclosure or leaking under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act and defamation (명예훼손).

sections.title: Rebuild the affair lawsuit with other evidence
body: We look again at whether the infidelity can be proved without the problematic material. Lodging CCTV can be secured through evidence preservation (증거보전), and call and payment records through court fact inquiries (사실조회) and document production orders (문서제출명령). We also gather lawful material, such as your own conversations with your spouse and any written statement your spouse made.

If you have already submitted the problematic recording in a lawsuit, you need to decide whether to withdraw that evidence and whether other material can show the same facts. If the other side has filed a criminal complaint based on that recording, your statements in the civil and criminal cases must also be kept consistent.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law first separates recording, tracking and accessing the phone act by act and identifies which parts are problematic. If a complaint has been filed against you, we rehearse with likely questions before questioning, sit in on the questioning and submit a defense lawyer's written opinion. The affair lawsuit is redesigned around lawful evidence.
You can tell us about it through the chat on this page before sending any files.

faqs.q: I saw a conversation recorded on the dashcam in my spouse's car.
faqs.a: If it was recorded automatically by a dashcam your spouse installed, you did not make the recording. However, other problems can arise depending on how you retrieve and use the file, so it needs to be checked before you submit it as evidence.

faqs.q: The private investigator did it on their own. Can I be punished too?
faqs.a: If you didn't know what methods the agency used, it may be hard to hold you responsible. Conversely, if you asked for location tracking or recording, or hired them knowing about it, you can be investigated as an accomplice. The messages exchanged with the agency will be used to decide this.

guides.title: When disciplinary proceedings start over a workplace affair
guides.lead: If the affair partner works at the same company and you've been notified of an HR investigation or a disciplinary committee hearing, you need to deal with the workplace issue separately from the affair lawsuit. Private life alone is rarely a legitimate ground for discipline, but things change if it became entangled with work.

seo.title: Disciplinary Hearing or Dismissal Over a Workplace Affair in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do right away, and what not to do, when you're notified of an HR investigation or disciplinary committee over a relationship with a coworker in Korea; the standard for disciplining private misconduct; explanation and challenge procedures; and how to keep your statements consistent with the affair lawsuit.

sections.title: What to do right now
bullets: Get the disciplinary notice and statement of grounds. If you were only told verbally, ask for it in writing
Check whether the rules of employment and disciplinary rules contain clauses on maintaining dignity or public morals
Ask for a copy of any statement you wrote during the company's investigation
Find out what the other person's spouse told the company
Note the date of the disciplinary committee and the deadline for submitting your written explanation
body: Depending on the company, the time from investigation to a disciplinary decision can be short, so secure the documents first.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Admitting too much or giving emotional statements in the HR investigation
Contacting the other person to align your stories
Continuing conversations about the relationship on the company messenger
Submitting a resignation letter in anger as soon as you're notified
body: A statement made at the investigation stage can be used again both before the disciplinary committee and in the affair lawsuit. Reread it before signing, and ask for anything untrue to be corrected.

sections.title: The standard for whether discipline is justified
body: For a company to discipline an employee over their private life, the conduct must be directly related to business activities or risk harming the company's public reputation (Supreme Court Decision 93누23275, rendered December 13, 1994). An affair itself is a private matter, so if the company took issue with that alone, there is room to contest it.

Conversely, if circumstances like those below existed, grounds for discipline may be recognized. Whether the severity of the discipline is excessive for the grounds, and whether only one of the two was disciplined heavily, are also examined separately. Public officials can be disciplined for violating the duty to maintain dignity even for conduct outside their duties, so the standard is stricter.
bullets: Whether the two kept meeting during working hours or business trips
Whether they used facilities such as company housing or vehicles
Whether a superior used their position over a subordinate
Whether office gossip disrupted work

sections.title: How the company found out also matters
body: If discipline began because the other person's spouse came to the company or spread it in a group chat, you need to check whether the company took that into account when deciding how severe the discipline should be. The responsibility for the gossip spreading does not lie with you alone.

If the other person's spouse's conduct amounts to defamation (명예훼손) or obstruction of business (업무방해), you can also file a criminal complaint or claim damages. However, this response affects the mood for mediation in the affair lawsuit, so decide the order before acting.

sections.title: Next steps
body: You are given an opportunity to explain yourself before the disciplinary committee. Set out in writing whether you have ended the relationship, that it did not affect your work, and how the company came to know. It is important that this does not conflict with what you will argue in the affair lawsuit. A written explanation is easier to read if it focuses on dates and facts rather than being long.

Get the disciplinary decision in writing and record the date you received it. If you think the discipline is unfair, you can apply to the Labor Relations Commission for a remedy within 3 months of the date of the action, such as dismissal, suspension or a pay cut. Public officials have separate challenge procedures, such as an appeal to the Appeals Commission (소청심사), so check the deadline first.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law reviews the statement of disciplinary grounds and the rules of employment and organizes the points to contest. Jisan Law writes your explanation focused on dates and facts, and if the company allows a representative to attend, we appear before the disciplinary committee with you to present it. If an affair lawsuit is running at the same time, we keep your statements consistent across both, and also look at whether the way the other person's spouse informed the company amounts to defamation or obstruction of business. If you apply to the Labor Relations Commission for a remedy after discipline is imposed, we write the application and attend the hearing with you.
A managing partner consults with you personally, and we explain the fees after the consultation. If the disciplinary committee date is close, contact us through the chat on this page first.

faqs.q: Can I bring a lawyer to the disciplinary committee?
faqs.a: It depends on company rules. Some companies allow a representative or companion, while others accept only the employee in person. If attendance is allowed, Jisan Law attends with you; if not, we prepare by submitting in advance a written explanation drafted by Jisan Law.

faqs.q: I'm facing discipline because the other person's spouse told my company. Can I hold that person responsible?
faqs.a: Depending on how and how widely they told, you can file a criminal complaint for defamation or obstruction of business, or claim damages. However, if an affair lawsuit is also pending, it is wise to decide the order of your response before acting.

guides.title: When you decide to reconcile with your spouse during the lawsuit
guides.lead: Sometimes, partway through an affair lawsuit, people decide to give their marriage another try. Whether you continue the lawsuit and on what terms you end it changes the compensation, the reimbursement issue and the tools available if it happens again.

seo.title: Reconciling with Your Spouse During an Affair Lawsuit in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: If you decide to get back together with your spouse during an affair lawsuit in Korea: whether to continue, or end it through mediation or withdrawal; how staying married affects compensation; the affair partner's right to reimbursement; requirements for withdrawing and the limitation period; and clauses to guard against a recurrence.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: What stage the lawsuit is at (before or after the answer is filed, before or after hearings close)
Whether the affair partner is in a position to claim reimbursement from your spouse
Whether you have evidence showing that your spouse's relationship with the affair partner has really ended
If you also filed a divorce lawsuit, what to do with that case
body: Even if you've decided to reconcile, leave the lawsuit papers as they are and don't contact the other side first. If they learn of the reconciliation before you've decided how to end the case, it may be harder to agree on terms in mediation.

sections.title: You can continue the lawsuit even after reconciling
body: Reconciling does not extinguish your claim against the affair partner. You can claim compensation (위자료) from the affair partner while staying married. If you hastily drop the lawsuit before confirming that the relationship between the two has really ended, it may be hard to bring this matter up again even if they meet again later.

However, if the marriage continues, the harm to it is assessed as less than where it ended in divorce, so compensation may be set lower. If you named the affair partner as a co-defendant in a divorce lawsuit, you also need to decide how to deal with the claim against the affair partner when you withdraw the divorce claim.

sections.title: Reimbursement comes back to your household
body: If the affair partner pays all the compensation, they can claim reimbursement (구상) from your spouse, who took part in the infidelity, up to your spouse's share. In a reconciled household, part of the money received may end up being paid back out of the household budget.

That is why, when ending the case through mediation or a court settlement, a clause is often included that the affair partner will not exercise the right to reimbursement (구상권) against your spouse. A judgment cannot include such a clause, so if you have reconciled, mediation is well worth considering.

sections.title: What to know when withdrawing the lawsuit
body: A lawsuit can be withdrawn until the judgment becomes final, but once the defendant has filed a brief or argued at a hearing, the defendant's consent is needed. If there is no objection within 2 weeks of the withdrawal being served, consent is deemed given (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 266). If you withdraw after a judgment on the merits, you cannot bring the same lawsuit again (Article 267(2)).

Withdrawal also cancels the interruption of the limitation period that came from filing. Only if you take steps such as refiling within 6 months is the period treated as interrupted from the original filing (Civil Act (민법) Article 170). Rather than withdrawing unconditionally, it is safer to record the terms in a settlement agreement.

sections.title: What to work out with your spouse
body: Reconciliation rests on promises between the two of you. Decide together how your spouse will cut off contact with the affair partner, how to reduce contact if they work at the same place, and what you will do if a problem arises again.
Many promises between spouses are hard to enforce by law, but any part admitting the affair becomes evidence later. It's better to put it in writing rather than leave it as words.

sections.title: Clauses to guard against a recurrence
body: You can write a separate pledge with your spouse, but excessive promises such as "If I cheat again, I'll hand over all my property" may not be recognized as valid. In the settlement with the affair partner, include the following.
bullets: A ban on contact and meetings between the affair partner and your spouse, with a penalty for breach (위약벌)
A confidentiality clause
The affair partner's waiver of the right to reimbursement
The period of infidelity this settlement covers

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law checks the stage of the lawsuit and compares for you whether continuing, mediation or withdrawal is better. We refine the mediation clauses and settlement wording so they can actually be used if it happens again. A managing partner consults with you personally, and we explain the fees after the consultation. If a hearing date has been set, contact us through the chat on this page before then.

faqs.q: My spouse says they'll pay the affair partner's share of the compensation for them.
faqs.a: Your spouse and the affair partner are jointly liable for the same harm, so if your spouse pays, the affair partner's liability is reduced by that much. In effect, household money is just moving around, so in this case it's worth reconsidering whether continuing the lawsuit is worthwhile.

faqs.q: If they see each other again after we reconcile, can I sue again then?
faqs.a: Infidelity that newly occurs after a settlement or judgment can be claimed separately. If you included a penalty clause, you can also make a claim under that clause.

guides.title: Is an infidelity pledge from your spouse legally binding?
guides.lead: After an affair comes out, many people get their spouse to sign a written pledge (각서) saying "I'll never see them again" or "If I do it again, I'll hand over all my property." A pledge is very useful as evidence admitting the affair, but it cannot make every promise written in it binding as it stands.

seo.title: Is an Infidelity Pledge Valid in Korea? Property Waivers and Penalties | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What effect an infidelity pledge from your spouse has in divorce and affair lawsuits in Korea: its value as evidence, the limits of advance waivers of property division and custody, penalty promises and notarization, and what to include if you write a new one.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Whether you have the original pledge, and whether your spouse wrote and signed it personally
Whether facts such as the affair partner, the period and where they met are stated specifically
Whether the date of writing is stated
Whether the situation was one in which coercion or threats could be alleged
Which promises it contains: money, property, custody or divorce

sections.title: The pledge as evidence
body: The most useful part of a pledge is not the promises but the passages admitting facts. If your spouse wrote down who the affair partner is and when they started seeing each other, it becomes important evidence in a divorce lawsuit and an affair lawsuit.

Your spouse may later claim "I was forced to write it," so it helps to keep messages showing the situation on the day it was written, or a recording of a conversation you took part in. A declaration of intent made under duress can be revoked (Civil Act (민법) Article 110), so how the pledge was written becomes a point of dispute.

sections.title: Promises with limited effect
bullets: Waiving all property division: an advance waiver made before divorce, so as a rule it has no effect
Waiving parental authority or custody: the court decides separately based on the child's welfare
Agreeing to divorce unconditionally: the intention to divorce must exist at the time of divorce, so it is hard to enforce
Paying a set sum upon breach: may be recognized, but can be reduced or partly invalidated
body: A promise to give up all property division (재산분할) in the event of divorce is an advance waiver made before the divorce, so as a rule it has no effect (Supreme Court Order 2015스451, issued January 25, 2016). Parental authority and custody are also decided by the court based on the child's welfare, so writing a waiver in a pledge does not make it so.

A monetary promise such as "If I cheat again, I'll pay this much" may be recognized as valid. However, if the amount is excessive, the court may treat it as liquidated damages and reduce it (Civil Act Article 398), and any part contrary to good morals may be void (Civil Act Article 103).

sections.title: How it relates to a lawsuit against the affair partner
body: A pledge with your spouse is separate from the affair partner's liability. Unless the pledge says you waive claims against the affair partner, you can claim compensation (위자료) from the affair partner separately, and the pledge becomes evidence of the infidelity in that lawsuit.

If your spouse promised in the pledge to pay the affair partner's share as well, the terms must be aligned with that when you settle with or sue the affair partner. You cannot be compensated twice for the same harm.

sections.title: Does notarization change anything?
body: Notarization makes it hard to dispute who wrote it and when. However, a promise whose content itself has no effect, such as an advance waiver of property division, does not come back to life through notarization.

A monetary promise can be made into a notarial deed (공정증서) with consent to compulsory execution, but if there is a dispute over whether the affair actually happened again, the matter may still have to go before a court.

sections.title: If you are getting a new pledge
bullets: Make the admission of facts specific (the other person, the period, the places)
Keep the no-contact promise and the amount payable on breach within a realistic range
Know that wording waiving property or custody has weak effect even if included
Date it, have it signed by hand and, if possible, notarized

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law separates the parts of a pledge you have already received that can be used as evidence from the parts with weak effect, and if you are writing a new one, works out wording with you that can actually be used. We also make sure its content does not conflict with any settlement agreement with the affair partner. A managing partner handles the consultation personally, and we explain the fees after the consultation. You can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time.

faqs.q: After writing the pledge, my spouse cheated again. Can I get the money written in the pledge?
faqs.a: If the amount is not excessive and it was written without coercion, you can try to claim it. If your spouse doesn't pay, you have to sue for it, and the court may reduce the amount. Prepare evidence of the new affair as well.

faqs.q: We ended up divorcing a year after the pledge was written. Does it affect property division?
faqs.a: The advance waiver of property division has no effect, but the part admitting the affair becomes evidence of who is responsible for the breakdown of the marriage. Property division is decided separately, based on the assets built up together during the marriage and each spouse's contribution.

guides.title: When the affair partner is pregnant or has had a child
guides.lead: The news that your spouse's affair partner is pregnant goes beyond compensation; it involves the child's legal status, child support and even inheritance. Separate what has been confirmed now from the legal relationships that may arise in the future.

seo.title: Affair Partner Pregnant or Child Born Outside Marriage in Korea | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: What to check first when your spouse's affair partner becomes pregnant or gives birth in Korea; acknowledgment of paternity and paternity suits; court-ordered DNA tests; child support and inheritance; the effect on compensation and divorce; and what not to do.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Who told you about the pregnancy or birth, and how
Whether it has been confirmed that your spouse is the father, or it is only the affair partner's word
Whether the affair partner is married (if so, the child is presumed to be her husband's)
Whether your spouse intends to acknowledge the child
Whether the affair partner is demanding money or a divorce
body: If you act on unconfirmed claims, it is hard to correct things later. Write down what you were told along with the date, and don't delete messages from the affair partner.

sections.title: If it is still at the pregnancy stage
body: Before the birth, the first step is to confirm the pregnancy and its timing. Things differ depending on whether the timing of the pregnancy matches the period your spouse was seeing her, and whether the affair partner had other partners.

Before the child is born, it is hard to establish paternity legally. The usual course is to confirm it by DNA testing in the process of acknowledgment or a paternity suit after the birth, so don't rush to meet the affair partner's demands in the meantime.

sections.title: The legal relationship between the child and your spouse
body: A child born outside marriage has a legal father-child relationship with the biological father once he acknowledges the child (인지) (Civil Act (민법) Article 855). Even if your spouse does not acknowledge the child, the child or the affair partner as the child's legal representative can file a paternity suit (인지청구의 소) (Civil Act Article 863), and the family court can order a DNA test if necessary (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 29).

Once the child is acknowledged, your spouse must pay child support for that child, and the child becomes an heir with the same rank and the same share as your spouse's other children (Civil Act Articles 1000 and 1009).

sections.title: How child support is decided
body: Child support for an acknowledged child is shared by both parents, and if they cannot agree on the amount, the family court decides it. Courts often refer to the child support guidelines (양육비 산정기준표), which are based on the parents' incomes and the child's age.

If your spouse pays child support for a child born outside the marriage, it affects your household finances. If you stay married, you need to consider how to absorb this; if you divorce, how to reflect it in property division and living-cost calculations.

sections.title: Effect on compensation and divorce
body: A pregnancy or birth outside the marriage can be considered, as a circumstance showing the infidelity was serious, when compensation for emotional distress (위자료) is set. As in other affair cases, how you claim depends on whether you stay married or divorce; if you divorce, you can file in the family court naming both your spouse and the affair partner as defendants.

Even if the affair partner demands a divorce or money because of the pregnancy, you don't need to act according to what she says. This is all the more true if the pregnancy itself has not been confirmed.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Demanding or pressuring the affair partner to terminate the pregnancy
Telling people around the affair partner about the pregnancy or birth
Handing over money in response to an unconfirmed claim of pregnancy
Secretly obtaining samples from the child to attempt a DNA test
body: Emotional fights over the pregnancy easily leave material that later works against both sides in the affair lawsuit and the child support issue.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law separates confirmed facts from the affair partner's claims, and sets the order for the affair lawsuit, the decision on divorce, and acknowledgment and child support, looking at them all together. If the affair partner's demands or contact come close to threats, we look at how to respond to that too. Issues concerning the child are tied to whether you stay married, so they need not all be decided at once; we deal with the most urgent first, step by step. A managing partner handles the consultation personally.
You can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: If my husband acknowledges the child, will my children's inheritance shares shrink?
faqs.a: An acknowledged child is also your husband's direct descendant and inherits the same share as his other children. As a result, the existing children's shares become smaller by that much. Inheritance arises when your husband dies, so there is not much that can be decided right now.

faqs.q: The other woman is married, and she says she's had a child.
faqs.a: A child conceived by a wife during her marriage is presumed to be her husband's child (Civil Act Article 844). Overturning this presumption requires a separate procedure, such as a suit to deny paternity (친생부인의 소), so until then it is hard for your husband to acknowledge the child directly.

guides.title: When the two keep meeting after a settlement or judgment
guides.lead: When you've received compensation and closed the matter, only to see signs that your spouse and the affair partner are in touch again, it is deeply disheartening. Depending on what the settlement agreement says and what has newly happened, there may be a way to claim again.

seo.title: Affair Resumed After Settlement or Judgment in Korea: Penalties and a New Lawsuit | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: When your spouse and the affair partner meet again after an affair settlement or judgment in Korea: the settlement wording to check first, claiming compensation for new infidelity, claims under breach payment and penalty clauses, the new evidence to gather and what to watch out for.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: The original settlement agreement, mediation record or judgment
Whether there is a no-contact clause and an amount payable on breach, and whether it is a breach payment or a penalty for breach
How far wording such as "no further claims will be made" extends
Whether the signs of renewed meetings come after the settlement or judgment (the dates)
What you will do about your relationship with your spouse
body: With a settlement agreement, a single phrase can decide the outcome. Find the original and first check the date, the signatures and who is named as a party.

sections.title: Before contacting the other side
body: When you catch signs that they are meeting again, you will want to confront the affair partner right away. But contact at this stage leads the other side to erase evidence, and emotional wording can escalate into accusations of threats (협박) or defamation (명예훼손).
The usual order is to organize the facts of the breach, first demand payment of the breach payment or penalty by certified letter (내용증명), and go to court if they don't comply.

sections.title: Meeting after a settlement or judgment is a new tort
body: What a judgment or settlement resolves is the infidelity up to that point. If they met again afterward and committed infidelity, you can claim compensation (위자료) separately for that new tort. The effect of a judgment does not extend to events that occur after the hearings close.
However, if the no-further-lawsuits wording in the settlement agreement is broad, there may be disputes over how much was waived. Reading the wording carefully comes first.

sections.title: If there is a breach payment or penalty clause
body: If the settlement agreement has a clause such as "If there is further contact, X will be paid," you can claim under that clause. A breach payment (위약금) is presumed to be liquidated damages, which the court can reduce if it finds it excessive (Civil Act (민법) Article 398); if it was set as a penalty for breach (위약벌), it is harder to reduce, but if excessively heavy it may be partly void.

The scope of the breach can also be disputed. If the agreement says only "no meeting" and the two only exchanged messages, whether that is a breach becomes an issue. The more specifically the agreement describes the methods of contact, the fewer the disputes. If both "breach payment" and "penalty for breach" appear, its nature is judged by looking at the agreement as a whole.

sections.title: Liability your spouse can face too
body: If this has made you decide to divorce, you can also claim divorce compensation from your spouse. The fact that your spouse had an affair again after the earlier settlement is a serious circumstance showing responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage.

If your spouse wrote a pledge earlier, that is also considered. The parts admitting facts serve as evidence, and claims under monetary promises are considered to the extent they may be recognized as valid.

sections.title: Evidence must be gathered anew
body: Evidence from the first case does not support this new claim. You need material dated after the settlement or judgment. Organize messages, photos of the two together, and lodging and payment records in date order, and consider evidence preservation (증거보전) for CCTV that may be erased. Clues from the first case that can still be used, such as the affair partner's contact details or car plate number, are put to use again.
This time too, avoid unlawful methods. Material obtained with a car recorder or location tracker is hard to use as evidence and also creates a risk of punishment.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law starts by reading the wording of the settlement agreement and judgment, and looks at whether a claim under the breach payment or penalty clause and a new compensation claim can be brought together. If the other side doesn't pay, we also consider compulsory execution. A managing partner consults with you personally, and we explain the fees after the consultation. You can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time.

faqs.q: The mediation record says 'a certain amount per contact.' Can I seize their assets right away?
faqs.a: A mediation record has the same effect as a final judgment, but the fact of contact must be proved separately, so in many cases you can't seize assets right away. You may need to prove the breach to obtain a certificate of enforcement (집행문) or bring a separate lawsuit.

faqs.q: The affair partner says, 'Your spouse contacted me first.'
faqs.a: Who made contact first can affect how the settlement clause is interpreted and the amount of compensation. However, if the agreement also imposed a duty not to respond to contact, simply not being the first to reach out will hardly clear them of liability. Keep the entire conversation in time order.

guides.title: When it's been nearly 3 years since you found out about the affair
guides.lead: A compensation claim against the affair partner has a time limit. But when the 3 years start running depends on whether you divorced and whether the relationship continued, so line up the dates before concluding the deadline has passed.

seo.title: Time Limit for Suing an Affair Partner in Korea: When Do the 3 Years Start? | Jisan Family Law Center
seo.description: The time limit for claiming compensation from an affair partner in Korea when you found out long ago: the basic rule of 3 years from when you learned, the 2026 Supreme Court ruling counting from the dissolution of the marriage after a divorce, cases where the relationship continued, and how to stop the clock.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: The day you first learned of the affair and who the affair partner was
Whether the two continued their relationship after that, and when they last met
Whether you divorced and, if so, the date (the date the divorce by agreement was registered or the date the judgment became final)
Whether you have ever sent a certified letter or filed a lawsuit
Whether the affair partner has ever acknowledged that they would pay

sections.title: The basic rule: 3 years from when you learned
body: A claim for damages in tort lapses 3 years after the day you learned of the damage and the wrongdoer, or 10 years after the day of the wrongful act (Civil Act (민법) Article 766). If you stay married and claim against the affair partner, the 3 years usually run from the day you learned of the affair and the affair partner. The 10 years run from the day of the infidelity regardless of when you learned of it, so something that happened very long ago is hard to claim for even if you only found out recently.

sections.title: If you divorced, the clock runs from the divorce
body: The Supreme Court has held that when infidelity breaks down a marriage and leads to divorce, the harm for divorce compensation (위자료) becomes fixed when the divorce is finalized, and the 3-year limitation period runs from the dissolution of the marriage (Supreme Court Decision 2025므10716, rendered January 29, 2026). Even if more than 3 years have passed since you learned of the affair, if that affair led to your divorce, you may still be able to claim against the affair partner within 3 years of the divorce.

The same ruling stated that a compensation claim against an affair partner on the ground of divorce is a family court case, while a claim targeting an individual act of infidelity regardless of divorce is a civil case. The starting date and the court differ depending on which way you claim. The date the marriage was dissolved is the date the divorce was registered for a divorce by agreement, and the date the judgment became final for a judicial divorce.

sections.title: If you held off because you didn't know their name
body: If you have been putting off a claim because you didn't know the affair partner's name and address, you can file a lawsuit with just a phone number or bank account number and confirm their identity through a court fact inquiry (사실조회). If you're worried about the deadline, consider filing first rather than waiting until you have all their details.

You can argue that the day you "learned of the wrongdoer" is when you became able to identify who the affair partner was. Keep separate records of the period when you knew only a phone number and the time you confirmed their identity.

sections.title: If the relationship continued or the deadline is near
body: If the two kept meeting after you learned of the affair, those later meetings can be considered separately. Even if the limitation period for the original affair has run out, you can claim on the basis of more recent infidelity. In that case, the complaint sets out, by date, which period of meetings forms the basis of the claim.

Making a claim by certified letter (내용증명) alone may not be enough. An out-of-court demand interrupts the limitation period only if you follow it with a lawsuit or similar step within 6 months (Civil Act Article 174), so if the deadline is near, it is safer to file the complaint quickly.

sections.title: What not to do
bullets: Concluding on your own that the deadline has passed and giving up
Contacting the affair partner directly to get them to admit liability so as to extend the limitation period (this can lead to accusations of threats)
Sending only a certified letter and letting 6 months pass
Coming to a consultation without documents showing the date of the divorce

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law lines up in a table the day you learned of the affair, the last meeting and the date of the divorce, and decides which court to file in and with what claim. If the deadline is near, we also consider filing the complaint first and supplementing the evidence during the lawsuit. A managing partner consults with you personally, and you can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time.

faqs.q: It's been 2 years since our divorce by agreement. I found out about the affair 5 years ago.
faqs.a: If the marriage broke down and ended in divorce because of that affair, there is case law counting the 3 years from the divorce, so you may still be able to claim. However, if a long time passed between the affair and the divorce, whether the divorce was caused by that affair may be disputed, so put together what happened in between.

faqs.q: I have a text from the affair partner saying, 'I'll pay you.'
faqs.a: Words acknowledging a debt may be treated as an acknowledgment that interrupts the limitation period (Civil Act Article 168). When they said it and in what words matters, so keep the original message exactly as it is.

guides.stage: My parent passed away and I don't know if there are debts
guides.title: When a Parent Has Died and You Do Not Know Whether There Are Debts
guides.lead: If the debts may be larger than the assets, you must decide within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began. Start by searching for assets, and above all, do not touch the deceased's property in the meantime.

seo.title: Checking a Parent's Debts After Death in Korea and Deciding on Renunciation or Limited Acceptance | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do, and what not to do, in Korea when a parent has died and you do not know whether there are debts. Covers applying for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service, actions that count as simple acceptance, choosing between renunciation and limited acceptance, next-in-line heirs, and calculating the 3-month deadline.
keywords: withdrawing from account after death Korea

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: Once the funeral is over, take the steps below in order. At this stage, gathering information comes before rushing a decision.
bullets: Write the date of death and the day you learned of it on a calendar, and mark the date 3 months later as your deadline.

When you report the death at the community service center (주민센터, your local district office), apply at the same time for the Safe Inheritance One-Stop Service (안심상속 원스톱서비스, a government service that searches a deceased person's assets and debts in one application). If you have already reported the death, you can apply separately through Government24 (the government's online portal).
Do not throw away mail from card companies, private lenders, surety insurers or courts; keep it all in one place with the envelopes.
Check the automatic transfers from the deceased's account, and switch payment of utility bills and insurance premiums to your own account.
Look through the deceased's text messages and notebooks for money that went out each month, money they lent, and any debts they backed as a surety, and write them down.

sections.title: What Not to Do
body: The following actions may be treated as disposing of the estate, which can amount to simple acceptance (단순승인). Once that happens, you cannot renounce even if you later find out the debts are larger.
bullets: Withdrawing money from the deceased's account for living costs because you know the PIN
Selling the deceased's car or putting it in your name
Collecting the deposit on the home the deceased lived in and splitting it among siblings
Collecting money from someone who owed the deceased and spending it
Stamping a division agreement among siblings before the search is even finished

sections.title: Decide After Seeing the Search Results
body: Some Safe Inheritance results, such as vehicles, come right away, but financial, national tax and pension results are processed by each agency and can take close to 20 days. When a result message arrives, print the details from that agency's website. Financial search results can no longer be viewed on the Financial Supervisory Service website once 3 months have passed from the application date.
