The results show loans and card debts, but money borrowed from individuals and some surety debts may not appear.

If the debts are clearly larger than the assets, consider renunciation of inheritance (상속포기). If you cannot tell which is larger, or you are worried about debts that did not show up, consider limited acceptance (한정승인). With limited acceptance, you only pay debts up to the value of what you inherited, but after acceptance you must go through a settlement process of public notice and proportional payment.

sections.title: Decide Together Who in the Family Will Do What
body: If you renounce, the debts pass to the next in line. If the spouse and children are the heirs and only the children all renounce, the spouse becomes the sole heir and nothing passes to the grandchildren; but if the spouse also renounces, the grandchildren, the deceased's parents, siblings and relatives within the fourth degree become heirs in that order. The court does not notify next-in-line family members.

That is why, in practice, a common approach is for the spouse or one child to take limited acceptance while the rest renounce. This settles the debts with the person who took limited acceptance, so they do not pass to next-in-line relatives. If a family member is a minor, the parent with parental authority acts on their behalf, but where their interests conflict, a special representative (특별대리인) may be needed.

sections.title: Some Money Can Be Received Even If You Renounce
body: One reason people hesitate to renounce is insurance and pensions. Death insurance where the beneficiary is set as the heirs or a specific family member, and the National Pension survivor pension and lump-sum death benefit, are generally treated not as part of the estate but as the recipient's own property, so in most cases they can be received even if you renounce. However, insurance money where the beneficiary is the deceased themselves can be part of the estate, and if the deceased had unpaid national taxes, you may have to pay them up to the amount of insurance money you received, so check the insurance policies and any unpaid tax records together.

sections.title: The Next Steps
body: Once you have decided, file with the family court that has jurisdiction over the deceased's last address. Submit the filing form, family relationship documents and certificate of seal impression (인감증명서), and for limited acceptance, attach a list of the estate. The filing only needs to be received within 3 months, and if the documents are in order, the written decision accepting it usually comes within 1 to 2 months.

If the search is delayed and it is hard to decide within 3 months, you can ask the family court for an extension before the period runs out. If you discover debts after the deadline, special limited acceptance (특별한정승인) remains an option, but its requirements must be proved separately, so it is much easier to settle things within the first 3 months.

If one sibling has already disposed of the deceased's property, only that sibling may be treated as having simply accepted, and as a rule this does not affect the other family members' renunciation or limited acceptance. However, if the family files together, the circumstances must be stated accurately, so check this in advance.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law looks at the search results and collection notices with you and works out whether renunciation or limited acceptance fits, and which family member should file what. We prepare the filing and the list of the estate within the deadline, and continue on to the public notice and proportional payment after limited acceptance, and any creditor lawsuits that come in after acceptance.

If you need to use the deceased's account for funeral or hospital costs, please ask us before you act. If the deadline is near and you need to move quickly, send us a message through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: I paid for the funeral from the deceased's account. Does that stop me from renouncing?
faqs.a: There is case law holding that paying funeral costs within a socially reasonable range from the estate is not an act of disposal. However, you must be able to show the amount and its use with receipts, and spending the remaining money personally causes a problem. Keep a record of what was spent and leave the rest untouched.

faqs.q: If the Safe Inheritance search shows no debts at all, can I relax?
faqs.a: The search results are based mainly on records from financial institutions and public agencies, so loans between individuals, some surety debts and debts not yet overdue may be missing. It is wise for family members who knew the deceased's life to look through their notebooks, text messages and regular withdrawals from their accounts as well.

faqs.q: I lost contact with my father long ago and only learned of his death much later.
faqs.a: The 3 months run not from the date of death but from the day you learned of the death and that you had become an heir. Keep the text messages or mail that show the date you were contacted, and file within 3 months from that date.

guides.title: When You Receive a Demand for the Deceased's Debts After the 3 Months Have Passed
guides.lead: Missing the renunciation deadline does not mean you have to give up. If you did not know, without gross negligence, that the debts exceeded the assets, you can take special limited acceptance within 3 months from the day you learned that fact.

seo.title: Debt Demands or Lawsuits After the Renunciation Deadline in Korea: Special Limited Acceptance | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when you receive a collection notice, complaint or payment order more than 3 months after a parent's death. Covers the requirements and deadline for special limited acceptance, explaining the absence of gross negligence, the 2 weeks for a payment order and 30 days for an answer, and how to handle estate property already used.

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: The day you received the demand may be the starting point of a new deadline. Pin down the dates first.
bullets: Keep the collection notice or complaint with its envelope to show the date you received it, and write that down along with today's date.
If the papers came from a court, check whether it is a payment order (지급명령) or a complaint. You must respond to a payment order within 2 weeks of receiving it, and to a complaint within 30 days.

If you have not yet used the Safe Inheritance (안심상속) search, apply now; if you did, find those results again. Once 1 year has passed from the last day of the month of death, the combined search is no longer available and you must check with each agency separately.
If you used or disposed of any of the deceased's property after the death, write down what, when and for how much.
Gather materials showing that you had lost contact with the deceased, or that it was hard to know the state of their finances.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Promising a debt collector on the phone that you will 'pay a little at a time', or paying part of the debt
Ignoring court papers because 'it isn't my debt anyway' (if they become final, they have the same effect as a judgment)
Hurrying to sell the deceased's remaining property or moving it into a family member's name
Filing a new renunciation because the deadline has passed (at this point renunciation will not be accepted; only limited acceptance is possible)

sections.title: When Special Limited Acceptance Is Available
body: Civil Act (민법) Article 1019(3) provides that an heir who, without gross negligence, did not know within 3 months that the estate's debts exceeded its assets and whose inheritance became a simple acceptance (단순승인), may take limited acceptance within 3 months from the day they learned that fact. This covers both cases where the inheritance became a simple acceptance because nothing was done for 3 months and cases where it was treated as one because estate property was disposed of.

The most important point is that you 'did not know without gross negligence'. You need to explain specifically, for example, that you had no contact with the deceased for a long time, that no mail arrived that would have revealed the deceased's assets or debts, or that the debt did not show up in the search results. On the other hand, if you had already received several collection demands, or lived with the deceased and could have known about the debts, it is hard to have the filing accepted.

If the inheritance occurred while you were a minor and became a simple acceptance, you can take limited acceptance within 3 months from the day, after becoming an adult, that you learned the debts were larger (paragraph 4 of the same Article).

sections.title: If You Have Already Used the Deceased's Property
body: Even if you withdrew and spent deposits or sold the car after the death, you can still take special limited acceptance (특별한정승인), because the law includes cases that became a simple acceptance through disposal. In return, you must list the property disposed of and its value in the filing, and when settling, you must pay creditors that value in addition to the remaining property, in proportion to their claims. Hiding money you spent can turn it back into a simple acceptance, so being honest in the filing is actually safer.

sections.title: The Next Steps
body: Special limited acceptance is filed with the family court that has jurisdiction over the deceased's last address. In addition to the documents for ordinary limited acceptance, attach materials explaining how you learned of the debts late, and if you have already disposed of estate property, submit a list of it with its value (Civil Act Article 1030(2)).

If court papers have arrived, you must respond to that case separately from the filing. For a payment order, file an objection within 2 weeks to move it into a lawsuit; for a complaint, file an answer within 30 days stating that you have filed for special limited acceptance, and later submit the written decision accepting it. Once it is accepted, we argue for the judgment to include the words 'up to the value of the estate'.

After acceptance, you go through public notice, notice to creditors and proportional payment, as with ordinary limited acceptance. The difference is that the value of property already disposed of must be added to the remaining property for payment.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law sets out by date what you knew and when, prepares a written explanation showing there was no gross negligence, and handles the special limited acceptance filing together with any payment orders or lawsuits already received. If you disposed of property, we also look at how to state its value.

Once 2 weeks have passed, a payment order becomes hard to challenge. If it has been a few days since you received the papers, take photos of them and send them to us first through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: What counts as the day I learned of the debts?
faqs.a: Usually you argue that it is the day you received a complaint, payment order or collection notice and first learned concretely that the debts exceeded the assets. However, if there were earlier signs you should have noticed, the court may set an earlier date, so it is important to put the mail and contacts you received in chronological order.

faqs.q: If one of my siblings has already taken special limited acceptance, do I still need to?
faqs.a: Limited acceptance is effective only for the person who filed it. If you are also in a state of simple acceptance, you must file separately, and the day each of you 'learned' is assessed separately.

faqs.q: My special limited acceptance was accepted, but I received a certificate of succession for execution.
faqs.a: This may be a case where a creditor obtained a certificate of succession for execution (승계집행문) to enforce an earlier judgment against the heirs. A separate procedure is needed to block enforcement by asserting the limited acceptance, so bring the written decision and all the papers you received and get advice right away.

guides.stage: My siblings and I can't agree on dividing the estate
guides.title: When You and Your Siblings Cannot Settle the Division of the Estate
guides.lead: There is no deadline for dividing an estate, but the longer you wait, the more heirs there are and the deeper the rift. The starting point, before anyone stamps anything, is to calculate what each person would actually receive.

seo.title: When Siblings Cannot Agree on Dividing an Inheritance in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when you and your siblings cannot agree on dividing a parent's estate. Covers listing the estate and lifetime gifts, wording to watch for in the division agreement, registration by statutory shares when a sibling will not stamp the agreement, special benefits and contribution shares, and family court mediation and adjudication.
keywords: division of estate agreement form Korea

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: If you line up the numbers and documents before emotions take over, both negotiation and adjudication become much easier.
bullets: List the real estate, deposits, stocks, insurance, vehicles and debts as of the date of death in one table. Leave blank anything you do not know.
Write down what you know about money, homes or wedding funds your siblings received during the parent's lifetime, and look for registry records or transfer records.
If you cared for your parent or paid hospital bills, gather transfer records and medical records showing the period and amounts.
Do not delete messages exchanged during the negotiations or any draft agreement the other side sent; save them.
Mark the inheritance tax filing deadline (6 months from the last day of the month of death) on a calendar.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Stamping an agreement 'for now' when you do not fully understand it
Leaving your registered seal and certificate of seal impression with one sibling
Breaking into your parent's home or removing belongings during a dispute with the sibling living there
Posting criticism of a sibling in the family group chat
Withdrawing and spending the deceased's deposits without the other siblings knowing

sections.title: Statutory Shares Are Only the Starting Point
body: With three children, each statutory share is one third, and if there is a spouse, the spouse's statutory share is 1.5 times one child's share. But in an actual division, property received in advance during the parent's lifetime (special benefit, 특별수익) is added back for the calculation, and the contribution share (기여분) of anyone who specially supported the parent is set aside first. So 'equal shares by law' can actually produce an unfair result.

Under the amendment of March 17, 2026, gifts received in return for specially supporting a parent are no longer treated as special benefits to that extent. If one of the siblings received such a gift, this must also be included in the calculation.

In a blended family, the calculation becomes more complex. A stepmother or stepfather whose marriage was registered is a co-heir as a spouse, and children from the father's earlier marriage and from his later marriage have equal shares. On the other hand, a stepmother's child from a previous relationship is not the father's heir unless he adopted them.

sections.title: When a Sibling Will Not Stamp the Agreement
body: Division by agreement requires the consent of every heir, so if even one objects, there is no agreement. In that case, one heir can register the inheritance in all the heirs' names according to their statutory shares. However, the objecting sibling's share is registered too, and this is not a final division reflecting special benefits or contribution shares.

If a sibling cannot be reached at all, an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인) must be appointed first, and if an heir is a minor, a special representative (특별대리인), before either an agreement or an adjudication can go ahead.

sections.title: What to Check Before Signing an Agreement
body: Before you stamp an agreement your sibling sent, check each of the points below. Once stamped, an agreement is hard to undo.
bullets: Whether any deposits, insurance, vehicles or lease deposits are missing from the list of assets
Whether the lot numbers and shares of real estate and the account numbers of deposits are written correctly
Who takes on the debts, and whether the loans can be transferred into that person's name
Whether it says how assets discovered later will be divided
If you are to receive a settlement payment, whether the amount, the payment date and what happens if payment is late are written in

sections.title: The Next Steps
body: If agreement proves impossible, you ask the family court for an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할). The person filing names all the other heirs as respondents, and because mediation must come first in these cases, a mediation date is usually set first. To claim a contribution share, you must file a petition to determine it together with the request for division.

During the case, orders to submit financial transaction information are used to confirm money the siblings received, and the market value of real estate is set by appraisal. If mediation succeeds, the estate is divided on those terms; if not, the court decides by adjudication who gets what and any settlement payments. Including mediation, it usually takes around a year.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first gathers the list of the estate, lifetime gifts and records of support, and prepares a table calculating each person's specific share. Based on that table, we put forward a settlement proposal or review the agreement the other side sent, and if agreement fails, we pursue an adjudication on division and a contribution share claim.

From the first consultation, the lawyer in charge handles your case personally. If you have been asked to sign an agreement, take a photo of it and send it to us through the chat on this page before signing.

faqs.q: My brother lives in our parents' house and pays no rent at all.
faqs.a: Until division, the estate is co-owned by all the heirs, so if one person is using it alone, the other heirs may be able to claim the benefit of use for their share as unjust enrichment. However, this is often settled within the division adjudication, so we choose the better approach depending on the situation.

faqs.q: I signed the agreement and later found out about a gift my brother received.
faqs.a: An agreement is a consensus of all the heirs, so as a rule it is hard to overturn. However, if the other side actively hid the gift and deceived you, we consider whether you can seek to cancel it on the ground of fraud. There is a time limit for cancellation, so record the date you found out.

faqs.q: How much does an adjudication on division of the estate cost?
faqs.a: The stamp duty and service fees paid to the court depend on the value of the estate and the number of parties, and if a real estate appraisal is needed, there is a separate appraisal fee. We explain the lawyer's fees after the consultation, once we have looked at the scope of the case.

guides.title: When the Estate Went to Just One Person
guides.lead: If your parent concentrated their property on one sibling through lifetime gifts or a will, you can claim your forced heirship share. You cannot claim once 1 year has passed from the day you learned of the gift or bequest, so check the dates first.

seo.title: Claiming a Forced Heirship Share in Korea When a Parent's Estate Went to One Sibling | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when a father gave his house to only one child or left a will giving everything to one person. Covers who is entitled to a forced heirship share and in what proportion, the 1-year limit, securing evidence of gifts, the 2026 rule of returning value in money with interest, how it relates to invalidating a will, and the lawsuit process.
keywords: parent gave property to one child Korea
forced heirship share returned in money
will and forced heirship share Korea

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: Whether you can claim a forced heirship share depends on 'when you learned'. In the first week, pin down the dates and documents.
bullets: Write on a calendar the day you obtained the registry record, the day you saw the will, and the day a sibling told you about the gift, and keep those documents.
Obtain registry certificates for real estate that was in your parent's name from the Internet Registry Office, and check the cause of transfer (gift, bequest or sale) and the date.
If there is a will, check whether it is notarized or handwritten, and if handwritten, find out whether a court inspection has taken place.
Honestly write down any money or property you yourself received from your parent during their lifetime. It will not be left out of the calculation.
Organize what you know about the assets and debts remaining on the date of death.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Letting the year slip by while trying to talk things out with your sibling
Sending the sibling who received the gift a written statement or message saying you will not claim a forced heirship share
Putting off a forced heirship share claim while arguing only that the will is invalid
Claiming a forced heirship share as a sibling of the deceased (this right was abolished by the 2024 unconstitutionality ruling)

sections.title: Check Whether You Can Claim
body: Only children, spouses and parents who become heirs have a forced heirship share (유류분). For children and spouses it is one half of the statutory share, and for parents one third. Grandchildren take over that share when their parent died first and they became heirs by representation (대습상속).

The calculation starts with the property on the date of death, plus gifts, minus debts. Under case law, gifts received by siblings are counted even if made long ago, and gifted property is revalued at its value around the time of death. If, after subtracting what you received and what you will inherit, there is still a shortfall, you can claim that amount. If plenty of the estate remains, there may be no shortfall even if the gifts were large.

If there are several recipients, you claim first from those who received property by will, and only if that is not enough, from those who received lifetime gifts. Within the same group, each returns in proportion to the value they received.

sections.title: Check What Changed in 2026
body: If the person died on or after March 17, 2026, the rule is that the forced heirship shortfall is returned in money, with interest from the date of the claim. If they died before then, the rule, as before, is return of the gifted property itself (as a share), but if it has already been sold, you receive money.

If the sibling who received the gift cared for the parent for a long time and specially supported them, and received the property in return, the portion matching that contribution may now be excluded from the calculation. Be prepared for the other side to make this argument.

sections.title: A Simple Calculation Example
body: Suppose the mother died first, and five years before his death the father gave the eldest son an apartment worth KRW 600 million and then died leaving nothing else. With three children, the base estate is KRW 600 million, each statutory share is one third, and the forced heirship share is half of that, one sixth, so the second son and the daughter can each claim KRW 100 million. Because the eldest son is a co-heir, the gift made five years earlier is included in the calculation.

In a real case, the apartment is appraised at its market value around the time of death, and gifts such as wedding money that the second son or daughter received, as well as any remaining debts, are taken into account, so the amounts change. That is why preparing a rough calculation table before filing a complaint also helps in negotiations.

sections.title: The Next Steps
body: First, send the person who received the gift a certified letter with proof of contents (내용증명) making clear that you are claiming return of your forced heirship share, and if no agreement is reached, file a civil lawsuit. If there are both a person who received property by will and a person who received lifetime gifts, you claim from the bequest recipient first.

In the lawsuit, orders to submit financial transaction information are used to find hidden cash gifts, and the value of real estate is set by appraisal. Many cases end in mediation during the lawsuit, and the first instance alone usually takes from 6 months to over a year. If there is a risk that the other side will dispose of property, apply for a provisional attachment or provisional injunction when you file.

If the validity of the will itself is doubtful, you can file a lawsuit to confirm the will is invalid, but the forced heirship share deadline keeps running in the meantime. Consider pursuing both claims together.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first calculates the forced heirship shortfall from the registry, the will and financial records, and tells you whether a claim is worthwhile. If it is, we state your claim and file suit before the time limit expires, and dispute the amount through appraisals and financial inquiries.

If it has been nearly a year since you learned of the gift, you should book a consultation today. You can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: While my father was alive, I signed a statement waiving my forced heirship share.
faqs.a: Under case law, waiving a forced heirship share before the inheritance begins has no effect. However, if you stated that you were waiving it after the death, the situation may be different, so check the date and content of the statement.

faqs.q: My sibling received cash, so there is no evidence.
faqs.a: Once you file a lawsuit, you can search your parent's account history and money sent to your sibling's account through the court. Even knowing which bank was used and roughly when is enough to start, so write down whatever you remember.

faqs.q: My mother is still alive, and all of my father's estate went to her.
faqs.a: Children can also claim a forced heirship share against the spouse. However, many families decide whether to claim with the family relationship and the mother's future inheritance in mind, and because of the time limit, the decision must be made within 1 year.

guides.title: When You Receive an Inheritance-Related Complaint or Petition
guides.lead: Even within 'inheritance lawsuits', a creditor's debt claim, a forced heirship share lawsuit and an adjudication on division of the estate each have different deadlines and responses. First check exactly what document you have received.

seo.title: Receiving an Inheritance Complaint, Payment Order or Division Petition in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do, by type of document, when you receive court papers related to an inheritance in Korea. Covers deadlines and writing an answer for creditors' complaints and payment orders, forced heirship share complaints, petitions for division of the estate, and complaints to invalidate a will or recover an inheritance, plus what not to do.
keywords: forced heirship share complaint answer Korea

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: Once you have opened the envelope, do the following before reading the contents in detail.
bullets: Write the date you received the papers on the envelope and on a calendar. Every deadline starts from that day.
Check the title and case number at the top of the document. The response differs depending on whether it is a 'payment order', 'complaint', 'petition' or 'notice of hearing date'.
Mark who the plaintiff (petitioner) is and the relief sought: what and how much they are demanding.
If you renounced or took limited acceptance, find the written decision; if there is a will, find a copy; and keep them with the papers.
Check the progress of the case by its number through the Supreme Court's case search service or the electronic litigation system (전자소송).

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Ignoring court papers because 'I renounced, so it has nothing to do with me'
Calling the sibling on the other side and demanding they withdraw the lawsuit
Selling the disputed real estate or moving it into a family member's name during the lawsuit
Writing only long emotional complaints in your answer without responding point by point to the other side's claims

sections.title: Each Document Has a Different Deadline
bullets: Payment order (a creditor's debt claim): file an objection within 2 weeks of receipt. If you miss it, it has the same effect as a final judgment

Complaint (civil lawsuits such as debt claims, forced heirship share, invalidity of a will, recovery of an inheritance): file an answer within 30 days of receipt. If you do not, judgment may be entered for the plaintiff without a hearing
Petition for division of the estate or contribution share: follow the dates and filing requests set by the court. File any contribution share claim within the period set by the court
Appealing a judgment or adjudication: for a civil judgment, appeal within 2 weeks of service; for a non-contentious family adjudication, file an immediate appeal within 14 days of notification

sections.title: How to Respond to Each Type of Document
body: For a complaint or payment order demanding payment of the deceased's debts, the key is whether you renounced (상속포기) or took limited acceptance (한정승인). If you renounced, file an answer or objection with the written decision attached; if you took limited acceptance, you must raise the defense that you are 'liable only up to the value of the estate'. If you did nothing and the 3 months have passed, we also check whether special limited acceptance is possible.

For a forced heirship share (유류분) complaint, the answer addresses whether the time limit has passed, whether the plaintiff also received something during the parent's lifetime, whether the gifted property was valued correctly, and whether the gift was received in return for supporting the parent. The amount in the complaint is only what the plaintiff claims, so do not panic and rush into a settlement.

For a petition for division of the estate (상속재산분할), all the heirs are parties, so you receive notice even if you do not intend to take anything. Submit in writing the division method and views you want and any materials on gifts other siblings received or your own contribution, and if you cannot attend, submit a written explanation.

For a complaint to confirm a will is invalid or to recover an inheritance, first secure the original will, the court inspection record and how the registration came about, and check each date in the other side's claims. A claim to recover an inheritance expires 3 years after learning of the infringement or 10 years after the infringing act, so if that period has passed, raise that first. If you have received a petition for a declaration of loss of inheritance rights, gather materials showing the opposite, such as evidence of support or contact records, and submit your views.

sections.title: The Next Steps
body: A civil lawsuit proceeds after the answer through preparatory hearings or hearing dates, and forced heirship share cases often take close to a year because of financial inquiries and appraisals. An adjudication on division of the estate starts with a mediation date, and if mediation fails, it proceeds through a hearing to an adjudication. In either case, a good share of cases end in mediation during the proceedings, so it is wise to decide from the start what range you can accept.

Even while the case is ongoing, the inheritance tax filing deadline runs separately, so coordinate the filing schedule with a tax accountant, noting that a dispute is pending. Even if you handle the case yourself, keep the court papers in date order and always keep copies of what you submit, so you do not lose track later.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law reads the papers you received, checks the deadlines first, and prepares an answer or written opinion that separates what to admit from what to dispute. For a debt claim we set out the renunciation or limited acceptance defense; for a forced heirship share case, the time limit and the calculation; and for a division adjudication, the materials on special benefits and contribution shares.
For papers with a 2-week deadline, such as a payment order, take photos and send them to us first through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: I renounced the inheritance, but another lawsuit came. Do I have to go to court?
faqs.a: In most cases it is resolved in writing by filing an answer with the written decision on the renunciation and documents showing it is final. If you receive a notice of a hearing date and do not attend, it may work against you, so when a date is set, attend or respond through a representative.

faqs.q: Can another creditor sue again over a debt case I already won?
faqs.a: As a rule, suing the same person again over the same claim is barred, but if the claim has been transferred to another company or it is a different debt, a new lawsuit can come. Each time a complaint arrives, respond in the same way within the deadline.

faqs.q: I cannot finish the answer within 30 days.
faqs.a: You can file an answer stating only your basic position first, and supplement the detailed arguments later in a preparatory brief. The most important thing is to state within the deadline that you dispute the plaintiff's claim.

guides.title: Can You Withdraw Money From a Parent's Account After Their Death?
guides.lead: Knowing the PIN does not mean you can freely withdraw the deceased's deposits. If you are considering renunciation, there is a risk of simple acceptance, and if you have siblings, it can escalate into a dispute or even a criminal matter.

seo.title: Withdrawing From a Parent's Bank Account After Death in Korea: Simple Acceptance and Exceptional Withdrawals | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: Whether you can withdraw money from a deceased parent's account in Korea. Covers the rapid blocking of deceased persons' financial transactions introduced in September 2026, exceptional withdrawals for funeral and hospital costs, the risk of simple acceptance, returning money withdrawn without siblings knowing and criminal issues, and the proper way to withdraw inherited deposits.
keywords: funeral cost withdrawal deceased account Korea

sections.title: Accounts Are Blocked From the Day After the Death Is Reported
body: From September 11, 2026, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service launched a 'rapid blocking system for financial transactions in the names of deceased persons'. Information on deaths is shared with financial institutions daily, so once a death report is received, transactions in the deceased's name are blocked across banks, insurers, card companies, securities firms and all other financial institutions from the next day. Strictly necessary transactions, such as deposits into the account, and exceptional withdrawals are still allowed.

What matters is that the cutoff is the day after the death is reported, not the date of death. Before the report, a debit card or mobile banking may still work, but that does not mean you may withdraw money. Inheritance begins at the moment of death, and from then on the deposits belong to the heirs.

sections.title: Use Exceptional Withdrawals for Funeral and Hospital Costs
body: If you urgently need money, for example for funeral costs or unpaid medical bills, use the financial institution's exceptional withdrawal system. You bring a family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서), your ID and the bill from the funeral home or hospital, and after checking them the institution sends the money directly to the hospital, care facility or funeral home.

Handled this way, there is a record of where the money went, which reduces problems both among siblings and later if you renounce or take limited acceptance. Automatic transfers may stop, so switch utility bills and insurance premiums to another account in advance.

Keep the amounts handled by exceptional withdrawal and the receipts together. They are used as proof of funeral costs when settling among the heirs later or when filing inheritance tax. If part of the funeral costs was covered by condolence money, write that down too to reduce misunderstandings among siblings.

sections.title: Problems With Withdrawing the Money Yourself
body: First, you may lose the ability to renounce or take limited acceptance (한정승인). Disposing of estate property is treated as simple acceptance (단순승인), so if you use the withdrawn money for living costs or to pay your own debts, you risk taking on the deceased's debts as well. There is case law holding that reasonable funeral costs are not a disposal, but you must be able to prove them with receipts.

Second, if you have siblings, you will have taken the other heirs' shares too. You may face a claim to return the money, and there have been cases where people who secretly transferred money using the deceased's card and PIN were punished for computer-related fraud or embezzlement. The Criminal Act has been amended so that, for offenses on or after June 27, 2024, family members can be punished if a complaint is filed.
Third, there is inheritance tax. Tax audits often ask what large withdrawals before and after the death were used for, and if you cannot explain where the money went, it can count against you.

sections.title: The Proper Way to Receive Deposits
body: The heirs can receive the deposits by agreeing on and writing an agreement on division of the estate, and going to the bank with certificates of seal impression (인감증명서) and family relationship documents. Required documents vary slightly by bank, so call ahead to check. Some banks have a procedure for paying out small deposits with only some of the heirs.

Under case law, ordinary deposits are divided by statutory shares at the moment of inheritance and belong to each heir, but in practice banks often require the consent of all the heirs. If there is no agreement, you can ask the bank to pay your statutory share, or resolve it within division of the estate proceedings.

If you are considering renunciation or limited acceptance, it is better not to withdraw the deposits even through the proper procedure, because the moment you withdraw them, it may be seen as a disposal. If you have taken limited acceptance, the deposits withdrawn are property to be distributed to creditors, so keep them separate and do not use them personally.

sections.title: If a Sibling Has Already Withdrawn the Money
body: First, obtain the transaction records of the deceased's account from before and after the death as an heir, and check the dates, amounts and receiving accounts. For withdrawals after the death, you can claim back your share; for withdrawals before the death, the issues are whether your parent allowed it and what it was used for, and it is resolved as a gift or through a claim for return.

A criminal complaint must be filed within 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was, and filing one can make family relationships even harder. Decide carefully, weighing it against recovering the money through civil proceedings. Jisan Law reviews the case with you in line with how it unfolds, from analyzing the transaction records to a claim for return and, if needed, a criminal complaint. If the situation is urgent, send us a message through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: If I put money I withdrew before reporting the death back into the deceased's account, is that all right?
faqs.a: If you returned it without spending it, it is much less likely to be treated as a disposal, but the assessment may vary depending on the circumstances. Keep the withdrawal and deposit records and anything showing that you did not spend the money in between.

faqs.q: My father told me while he was alive that this money was for me.
faqs.a: A verbal promise alone is hard to assert against the other heirs. If you received a transfer during his lifetime, it can be treated as a gift, but money withdrawn after his death is part of the estate. Words that do not meet the formal requirements for a will have no effect as a will.

faqs.q: What should we do with refunds or insurance money paid into the deceased's account?
faqs.a: Money paid into the deceased's account becomes part of the estate. If you are considering renunciation, leave it there; if you plan to accept the inheritance, withdraw it through the inheritance procedure together with the other deposits. Insurance money where the heirs are named as beneficiaries is claimed directly by the beneficiaries, not paid through the account.

guides.title: When You Find a Handwritten Will at Home
guides.lead: A handwritten will must be kept exactly as it is, in its original form, and submitted to the family court with a request for a court inspection. If it is sealed in an envelope, the family must not open it.

seo.title: Found a Handwritten Will in Korea? Court Inspection Procedure and Precautions | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when you find a handwritten will among a parent's belongings. Covers preserving the original and opening a sealed will, the competent court and documents for a court inspection, the inspection hearing, registration and banking after inspection, and what to do, including the forced heirship share deadline, if the will's validity is in doubt.

sections.title: Keep the Original as It Is; Just Take Photos
body: When you find a will, first photograph the front and back, then put the original, still folded as it was, into an envelope and keep it safe. Tracing over faint writing, taping torn parts or adding notes can lead to claims of forgery or alteration.

If it is sealed in an envelope, do not open it. A sealed will is opened by the court in the presence of the heirs, their representatives or others (Civil Act (민법) Article 1092). If it has already been opened, write down how that happened and request a court inspection as it is.

Also keep any notes, notebooks or letters found in the same place as the will. They can serve as handwriting samples for comparison and as evidence of what the deceased was thinking around the time the will was written.

sections.title: Where to Request the Inspection and What to Submit
body: A person who keeps or finds a will must request a court inspection (검인) from the family court without delay after the testator's death. The competent court is the one for the place where the inheritance began, usually the family court with jurisdiction over the deceased's last address.

Submit the original will with the request, and attach the deceased's basic certificate (기본증명서), family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) and certificate of removed family register (제적등본), along with documents showing the addresses of all the heirs. The court must notify the heirs of the date, so it is important to give their addresses accurately.

When requesting the inspection, it helps to note briefly how you came to keep or find the will. Other heirs often ask 'why has this only turned up now?', so when, where and by whom it was found can become an important fact later.

sections.title: What Happens at the Inspection Hearing
body: At the inspection hearing, the court checks the paper, writing instrument, handwriting, date and seal of the will and prepares a written record. It may ask the heirs present whether the handwriting and seal are the testator's, and their answers are recorded. The inspection goes ahead even if heirs do not attend.

The court inspection is only a procedure for confirming and preserving the condition of the will; it is not a trial that decides whether the will is valid. An inspection does not make a will valid, and the lack of one does not make it void.

If there are many heirs, or some addresses are unknown, notices of the date may be delayed and the inspection can take longer. Even someone who receives property under the will reduces disputes by waiting for the inspection record before registering property or withdrawing deposits, rather than rushing ahead.

sections.title: What to Do After the Inspection
body: A person who receives real estate under the will applies for registration with a certified copy of the inspection record attached. However, if another heir disputed at the inspection hearing that 'this is not the deceased's handwriting', the registry office often requires written consent from the other heirs or the application is blocked, and the matter frequently ends up in a lawsuit to confirm the will's validity. Requirements for deposits also vary by bank, so check in advance.

Check the will's requirements again from the start. See whether the full text, the year, month and day, the address and the name were handwritten and a seal affixed; if any of these is missing, its validity may be disputed. An heir whose share is reduced by the will can claim a forced heirship share (유류분), and keep in mind that the 1-year deadline from the day they saw the will is already running.

If the will names an executor, that person handles registration and the transfer of deposits; if not, the heirs become the executors. If disputes among the heirs make execution difficult, you can ask the family court to appoint an executor.

sections.title: Check the Will's Requirements Yourself
body: While waiting for the inspection, checking the requirements below one by one using your photos will make it easier to decide what to do next.
bullets: Whether the entire text is handwritten (and whether any part is printed)
Whether the year, month and day are all written
Whether an address is written (and, even without the building and unit number, whether it can be identified as an address)
Whether the name was handwritten
Whether a seal or thumbprint was affixed
If anything was corrected, whether it was rewritten and sealed at that spot

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first checks the will's requirements and prepares the request for a court inspection and the attached documents. If registration is blocked after the inspection, or another heir disputes the will's validity, we continue with a lawsuit to confirm the will's validity or invalidity, and if a forced heirship share issue is involved, we also manage that deadline. If there are many heirs, or family members whose addresses you do not know, let us know at the consultation.

faqs.q: Do I have to attend the inspection hearing?
faqs.a: As a rule, the person who requested the inspection submits the original and attends the hearing. The inspection goes ahead even if other heirs do not attend, but if you have views on the handwriting or seal, attending and having them recorded will help if there is a dispute later.

faqs.q: We found two wills, and they say different things.
faqs.a: If both wills meet the formal requirements, the later will is treated as revoking the earlier one where they conflict (Civil Act Article 1109). The dates are important, so request a court inspection for both.

faqs.q: Does a notarized will also need a court inspection?
faqs.a: A notarized will is not subject to court inspection. You can obtain the authenticated copy or a certified copy from the notary office and use it right away for registration or banking.

guides.title: When a Sibling Cannot Be Reached or an Heir Is a Minor
guides.lead: An agreement on division of the estate requires all the heirs. If a sibling's whereabouts are unknown or an heir is a minor child, the court must first appoint someone to take part on their behalf.

seo.title: Missing or Minor Heirs and Division of an Estate in Korea | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: For when settling an inheritance in Korea is blocked because an heir is an unreachable sibling or a minor. Covers appointing an administrator of an absent person's property and court permission, how this differs from a declaration of disappearance, special representatives for minor children, registering statutory shares first, and representation issues in renunciation.

sections.title: When an Heir Cannot Be Reached
body: If the person has a registered address but is simply avoiding contact, you can demand their participation by certified mail with proof of contents (내용증명) or through service of court papers. If no agreement is ever reached, you can request an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할) naming that person as a respondent too, and if their address is unknown, the case may proceed by service by public notice.

If the person left home long ago and it is not even known whether they are alive, ask the family court to appoint an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인). The appointed administrator manages property on the absent person's behalf and, with the court's permission, takes part in the division agreement or protects the absent person's share in the adjudication. Note that administrators usually negotiate to secure the absent person's statutory share, so an agreement that reduces that share is hard to get approved.

The appointment is requested from the family court for the absent person's last address or the place where their property is. It helps to prepare the record of cancellation of their resident registration, the receipt for a missing person report, and statements from family members that there has been no contact for a long time.

sections.title: A Declaration of Disappearance Is a Different Procedure
body: If it has been unknown for 5 years or more whether the person is alive, you can apply for a declaration of disappearance (실종선고), and once it becomes final, the person is treated as having died at the end of that period. In that case, the missing person's own heirs take their place, which changes the inheritance relationships. Which procedure fits depends on how long the person has been missing and the circumstances.
A declaration of disappearance takes time because it involves a public notice procedure by the court, so if the division needs to happen soon, the administrator procedure is often pursued first.

sections.title: When an Heir Is a Minor
body: When a father dies and the mother and minor children become heirs together, the interests conflict if the mother negotiates the division on the children's behalf. In this case, a special representative (특별대리인) must be appointed by the family court for each child, and that person must sign the agreement (Civil Act (민법) Article 921). An agreement in which the parent represented the child without a special representative can be challenged.

Usually a relative with no stake in the inheritance is proposed as special representative, and the court checks that the agreement is not excessively unfavorable to the child. An agreement that gives the child nothing is hard to get approved, so decide from the start how the child's share will be preserved when drafting the proposal.

The same applies to renunciation. If the parent and child renounce together, there is usually no problem, but if the parent inherits and only the child renounces, a special representative may be needed.

If the child will soon become an adult, another option is to have them take part in the agreement themselves after reaching adulthood. However, you also need to consider whether the inheritance tax filing or plans to sell real estate can wait that long.

sections.title: What You Can Do While Waiting
body: Even if the agreement is delayed, one heir can register the inheritance in all the heirs' names according to their statutory shares. Inheritance tax must be filed within the deadline, so if the agreement is not finished, discuss with a tax accountant how to file in the current state and adjust after the division.

The longer it takes, the more likely it is that another heir dies and the number of parties grows. Appointing an administrator or special representative can take several months, so it is better to start early.

As a rule, deposits forming the missing heir's share should be left untouched until an administrator is appointed; if another heir withdraws and spends them, there may later be a claim for their return.

sections.title: When an Heir Lives Abroad
body: An heir living abroad is not missing, but preparing their documents takes time. If they are a Korean national, they can obtain a certificate of seal impression or a signature certificate at the local Korean consulate; if they have become a foreign national, local notarization and translation may be needed. When an heir has an address abroad, the schedule also changes, for example the inheritance tax filing deadline is extended to 9 months, so it is wise to decide from the start how the overseas heir's documents will be obtained.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law checks how long the person has been missing, their last address and the family relationships, and chooses the right route among an administrator of an absent person's property, service by public notice and a declaration of disappearance. If an heir is a minor, we prepare the petition to appoint a special representative together with the draft agreement. Because a series of procedures requiring court permission follow, we line up the documents in the right order for you.

faqs.q: How does a sibling living abroad sign the agreement?
faqs.a: A common approach is for a Korean national abroad to obtain a certificate of seal impression or a signature certificate at the local consulate, have the agreement notarized and send it. If they have changed nationality, a local notarization procedure may be needed, so check in advance.

faqs.q: Who can be a special representative?
faqs.a: The law does not set specific qualifications, but usually a relative with no stake in the inheritance is proposed. If the court finds that person unsuitable, it can appoint someone else.

faqs.q: How long does it take to appoint an administrator of an absent person's property?
faqs.a: It depends on the court and the case, but it often takes several months, and separate permission for the agreement must be obtained afterwards. If inheritance tax or a sale is on a schedule, count back from those dates and apply early.

guides.title: When a Family Member Who Never Kept in Touch Demands an Inheritance
guides.lead: If a parent who abandoned their child, or a spouse or child who turned away during a long illness, becomes an heir, you can ask for a declaration of loss of inheritance rights. Since the March 2026 amendment, this applies to all heirs.

seo.title: Declaration of Loss of Inheritance Rights in Korea (the 'Goo Hara Act'): Requirements and Deadline | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to seek a declaration of loss of inheritance rights in Korea when a parent or family member who had no contact for decades demands an inheritance. Covers who it now applies to after the 2026 amendment, what a serious breach of the duty of support means, the 6-month filing period, loss of rights by will, how it differs from disqualification of an heir, and the evidence needed.
keywords: petition loss of inheritance rights Korea
breach of duty of support inheritance Korea

sections.title: Disqualification and Loss of Inheritance Rights Are Different
body: A person who falls under Civil Act (민법) Article 1004, such as someone who tried to kill the deceased or forged or hid a will, automatically cannot be an heir, without any court ruling. These grounds are limited to those listed in the law, so abandoning a child's upbringing or cutting off contact does not by itself lead to disqualification (상속결격).

The declaration of loss of inheritance rights (상속권 상실 선고) was created to fill that gap. An heir who seriously breached the duty of support, or committed a serious crime against or grossly unjust treatment of the deceased, loses inheritance rights when the family court makes the declaration. It took effect on January 1, 2026, and since the amendment of March 17, 2026, it applies to all heirs, including children and spouses, not just parents.

sections.title: Who Files, and by When
body: If the deceased expressed the wish, in a notarized will made during their lifetime, that an heir should lose inheritance rights, the executor must file with the family court. In that case, serious crimes or unjust treatment against the deceased's spouse or lineal blood relatives are also grounds.

If there was no will, a co-heir can file within 6 months from the day they learned that the person became an heir. If there is no co-heir to file, or all of them have such grounds against them, the person who would become an heir once the declaration becomes final files. Six months is short and easily slips by in the busy period after a funeral.

The period is counted not from the date of death but from the day you learned that the person became an heir. Usually you learn this while checking the family relationships right after the death, so it is safest to treat the 6 months as running from around the date of death and act quickly.

sections.title: How Serious Must It Be?
body: The court decides whether to grant the petition by looking at all the circumstances, including how the grounds arose and how serious they were, the relationship between the heir and the deceased, and the size of the estate and how it was built up. A bad relationship or a few years without contact is not enough; you need concrete facts, such as leaving a minor child and never paying child support, or ignoring the deceased throughout a long illness and leaving all the care and costs to other family members.

Evidence includes divorce judgments and child support orders, records of unpaid child support, school and hospital records showing who was listed as guardian, records of contact and visits during the illness, and investigation or trial records of violence or abuse.

Even if the petition is not granted, gifts that person received during the deceased's lifetime, or support that other family members took on, can still be argued in the division of the estate as special benefits or contribution shares.

sections.title: What Happens Once the Declaration Is Made
body: If the declaration becomes final after the inheritance began, the person loses inheritance rights back to the time the inheritance began, and also loses the forced heirship share (유류분). However, rights acquired by third parties before it became final are not affected. The lineal descendants of the person who lost the rights inherit by representation (대습상속), but that person's spouse does not.

Once a petition is filed, the court can, at the request of an interested party, appoint an administrator of the estate or order measures needed to preserve the property. If there is a risk that the other side will withdraw deposits or dispose of real estate in the meantime, apply for this at the same time.

Money paid under specific laws or contracts rather than as part of the estate, such as the National Pension survivor pension or death insurance, may be handled separately from the loss of inheritance rights, so check the payment rules of each body separately.

sections.title: Materials to Organize Before Filing
body: Because the court weighs many circumstances together, materials organized in chronological order make the case far more persuasive.
bullets: Changes in family relationships shown in family relationship certificates and marriage certificates
Divorce judgments or agreements, child support orders and records of non-payment
School and hospital records showing who your guardian was in childhood
Hospital records from the period of illness and materials showing who provided the care and paid the costs
Messages or call records showing attempts at contact that went unanswered
Copies of any investigation or trial records concerning violence or abuse

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first confirms the day you learned that the other person became an heir to calculate the 6-month deadline, organizes the records of upbringing and support year by year, and prepares the petition. We also consider whether measures to preserve the estate are needed. If the deadline is close, contact us first through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: My parent died before January 2026. Can I still file?
faqs.a: The addenda provide that the amended provisions apply to inheritances that began on or after April 25, 2024. However, the special filing period for co-heirs who already knew of the grounds before the amendment (6 months from the effective date) ended in mid-September 2026. If you learned that the other person became an heir after that, you may be able to count 6 months from the day you learned, so start by confirming when you found out.

faqs.q: If a will says 'this child gets nothing', does that child lose inheritance rights?
faqs.a: That sentence alone does not take away inheritance rights, and the child can claim a forced heirship share. If you want an heir to lose inheritance rights, where statutory grounds exist, you must state that wish in a notarized will, and after the death the executor must petition the family court and obtain the declaration.

faqs.q: If I file for a declaration of loss of inheritance rights, will the other person be told?
faqs.a: It is a family litigation procedure, so the petition is served on the other side and they are given a chance to respond. If contact with them is a burden for you, Jisan Law handles the procedure as your representative.

guides.title: When Large Sums Left a Parent's Account Before Their Death
guides.lead: If a sibling who managed your parent's account withdrew large sums before the death, how to resolve it depends on whether the money was taken with your parent's consent and what it was used for.

seo.title: Withdrawals From a Parent's Account Before Death in Korea: Recovering Money From a Sibling | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: For when a sibling who managed a parent's account in Korea withdrew large sums while the parent was alive. Covers obtaining transaction records, how the parent's consent and the use of the money affect the outcome, the differences between special benefit, forced heirship share and unjust enrichment claims, financial inquiries during a lawsuit, and inheritance tax presumptions about withdrawn money.
keywords: order to submit financial transaction information

sections.title: First, Secure the Transaction Records
body: Heirs can obtain the transaction records of the deceased's accounts by submitting family relationship documents to the financial institution. After checking through the Safe Inheritance (안심상속) search which institutions held accounts, obtain the records for each account and set out the dates, amounts and recipients in a table. The period covered may differ by bank.

Cash withdrawals do not show who received the money. In that case, whether a similar amount was deposited into the sibling's account on the same day, or whether the sibling bought a home or car around that time, is confirmed after filing a lawsuit, through the court's orders to submit financial transaction information and fact-finding inquiries.

When making the table, use separate columns for the date, withdrawal method (counter, ATM or transfer), amount, recipient and your parent's condition at the time (for example, whether they were in hospital). This makes transactions your parent could hardly have made themselves, such as counter withdrawals while they were in hospital, stand out.

sections.title: Did Your Parent Allow It, and What Was It Used For?
body: Being entrusted with managing an account does not give a person the right to spend the money as they like. Nor does the mere fact of a withdrawal prove wrongdoing. Money spent for the parent, such as on hospital, care, nursing home or living costs, is usually not a problem, and who must prove this depends on how the dispute arises.

If your parent told the sibling to take the money, it is a gift. In that case, rather than getting it back, it is resolved by treating it as that sibling's special benefit (특별수익) and reducing their share in the division of the estate, or by including it in the forced heirship share (유류분) calculation.

If the sibling took the money without your parent's knowledge and spent it personally, the right your parent had to demand its return from that sibling passes to the heirs. Each heir then claims return of unjust enrichment or damages up to their own inheritance share.

sections.title: Choose the Claim Based on Time Limits and Proof
body: The method of claim and the deadline differ depending on whether the money is treated as a gift or as an unauthorized withdrawal. A forced heirship share claim has a short limit of 1 year from the day you learned of the gift, while a special benefit argument is resolved within the adjudication on division of the estate. Unjust enrichment and damages claims are subject to the general civil limitation periods.

In practice, if the sibling says 'our parent gave me the money', we pursue special benefit and forced heirship share arguments on the basis that it was a gift; if they say 'I used it for our parent's hospital bills', we demand proof of how it was used and consider a claim for return as well.

The more money the other side cannot account for, the more realistic a claim for return becomes; the more signs there are that your parent gave it directly, the more realistic a special benefit or forced heirship share argument often is.

sections.title: Be Ready for Questions From the Tax Office Too
body: If, for each type of property, KRW 200 million or more was withdrawn within 1 year before the inheritance began, or KRW 500 million or more within 2 years, and its use is unclear, it is added to the taxable value for inheritance tax (Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (상속세 및 증여세법) Article 15). This means money a sibling spent can become an inheritance tax burden for the other siblings, so records of how it was used serve both the dispute and the tax matter.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Secretly looking through your sibling's phone or bankbook
Declaring them an embezzler in the family group chat
Closing your parent's accounts or moving the remaining money first
Inflating unconfirmed amounts in a lawsuit or criminal complaint

sections.title: If You Are Considering a Criminal Complaint
body: Both taking a parent's money without permission while they were alive and taking the heirs' money after the death can amount to embezzlement or fraud. For offenses on or after June 27, 2024, prosecution is possible on a complaint even within the family, but the complaint must be filed within 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was. Complaints are filed with the police, and from October 2026, after the police investigation, a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) decides whether to indict.

Criminal proceedings do not get your money back, so civil claims must be pursued alongside. Decide on the timing after also weighing the effect a complaint will have on family relationships and the chance of a settlement.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law splits the transaction records into before and after the death, separates money whose use is confirmed from money that needs explaining, and chooses among special benefit, forced heirship share and return claims the method that fits the deadlines and burden of proof. In a lawsuit, we trace the flow of money through applications for financial inquiries. Where there is also a criminal issue, such as unauthorized withdrawals after the death, we consider whether to file a complaint, and if you decide to, we draft it and attend the complainant's questioning with you.

faqs.q: My brother says he used it for our parent's hospital bills but has no receipts.
faqs.a: The actual costs can be worked out from your parent's hospital admission records, payment records at the hospital and nursing home records. If the withdrawals are much larger than that, ask for an explanation of the difference, and in a lawsuit, argue that he must show how it was used.

faqs.q: Can I challenge money taken out 10 years ago?
faqs.a: Treating it as a gift and including it in the special benefit calculation or the forced heirship share calculation against a co-heir may be possible even if it was long ago. However, a claim for return of an unauthorized withdrawal may be time-barred, so choose the type of claim carefully.

faqs.q: My brother says he has a power of attorney from our parent to manage the account.
faqs.a: A power of attorney usually only means that management was entrusted to him; it often does not show an intention to give him the money to spend freely. Money used personally beyond the scope of the authority can be subject to return, and the authority ends when the parent dies, so withdrawals after the death cannot be explained by the power of attorney.

guides.title: What to Do After Your Limited Acceptance Is Accepted
guides.lead: Limited acceptance does not end with receiving the written decision. You protect your own property only by following the steps in order: public notice, notice to creditors and proportional payment.

seo.title: After Limited Acceptance of an Inheritance in Korea: Newspaper Notice, Notice to Creditors and Proportional Payment | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: The settlement procedure to follow in Korea after the court accepts a limited acceptance of inheritance. Covers the newspaper notice within 5 days and the 2-month reporting period, notice to known creditors, refusing payment and liability for improper payment, real estate auctions, the order of distribution, and raising the limited acceptance defense in later creditor lawsuits.

sections.title: Publish a Notice Within 5 Days
body: A person who has taken limited acceptance (한정승인) must, within 5 days from the day of the limited acceptance, publish a notice to general creditors and recipients of bequests stating that they have taken limited acceptance and asking them to report their claims or bequests within a set period. The reporting period must be at least 2 months (Civil Act (민법) Article 1032). In practice, the notice is published in a daily newspaper.

The starting point is generally taken to be the day you were notified of the decision accepting the limited acceptance, but it is safest to prepare the notice as soon as you receive the written decision. The notice states the deceased's name and last address, the fact of limited acceptance, the reporting period and where to report.
Costs of the settlement, such as notice and auction costs, can be paid from the estate. Keep receipts for these costs and include them when preparing the distribution table.
The notice must also state that anyone who does not report within the period may be excluded from the settlement (Civil Act Article 1032(2) and Article 88(2)).

sections.title: Notify Known Creditors Individually
body: Send each creditor you know of from the search results or collection notices an individual demand to report their claim. Sending it by certified mail with proof of contents (내용증명) leaves a record of when you notified them. Known creditors must not be left out of the distribution even if they do not report.

The notice states the deceased's name and date of death, the case number and acceptance date of the limited acceptance decision, the reporting period and where to report. Keep all replies and claim reports from creditors, as they form the basis for the distribution table.

sections.title: Do Not Pay Anyone First During the Reporting Period
body: Until the reporting period ends, you can refuse payment no matter which creditor presses you (Civil Act Article 1033). If you pay only the creditor who contacted you first, the other creditors' shares shrink, and the person who took limited acceptance may have to compensate them for that loss (Article 1038).

Leave any remaining deposits untouched rather than using them personally. If, after limited acceptance, you hide estate property, use it wrongfully or deliberately leave it off the list, it is treated as simple acceptance (단순승인) and you may end up liable for all the debts.

sections.title: Convert the Assets to Money and Pay in Proportion
body: Property that must be sold, such as real estate, is disposed of by auction under the Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) (Civil Act Article 1037). If a mortgage holder has already applied for an auction, distribution takes place in that procedure. Tax issues can arise during the auction, so check in advance.

When the reporting period ends, you pay the creditors who reported and the creditors you know of in proportion to their claims. Creditors with priority, such as mortgage holders, are paid first, and recipients of bequests receive anything only after all creditors have been paid. When the property runs out, the heir has no obligation to pay the remaining debts from their own property. If there are many creditors and the estate is complicated, estate bankruptcy is sometimes considered.

From the auction proceeds, auction costs and priority claims are deducted first, and the rest is divided among general creditors in proportion to their claims. Preparing a distribution table setting out the basis of the calculation and sending it to the creditors reduces disputes later.

sections.title: If There Are Many Creditors or the Estate Is Complicated
body: If there are many creditors and the estate includes several kinds of assets, such as real estate, shares and money owed to the deceased, it is not easy for the person who took limited acceptance to draw up the distribution table and run the auction alone. In such cases, another option is to apply for estate bankruptcy so that a trustee appointed by the court handles the settlement. Which is better depends on the size of the estate, the number of creditors and how much time the heir can give.

If the heir personally was owed money by the deceased, that right does not disappear with limited acceptance (Civil Act Article 1031), so the heir can request distribution in the same order as other creditors.

sections.title: If a Lawsuit Comes Later, Assert Your Limited Acceptance
body: Even after the settlement is finished, creditors can still sue the heirs. If you assert your limited acceptance at that point, the court will order payment only 'up to the value of the estate', and the creditor cannot enforce against the heir's personal property. If you fail to raise this and an ordinary judgment becomes final, it is very hard to challenge later.

Jisan Law handles everything after acceptance in sequence: drafting the public notice, notifying creditors, preparing the distribution table, dealing with the auction, and raising the limited acceptance defense in any lawsuits that follow. If the notice deadline is tight, contact us on the same day you receive the written decision.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not publish the notice?
faqs.a: If you neglect the notice or individual demands and pay only some creditors so that others cannot be paid, you may have to compensate them. The limited acceptance itself does not immediately lose its effect, but following the procedure helps you avoid unnecessary liability.

faqs.q: Do I have to publish a notice even if there is almost nothing in the estate?
faqs.a: The law requires the notice regardless of the size of the estate. If there is almost nothing, record that after the notice and the reporting period there was nothing to distribute, and if a lawsuit comes later, finish by raising the limited acceptance defense.

faqs.q: After limited acceptance, I found assets I did not know about.
faqs.a: If assets missing from the list turn up, apply to the court to correct the list and include those assets in the settlement. What matters is that you did not leave them out on purpose, so keep a record of how you found them.

guides.title: When a Sibling Claims a Contribution Share for Caring for Your Parents
guides.lead: When a sibling who lived with and cared for your parents says they should receive more, calmly start by examining what actually counts as a contribution share. Having lived together does not by itself increase a share.

seo.title: A Sibling's Contribution Share Claim in Korea: Should You Accept It as It Is? | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to check in Korea when a sibling who cared for your parents demands a contribution share. Covers the standard for special support, cases where the sibling lived off the parents' property, the procedure and deadline for claiming a contribution share, contribution shares in forced heirship share lawsuits, and the 2026 amendment.
keywords: caring for parents contribution share Korea

sections.title: What to Check First
body: Just because a contribution share has been raised does not mean you must start negotiating percentages. First get in writing what the other side is basing the claim on and how much they are asking for, then match the supporting materials and the opposing circumstances point by point.

If an adjudication on division of the estate is already under way, the court may set a period for contribution share claims, and you must submit your opposing materials within it. If you have received a petition or a certified letter, first check the claims and deadlines stated in it.
bullets: Get the support period and method the other side describes, and the share they are asking for, in a text or in writing
List the money that went from your parents' account to that sibling and the period they lived rent-free in your parents' home
Check receipts and transfer records to see who actually paid hospital and care costs
Gather records of living costs paid and hospital visits made by the other siblings

sections.title: Living Together and Providing Care Are Not Enough on Their Own
body: A contribution share (기여분) is recognized where a person specially supported the parent, for example by living with or nursing them for a considerable period, or specially contributed to maintaining or increasing their property (Civil Act (민법) Article 1008-2). Support at the level normally expected of a child does not count.

If the sibling saved on housing by living in the parents' home, or covered living costs from the parents' pension and savings, the weight of their support is reduced accordingly. Whether care was provided through long-term care insurance or a paid caregiver is also considered.

Conversely, if the other side cared for the parent alone for a long time and paid hospital bills with their own money, you also need to assess realistically that the claim may be recognized. In such cases, rather than disputing everything, it is often more realistic to agree on terms that partly accept the contribution share while counting the lifetime gifts the other side received as special benefits (특별수익), so that the overall shares balance out.

sections.title: Where and When a Contribution Share Is Decided
body: A contribution share is set by agreement among the heirs, or by the family court if they cannot agree.
