To claim a contribution share from the family court, there must be a request for division of the estate (paragraph 4 of the same Article), and a contribution share claim filed after the period set by the court may be dismissed (Family Litigation Rules (가사소송규칙) Article 113).

The situation is different in a forced heirship share lawsuit. The Supreme Court has held that a contribution share not set by agreement or adjudication cannot be raised in a lawsuit to recover a forced heirship share (Supreme Court Decision 2013다60753 of October 29, 2015). However, under the amendment of March 17, 2026, gifts received as compensation for special support or contribution are not treated as special benefits to that extent, and this rule also applies to the forced heirship share (유류분), so the other side may argue that the gifts they received were compensation.

sections.title: Points to Watch When Negotiating
body: Even if you accept a contribution share to some degree, settle the basis before the amount, so you do not have to fight again if other assets turn up later. State clearly in the agreement that the contribution share has been reflected and which assets it covers.

This is an issue where remarks like 'so the one who cared for them loses out?' come up easily. Separating acknowledgment of the other side's efforts from legally increasing their share makes it much easier to keep the negotiation going.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law checks the support period and costs the other side relies on against bank records and medical and care records, and examines whether they amount to special support. If agreement is difficult, we prepare a rebuttal to the contribution share claim together with special benefit arguments in the adjudication on division of the estate. Consultations are conducted by our managing partner personally, and if you face an urgent deadline, let us know first through the chat on this page.

faqs.q: My brother managed our parents' bank accounts and even their taxes. Is that a contribution share too?
faqs.a: Handling accounts or paying taxes alone is hard to treat as a special contribution. It must also be shown that this management actually maintained or increased the property and that he received nothing in return. The withdrawal records from the period he managed the accounts can instead become material he has to explain.

faqs.q: If the other side's contribution share is recognized and my share falls below my forced heirship share, what happens?
faqs.a: Case law holds that even if a contribution share causes a shortfall in your forced heirship share, you cannot claim a return against the contribution share (Supreme Court Decision 2013다60753 of October 29, 2015). That is why it is important to fully dispute the contribution share at the division adjudication stage.

guides.title: When a Remarried Parent Dies
guides.lead: When a stepmother or stepfather and half-siblings become heirs together, it is easy to get confused about who the heirs are and who can inherit from whom. Marriage registration and adoption are what decide the rights.

seo.title: Inheritance in Blended Families in Korea: Dividing an Estate With a Stepmother and Half-Siblings | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to settle an inheritance in Korea with a stepmother and half-siblings after a remarried father or mother dies. Covers inheritance rights depending on legal versus de facto marriage and adoption, issues when the stepmother later dies, and minor half-siblings and special representatives.

sections.title: What to Check First
body: Documents come before emotions. Obtaining the marriage certificate, detailed family relationship certificate (가족관계증명서) and adoption certificate based on the deceased will settle most questions about who the heirs are.
bullets: Whether the marriage to the stepmother (or stepfather) was registered and still in place at the time of death
Whether the children from the earlier marriage were adopted by the stepmother, and if so, whether by full adoption or ordinary adoption
Whether there are half-siblings born after the remarriage, and whether they are minors
Whether any property went to the stepmother or a particular child before the death

sections.title: Who Are the Heirs?
body: A stepmother whose marriage was registered is a legal spouse and becomes an heir together with the children. A de facto spouse who lived with the deceased without registering the marriage is not an heir. Half-siblings are also the father's children, so they receive the same share as the other children. If the father had no children and his parents are no longer alive, the stepmother becomes the sole heir.

Unless there was an adoption, there is no legal parent-child relationship between a stepmother and the children of the earlier marriage, however long they lived together. So they inherit from the father together, but when the stepmother later dies, the children of the earlier marriage do not become her heirs.

sections.title: Look at the Two Inheritances Together
body: Property the stepmother received from the father's estate passes to her own children or siblings when she dies. An agreement putting the father's house solely in the stepmother's name may mean that the house never comes back to the children of the earlier marriage.

If the father transferred property to the stepmother or half-siblings during his lifetime, special benefits (특별수익) and the forced heirship share (유류분) must be examined. The stepmother may also claim a contribution share (기여분) for long-term care, and the test is whether it went beyond the support normally given by a spouse. From March 17, 2026, a petition for loss of inheritance rights can also be brought against a spouse who seriously abandoned the duty of support (Civil Act (민법) Article 1004-2).

How to set the stepmother's share must be settled at the stage of the father's inheritance, because after the stepmother dies, children from the earlier marriage who were not adopted have almost no way to contest that property.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Stamping an agreement the other side brings right after the funeral without examining its contents
Using your father's bankbook or card without the other heirs' consent
Negotiating only with the stepmother, as the parent with parental authority over a minor half-sibling, and signing an agreement without a special representative
Posting criticism of the other side in group chats or on social media while emotions are running high

sections.title: If There Is a Minor Half-Sibling
body: If the stepmother and her minor child are heirs together, the stepmother negotiating the division on the child's behalf is an act where their interests conflict. A special representative (특별대리인) must be appointed for the child by the family court for the agreement to be valid (Civil Act Article 921).

If no agreement is reached, apply to the family court for mediation on division of the estate (상속재산분할) against all the other heirs. Where the parties find it hard to deal with each other, going through the court from the start can also reduce the emotional toll.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first confirms the heirs and their shares from the family relationship documents, and calculates with you what a division proposal with the stepmother's side would mean, all the way through to the second inheritance. If lifetime gifts or contribution shares are claimed, we check them against the records and respond, and if agreement is difficult, we pursue mediation and adjudication.

faqs.q: My stepmother says she will keep living in my father's house. Can we make her leave?
faqs.a: The stepmother is also a co-heir and has the right to use the house to the extent of her share, so it is hard to make her leave right away. Decide who gets the house in a division agreement or adjudication, and until then consider settling a usage fee for use beyond her share.

faqs.q: I was adopted by my stepfather. Can I still inherit from my biological father?
faqs.a: With an ordinary adoption, your family relationships from before the adoption remain, so you are also your biological father's heir (Civil Act Article 882-2). With a full adoption (친양자 입양), your family relationship with your biological father's side ends, so you are not his heir (Article 908-3). Check which type of adoption it was on the adoption certificate.

guides.title: When You Suspect a Will Has Been Forged
guides.lead: If the handwriting is not your parent's, or your parent was in no condition to write on the date shown, you need to respond in order, from the court inspection to a lawsuit to invalidate the will and a criminal complaint. A court inspection does not make a will valid.

seo.title: Suspected Forged Will in Korea: Handwriting Analysis and Lawsuits to Invalidate a Will | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to do in Korea when you suspect a handwritten will has been forged. A step-by-step guide covering stating your views at the court inspection, gathering handwriting samples for comparison, provisional injunctions prohibiting disposal, lawsuits to confirm a will is invalid, disqualification of an heir who forged a will, and criminal complaints for forgery of a private document.

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: The authenticity of a will is argued using the original and samples for comparison. If the other side has the original, secure at least a copy, and quickly gather materials containing handwriting your parent wrote during their lifetime.
bullets: Secure a copy or photo of the will and note how it was found (by whom, when and where)
Gather handwritten materials your parent wrote around the same time (letters, notebooks, contracts, handwritten entries on bank forms)
Request medical and hospital records from around the date written on the will
When a notice of the inspection date arrives, prepare to attend and have your views recorded

sections.title: A Court Inspection Does Not Decide Validity
body: The family court's inspection (검인) only confirms and preserves the condition of the will; it does not decide whether the will is valid. If you attend the inspection hearing and state that the handwriting is not the deceased's, this is recorded and can be referred to later in a lawsuit.

The other side may try to register property or withdraw deposits using the inspected will. If you intend to challenge its validity, apply for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal of the real estate so the property does not pass to someone else in the meantime. If you could not attend the inspection hearing, you can request a certified copy of the inspection record to check the will's condition at that time and the statements of those present.

sections.title: Handwriting Analysis and a Lawsuit to Confirm the Will Is Invalid
body: The way to challenge a forgery is a lawsuit to confirm that the will is invalid. In the lawsuit, an examiner appointed by the court compares the handwriting on the will with the deceased's handwriting from their lifetime, and the more samples there are and the closer they are in time, the more reliable the result. Materials clearly written by the deceased personally, such as bank application forms or contracts, carry weight, while notes a family member wrote for them only cause confusion.

A handwritten will requires the entire text, the year, month and day, the address and the name to be handwritten and sealed (Civil Act (민법) Article 1066). Along with the handwriting dispute, it is common also to argue that one of these formal requirements is missing or that the person lacked mental capacity at the time. If the will is held invalid, the estate is divided based on the statutory shares.

sections.title: A Person Who Forged a Will Loses the Right to Be an Heir
body: A person who forged, altered, destroyed or hid a will concerning inheritance is disqualified (상속결격) and cannot be an heir (Civil Act Article 1004, item 5). The disqualified person's children can inherit by representation, but from March 17, 2026, the disqualified person's spouse cannot.

Criminally, you can file a complaint for forgery of a private document and use of a forged private document (Criminal Act (형법) Articles 231 and 234), and there is no family exception for these crimes. While waiting for the criminal outcome, make sure the deadlines for civil claims, such as a forced heirship share claim, do not pass.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Taking or damaging the original will (destroying or hiding a will is itself a ground for disqualification)
Sending the other side messages declaring them a forger
Throwing away or clearing out handwritten materials your parent left, such as notebooks or letters
Waiting only for the handwriting analysis result and letting other claim deadlines pass

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law first reviews the copy of the will and the comparison samples to separate handwriting issues from formal issues, and then handles everything in one flow: stating your views at the inspection hearing, the provisional injunction, the lawsuit to confirm the will is invalid, the disqualification argument and whether to file a criminal complaint. Consultations are conducted by our managing partner personally.

faqs.q: Can I commission a handwriting analysis privately?
faqs.a: You can get a private analysis before a lawsuit to gauge the direction, but in court, the analysis by the examiner the court appoints is what counts most. A private report is often only supporting material, so gathering good comparison samples matters more.

faqs.q: What if the forced heirship share deadline passes while I am suing to invalidate the will?
faqs.a: A common approach is to file a forced heirship share (유류분) claim as well, in case the will is found valid. By mainly arguing that the will is invalid while making a forced heirship share claim in the alternative, you avoid missing the 1-year deadline from the day you learned of the gift or bequest.

guides.title: When You First See a Division Agreement Bearing Your Seal
guides.lead: If registration was transferred or deposits were withdrawn using an agreement on division of the estate that you never agreed to, that agreement was not made by all the heirs, so its validity can be challenged. Secure the documents before the evidence scatters.

seo.title: Forged Estate Division Agreement or Misused Registered Seal in Korea: What to Do | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to respond in Korea when your registered seal was stamped on an estate division agreement you did not agree to and property was registered or money withdrawn. Covers checking the issuance history of your certificate of seal impression, checking the registration application documents, provisional injunctions prohibiting disposal, cancelling the registration and requesting a new division, and criminal complaints for forgery.

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: First, find out when and how your registered seal was used. The division agreement and certificate of seal impression submitted to the registry office or bank are the most important evidence.
bullets: Obtain the registry record and check the date of the inheritance registration, the cause of registration and who received the property
Check the issuance history of your certificate of seal impression (인감증명서) at the community service center (주민센터, your local district office), and report a change of seal if needed
Ask the registry office whether you can inspect or get copies of the registration application documents
Write down whether you ever entrusted your registered seal or certificate to anyone, and what they said it would be used for

sections.title: An Agreement Is Valid Only If All the Heirs Make It
body: An agreement on division of the estate (상속재산분할) requires every heir to take part, and if even one did not genuinely consent, the agreement has no effect. A registration made using that agreement has no valid cause, at least to the extent of your share, and you can claim its cancellation or a transfer of your share.

If you entrusted your seal after being told it was for another purpose and it was then used on the agreement, the matter is a little more complicated. What you entrusted and how far you authorized its use become the issues, so find the text messages or call records from that time.

If, after learning of the agreement, you say you will leave it as it is, or receive a settlement payment under it, it may become hard to argue later that it is invalid. Once you discover the problem, make it clear in writing, for example by certified mail with proof of contents (내용증명), that you do not consent.

sections.title: Before More Property Changes Hands
body: If the other side sells or mortgages the real estate they received, a third party becomes involved and recovery becomes difficult. It is usual to apply for a provisional injunction prohibiting disposal of the real estate before filing a lawsuit.

If deposits were withdrawn, check the division agreement submitted to the bank and the payment records. Then, on the basis that the agreement is invalid, request a new division of the estate or claim back the money corresponding to your share.

If the other side has already sold the house to a third party, recovering it takes longer and involves more parties. Depending on the situation, claiming the money for your share from the other side, rather than reversing the registration, may be more realistic.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Going to the other side's home and fighting to make them hand over documents
Posting in the family group chat that it was forged before you have checked
Continuing to leave your registered seal and certificate of seal impression with someone else

sections.title: How a Criminal Complaint Works
body: Making a division agreement with someone else's registered seal amounts to forgery and use of a private document and misuse of a seal, and using that document for registration also raises false entry in an authenticated original document and its use. The family exception does not apply to these document crimes, so an investigation proceeds even against a sibling.

The complaint is filed with the police, and from October 2, 2026, after the police investigation, a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) decides whether to indict. Separately from the criminal case, the registration and the money must be recovered through civil proceedings, so decide the order of the two together.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law checks the registry record, the seal certificate issuance history and the registration application documents to determine first whether it was a forgery or a use beyond what you entrusted. We pursue the provisional injunction and cancellation of the registration or an adjudication on division of the estate, and if a complaint is needed, we prepare and submit the complaint and evidence and attend the complainant's questioning with you. If the other side shows signs of disposing of the property, let us know first through our 24-hour line.

faqs.q: This happened several years ago. Can I still challenge it?
faqs.a: If the agreement is invalid, a claim to cancel the registration can often be made even after a long time. However, it may be disputed whether the time limits for a claim to recover an inheritance (3 years from learning of the infringement, 10 years from the infringing act) apply on the basis that the other side infringed your inheritance rights, so start by examining the dates.

faqs.q: I was the one who entrusted my seal to my brother. Can it still be forgery?
faqs.a: If it was used beyond the purpose for which you entrusted it, it can be forgery or misuse of a seal. However, the other side will argue that you allowed it to be used on the agreement, so the key points are what was said when you entrusted it and whether you knew the content of the agreement afterwards.

guides.title: When a Sibling Is Managing the Assets of a Parent With Dementia
guides.lead: While your parent is alive, the other children do not own that property, so it is hard to demand its return directly. The legal tool for protecting a parent's property is guardianship through the family court, and the records you keep now will carry through to any inheritance dispute later.

seo.title: When a Sibling Manages a Parent's Assets During Dementia in Korea: What You Can Do | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to respond in Korea when one sibling manages the bank accounts and home of a parent with dementia and money keeps disappearing. Covers recording the parent's condition, applying for adult or limited guardianship, interim measures, claiming money back after a guardian is appointed, and organizing records with the future inheritance in mind.

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: The most important thing is to record your parent's condition and the flow of money now. Medical records can be obtained later, but materials explaining the situation at the time disappear over time.
bullets: Secure your parent's dementia diagnosis, cognitive test results and long-term care grade documents
Obtain the registry records for real estate in your parent's name and list the accounts you know of
Note by date when and how your sibling started managing things, and any signs of large sums going out
If there is talk of selling the house or taking out a loan, find out when and with whom

sections.title: There Is Not Much a Child Can Do Directly
body: Your parent owns their property, so while they are alive, the other children have, as a rule, no right to sue a sibling for its return. It is also hard to obtain your parent's account records unless you are the account holder or their legal representative. Still, you can start by asking your sibling to show you hospital and care cost receipts regularly. Keeping that request and the reply in text messages becomes evidence later that the management was not transparent.

If your parent cannot make decisions on their own, the starting point is to apply to the family court for guardianship. Any relative within the fourth degree can apply, and after applying, if the matter is urgent, you can also apply for an interim measure (사전처분) to block disposal of the property (Family Litigation Act (가사소송법) Article 62).

sections.title: What Changes Once a Guardian Is Appointed
body: The court chooses the guardian on its own authority, and if the siblings are in serious conflict, it may choose someone outside the family. The guardian prepares a list of the parent's property within 2 months and is supervised by the court, and needs court permission to dispose of the home the parent lives in.

On the parent's behalf, the guardian can ask how money a sibling took was used and claim its return. At the request of relatives or others, the family court can also investigate the parent's financial situation and order the guardian to take necessary measures (Civil Act (민법) Article 954). If a sibling has already become guardian and problems appear, you can request such an investigation and also ask for a guardianship supervisor to be appointed or for the guardian to be changed (Article 940).

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Taking your parent's bankbook or registered seal without your sibling knowing
Having your parent sign particular documents or write a will
Posting in the family group chat that your sibling is an embezzler
Arguing about money in front of your parent

sections.title: If You Are Thinking Ahead to the Inheritance
body: The list of assets and transaction records organized during the guardianship are used directly after your parent's death in disputes over special benefits, the forced heirship share and the scope of the estate. Gifts or wills made in your parent's name during this period can be challenged on the basis of mental capacity, so keep obtaining medical records. If your parent's judgment still remains, voluntary guardianship (임의후견), in which your parent makes a guardianship contract by notarial deed with someone they trust, is also worth considering.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law looks at your parent's condition and assets, decides whether to apply for adult (성년후견), limited or specific guardianship, and explains to the court the proposed guardian and supervision arrangements. After guardianship begins, we continue with claims for return and applications for permission to dispose of property, and consultations are conducted by our managing partner personally.

faqs.q: If we apply for guardianship, will our parent have to go to court?
faqs.a: As a rule, the court must hear from the person, except where they are unconscious or cannot express their wishes. If they have difficulty getting around, the court may confirm their condition in another way. A psychiatric evaluation is also required as a rule, but it can be skipped if there is other sufficient evidence.

faqs.q: My brother has already sold our parent's house. Can it be undone?
faqs.a: If your parent lacked mental capacity at the time of the sale, the contract is void, and the guardian can assert that it is void. If the buyer has already had the registration transferred, the dispute will be long, so first check the medical records from the time of the sale.

guides.title: When Your Parents Want to Give One Child a House in Advance
guides.lead: Parents can make lifetime gifts as they wish, but after their death those gifts come back into the calculation of the other children's forced heirship shares and inheritance shares. Putting things in order before the gift can greatly reduce disputes later.

seo.title: What to Check Before a Lifetime Gift in Korea: Forced Heirship Share and Filial Support Contracts | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: What to check in Korea when parents want to give one child a house or a large sum in advance. Covers the forced heirship share and special benefits, gifts in return for contribution under the 2026 amendment, wording for filial support contracts, how this differs from a will or a will substitute trust, and recording the parent's mental capacity at the time of the gift.
keywords: lifetime gift forced heirship share Korea
gift in return for contribution Korea
planning for forced heirship share Korea

sections.title: What to Check First
body: A gift is not only a tax matter. The key is to think through in advance what the other children could later dispute, and to have the documents in place.
bullets: What share of the parents' total property the gift represents
Whether enough property will remain for the other children and the spouse to cover their forced heirship shares
Whether there are records showing the reason for the gift (care, contribution to a business, living support and so on)
How the parents' living costs and housing will be handled after the gift

sections.title: Lifetime Gifts Are Recalculated at Inheritance
body: A gift to a child is counted after the death as a share received in advance (special benefit, 특별수익) in the division of the estate, and if another child's forced heirship share (유류분) falls short, it becomes subject to a claim for return. The forced heirship share is one half of the statutory share for children and spouses and one third for parents; siblings have none. Registry records and account records remain, so even hidden gifts often come to light later during a lawsuit through fact-finding inquiries or orders to submit financial transaction information.

For inheritances that began on or after March 17, 2026, the forced heirship share must, as a rule, be returned in money (Civil Act (민법) Article 1115). This means the child who received the house may keep it but have to raise cash, so this burden should be considered at the gift stage.

sections.title: What to Discuss With the Other Children in Advance
body: Telling the other children about the gift and the reasons in advance, and keeping a record of the views expressed, reduces emotional disputes later about something being received behind their backs.

However, under case law, a written statement by another child waiving their forced heirship share before the inheritance begins has no effect. Rather than expecting such a statement to prevent disputes, it actually helps more to set out what property remains and the reasons for the gift.

sections.title: If It Is Compensation for Contribution, Keep Records
body: Under the amendment of March 17, 2026, a gift made as compensation for specially supporting the parent, for example by living with and nursing them for a considerable period, or for specially contributing to increasing their property, is not treated as a special benefit to that extent (Civil Act Article 1008, proviso). This rule also applies to the forced heirship share.

For this to apply, it must be clear what the gift compensates. Writing the period and nature of the support in the gift contract, and keeping care records or records of hospital costs paid, provides a basis if other children dispute it later.

sections.title: If You Attach Conditions, Be Specific
body: A filial support contract (효도계약, a gift with a burden) that attaches conditions such as living with the parent or paying hospital bills provides grounds to cancel the gift and get it back if the child does not keep the conditions. Write it so compliance can be judged, for example the number of calls and visits or the amount of living money, and having it notarized reduces disputes over how it was made.

If the parent is in the early stages of dementia, their mental capacity at the time of the gift may be disputed later, so obtaining a medical certificate just before the gift helps. Another difference is that using a will or a will substitute trust instead of a gift lets the parent keep managing the property while they are alive.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law calculates in advance, from the family structure and size of the property, the forced heirship shares and special benefits that will remain after the gift, and prepares the wording of a filial support contract and the supporting records for a gift in return for contribution. Taxes are reviewed together with a tax accountant who cooperates with Jisan Law.

faqs.q: If the house is given away, how can the parents keep living there?
faqs.a: You can include in the gift contract an agreement that the parents may live there for as long as they live, or set up a right such as a jeonse right (전세권, a registered lease right). Once ownership passes, the parents' housing could be at risk if the child sells or mortgages the house, so settle this before the gift.

faqs.q: Can the gift be cancelled if the parents change their minds afterwards?
faqs.a: A gift made only verbally, without anything in writing, can be rescinded before it is carried out, but once a contract has been signed and the registration transferred, it is in principle hard to reverse. With a filial support contract that sets out obligations, the gift can be cancelled if the child fails to meet them, so it is safer to put the conditions in the contract from the start.

guides.title: When You Live Abroad and Need to Settle an Inheritance in Korea
guides.lead: If your parent died in Korea while you live abroad, the deadlines run by Korean rules while the documents have to be prepared abroad. Once you decide which documents to have authenticated and where, most of the process can be handled without coming to Korea.

seo.title: Settling a Korean Inheritance While Living Abroad: Documents, Powers of Attorney and Deadlines | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How heirs living abroad can handle an inheritance in Korea. Covers the 3-month deadline for renunciation, authentication at Korean diplomatic missions and apostilles, appointing a representative in Korea, the real estate acquisition report for foreign nationals, and the 9-month tax filing deadline.
keywords: inheritance power of attorney consulate Korea
foreigner inherit real estate report Korea

sections.title: What to Do Right Now
body: First, get information on the heirs and the state of the estate from family in Korea, and work out what you will need to sign. In many countries, booking an appointment with the authenticating authority takes time.
bullets: Write down the date your parent died and the day you heard the news
Check whether you still hold Korean nationality, and find your passport and any record of loss of Korean nationality
Check the authentication services and how to book an appointment at the nearest Korean embassy or consulate
Decide which family member or representative will submit documents on your behalf in Korea

sections.title: The Deadlines Are the Same Even If You Are Abroad
body: Renunciation (상속포기) and limited acceptance (한정승인) must be filed within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began, and living abroad does not extend this period. If your documents may be delayed, you can ask the family court to extend the period before the 3 months run out. If you became an heir later because heirs ahead of you renounced, the 3 months run from the day you learned of that.

For acquisition tax and inheritance tax, if an heir has an address abroad, the filing deadline is extended to 9 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began (Local Tax Act (지방세법) Article 20; Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act (상속세 및 증여세법) Article 67). Tax filings are handled on a schedule coordinated with a tax accountant who cooperates with Jisan Law.

sections.title: Documents Depend on Your Nationality
body: Korean nationals living abroad usually have their signature on the division agreement or power of attorney authenticated at a Korean embassy or consulate in their country of residence, in place of a certificate of seal impression (인감증명서). Choose either to sign the agreement yourself or to give a family member in Korea the authority to negotiate, and the power of attorney must state the property and powers specifically. Courts, registry offices and banks each require different forms and content, and trying to use one document for everything often means getting authenticated again, so first make a list of where documents will be submitted and then have them all authenticated at once.

Foreign nationals need notarization by a local notary plus an apostille (in member countries of the Apostille Convention) or consular confirmation (in non-member countries), and a Korean translation. Also prepare a record of loss of Korean nationality or other proof that the name in the Korean family relationship register and the name in your foreign passport belong to the same person.

sections.title: If a Foreign National Receives Real Estate
body: A foreigner who acquires Korean real estate by inheritance must report it to the competent authority within 6 months from the date of acquisition (Act on Report on Real Estate Transactions (부동산 거래신고 등에 관한 법률) Article 8(2)). To register it, you may also need to obtain a separate real estate registration number.

If you receive real estate, sell it and want to send the money abroad, you will need the bank's overseas remittance procedure and tax settlement documents. Compare from the start whether to take the real estate or to let another heir take it and receive a settlement payment.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Signing a blank power of attorney without seeing what has been agreed
Waiting in the belief that unauthenticated scans or photos will be accepted as documents
Only looking into the procedure when the 3 months are almost over

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law sets out the authentication method and document list each heir needs, and, acting under a power of attorney, handles renunciation or limited acceptance filings, the division agreement, and mediation or adjudication on division in Korea. Despite the time difference, you can send us a message through the chat on this page at any time.

faqs.q: I lost Korean nationality long ago, but Korean records still show my old details.
faqs.a: If the loss of nationality was never reported, your old details may remain in the family relationship register. To show you are the same person in the inheritance documents, a report of loss of nationality or proof of identity may be needed, so check which documents are required before getting your signature authenticated.

faqs.q: What if a sibling living abroad will not cooperate in the agreement?
faqs.a: Even while abroad, they become a respondent in mediation and adjudication on division of the estate. Service abroad takes a long time, so secure their exact address and allow plenty of time in your schedule.

guides.title: When You Find Land Still in the Name of a Grandparent Who Died Long Ago
guides.lead: Even land in the name of a grandfather who died decades ago can be registered by inheritance now. However, several inheritances will have piled up in the meantime and older versions of the Civil Act apply, so even identifying the heirs and their shares is not easy.

seo.title: Registering Inheritance of a Grandparent's Land in Korea When There Are Dozens of Heirs | Jisan Law Family Law Center
seo.description: How to settle land left in the name of a grandparent or parent who died long ago in Korea. Covers the deadline for inheritance registration, which law applies at the time of death, finding heirs through removed family register certificates, relatives who cannot be reached, division adjudication and arranging shares, claims of ownership by long-term possession, and acquisition tax penalties.
keywords: grandfather's land in his name Korea

sections.title: What to Check First
body: The older the land, the more the starting point is redrawing the family tree from documents. Relying on memory easily leads to the registration being rejected because an heir was left out. If you know the registered owner but not where the land is, you can search through the ancestral land search service at the city, county or district office.
bullets: Check the current registered owner, area and land category from the land registry and the land ledger
Check the registered owner's certificate of removed family register (제적등본, from birth to death) and date of death
If any heirs have died since, obtain their family relationship documents in turn
Check who is currently using the land and who has been paying the property tax

sections.title: There Is No Deadline, but the Old Law Applies
body: There is no statutory deadline for inheritance registration (상속등기), so it can be done even after decades. However, the heirs and their shares are determined by the law in force at the time of death, so if the person died long ago, an order of heirs or shares different from today's may apply. There were periods when sons, daughters and married daughters received different shares from today, so even within the same family, the shares differ depending on who died when.

If any of the heirs has died in the meantime, that person's share passes in turn to their own heirs. When inheritances pile up like this, the co-heirs, down to grandchildren and great-grandchildren, can number in the dozens.

sections.title: How to Settle Things When There Are Many Heirs
body: If all the heirs stamp a division agreement with their registered seals, the land can be registered in the name of whoever is chosen. If even one cannot be reached or objects, you ask for an adjudication on division of the estate (상속재산분할) against all the other heirs, and for anyone whose whereabouts are unknown, an administrator of an absent person's property (부재자재산관리인) is appointed.

If the land is not worth much, it is sometimes more realistic to first register it in everyone's names by statutory shares and then have the person who needs it buy the other relatives' shares. Grandchildren who received only a small share can end up paying property tax they do not want, so decide together who will transfer shares and who will receive them.

When there are many heirs, collecting everyone's registered seal documents takes months. Certificates of seal impression used for registration must be reissued if they are too old, so plan the order so that the first people's documents do not expire by the time you receive the last person's.

sections.title: What Not to Do
bullets: Writing a division agreement only among close relatives without confirming all the heirs
Suddenly telling a relative who has been using the land to leave
Filing for registration before checking the taxes

sections.title: Problems That Are Easy to Miss
body: If one relative has used the land as their own for a long time, they may claim to have acquired ownership by 20 years of possession (Civil Act (민법) Article 245). Check how their possession began and whether they paid for its use.

Acquisition tax is supposed to be reported within 6 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began, so an inheritance put off for a long time may come with a penalty tax. It is wise to check the taxes with a tax accountant or the local government before registering.

sections.title: How Jisan Law Can Help
body: Jisan Law uses certificates of removed family register to confirm the family tree and the law in force at each time of death, sets out the heirs and their shares, and, dividing the relatives into those who can agree and those who cannot, chooses the right route among a division agreement, appointment of an administrator of an absent person's property and an adjudication on division of the estate. Jisan Law also goes on to handle the application for inheritance registration.

faqs.q: It is my grandfather's land, and my father has also died. Am I directly an heir?
faqs.a: If your grandfather died before your father, your father was your grandfather's heir, and when your father died, that share passed in turn to your father's heirs. If your father died before your grandfather, the grandchildren take your father's place through inheritance by representation (대습상속). Either way, your father's spouse may also be an heir, so start by checking the order of deaths.

faqs.q: I just want to give up my share. Can I still renounce the inheritance now?
faqs.a: Renunciation must be made within 3 months from the day you learned that the inheritance began, so if you learned of it long ago, you can no longer renounce. Instead, you can agree in the division not to take a share, or transfer an already registered share to another relative. Tax may be charged in that case, so check in advance.

moreFaqs.q: How are consultation fees and retainer fees set?
moreFaqs.a: We explain the fees after the consultation, once we have looked at the issues in your case and the scope of the claims. The work involved differs greatly depending on whether it is a review of a divorce-by-agreement settlement or a lawsuit disputing both property division and custody. You can hear our explanation first and then decide.

moreFaqs.q: Where can I have a consultation?
moreFaqs.a: Consultations are available at our main office in Seoul and our branch offices in Incheon, Hongseong and Songpa. Send us a message through the chat on this page and we will arrange the most convenient office and time.

moreFaqs.q: Who will handle my case after the consultation?
moreFaqs.a: The managing partner handles consultations personally. We do not hide behind office managers or associate lawyers, and we set the direction of your case together based on what we hear in the consultation.

moreFaqs.q: Can I receive living expenses during a divorce lawsuit?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. When you file for divorce mediation or a lawsuit, you can apply for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) asking the court to set living expenses or child support temporarily, and you can also make a separate claim for spousal support (부양료) or marriage expenses (혼인생활비용). If it would be hard to get through a long lawsuit without income, it is better to apply for these from the start.

moreFaqs.q: Which court do I file a divorce lawsuit in?
moreFaqs.a: If both spouses live within the jurisdiction of the same family court, you file there. If not, you file in the court for the place where you last lived together, as long as one of you still lives there. Otherwise, you file in the court where the other spouse lives (Family Litigation Act Article 22). If you are separated and live at different addresses, the first step is to check where to file.

moreFaqs.q: Can I divorce without facing my spouse?
moreFaqs.a: If you hire a lawyer, often only the lawyer attends the hearings, and with the court's permission a lawyer can also attend mediation sessions on your behalf. If there has been domestic violence, you can ask the court to provide separate waiting areas. However, some procedures, such as the family investigation (가사조사), require you to take part in person.

moreFaqs.q: Who pays off the home loan after a divorce?
moreFaqs.a: In property division, the spouses also decide who will take on loans taken out for their life together. But this is an agreement between the spouses, and the borrower in the bank's eyes remains the person named on the loan. The spouse taking over the home should check with the bank in advance whether the loan can be transferred into their name, to avoid problems later.

moreFaqs.q: After the divorce, can I change my child's surname to mine?
moreFaqs.a: If it is needed for the child's welfare, you can change the child's surname and family origin (성·본) with the family court's permission (Civil Act Article 781(6)). The court decides based on the child's age and wishes, and how changing the surname would affect the child's life.

moreFaqs.q: There is a judgment, but my ex-spouse won't pay the property division amount.
moreFaqs.a: If you have a judgment or a mediation record (조정조서), you can apply for compulsory execution against the other side's deposits, wages or real estate. You can also apply to the family court for a performance order (이행명령) requiring payment, and an administrative fine can be imposed if it is violated.

moreFaqs.q: Can I divorce even if my spouse lives abroad?
moreFaqs.a: For a divorce by agreement (협의이혼) where one spouse does not live in Korea, there is a procedure for confirming the intent to divorce through the Seoul Family Court or a Korean embassy or consulate abroad (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 75). For a lawsuit, you first need to work out which country's court will hear it and which country's law applies.

moreFaqs.q: Do we both have to go to court together to apply for divorce by agreement?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. In principle, the spouses must go together to the family court with jurisdiction, submit the application and receive the divorce guidance (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 73). Only when one spouse is a Korean national living abroad or is in a prison or detention center and cannot attend may one spouse apply alone. A lawyer cannot apply or receive the confirmation on your behalf.

moreFaqs.q: My husband didn't show up at the confirmation hearing. Is our divorce by agreement over?
moreFaqs.a: Missing one hearing does not end it right away. If you both attend the second confirmation hearing you were told about when you applied, you can receive the confirmation. However, if a spouse fails to appear twice after receiving notice, the application is treated as withdrawn (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 77(2)). If your spouse is not showing up because they no longer want a divorce, you should consider mediation or a lawsuit.

moreFaqs.q: I received the confirmation from the court, but I've changed my mind. Can I undo it?
moreFaqs.a: If the divorce report has not been filed yet, you can submit a withdrawal of intent to divorce (이혼의사철회서), with the certified copy of the confirmation attached, to the city, town or township office of your place of family registration or address (Rules on the Registration of Family Relationships Article 80). However, if your spouse files the divorce report first, that report is accepted, so you need to act quickly. If no one files a report within 3 months, the court's confirmation also loses its effect.

moreFaqs.q: If our divorce-by-agreement settlement is notarized, can it be enforced right away?
moreFaqs.a: The part that promises to pay a fixed sum of money can be enforced without a lawsuit if it is made into a notarized deed (공정증서) with a clause consenting to compulsory execution (Civil Execution Act Article 56, Item 4). But a promise to transfer ownership of real estate cannot be enforced with a notarized deed, so if your ex-spouse does not hand over the documents, you will end up having to sue. For this reason, if the terms are complicated, we also consider going through mediation to obtain a mediation record.

moreFaqs.q: If mediation fails, do I have to file a new complaint from scratch?
moreFaqs.a: No. If mediation fails, the lawsuit is treated as filed when mediation was requested, and the case moves to litigation (Family Litigation Act Article 49; Civil Conciliation Act Article 36). Instead, the court issues a correction order (보정명령) to pay the shortfall in stamp fees and service fees needed for the lawsuit. If you do not pay, the case can be dismissed, so be sure to check the court documents.

moreFaqs.q: I received a decision in lieu of mediation from the court. What happens if I do nothing?
moreFaqs.a: If no one files an objection within 2 weeks of being served with the original copy of the decision, it becomes final and has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Family Litigation Act Article 49; Civil Conciliation Act Article 34). If you object, even because you dislike only part of it, the entire decision loses its effect and the case moves to litigation. The period runs from the day you were served, not the day of the decision, so review it in the same week you receive it.

moreFaqs.q: I filed for mediation within 6 months of learning of the affair, but the mediation session was set for later. Has the deadline passed?
moreFaqs.a: The deadline is judged by the date you filed for mediation. This is because if mediation fails and the case moves to litigation, the lawsuit is treated as filed when mediation was requested (Civil Conciliation Act Article 36). However, if the person who filed for mediation fails to attend two sessions, the application is treated as withdrawn (Article 31 of the same Act), so be sure to attend.

moreFaqs.q: My spouse didn't file an answer. Will the judgment come out right away?
moreFaqs.a: Unlike ordinary civil lawsuits, the rule on deemed admission does not apply to judicial divorce (Family Litigation Act Article 12, proviso), so the plaintiff's claims are not automatically accepted just because there is no answer. The court decides whether there are grounds for divorce by looking at the evidence, so the plaintiff must still submit thorough material. Even so, if the other side does not contest the case, it generally ends sooner than a contested one.

moreFaqs.q: Do I have to split in half a home I bought with my own money before the marriage?
moreFaqs.a: In principle, assets you owned before the marriage are not subject to property division. However, if the marriage was long and your spouse helped keep or increase the value of that home by repaying the loan or maintaining it, it may be included. If money you saved before the marriage became the seed money for a home bought after the marriage, the whole home is usually included in the division, and that money is often reflected as a factor that raises your share of contribution.

moreFaqs.q: Is there property division even if our debts exceed our assets?
moreFaqs.a: Yes, there can be. The Supreme Court has held that a property division claim can be accepted even if the couple's debts exceed their assets and the result is a division of debt (Supreme Court en banc decision of June 20, 2013, 2010므4071, 4088). However, not every debt is divided. The test is whether the debt arose for the marriage, such as for living costs or acquiring joint assets. Debts one spouse ran up alone, such as gambling debts, stay with that spouse.

moreFaqs.q: If I receive the home through property division, do I pay capital gains tax or gift tax?
moreFaqs.a: Courts and the National Tax Service treat assets transferred through property division as a settlement of assets the couple built together, so they are not subject to capital gains tax for the transferring spouse or gift tax for the receiving spouse. On the other hand, if a home is transferred instead of compensation for emotional distress (위자료), it is treated as a sale, and capital gains tax may arise for the transferring spouse. Which one applies is judged not only by the label written in the record or judgment but by the substance, such as what the judgment says and how the divorce came about. If the share received greatly exceeds a reasonable range and appears to be a way to avoid tax, gift tax may be imposed on the excess (Supreme Court decision of September 12, 2017, 2016두58901), and if you transfer the title before reporting the divorce, it may be taxed as a gift even if there is a mediation record. Acquisition by property division also qualifies for a special acquisition tax rate (Local Tax Act Article 15(1), Item 6). Get tax advice as well before deciding the wording and the timing of the registration.

moreFaqs.q: Do I have to share money I earned after we separated?
moreFaqs.a: In a judicial divorce, property division is in principle based on the time the final hearing on the facts ends. However, assets one spouse built up alone during a long separation, unrelated to assets made together during the marriage, may be excluded. On the other hand, assets that grew from resources built together before the separation are included. Keep a record of the date the separation began and who paid the living costs after that.

moreFaqs.q: Can a father get custody?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. The court decides based on the child's welfare, not on whether the parent is the mother or the father. It looks at who has mainly cared for the child, whether the child is living stably now, and whether the parenting plan after the divorce is realistic. Financial ability is only one factor, and any shortfall is considered to be made up through child support. If you have actually handled school drop-offs and pick-ups, doctor visits and school matters, records of that are your strongest material.

moreFaqs.q: Does the court listen to the child's opinion?
moreFaqs.a: If the child is 13 or older, the court must in principle hear the child's opinion before deciding the person with parental authority or the custodial parent (Rules on Family Litigation Articles 18-2 and 100). Younger children may also be interviewed during the family investigation. What the child says does not decide the outcome on its own, and coaching a child to give the answer a parent wants can actually work against that parent.

moreFaqs.q: Can the custodial parent set at the divorce be changed later?
moreFaqs.a: If it is needed for the child's welfare, you can ask the family court to change the arrangements for custody (Civil Act Article 837(5)), and you can also ask to change the person with parental authority (Civil Act Article 909(6)). An agreement between the parents does not automatically change a court decision, so you must go through the change procedure. You need material showing what has changed since the divorce and how that change affects the child.

moreFaqs.q: The lawsuit is ongoing, and my spouse left home with our child.
moreFaqs.a: You can apply at the same time for a pre-trial measure designating who will care for the child until the judgment (designation of a temporary custodial parent) and for an order to hand over the child (유아인도) (Family Litigation Act Article 62). The court looks carefully at where and how the child is living now, and whether changing the child's environment would be better for the child. Struggling to take the child back at school or daycare can work against you, so go through the court procedure.

moreFaqs.q: We divorced without setting child support. Can I also receive past child support?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. If you ask the family court for a ruling on child support, you can claim not only future child support but also the past child support you paid alone. Case law holds that the limitation period for past child support does not run while the child is a minor, and starts when the child becomes an adult (Supreme Court en banc decision, 2024). If your child is already an adult, the period is already running, so do not delay. However, past support is often reduced in light of the parents' circumstances at the time.

moreFaqs.q: If I remarry, will my ex-spouse's child support stop?
moreFaqs.a: Remarriage alone does not stop it. Even if the custodial parent remarries, no parent–child relationship arises automatically between the new spouse and the child, so the biological parent's duty to pay child support remains. If income or the number of dependents has changed greatly after remarriage, you can ask to change child support, but the court looks at the parents' overall finances and the child's needs together, not just the fact of remarriage.

moreFaqs.q: I quit my job and want to reduce child support. Can't I just send less?
moreFaqs.a: If you reduce payments on your own, the shortfall becomes unpaid support, and you may face sanctions such as a performance order, detention for contempt (감치) or suspension of your driver's license. If your circumstances have changed, you must reach an agreement with the other parent or ask the family court to change (reduce) the child support (Civil Act Article 837(5)). Child support that is already overdue is hard to reduce later, so file as soon as your circumstances change. Quitting voluntarily or investment losses are rarely accepted as grounds for a reduction.

moreFaqs.q: Who can receive advance payment of child support?
moreFaqs.a: You can apply if you have a basis such as a judgment setting child support or a child support protocol (양육비부담조서); the average child support received in the 3 months, or the 3 consecutive payments, before applying is less than the advance payment amount; and you have applied to the Child Support Enforcement Agency (양육비이행관리원) for legal or collection support or have gone through procedures such as a performance order or compulsory execution (Act on Securing and Supporting Child Support Payments Article 21-6; Enforcement Decree of the same Act Article 17-5). For cases decided by October 28, 2026, there is an income requirement of 1.5 times the standard median income or less, and from cases decided on or after October 29, this requirement no longer applies. Under current government guidance, the amount is KRW 200,000 per child per month. For inquiries, contact the Child Support Enforcement Agency (1644-6621).

moreFaqs.q: My ex won't let me see our child. Do I still have to pay child support?
moreFaqs.a: Yes, you do. Visitation and child support are separate obligations, so if you stop paying because you cannot see your child, you become the one subject to a performance order and sanctions. Visitation should be pursued separately through a performance order for visitation.

moreFaqs.q: When and how can I receive a share of my ex-spouse's National Pension?
moreFaqs.a: You can receive a split pension (분할연금) if, during your ex-spouse's coverage period, you actually lived together as a married couple for 5 years or more, and after the divorce your ex-spouse becomes entitled to an old-age pension and you reach the pension age (National Pension Act Article 64). You must claim it within 5 years of meeting all the requirements, and if you have not yet reached the age, you can file an advance claim within 3 years of the divorce (Article 64-3 of the same Act). Periods with no real marital relationship, such as separation or one spouse leaving home, are excluded from the marriage period.

moreFaqs.q: The judgment is final. Do I still have to report the divorce?
moreFaqs.a: A judicial divorce takes effect when the judgment becomes final, but to have it reflected in the family relationship register, you must report it within 1 month of the date it became final, attaching a certified copy of the judgment and a certificate of finality (Act on the Registration of Family Relationships Articles 78 and 58). The person who filed the lawsuit makes the report, and the other spouse may also do so. Missing the deadline without a valid reason can lead to an administrative fine (Article 122 of the same Act).

moreFaqs.q: Can I handle a divorce lawsuit on my own without a lawyer?
moreFaqs.a: Yes, you can. When the divorce and its terms are mostly agreed, some people file for mediation themselves and finish that way. However, if the assets are large, your spouse seems to be hiding assets, or custody is disputed, it is easy to lose out by not using procedures such as provisional attachment (가압류) or asset inquiries at the right time. Even if you proceed on your own, it is a good idea to have the wording of the complaint or the mediation record checked once.

moreFaqs.q: What should I bring to the first consultation?
moreFaqs.a: Please bring your marriage relationship certificate, a note listing in date order when problems occurred, a list of the assets and loans you know of, and material such as KakaoTalk messages, recordings and medical certificates. If you have received a complaint or court documents, bring them in their envelope. It is fine if you have not gathered everything yet. We will decide together in the consultation what else needs to be collected.

moreFaqs.q: I had an affair. Can I still file for divorce first?
moreFaqs.a: You can file a lawsuit, but if you are mainly responsible for the breakdown of the marriage, the divorce claim is in principle not accepted. You first need to examine whether you fall under an exception recognized by case law, such as when your spouse also has no intention of continuing the marriage, or when you have shown consideration that offsets your responsibility, such as steadily sending living expenses and child support.

moreFaqs.q: What happens if someone violates a victim protection order?
moreFaqs.a: Anyone who approaches or contacts the victim despite a protection order (보호명령) or temporary protection order can be punished by imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine of up to KRW 20 million, or short-term detention (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence Crimes Article 63). Report any violation to 112 right away and keep the messages and call records.

moreFaqs.q: My partner secretly used my seal to register our marriage.
moreFaqs.a: Since there was no agreement to marry, you can file a claim for nullity of the marriage (혼인무효), and you can file at any time without a time limit (Civil Act Article 815, Item 1; Family Litigation Act Article 23). A criminal complaint over the forged documents can also be considered.

moreFaqs.q: I never asked for living expenses. Can I receive several years' worth at once?
moreFaqs.a: That is difficult. Case law holds that past support can be claimed only for the period after it was requested but not paid (Supreme Court decision of August 25, 2017, 2014스26). Start now by making a request in writing, with the amount and date, so there is a record.

moreFaqs.q: More than 2 years after the divorce, I found out about hidden assets.
moreFaqs.a: The right to claim property division expires 2 years after the date of divorce, so in principle you can no longer claim division of those assets. Even when assets not dealt with in the judgment are found later, any additional claim must be made within the 2 years.

moreFaqs.q: My ex-husband was a public official. Can I also receive a share of his civil service pension?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. If the marriage lasted 5 years or more during his period of service, you are divorced, your former spouse is entitled to a retirement pension, and you have reached age 65, you receive a split pension. You must claim it from the Government Employees Pension Service within 3 years of meeting the requirements (Public Officials Pension Act Article 45).

moreFaqs.q: I received a divorce judgment from a foreign court. Am I also divorced in Korea?
moreFaqs.a: A foreign judgment is recognized in Korea only if it meets the recognition requirements in Civil Procedure Act Article 217. If the judgment meets them, you report the divorce with the judgment and a translation attached, and it is reflected in the family relationship register. If the other spouse was only served by public notice (공시송달), the judgment may not be recognized.

moreFaqs.q: If I change my child's surname, does it cut off the relationship with the biological father?
moreFaqs.a: No. A change of surname and family origin only changes the name, so the relationship with the biological father for inheritance, support, visitation and child support stays as it is. Changing the legal parent–child relationship itself requires a separate procedure called full adoption (친양자 입양).

moreFaqs.q: My child lives with me, but my ex-husband is the person with parental authority, so school matters are a hassle.
moreFaqs.a: You can ask the family court to change the person with parental authority (Civil Act Article 909(6)). If the other parent also agrees, it is often settled fairly quickly through mediation, and once the decision becomes final, you report the change of the person with parental authority within 1 month.

moreFaqs.q: It's been four months since I learned my spouse hid a previous marriage. Can our marriage be annulled?
moreFaqs.a: Annulment of a marriage due to fraud cannot be claimed once 3 months have passed since you learned of the fraud (Civil Act Article 823). If the period has passed, instead of annulment, we consider pursuing a divorce and compensation for emotional distress. When you found out may become a point of dispute, so write down how you came to know.

moreFaqs.q: Which court do I file an affair lawsuit in?
moreFaqs.a: If you stay married and claim only against the affair partner, you file in a civil court (the district court); if you claim together with a judicial divorce, you file in the family court. In a civil case, the court for the defendant's address is the default, and in some cases you can also file at the court for the place where the wrongful act occurred. This differs from case to case, so we confirm it before filing the complaint.

moreFaqs.q: Can I bring an affair lawsuit if the affair partner is the same sex?
moreFaqs.a: Infidelity (부정행위) means unfaithful conduct that breaches a spouse's duty of fidelity, so it is not limited by the other person's sex. Even a relationship with a same-sex partner allows a claim for compensation for emotional distress (위자료) if it harmed the couple's shared married life. The requirements and the way of proving it are the same as in other cases.

moreFaqs.q: They say they only talked online and never actually met. Can I still sue?
moreFaqs.a: Even without meeting in person, a long-running conversation premised on a romantic relationship may be recognized as infidelity. However, whether it is recognized and how much is awarded vary greatly with the intensity and duration of the conversations. We organize the content and frequency of the messages by period and assess it from there.

moreFaqs.q: Can I report the affair to the police?
moreFaqs.a: The crime of adultery lost its effect after the Constitutional Court ruled it unconstitutional in 2015, so an affair itself cannot be punished criminally. The way to hold the affair partner responsible is a civil claim for compensation for emotional distress (위자료). However, if another crime such as threats or assault occurred along the way, you can file a separate criminal complaint for that part.

moreFaqs.q: We divorced by agreement and I never raised the affair. Can I sue the other woman after the divorce?
moreFaqs.a: A claim against the affair partner is separate from the divorce, so you can bring it even after divorcing. You do need to check the time limit, though: if you claim on the ground that the marriage broke down, the 3 years run from the date of the divorce; otherwise, they run from the day you learned of the infidelity and the affair partner. If you settled compensation with your spouse in the divorce by agreement (협의이혼), that amount may be taken into account.

moreFaqs.q: My husband saw two different women. Do I have to sue them separately?
moreFaqs.a: Each affair partner is separately liable for their own infidelity. You can name several defendants in one complaint or file separately, but the amount and liability are decided person by person. The evidence and the date you found out differ for each affair partner, so calculate each time limit separately as well.

moreFaqs.q: During my affair lawsuit, my spouse served me with a divorce complaint.
moreFaqs.a: The two cases proceed separately but dispute the same facts. In the divorce lawsuit, you can raise your spouse's infidelity as a ground for divorce and a basis for compensation, and you can also use the material submitted in the affair lawsuit. Keep your statements consistent so that what you say in the two cases does not conflict.

moreFaqs.q: Apart from the compensation from the affair lawsuit, can I also get compensation from my spouse in the divorce?
moreFaqs.a: You can also claim divorce compensation (위자료) from your spouse. However, if it is for the same emotional suffering caused by the same infidelity, the amount you received from the affair partner may be taken into account, so you may not receive the full amount twice. If there are grounds separate from the affair, such as your spouse's verbal abuse or refusal to care for the children, raise those separately.

moreFaqs.q: Can I recover KakaoTalk chats my spouse deleted?
moreFaqs.a: If your spouse consents, deleted chats may be recovered through digital forensics. If you give your spouse's phone to a recovery company without their consent, other legal problems can arise. If recovery is difficult, we first look for material that can be obtained through court procedures.

moreFaqs.q: Is a motel receipt and a card statement enough?
moreFaqs.a: A lodging payment record is meaningful circumstantial evidence, but it does not show who was there. It gains strength when combined with messages, photos and car movements from the same day. If the payment date is recent, it can also serve as the basis for applying to preserve CCTV footage (증거보전) for that date.

moreFaqs.q: I opened my spouse's phone and took photos of the KakaoTalk chats. Can I use them?
moreFaqs.a: They are sometimes accepted as evidence in a civil trial, but being usable as evidence and being punishable are separate questions. If you unlocked the phone or found out the password and opened it secretly, it may raise issues such as violation of secrecy (비밀침해). If you already have such material, review with us how it was obtained before submitting it.

moreFaqs.q: Will my spouse or the affair partner find out if I apply for evidence preservation?
moreFaqs.a: The application names the other party, and as a rule the other party is also notified of the evidence examination date (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 381). In urgent cases, notice may be omitted. If you don't know the affair partner's name, the court may appoint a special representative (특별대리인) to proceed (Article 378 of the same Act).

moreFaqs.q: Can I hire a private investigator?
moreFaqs.a: Methods such as following and filming someone or secretly finding out a person's address can create legal problems even for the person who hired the investigator. Even if the agency brings back material, an unlawful method of collection gives the other side grounds to file a criminal complaint. Before hiring anyone, confirm what they will do and how, and first check whether the material can be obtained through court procedures.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: Will my company find out that I've been sued in an affair lawsuit?
moreFaqs.a: The court does not separately notify your company of the lawsuit or the judgment. However, if a provisional attachment (가압류) or seizure is placed on your salary, your company receives the court order, so it may come out that way. Some people resolve the case through mediation or settlement to avoid this.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: What if the other person's spouse testifies as a witness that I approached first?
moreFaqs.a: Sometimes the other person's spouse gives an untrue account to protect their own family. In that case, you rebut it with objective material, such as chat records that contradict the testimony or messages in which they first suggested meeting. This is why you should not delete your records with the other person's spouse.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: I'm married too, and I've been sued in an affair lawsuit. I'm afraid my family will find out.
moreFaqs.a: The court does not separately inform your family about the lawsuit. However, if the complaint or other documents are delivered to your home, a family member may receive them. Once you appoint a legal representative, later documents go to the representative, so it is better to decide quickly, even after the first service.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: The plaintiff came to my workplace and posted about me on social media. Can I file a complaint too?
moreFaqs.a: If they spread the facts at your company or on social media, you can file a separate criminal complaint for defamation (명예훼손) under Criminal Act (형법) Article 307; if they came and threatened you, for threats (협박) and similar offenses. However, that complaint and your liability for the affair are judged separately. Save the posts and messages so the dates are visible.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: I only learned that a judgment was entered after service by publication when I got a seizure notice.
moreFaqs.a: If you were unaware of the lawsuit through no fault of your own, you can file a late appeal (추후보완 항소) within 2 weeks from the day that reason ceased, usually the day you learned of the judgment entered after service by publication (공시송달) (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 173). The period is short, so check the seizure order and the judgment right away. To stop enforcement, you must also file a separate application for a stay of execution (집행정지).

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: It's already over between me and the other person's spouse, but they keep contacting me during the lawsuit.
moreFaqs.a: It is wiser not to reply. Contact during the lawsuit can be used by the plaintiff as evidence that the relationship is continuing, and it becomes a reason to raise the amount. Keep a record of declining contact, but do not continue the conversation.

moreFaqs.category: Infidelity & Affair Lawsuits · Responding as Defendant
moreFaqs.q: I received a recommendation for settlement, but the amount is higher than I expected.
moreFaqs.a: If you file an objection within 2 weeks of receiving the original of the recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정), the case goes back to trial (Civil Procedure Act (민사소송법) Article 226). If you don't object, it takes the same effect as a judicial settlement and can no longer be contested. Compare it with the amount you would expect from a judgment and decide within the deadline.

moreFaqs.q: Can a settlement amount be higher than what a judgment would award?
moreFaqs.a: A settlement amount is decided by the parties, so it can be higher or lower than what a judgment would likely award. The amount may also change if the other side wants to finish quickly or wants to avoid a written judgment on record. Also keep in mind that insisting on an unreasonable amount can break down the settlement and drag out the lawsuit.

moreFaqs.q: Can we settle even while the lawsuit is going on?
moreFaqs.a: You can settle at any time before judgment is delivered. Once you settle, the case ends with a withdrawal of the lawsuit or with court mediation (조정) or a recommendation for settlement (화해권고결정). If it is resolved through the court, it has the same effect as a judicial settlement, so you can seek compulsory execution if the promise is not kept.

moreFaqs.q: Can I agree to receive the settlement money in installments?
moreFaqs.a: Installments are possible. However, include a clause that if even one payment is missed, the remaining balance becomes due at once, and if you put it in a notarial deed (공정증서) consenting to compulsory execution, you can enforce it immediately when a payment is missed. Also write the payment dates and the bank account in the settlement agreement.

moreFaqs.q: Can a settlement agreement stop the two of them from seeing each other again?
moreFaqs.a: A settlement agreement cannot physically prevent them from meeting. Instead, if you set a no-contact clause and a penalty for breach (위약벌), the price of meeting again becomes clear. If the clause is breached, you claim the penalty, and for any relationship newly continued after the settlement, we look at whether a separate claim for compensation is possible.

moreFaqs.q: I signed a settlement agreement, but the plaintiff has sued me again.
moreFaqs.a: If the agreement contains a no-further-claims clause (부제소 합의) saying no further lawsuit will be brought over this matter, you submit the agreement and ask the court to dismiss the lawsuit. However, a lawsuit over new meetings after the period covered by the settlement may be judged separately. Keep the original agreement and the payment records.

moreFaqs.q: How much compensation is usually awarded in an affair case?
moreFaqs.a: There is no fixed table and the differences between cases are large, so it is hard to name a figure in advance. The court sets the amount by looking at the length and extent of the relationship, whether the affair partner knew of the marriage, their attitude after being found out, and whether the marriage broke down. A long relationship, continuing to meet after being found out, or a marriage that ended in divorce pushes the amount up; a short relationship that ended soon, or a marriage that had already been badly shaken beforehand, pushes it down.

moreFaqs.q: We've been married less than a year. Will the compensation be lower?
moreFaqs.a: The length of the marriage is one of many factors. A short marriage can be a factor that lowers the amount, but infidelity from the very start of a marriage is sometimes seen as having deepened the suffering. In the end, the nature of the infidelity and what happened afterward are considered together.

moreFaqs.q: If the affair partner apologizes during the lawsuit, will the amount go down?
moreFaqs.a: A sincere apology and ending the relationship can be taken into account when the amount is set. On the other hand, what is written in a letter of apology can also be used as evidence admitting liability. If you are the defendant, decide the scope and wording of the apology first; if you are the plaintiff, weigh the terms separately from the apology before accepting it.

moreFaqs.q: If I garnish her salary, will the other woman's company find out?
